### #82 Macro arithmetic (growth/annualize/deflate/rebase/per-capita/contributions) — the standard library (`c00_data_utilities/macro_arithmetic.py`)
**Functions:** `macro_growth`, `macro_deflate`, `macro_rebase`, `macro_per_capita`, `macro_contributions`

**When:** the everyday deterministic **macro identities** with explicit, checked conventions — growth rate (period-over-period or log-diff, with optional annualization), nominal→real via a deflator, rebasing to an index (base=100 default), a magnitude per capita, and the decomposition of component contributions to an aggregate growth rate with a **hard additivity check**. This is the most correctness-critical file: no RNG, pure identities, structural gates.

**When NOT:** for class-agnostic transformations over ts/xts/tsibble (without macro semantics) → `time_series_class` #78; for chain-linked real indices where the contributions are NOT exactly additive — `macro_contributions` **exposes** the chain-link residual (it does not make it disappear) and requires already-consistent contribution-to-growth inputs.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** all numeric inputs **FINITE** (no NA/NaN/Inf — no silent propagation in a deterministic operation); equal lengths (deflate/per_capita); positive integers `periods`/`frequency`/`base_period` (round-based, overflow-safe); `deflator>0`, `population>0`, `anchor≠0`, `log=TRUE ⇒ x>0`, `annualize=TRUE ⇒ frequency`; `weights` conformable with `ncol(components)`. The inputs are usually long-format `value` vectors (the user's upload) — run `imputeTS` #80 first if there are NA (the finite gate blocks).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `macro_growth` vs `ts_transform` (#78 `ts_pc`/`ts_pcy`/`ts_pca`) — prefer `macro_growth` when you need the **explicit annualization convention and the division-by-zero flag**; `macro_rebase` (base_value=100) vs `ts_rebase` (#78, base=1 and date-anchored). `log=TRUE` for log growth (additively decomposable, suitable for large changes/aggregation) vs simple growth (directly interpretable %).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp` — atomic/matrix):
- `macro_growth`: `growth` (the first `periods` points = **structural leading NA**, not an error), `annualized` (NULL if `annualize=FALSE`), `annualize_convention` (**simple: `(1+g)^(freq/periods)-1` compound; log: `g*(freq/periods)` linear**), `n_nonfinite_growth` (**division-by-zero flag** — a zero base), `n_nonfinite_annualized` (a negative base^fractional = NaN, e.g. a level crossing 0).
- `macro_deflate`: `real = nominal/deflator*base`; `macro_rebase`: `index`, `anchor`=`x[base_period]`; `macro_per_capita`: `per_capita = x/population*scale`.
- `macro_contributions`: `contributions` (matrix →nested rows+dimnames), `contribution_total` (rowSums), **`additivity_checked`/`max_abs_residual`/`checks_passed`** — if `aggregate_growth` is supplied and `max|sum(contrib) − aggregate|>tol` ⇒ a **hard `stop`** (the contributions do NOT add up; possible chain-link/inconsistent inputs).
- **Interpretation traps**: (1) annualization is compound for simple growth (q/q 1% → 4.06%, NOT 4%). (2) `n_nonfinite_*>0` means a silent NaN that `to_mcp` would serialise to null — check it explicitly. (3) `macro_contributions` takes **growth rates** per component (column) and period (row), NOT levels.

**Sources:** the standard library (no external dependency) — arithmetic identities; the compound annualization convention (live-verified in the wrapper); IMF/OECD growth-accounting conventions; log-growth additivity (Tornqvist/log-diff decomposition, standard).

### #252 Correlation filter — greedy removal of redundant variables — `caret` + `stats` (`c00_data_utilities/correlation_filter_greedy.py`)

**Functions:** `cf_cor_matrix` [`cor`] — a **checked** p×p correlation matrix (hard gate on zero variance) + `mean_abs_cor`/`max_abs_offdiag`/PSD diagnostics. `cf_find_correlation` [`findCorrelation`] — **which** columns leave (indices **and** names) + max|r| before/after. `cf_filter` [end-to-end] — data → correlation matrix → greedy filter → **filtered data**, with a second **APPLY** path (`keep =`) for out-of-sample use.

**When:** as **pre-processing before** any collinearity-sensitive model (regression, PCA, high-dimensional ML) over an **observations × variables** matrix (countries × indicators, periods × variables): you drop as many columns as needed so that **no** remaining pairwise |r| exceeds `cutoff`. The rule is explicit in the help page itself: "If two variables have a high correlation, the function looks at the **mean absolute correlation** of each variable and **removes the variable with the largest** mean absolute correlation" — that is, the **globally most redundant** one leaves, not an arbitrary member of the pair. Flow: `cf_cor_matrix` (what is there) → `cf_find_correlation` (what leaves) → `cf_filter` (fit **and** apply).

**When NOT:** on **time series in I(1) levels** — the sample correlation does not converge to a population parameter (spurious; Granger–Newbold 1974) ⇒ supply **explicit differences** upstream, never implicit differencing here. For correlation **significance** (p-values/CI/multiplicity) → `desc_cor_test` (#81). For **distances/clustering/MDS** (`as.dist(1-r)`) → `dm_cor_dist` (#240, cat 29) — **a different object with different semantics**, it does not feed `findCorrelation`. For **compression** instead of **selection** → `composite_index_dimensionality` (#117). For exact **linear combinations** → `findLinearCombos` (not exposed). For stateful pipelines (`preProcess`/`recipes`) → **explicitly rejected** (`the normative gate spec` §3b: they break "one wrapper = one node"). Charts: **frontend only** (§5).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Raw data** (`cf_cor_matrix`/`cf_filter` FIT): a numeric `matrix`/`DataFrame` with **rows = observations**, **columns = variables**; **all** columns numeric (`cor`: "'x' must be numeric"); **without NA/NaN/Inf**; **n ≥ 3**; **p ≥ 2**; **no constant** column; **no duplicate colnames** (the names *are* the fitted params). Tool: `imputeTS` (#80) for the NA; `run_adf_test` (#1) if the columns are time series.
- **Correlation matrix** (`cf_find_correlation`): numeric, **square**, **symmetric**, with a **unit diagonal**, |r| ≤ 1, without NA, without duplicate names. **None** of these checks is performed by `caret` (see the traps) — they are all ours.
- **`0 < cutoff < 1`** (typically 0.75–0.95) and **`exact` logical**. The checking tool before you choose a `cutoff`: **`cf_cor_matrix`** (`max_abs_offdiag`, `mean_abs_cor`, `n_pairs`).
- **APPLY** (`cf_filter(keep=)`): non-empty, unique names that **all exist** in the new data; there **n ≥ 1** suffices (the names are given, not estimated).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `exact = TRUE` (**default**) always, unless `p` is prohibitively large: it recomputes the mean correlations at every step and "will remove a **smaller** number of predictors but can be much slower" (help Details). `exact = FALSE` only as an **explicit** speed choice — the two paths give **different sets** (live on the help-page `R1`, `cutoff = 0.6`: exact → {x1,x4,x5}; fast → {x1,x3,x4,x5}). `method = "spearman"/"kendall"` when the relationship is monotone-nonlinear or there are outliers (`kendall` is O(n²)). `cf_filter(keep =..)` for **every** out-of-sample application. `cutoff` 0.75 (aggressive) / 0.9 (default) / 0.95 (conservative) — but read `max_abs_offdiag` first: if it is below the cutoff, **nothing leaves**.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `cf_cor_matrix`: `cor` (p×p — chart-data heatmap), `mean_abs_cor` (**the criterion of the greedy algorithm** per variable), `max_abs_offdiag`/`max_abs_pair`/`max_abs_index`, `min_cor`/`max_cor`/`n_pairs`, `method`/`use` (`"everything"`, PINNED), `eigen_min`/`is_psd`.
- `cf_find_correlation`: **`remove_index`/`remove_names`** and **`keep_index`/`keep_names`** (= the **fitted params**, §3b gate 6; always sorted ascending), `n_removed`/`n_kept`/`share_removed`, and the **before/after** pair: `max_abs_before` vs `max_abs_after`, `n_pairs_above_before` vs `n_pairs_above_after` (**always 0** — the invariant of the algorithm, confirmed as a post-check).
- `cf_filter`: **`data`** (the filtered data — the **only producer/`register`** of the card; it becomes a handle for downstream regression/ML/PCA), `mode` (`"fit"` | `"apply"`), `keep_names`/`remove_names`, `n_variables_in`/`out`. **In `mode = "apply"`** `cor`/`mean_abs_cor` are `NULL` and `max_abs_before/after` are `NA` — this is **documented** and means "**no** re-estimation".

**Critical traps** (all live-verified, version 4.6.1 / caret 7.0.1):
- **`exact` PINNED — determinism (§5).** The documented default is `exact = ncol(x) < 100`: **the algorithm changes at 100 columns**. A node that changed path because the user added the 100th variable would not be reproducible ⇒ **an explicit argument with our own fixed default `TRUE`**, never the package default.
- **Canonicalization.** The output order of `caret` depends on the column order (the same **set**, a different **order** when they are reversed) ⇒ we always return **sorted** indices/names. No randomness anywhere; `identical` over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (wrapper **and** node).
- **`findCorrelation` requires a correlation matrix — but does not enforce it.** With `exact = FALSE` it **silently accepts raw data** (a 10×5 random matrix → "2 3 1"), a **non-square** 3×4 → `numeric(0)`, **p = 1** → `numeric(0)`. Only the `exact` path checks symmetry ("correlation matrix is not symmetric"). **`diag = 5` and `r = 3` pass silently on both** — anything symmetric is accepted as a "correlation" (did you perhaps supply a **covariance** matrix? → `cov2cor`).
- **A constant column ⇒ `cor` → NA with only the warning** "the standard deviation is zero", and then `findCorrelation` fails cryptically ("The correlation matrix has some missing values." / "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed") ⇒ a hard gate that **names** the constant columns.
- **`n = 1` ⇒ the whole matrix is NA with no warning at all; `n = 2` ⇒ every |r| is 1 by construction** (two points define a line) ⇒ a hard gate `n ≥ 3` on the fit.
- **`cutoff` outside (0,1):** 1.5 → `integer(0)` silently (nothing is filtered); ≤ 0 → removes almost everything. `caret` does not check.
- **PSD = a diagnostic, not a gate** (a documented deviation): a non-PSD matrix cannot come from data, but the greedy algorithm remains well defined — and **the help page's own `R1` matrix has a minimum eigenvalue of −0.2634288** (the same holds for published matrices rounded to 2 decimals) ⇒ it is exposed as `eigen_min`/`is_psd`, it does not block.
- **PINNED arguments:** `verbose = FALSE` (`verbose = TRUE` **prints with `cat`** — "Compare row 1 and column 5 with corr 0.85 …" — a §5 violation); `names = FALSE` (the **Value section of the help page is inverted**: "A vector of indices … when `names = TRUE`", whereas live it returns **names** — we give **both**, produced by us); `cor(use = "everything")` (`pairwise.complete.obs` computes each pair on a **different sample** ⇒ possibly non-PSD, an inconsistent filter).
- **§3b gate 6 — fit/apply externalization.** `keep_names`/`remove_names` **are** the fitted params and are passed back into `cf_filter(keep = …)`. **Critical:** a re-fit on the test set changes the **set** of columns (different correlations) and the coefficients of the trained model are applied to the **wrong columns** (live-verified in the tests: a different sample → a different filter). The model: KNIME Normalizer → "Normalize Model".
- **§3b gate 2 — no implicit standardisation.** Correlation is invariant to linear transformations ⇒ there **is no** `scale`/`center` argument (it would be a no-op implying a non-existent option).
- **Masking:** `library(caret)` is **not** called — `requireNamespace` + `findCorrelation`. `caret` drags in `ggplot2` (Depends), which **masks `Position`** in the shared `source` env (live `conflicts(detail = TRUE)`). The S3 registration at namespace load (131 methods) is **entirely** on generics of `caret` itself (`train.`/`rfe.`/`varImp.`/`predictors.` …) — **no** `predict.*`/`plot.*`/`update.*` on a base/stats generic (cf. `quanteda $.dfm`, `proxy` on `dist`).

**Sources:** **caret 7.0.1** `the findCorrelation documentation` (live-verified version 4.6.1): Usage `findCorrelation(x, cutoff = 0.9, verbose = FALSE, names = FALSE, exact = ncol(x) < 100)`; Details (the mean-absolute-correlation rule; `exact` = re-evaluation, "will remove a smaller number of predictors but can be much slower"); the **inverted Value**; the `R1` example — < Kuhn & Johnson (2013) *Applied Predictive Modeling*, Springer, ch. 3 "Data Pre-Processing" (Removing Predictors / between-predictor correlations — the textbook source of the greedy procedure, as cited in the wrapper header); version 4.6.1 `the cor documentation`/`the sd documentation`/`?cov2cor` (warning-only "the standard deviation is zero", live-verified); Granger & Newbold (1974) "Spurious regressions in econometrics", *Journal of Econometrics* 2(2) 111-120; Hamilton, Ma & Xi, NBER WP 32068 (§3b gate 3 — see #256); `the normative gate spec` §3b normative gates 2 & 6 (fit/apply externalization; KNIME "Normalize Model") + REJECTED `recipes`/`preProcess`; wrapper footer *IMPLEMENTATION NOTE* (7 live-verified silent-wrong behaviours; `conflicts(detail = TRUE)`; the invariant "no remaining |r| > cutoff" over 600 random cases, exact **and** fast, 0 violations).

### #253 Polynomial and interaction terms — the design matrix — `stats` + `base` (`c00_data_utilities/design_matrix_orthogonal.py`)

**Functions:** `ply_poly` [`poly`] — **orthogonal** (default) or **raw** polynomials of one column + the **mandatory return** of `attr(poly, "coefs")` (`alpha`, `norm2`) + an **APPLY path**. `ply_interactions` [`model.matrix`, **with no formula surface**] — verified column names and an explicit interaction order; the formula is built **internally** from language objects. `ply_model_matrix` [`model.matrix` **with** a one-sided formula] — the advanced path, **doubly** allowlisted. `ply_interaction_factor` [`interaction`] — **one** combined factor (drop/sep/lex.order) + empty levels + an optional 0/1 indicator matrix.

**When:** immediately **before** any regression/ML node, when you need **non-linearity** (polynomials: Phillips curve, diminishing returns) or **interactions** (`a*b`, regime × variable, country × sector). The node builds the **design matrix** explicitly, gated and — most critically — **reproducibly out of sample**: it returns **and accepts back** the fitted params (`coefs_alpha`/`coefs_norm2` for the poly; `xlev` + `contrasts` + `column_names` for the matrix).

**When NOT:** for model **estimation** — the node gives **only** X (the formula is **one-sided**; the dependent variable does not belong here). For splines/semi-parametric bases (`ns`/`bs`) → a different family with its own card. For **discretising** a continuous variable into categories → #255 (`discretisation_numeric_column`). For **calendar** dummies → #254 (`hd_dummies`). For **filtering** collinear columns → #252 (`cf_filter`). For sparse matrices (`sparse.model.matrix`) → a new dependency, out of scope. For stateful pipelines (`recipes` prep/bake) → **explicitly rejected** (`the normative gate spec` §3b). Charts: **frontend only** (§5).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **`data`**: a `DataFrame`, non-empty, with **unique, valid** column names (`^[A-Za-z.][A-Za-z0-9._]*$` — the formula is built from **symbols**, not text); **no list columns** ("invalid type (list) for variable"); `numeric`/`factor`/`character`/`logical` are allowed.
- **No NA/Inf at all** in the columns that are **actually** used — a hard gate **before** the call, because `model.frame` **silently drops** the incomplete rows (live 6 → 5) and breaks the alignment with y. Tool: `imputeTS` (#80).
- **Factors**: **≥ 2 levels** ("contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels" — cryptic, caught beforehand) and **≤ `max_levels`** (default 30). The **upper bound on columns** is checked **before** construction (`column_bound` ≤ `max_columns`, default 200) ⇒ a giant matrix is **never** built.
- **`ply_poly`**: **one** numeric column (n×1), ≥ 2 values, without NA/NaN/Inf; **`degree` a positive integer strictly smaller** than the number of unique values; `name` a valid identifier; `coefs_alpha` **and** `coefs_norm2` together, of length **exactly** `degree` and `degree+2` (strictly positive), **only** with `raw = FALSE`.
- **`ply_interaction_factor`**: **≥ 2 unique categorical** columns — **numeric ones are rejected** (see the traps); `prod(nlevels) ≤ max_levels` when `drop = FALSE`. Tool: `bn_quantile_bins` (#255) to discretise first.
- Dimension-checking tool: **`ply_interactions(order = 1)`** — look at `column_bound`/`n_columns` **before** you raise the order (interactions multiply).

**Alternatives + criterion:** **`ply_interactions` is the recommended route** (no formula from the user ⇒ the RCE surface **does not even exist**); `ply_model_matrix` **only** when you genuinely need an expression that cannot be expressed as "names + order" (`I(x^2)`, `log(x)`, nested factors). `raw = TRUE` for **interpretable** coefficients on the original scale — the price: heavy collinearity, and the p-values of the lower degrees **change** when a higher one is added; `raw = FALSE` (default) = orthogonal, numerically stable, uncorrelated columns. `contr.sum` when you want interactions as **deviations from the mean**; `contr.poly` for **ordered** factors. `ply_interaction_factor` when you want **one categorical column** (grouping/fixed effects) instead of products of columns. `rank_check = "report"` when the downstream node is regularized (ridge/lasso, cat 20).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `ply_poly`: `basis` (n×degree — chart-data), `column_names` (`x_poly1…d`), **`coefs_alpha`/`coefs_norm2`/`coefs_source`** (`"fitted"`|`"supplied"`|`"raw"`) = the **fitted params**, `orthonormality_error`/`centering_error` (**only** on the fit path — see the traps), `n`/`n_unique`/`x_min`/`x_max`.
- `ply_interactions` / `ply_model_matrix`: **`design`** (an n×k bare numeric matrix), `column_names`/`n_columns`/`n_rows`, **`column_term` & `assign`** (column → term; 0 = intercept — this is the mapping the downstream node needs in order to interpret coefficients), `term_labels`/`n_terms`/`intercept`, `formula` (deparsed), **`xlev`/`xlev_source`/`contrasts`** (fitted params), `rank`/`rank_deficient`/`rank_check`, `column_bound`.
- `ply_interaction_factor`: `levels`, `codes` (1.n_levels per row), `counts` (chart-data), `empty_levels`/`n_empty_levels`/`has_empty_levels`, `indicator` (n×n_levels 0/1 or `NULL`), `input_levels` (fit/apply), `combinations`.

**Critical traps** (all live-verified, version 4.6.1):
- **§3b gate 6 — the node's reason for existing.** An **orthogonal** polynomial is **not** a function of x alone: it depends on the centres/norms (`alpha`, `norm2`) of the **training sample**. A re-fit of `poly` on the new data ⇒ **a different basis** ⇒ the model coefficients **mean nothing**. This is why the coefs are returned as **numbers** and accepted back; `poly(simple = TRUE)` **discards** the coefs (live: attributes only `dim`/`dimnames`) and is therefore **not exposed**.
- **§3b gate 6 (b) — the silent-wrong of `model.matrix`.** Newdata with **fewer** factor levels produces **fewer columns with no error whatsoever** (live: `~a*g` with 3 levels → `(Intercept),a,gy,gz,a:gy,a:gz`; the same with 2 levels → `(Intercept),a,gy,a:gy`) ⇒ the coefficients land in the **wrong positions**. Hence `xlev` + `expect_columns`, with a hard gate on an **unknown level** ("factor a has new level …") **and** on a different set of columns.
- **Security — never `eval(parse)`** (`.claude/rules/security.md`). `ply_interactions`: the RHS is built with `call`/`as.symbol` over names that (a) exist in `data` and (b) pass a strict identifier regex, and is implanted into a **template** formula (`f <- ~0; f[[2]] <- rhs; environment(f) <- baseenv`) ⇒ **zero** `parse`/`str2lang`/`as.formula(text)`/`eval`. `ply_model_matrix`: **three layers of defence** — (1) at L3 the string passes **only** through `adapt_formula` (`the formula allowlist`, a default-deny walk + a sealed enclosure); (2) the wrapper **does not accept a string at all**; (3) an **autonomous** default-deny allowlist walk that works **even under a bare `source`** and restricts **every symbol** to the column names of `data`. Only `~ + - * : ^ ( I log log1p log2 log10 exp sqrt abs poly factor as.factor ordered interaction` are allowed; the `.` shorthand is **explicitly rejected**; depth ≤ 64; the call head **only a plain symbol** (not `fn` or `(fn)`).
- **`poly` silent-wrongs:** a **decimal** `degree` does not error — it is silently truncated (`degree = 1.5` → 1 column); **wrong coefs lengths** → a column **full of NA** with no error (gate: `length(alpha) == degree`, `length(norm2) == degree+2` — live-verified 3 and 5 for degree 3); **coefs together with `raw = TRUE`** → silently ignored; `degree ≥ n_unique`: the orthogonal path errors ("'degree' must be less than number of unique points") but the **raw path does not** — it produces linearly dependent columns ⇒ the **same gate on both paths**.
- **NA ⇒ silent row dropping.** PINNED `na.action = na.fail` + our own NA/Inf gate; PINNED `drop.unused.levels = FALSE` (`TRUE` would **invalidate** `xlev`).
- **Rank deficiency ⇒ silently NA coefficients.** Empty level combinations give aliased columns — live `qr(mm).rank = 2` on **4** columns with no error, and `lm` returns **silent NA**. The node **always** computes the rank; `rank_check = "auto"` (default) = **`stop` on FIT** (a real design error) and **`report` on APPLY** (when `xlev` is supplied: in a new sample a missing level is **normal** ⇒ a zero column, which for **scoring** is correct).
- **`interaction` on a numeric column ⇒ one level per value** (live: levels "1.5.a" …) — a hard gate; with `drop = FALSE` (the documented default) the **empty** levels remain and are reported explicitly, but **`indicator = TRUE` is blocked** on empty levels: each empty one gives a column **full of zeros** → rank deficiency → silent NA in `lm`.
- **Orthonormality is checked on the fit only.** Out of sample it **does not hold by design** (the basis is orthogonal *with respect to the training sample*) ⇒ on the apply path `orthonormality_error`/`centering_error` are **NA** — expected, not an error.
- **Masking: zero.** The file **does not call `library`** on any package (only `stats`/`base`/`utils`, always attached); the live `conflicts(detail = TRUE)` is **identical** to the baseline. Conversely, because other wrappers in the shared env mask basic generics, **all** calls are // qualified.
- **Determinism (§5):** no RNG path (poly = QR/three-term recursion; `model.matrix`/`interaction` = combinatorial) ⇒ **no seed**; `identical` over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (wrapper **and** node). **Terminal** nodes (no `register`): fit/apply is **explicit** — the user passes back `coefs_alpha`/`coefs_norm2` or `xlev`/`expect_columns`.

**Sources:** version 4.6.1 `the poly documentation` (live-verified: `poly(x, …, degree = 1, coefs = NULL, raw = FALSE, simple = FALSE)`; `attr "coefs" = list(alpha, norm2)` only with `raw = FALSE`, of lengths `degree` and `degree+2`; `simple = TRUE` → attributes only `dim`/`dimnames`; "'degree' must be less than number of unique points"; `predict.poly` ≡ `poly(new, degree, coefs=)`); `the model.matrix documentation`/`the terms documentation`/`the model.frame documentation` (attr `assign`/`contrasts`, `contrasts.arg`, `na.action`, `drop.unused.levels`; "contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels"; live-verified silent loss of columns and rows); `the interaction documentation` (`drop = FALSE`, `sep = "."`, `lex.order = FALSE`); `the qr documentation` (rank); `the contr.treatment documentation`/`contr.sum`/`contr.helmert`/`contr.poly`; `.claude/rules/security.md` ("Never use `eval(parse(text = user_input))` with untrusted input") + `the corresponding module`; `the normative gate spec` §3b **normative gate 6** (fit/apply externalization — explicitly "`attr(poly,"coefs")` … otherwise the out-of-sample apply is not reproducible"; the KNIME Normalizer → "Normalize Model" model) + the live-verified `poly` gate + REJECTED `recipes`; wrapper footer *IMPLEMENTATION NOTE*.

### #254 Calendar effects — G7+CH & financial-centre holidays as 0/1 dummies — `timeDate` (`c00_data_utilities/calendar_effects_holidays.py`)

**Functions:** `hd_list` [`listHolidays`] — **catalog/discovery**: which holiday names exist (**120** in total) + counts per country. `hd_holidays` [`holiday` + `holidayNYSE`/`LONDON`/`ZURICH`/`TSX`] — **the dates themselves** per holiday/year. `hd_dummies` [+ `isWeekday`/`isBizday`] — **0/1 columns aligned** to a given vector of dates (+ aggregate) and weekday/bizday flags.

**When:** daily/weekly macro and financial series carry **deterministic calendar disturbances** — holidays, exchange closures, the **moving** Easter. If these do not enter as **explicit exogenous dummies** (`xreg` for ARIMA/regression/GARCH), the calendar **contaminates the residuals** and shows up **spuriously** as seasonality or ARCH. Flow: `hd_list` (which names exist) → `hd_holidays` (the dates) → `hd_dummies` (the columns, aligned to your own calendar index).

**When NOT:** for **counting business days** / date rolling / offsets under a custom calendar → `business_day_calendar` (#112). For general date/frequency algebra → `date_parsing_rounding` (#111) / `tidy_temporal_frames` (#113) / `time_series_class` (#78). For **seasonal adjustment** with trading-day and Easter regressors **inside** the model (X-13/SEATS) → `Seasonal-wrapper` (#4). For **monthly/quarterly** data, where a holiday is not a discrete event (there you want trading-day/leap-year regressors, not day dummies). For **non-calendar** regime dummies → #255 (`discretisation_numeric_column`) or #253 (`ply_interaction_factor`). For countries **outside** the `timeDate` catalog — the catalog is **closed** (see `hd_list`). Charts: **frontend only** (§5).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **`year` mandatory**, an integer, within **[1583, 2200]**. The `timeDate` default is `getRmetricsOptions("currentYear")` = **the current year from the clock** ⇒ non-reproducible (§5), which is why it is required explicitly. The lower bound **1583** = the 1st **complete** year of the **Gregorian** calendar (the 1582-10-15 reform) — the `timeDate` Easter algorithm is Gregorian.
- **Holiday names**: every name is validated **against `listHolidays` before** the call; without NA/empties; **without duplicates** (they would give identical, perfectly collinear columns). Tool: **`hd_list`** (a mandatory first step).
- **`dates`** (`hd_dummies`): `Date` or **strictly** `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, **unique**, within [1583, 2200]; **not `POSIXt`** (the conversion depends on the time zone and would shift days).
- **At least one source**: `holidays` or `calendar` — otherwise the node would be a silent no-op. `nyse_type` applies **only** with `calendar = "NYSE"`.
- **`wday` ∈ [0, 6]** (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday; default `1:5`).
- The checking tool before the dummies: **`hd_holidays`** (`empty_sources` = the holiday really does exist in the requested years; `n_on_weekend` = how many fall on Sat/Sun).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `dummy_type = "per_holiday"` (**default**) when you want a **different coefficient per holiday** (Christmas ≠ Thanksgiving); `"aggregate"` (a single `holiday_any` column) when you have few observations/events — **fewer degrees of freedom**; `"both"` for model + chart. The `is_holiday` vector is **always** returned, regardless of the choice. `calendar = "NYSE"/"LONDON"/"ZURICH"/"TSX"` for daily financial data: a **closed market is a structural gap**, not a missing value. `nyse_type = "special"` when you want **only the exceptional** closures (e.g. 2001-09-11…14) as shock events. `hd_dummies(holiday_dates = …)` for **every** out-of-sample sample (§3b gate 6). `business_day_calendar` (#112) when you want to count/shift dates rather than dummies.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `hd_list`: `holidays` (those matching `pattern`), `all_holidays`/`n_all` (**120**), `count_by_country` (chart-data bar — **live-verified**: US 18 · CA 6 · GB 4 · DE 5 · FR 6 · IT 6 · JP 33 · CH 5), `calendars`, `year_min`/`year_max`.
- `hd_holidays`: `dates` (sorted, unique), `date_table` (records `{source, year, date}` — chart-data), `count_by_source`, **`holiday_dates`** (= the **fitted param**), `empty_sources`/`n_empty_sources`, `n_on_weekend`/`share_on_weekend`, `dates_per_year`.
- `hd_dummies`: **`dummies`** (n×k 0/1 — **rows = the supplied dates in the supplied order**, **columns = the sources in the supplied order** ⇒ a deterministic shape), **`dummy_levels`** (column names **and order** = a fitted param), `count_by_column`, `is_holiday`/`n_holiday`/`share_holiday`, `is_weekday`/`is_bizday`/`n_holiday_on_weekday`, `mode` (`"fit"`|`"apply"`), and **`constant_columns`/`n_constant_columns`** = the **all-zero** columns (the holiday does not fall inside the sample): they are **not removed** — that would break fit/apply — but they are **flagged** as a rank-deficient design (`lm` produces a **silent NA** coefficient, the same pattern as #253).

**Critical traps** (all live-verified, version 4.6.1 / timeDate 4052.112):
- **Trap #1 — `holiday` resolves names via `get`.** It calls `match.fun(Holiday)` on a string ⇒ `get(name, mode = "function", envir = <caller>)`; **without an attach the name is not found**: "object 'USNewYearsDay' of mode 'function' was not found". **Solution:** we pass the **function object** via `getExportedValue("timeDate", nm)` — the help page itself documents this ("**a list of the unquoted function names**") ⇒ `requireNamespace` **suffices** and masking is avoided entirely. In addition a **hard gate**: every name is checked against `listHolidays` **before** the call, with an explicit message + "near" names.
- **Masking — why `library(timeDate)` is not called.** Live `conflicts(detail = TRUE)` after an attach: `abline`, `lines`, `plot`, `points`, `getDataPart`, `initialize`, `Ops`, `show`, **`sample`**. `plot`/`lines`/`abline`/`points` are **harmless** (§5: we never draw) — **the critical one is `sample`**: `timeDate` promotes it to an **S4 standardGeneric** (live: `isGeneric("sample")` → `TRUE`), and `sample` is used by bootstrap/simulation wrappers in the **shared `source` env** (boot/MCS/tsDyn/BVAR); likewise `Ops`/`show`/`initialize`/`getDataPart` are S4 generics of other packages. **With `requireNamespace` the `conflicts` output is identical to the baseline** (zero new entries). The S3 registration at namespace load (`as.timeDate.*`, `timeCeiling.*`, `skewness.*`, `kurtosis.*`) is **entirely** on generics of `timeDate` **itself** (cf. `quanteda $.dfm`, `proxy` on `dist`).
- **Trap #2 — S4 → `to_mcp`.** `holiday`/`holidayNYSE` returns an **S4 `timeDate`** and `to_mcp` **stubs it out** (`@mcp_serialized = FALSE`) ⇒ **the dates would be lost**. Every `timeDate` is converted **here** to a character `"YYYY-MM-DD"` (pinned in the tests: **no S4 leaks**).
- **Silent NA in `timeDate` (three forms).** (a) **Years**: outside `[1000, 9999]` it does not error — it returns NA with **only a warning** "character string is not in a standard unambiguous format" (year 0 → NA, 10000 → NA); the same for a **non-integer** year (2024.5 → NA) and for NA. (b) **Dates**: `timeDate("not-a-date")` → NA; `timeDate("2024-02-30")` → NA ⇒ any invalid date would **silently** become a row of all zeros. (c) **`wday`**: `isWeekday(x, wday = 99)` does not error — it returns **all FALSE** ("no day is a business day"). All three are **our own hard gates**.
- **§3b gate 6 — fit/apply externalization.** `holiday_dates` (a named list) + `dummy_levels` (column names **and order**) are returned as plain character/numeric fields **and accepted back** ⇒ an out-of-sample apply with **identical** columns, **independently of the version** of `timeDate` (the help page states explicitly that the catalog "is changed from time to time"). The two paths are **mutually exclusive** — otherwise the train/test columns could differ silently. The model: KNIME Normalizer → "Normalize Model".
- **Silent gaps that are not errors (but are flagged explicitly):** a holiday that **did not yet exist** returns **0 dates with no error** (live: `USJuneteenthNationalIndependenceDay` before 2021 · `CAFamilyDay` in 2000 · `JPMountainDay`/`GBEarlyMayBankHoliday` in old years · `specialHolidayGB` in 2024) → `empty_sources`; an **empty** holiday set ⇒ `isBizday` **degenerates into `isWeekday`** (live, with no error) → `empty_holiday_set`.
- **`listHolidays` matches the regex anywhere inside the name, not as a prefix** — which is why `"GB"` gives **4** while the names with the `GB` prefix are **3** (the 4th is `specialHolidayGB`), live-verified. An invalid regex → a labelled stop.
- **`holidayNYSE(type = "")`:** the **documented default `""` cannot be passed explicitly** — the `match.arg` inside `holidayNYSE` errors ("'arg' should be one of “standard”, “special”") ⇒ for `nyse_type = "all"` we **omit the argument entirely**.
- **`holiday(names = TRUE)` was omitted:** the names are produced via `substitute`/`all.names` over the **unevaluated** argument; with function objects the help page says that "as a last resort … generated names are used" (H1, H2, …) **and it prints with `cat`** (live-verified in the body — a §5 violation) ⇒ we call **one holiday at a time** and build the mapping **ourselves**.
- **Determinism (§5):** no randomness (pure calendar computations, no RNG/seed); **FinCenter PINNED to `"GMT"`** — live-verified **identical** dates under `TZ=Pacific/Auckland` **and** `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`; the output is always sorted (`sort`+`unique`) and the column order = the **supplied** order; `identical` over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (wrapper **and** node).
- **Internal prefix `.hdum_` (not `.hd_`):** `.hd_call` **already exists** in `c07_causality_policy/honest_robust_inference.py` and all wrappers are loaded into the **same** `source` env ⇒ it would be a silent override. The **exported** `hd_*` names were checked and are free.

**Sources:** **timeDate 4052.112** ref manual (live-verified version 4.6.1): `the holiday documentation` — `holiday(year = getRmetricsOptions("currentYear"), Holiday = "Easter", …, names = FALSE)` + "Holiday: one or more names of holidays as a character vector **or a list of the unquoted function names**" + the `cat` fallback for generated names; `the listHolidays documentation` (`pattern = ".*"`; "the list is changed from time to time"); `the holidayNYSE documentation` (`type = c("", "standard", "special")`); `holidayLONDON`/`holidayZURICH`/`holidayTSX`; `the isWeekday documentation`/`the isBizday documentation` (`wday = 1:5`); `the timeDate documentation` (FinCenter) — < **live-verified counts** `listHolidays(".*")` = 120 (US 18 · CA 6 · GB 4 · DE 5 · FR 6 · IT 6 · JP 33 · CH 5) and a **live-verified `conflicts(detail = TRUE)`** after an attach (`… sample`; `isGeneric("sample")` → TRUE); the Gregorian reform (the bull "Inter gravissimas", in force 1582-10-15 ⇒ 1583 = the 1st complete year); `the normative gate spec` §3b (the live-verified gate "object 'X' of mode 'function' was not found", the masking table for `timeDate`, normative gate 6); `docs/catalog/merge-wrapper.md` (catalog row — zero new dependencies, the same verified counts); wrapper footer *IMPLEMENTATION NOTE*.

### #255 Discretisation (binning) — from a continuous variable to regimes — `stats` + `base` (`c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column.py`)

**Functions:** `bn_quantile_bins` [`quantile`, **type 7 PINNED**] — **equal-population** bins (sample quantiles; `n_bins` or explicit `probs`). `bn_equal_width` [`seq`] — **equal-width** bins over the range **or over a supplied fixed domain** (`range_min`/`range_max`). `bn_apply` [`cut`] — **applying stored breaks** to new data (§3b gate 6), with an explicit out-of-range policy.

**When:** converting **one** continuous macro variable into **discrete regimes** — "high vs low inflation", "growth quartile", "spread zone" — in order to produce **regime dummies** for a regression, or integer codes as input to a categorical node (#257). **One node per variable** (fan-out from the frontend). Binning is inherently **fit + apply**: the fit **learns** the boundaries from the sample, `bn_apply` **re-uses them verbatim**.

**When NOT:** on **non-stationary I(1) levels with sample quantiles** — the "quartiles" reflect the **position in time**, not an economic regime (see the Preconditions; the way out is `bn_equal_width` with **exogenous** boundaries). For **endogenous** regime detection from the data themselves → Markov-switching/threshold (cat 06) or `mclust` (#244, cat 29). For **structural change points** in time → `structural_change` (#3). For **many columns** at once — one node per variable. For **non-linearity without loss of information** → `ply_poly` (#253): binning **discards** the within-bin variance, polynomials do not. For already categorical variables (binning is unnecessary). Charts/histograms: **frontend only** (§5).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Input**: a numeric vector or a `matrix`/`DataFrame` with **one** numeric column (`cut`: "'x' must be numeric"); non-empty; **≥ 2** finite values on the fit (**≥ 1** in `bn_apply`, where the boundaries **are supplied**).
- **NA/NaN/Inf** per `na_action`: **`"fail"` (default)** = blocked-by-gate; **`"keep"`** = the boundaries are estimated from the finite values and the incomplete **positions are preserved** with an NA code. There is **no `"omit"`** — see the traps. Tool: `imputeTS` (#80).
- **`n_bins`** an integer **≥ 2** **and strictly smaller** than the number of **unique** values; **`probs`** (as an alternative) finite, ≥ 3 points, **strictly increasing**, with endpoints **exactly 0 and 1**; `n_bins` **and** `probs` together → stop (one of them would be ignored silently).
- **`labels`** (if supplied): **exactly** `n_bins`, unique, non-empty.
- **`bn_equal_width`**: `range_max > range_min`, and the domain **must cover** the data (otherwise the values outside would silently become NA; for out-of-sample use with fixed boundaries → `bn_apply(out_of_range=)`).
- **`bn_apply`**: `breaks` **strictly increasing**, finite, ≥ 3 points; `out_of_range = "clamp"` requires `include_lowest = TRUE`.
- **§3b gate 3 — non-stationarity:** if the column is a time series, run `run_adf_test` (#1). On an I(1) series the **sample** quantiles **do not converge** to a population parameter (Hamilton–Ma–Xi) ⇒ discretise **differences/rates** or supply **theoretical, exogenous** boundaries. **Never a silent correction here** (gate 2: no hidden conversion).
- Tie-checking tool: **`bn_quantile_bins`** (`n_distinct`, `counts`, `n_breaks_dropped`).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `bn_quantile_bins(n_bins = 4)` (**default**) when you want **equal-population** bins — the same number of observations ⇒ **the same statistical power** per dummy (3 = terciles, 5 = quintiles, 10 = deciles). `probs = c(0,.1,.9, 1)` for **unequal** bins with economic meaning ("tails vs centre"). `bn_equal_width` when you want **interpretable value ranges** instead of equal population (on a skewed distribution the extreme bins may end up **empty** — they are reported in `empty_bins`). **`bn_equal_width(range_min, range_max)`** when you want bins **comparable across countries/samples** or when gate 3 forbids sample quantiles (e.g. bands around a 2% inflation target). `bn_apply` for **every** out-of-sample sample. `out_of_range = "na"` when you want to **know** which new values fell outside; `"clamp"` when the regimes are defined as "below/above X" (but it **distorts** the extreme-value information). `dedupe_breaks = TRUE` **only as explicit consent** in the presence of many ties. `dummies = TRUE` when you want the 0/1 matrix directly as regressors.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `bin` (**integer codes** 1.`n_bins` per observation) + `bin_label` (character per observation) + `labels` — **never a factor** (JSON-safe).
- **`breaks`** (numeric, `n_bins+1` boundaries) = **the fitted param** (§3b gate 6); it is passed back verbatim to `bn_apply` **together with** `labels`/`right`/`include_lowest`.
- `counts`/`share` (chart-data histogram) + `bin_lower`/`bin_upper`/`bin_width` (**the boundaries**) + `bin_min`/`bin_max`/`bin_mean`/`bin_median` (**the observed** range *inside* each bin) + `empty_bins`/`n_empty_bins`.
- `dummies` (n×n_bins 0/1 or `NULL`; **NA** — not 0 — on the unassignable rows: 0 would mean "definitely not in this bin") + `method` (`"quantile"`|`"equal_width"`|`"apply"`) + `right`/`include_lowest` + `out_of_range`/`n_out_of_range`/`out_of_range_labels`/`n_clamped` + `n`/`n_valid`/`n_missing`/`missing_index`/`n_distinct`/`column`.
- **`bn_quantile_bins`**: `probs` + **`quantile_type` (always 7)** — so that two fits are comparable **only** if they come from the **same** estimator — + `n_bins_requested`/`n_breaks_dropped`/`dedupe_breaks`/`data_min`/`data_max`.
- **`bn_equal_width`**: `width` + `range_min`/`range_max` + **`range_supplied`** (whether the boundaries are **exogenous** or sample-based) + `data_min`/`data_max`.

**Critical traps** (all live-verified, version 4.6.1):
- **§3b gate 6 — why there are three functions.** The fit **learns** the breaks; a re-fit on new data gives **different** boundaries ⇒ the regime dummies **are not comparable** and the out-of-sample use is "reproducible **only by luck**". This is why `breaks` is returned as a **numeric field** and `bn_apply` accepts it back (the model: KNIME "Auto-Binner" → PMML model / Normalizer → "Normalize Model").
- **§3b gate 3 — non-stationarity.** On an I(1) series the sample quantiles do not converge ⇒ the "quartiles" encode the **position in time** (an early period = a low bin), not a regime. A documented precondition — **never** a silent correction here.
- **Determinism #1 — `type = 7` PINNED and not exposed.** The **nine** types of Hyndman & Fan (1996) give **different breaks on the same data**; an interchangeable `type` would break the reproducibility of **stored** workflows ("stored workflows pin node versions", §5). The type is **always** exposed as `quantile_type`.
- **Determinism #2 — an explicit `seq`, never `cut(x, breaks = <number>)`.** The help page itself: "the **outer limits are moved away by 0.1% of the range** to ensure that the extreme values both fall within the break intervals" — a **hidden shift** *and* it **does not return** the boundaries it used ⇒ a **non-externalisable** fit (it would break gate 6). No RNG/sampling/parallelism; `identical` over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (wrapper **and** node).
- **`cut` lives in `base`, not in `stats`** (`quantile` is in `stats`) — all calls are fully qualified.
- **The eight silent-wrongs of `cut`, all hard-gated here:** (a) **values outside the breaks → silently NA** ("Values which fall outside the range of `breaks` are coded as `NA`") ⇒ on an apply this means **lost observations with no indication**, hence `out_of_range` with the default `"fail"`; (b) **unsorted breaks are sorted silently** ("The default method will sort a numeric vector of `breaks` … `labels` will correspond to the intervals **after sorting**") ⇒ the **regime names land in the wrong bins**; (c) an **NA inside the breaks** is ignored silently (`cut(1:10, c(0, NA, 10))` → **one** bin instead of two); (d) **duplicate labels are merged silently** into one level (`labels = c("a","a")` → a single `"a"` for **all** values); (e) **breaks as a factor** → the level **codes** are used silently; (f) **`include.lowest = FALSE`** → the **minimum** value becomes NA silently; (g) **`Inf`** in the data → a silent NA bin; (h) **ties** → "'breaks' are not unique".
- **`n_bins = 1` is not a discretisation** — `cut` with 2 breaks returns **one** level with no error ⇒ gate `n_bins ≥ 2` **and** strictly < the number of unique values.
- **Ties — the most frequent real cause of failure.** In a column with many repetitions the quantiles **coincide**. The node catches this **before** the call, with the **column name** and the number of duplicates; the ways out: reduce `n_bins` **or** set `dedupe_breaks = TRUE` explicitly (then **fewer** bins, **not** of equal population — see `n_breaks_dropped`). **In `bn_apply` duplicates are always a hard stop**: deduplicating there would change the number of bins relative to the fit.
- **NA policy: `"fail"` | `"keep"` — no `"omit"`.** The regime dummies **must** stay aligned with the series/panel; removing rows would break the alignment with y (**exactly** the error `model.frame` makes silently — see #253).
- **`right`/`include_lowest` must be the same on the apply as on the fit** (the fits here are **always** `include_lowest = TRUE`), otherwise the **boundary** observations change bin; `out_of_range = "clamp"` **requires** `include_lowest = TRUE` (otherwise the "clamped" value would become NA **again**).
- **The output is never a factor:** the factor is kept internally and **decomposed** into integer codes + character labels (JSON-safe, §5); the **ordering** lives in the order of `labels` (which is why `ordered_result` is omitted); `dig.lab` is PINNED to 3 (the reference default) with a **post-check on uniqueness/number of levels** — `cut` itself raises the digits up to 12 and falls back to `"Range_k"` labels when the boundaries differ at the 14th digit.
- **Masking: zero** — no `library` (only `base`/`stats`, always attached); the live `conflicts(detail = TRUE)` is **identical** before/after the `source`. Conversely, because **other** wrappers in the shared env mask basic generics (`proxy` → `dist`/`as.matrix`; `sn` → `sd`; `ARIMA` → `ARIMA`), **all** calls here are / qualified.
- **A terminal node** (no `register`/chaining): it returns chart-ready numbers; fit/apply is **explicit** (the user passes the `breaks` back).

**Sources:** version 4.6.1 `the cut documentation` / `cut.default` (live-verified verbatim: "Values which fall outside the range of `breaks` are coded as `NA`"; "The default method will sort a numeric vector of `breaks` … `labels` will correspond to the intervals after sorting"; "the outer limits are moved away by **0.1% of the range**"; "'breaks' are not unique"; "number of intervals and length of 'labels' differ"); version 4.6.1 `the quantile documentation`/`quantile.default` (**the default `type = 7`** live-verified; "missing values and NaN's not allowed if 'na.rm' is FALSE"); **Hyndman, the reference.J. & Fan, Y. (1996)** "Sample Quantiles in Statistical Packages", *The American Statistician* **50(4) 361-365** (the nine types; type 7 = the the classical statistical packages default ⇒ pinning it is a §5 requirement); Hamilton, Ma & Xi, **NBER WP 32068** (§3b gate 3 — see #256); `the normative gate spec` §3b **normative gates 2 & 6** + the live-verified gate "`cut`: 'breaks' are not unique … ⚠️ `cut` is in **`base`**, NOT `stats`"; `docs/catalog/merge-wrapper.md` (catalog row: zero new dependencies; "return of the breaks (fit/apply)"; "type=7 = the the classical statistical packages/Excel default"); wrapper footer *IMPLEMENTATION NOTE*.

## §4. Preparation and prechecks — `c01_preparation_prechecks/`

when this category applies: **first, always, before any substantive econometric method** — here you check the properties of the series that determine WHICH method is allowed downstream: order of integration / stationarity (unit root), structural changes (structural breaks), seasonality and seasonal non-stationarity, outliers, residual normality, and — for panels — panel unit root. Every other category (VAR/VECM #05, cointegration, forecasting #02) **presupposes** that you have passed through here: the choice "levels vs differences", "VAR vs VECM", "trend-stationary vs difference-stationary" is the RESULT of these tests, not an assumption. The polarity rule that runs through the WHOLE category: **ADF/PP/ERS/HEGY have H0 = a unit root (non-stationarity)**, whereas **KPSS/Canova-Hansen have H0 = stationarity/stability** — the interpretation of a rejection is OPPOSITE and using them confirmatorily (ADF + KPSS together) is the good practice.

---

### #1 Unit-root & normality prechecks (ADF/KPSS/PP/JB) — `unit_root_normality` (`c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.py`)
**Functions:** `run_adf_test` [`adf.test`], `run_kpss_test` [`kpss.test`], `run_pp_test` [`pp.test`], `run_jarque_bera_test` [`jarque.bera.test`]

**When:** the **fast, standardised first look** at the stationarity of a univariate series and at residual normality. `unit_root_normality` gives **ready-made p-values** (via tabulation/interpolation), so it is the friendly path for an automatic decision: ADF (H0: unit root), KPSS (H0: stationarity — level or trend), PP (H0: unit root, robust to heteroskedasticity/autocorrelation without augmentation), JB (H0: normality, from skewness+kurtosis).

**When NOT:** (a) when you want to read the test regression / to see teststat-vs-critical-values explicitly or to choose the detrending model → `#2 urca` (richer output, DF-GLS/Zivot-Andrews). (b) When you suspect a **structural break** — ADF/PP have low power in the presence of a break and spuriously "see" a unit root → `#2 ur.za` or `#3 strucchange`. (c) For **seasonal** non-stationarity (monthly/quarterly) plain ADF/PP do not suffice → `#89 uroot` (HEGY). (d) For panels → `#6 plm`.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no formal statistical precondition (this is the STARTING POINT). **Hard data-quality gates** are enforced, however: `x` numeric and univariate; **no NA** (the documentation: "Missing values are not allowed/handled" → `stop`); `length(x) >= 10`; `var(x) > 0` (on a constant series the test is meaningless); `k` (the ADF lag) is not allowed to be `>= n-2`. `alpha` (default 0.05) is a wrapper addition for the automatic `decision`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`#2 urca`** — prefer it when you need DF-GLS (higher power, Elliott-Rothenberg-Stock), explicit critical values, or a break-aware test.
- **ADF + KPSS **confirmatory** together** (same package) — the established practice: if ADF does **not** reject a unit root AND KPSS rejects stationarity ⇒ strong evidence of I(1); if they conflict ⇒ unclear, look for a break/seasonality (Enders 2015).
- **`#89 hegy.test`** — if the non-stationarity may be seasonal.

**Reading the output:** the wrapper does NOT return an `htest`; it returns class `tseries_wrapper` (a plain list) which `to_mcp` **recurses into atomic fields**:
- `statistic` — the value of the statistic; `p_value` — the **ready-made p-value** (the primary basis of the decision).
- `lag_order`/`truncation_lag` — the lag `k` (ADF) or the truncation lag (KPSS/PP); `df` (JB) = 2 degrees of freedom.
- `decision` — a pre-computed interpretation at `alpha`.
- `warnings` — **critical**: `adf.test`/`kpss.test`/`pp.test` emit the warning "p-value smaller/greater than printed" when the statistic falls OUTSIDE the table of critical values ⇒ the p-value is **truncated (clamped at 0.01 or 0.10)**, not exact. The wrapper catches it and exposes it.
- **KPSS polarity trap (the top one):** in KPSS **H0 = stationarity**, so **a rejection (small p) = NON-stationarity / a unit root** — the opposite of ADF/PP. Do not read it like ADF.
- **Power trap:** a non-rejection by ADF does not "prove" a unit root — it merely fails to reject it (low power). Hence the confirmatory KPSS.

**Sources:** `unit_root_normality` (`help("adf.test")`, `kpss.test`, `pp.test`, `jarque.bera.test`) < Said & Dickey 1984 (*Biometrika* 71:599, augmented DF); Dickey & Fuller 1979 (*JASA* 74:427); Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt & Shin 1992 (*J. Econometrics* 54:159, KPSS); Phillips & Perron 1988 (*Biometrika* 75:335); Jarque & Bera 1987 (*Int. Stat. Review* 55:163); Enders 2015 *Applied Econometric Time Series* 4th ed. ch. 4; p-value tables: Banerjee et al. 1993.

### #2 Unit-root suite (ADF/KPSS/PP/ERS-DFGLS/Zivot-Andrews) — `unit_root_suite` (`c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_suite.py`)
**Functions:** `wrap_ur_df` [`ur.df`], `wrap_ur_kpss` [`ur.kpss`], `wrap_ur_pp` [`ur.pp`], `wrap_ur_ers` [`ur.ers`], `wrap_ur_za` [`ur.za`]

**When:** the **heavy, "regulatory" unit-root check** when you need more than a p-value: (a) an explicit choice of the deterministic model (`none`/`drift`/`non_parametric_trend`), (b) DF-GLS (ERS) for **higher power** than plain ADF, (c) Zivot-Andrews, which **endogenously locates ONE structural break** and tests for a unit root under that break (ignoring a break makes ADF spuriously declare a unit root). The choice of the detrending model (constant vs trend) determines whether you are judging level or trend stationarity.

**When NOT:** (a) when you want only a quick yes/no decision with a p-value → `#1 tseries` (friendlier). (b) Seasonal non-stationarity → `#89 uroot`. (c) **More than one** break → Zivot-Andrews handles **ONLY ONE**; for multiple breaks → `#3 breakpoints` (Bai-Perron). (d) Panels → `#6 plm`.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no formal statistical precondition (a starting point). Wrapper gate: an **NA check** (`stop`, an optional addition — the documentation does not require it, but it protects). Choice of `type`/`model`/`lags`/`selectlags` via `match.arg` (1st = default). For `ur.za` the `lag` default is `NULL`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`#1 tseries`** — fast, ready-made p-value, when you do not need the test regression.
- **`ur.ers` (DF-GLS)** instead of `ur.df` — when power is critical (series close to unity); ERS 1996.
- **`ur.za`** instead of plain ADF — when you suspect ONE break at an unknown date; `bpoint` gives you the estimated date.
- **`#3 strucchange` / `#05 cointegration (ca.jo, a separate file)`** — for multiple breaks / cointegration respectively.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`): the `unit_root_suite` objects are **S4 with slots** — the wrapper extracts the slots into a plain named list and `to_mcp` recurses:
- `teststat` — numeric (or a row vector; ur.df gives tau + phi joint stats). `cval` — the **matrix of critical values** at 1%/5%/10% → `to_mcp` turns it into nested rows + `dim` + `dimnames`.
- **TOP trap (urca):** the `ur.*` tests do **NOT give a p-value** — you decide by **comparing `teststat` with `cval`**. Polarity: for ADF/PP/ERS/ZA (H0: unit root) you reject when the teststat is **more negative** than the critical value (left tail); for KPSS (H0: stationarity) you reject when teststat **> cval** (right tail, the OPPOSITE direction).
- `model`/`type`/`lag` — the deterministic spec and lags that were used (documentation of the decision).
- `bpoint` (only `ur.za`) — the **estimated break position** (index); `tstats` — the rolling t-stat profile (useful for a chart). `yd` (only `ur.ers` DF-GLS) — the GLS-detrended series.
- `testreg`/`model`/`res`/`testreg` — heavy `lm`/text objects → **stubbed** by `to_mcp` (keep a compact summary).

**Sources:** `unit_root_suite` (`help("ur.df")`, `ur.kpss`, `ur.pp`, `ur.ers`, `ur.za`) — Pfaff 2008 *Analysis of Integrated and Cointegrated Time Series with the reference* 2nd ed. < Dickey & Fuller 1979; KPSS 1992; Phillips & Perron 1988; Elliott, Rothenberg & Stock 1996 (*Econometrica* 64(4):813, DF-GLS/P-test; critical values MacKinnon 1991 for the constant); Zivot & Andrews 1992 (*JBES* 10(3):251, endogenous break); Enders 2015 ch. 4.

### #3 Structural change (Bai-Perron multiple breaks / Chow-F / CUSUM) — `structural_change` (`c01_preparation_prechecks/structural_change.py`)
**Functions:** `run_breakpoints` [`breakpoints`+`breakdates`+`confint`], `run_Fstats` [`Fstats`], `run_efp` [`efp`], `run_sctest` [`sctest`]

**When:** testing and estimating the **structural stability** of a regression relationship (`y ~ x`, or `y ~ 1` for a mean shift). Three complementary logics:
- `run_efp` (**Empirical Fluctuation Process** — CUSUM/MOSUM/RE/ME): tests whether the coefficients drift over time (H0: stability); good for **visual/dating-free** detection.
- `run_Fstats` (**Chow / sup-F**): F statistics at every potential break, with `run_sctest(type="supF"/"aveF"/"expF")` for the p-value (H0: no break; a rejection ⇒ there is a break at an unknown position).
- `run_breakpoints` (**Bai-Perron multiple breaks**): estimates the number and positions of multiple breaks SIMULTANEOUSLY by minimum BIC, + `breakdates` (dates) and `confint` (confidence intervals).

**When NOT:** (a) when the question is simply unit root yes/no (not a break) → `#1/#2`. (b) When you know ONE suspect date in advance and want an endogenous break test in a unit-root setting → `#2 ur.za`. (c) Regime switching with **probabilistic** regimes (Markov) instead of abrupt breaks → Markov-switching (category 10, MSwM — **note: MSwM handles gaussian/lm only**). (d) It does not handle seasonality.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** none formal; it is a diagnostic. Structural requirements: a valid `formula`; `h` (the minimum segment size) ∈ (0,1) or an integer (default 0.15 ⇒ no segment smaller than 15% of the sample). `run_sctest` accepts **RAW** `Fstats`/`efp` objects (not the wrapper lists) — gate: `inherits(x, "Fstats"/"efp")`, otherwise `stop`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`#2 ur.za`** — when the break is tied to the unit-root question (one break, endogenous).
- **Markov-switching (10)** — for smooth/probabilistic regime changes instead of discrete breaks.
- **CUSUM (`run_efp`) vs Bai-Perron (`run_breakpoints`)**: CUSUM = "is there instability?" without dating; Bai-Perron = "how many and where" with dates. Use CUSUM as screening, Bai-Perron for dating.

**Reading the output** (L2 `to_mcp`):
- `run_breakpoints`: `breakpoints_minBIC` — the index(es) of the breaks (the min-BIC solution); `breakdates` — the dates (in time units); `confint` — a **matrix** `lower/breakpoint/upper` (→ nested rows); `confint_dates` — the intervals as dates. `nobs`/`nreg` for reporting. `breakpoints_full` = a heavy `breakpointsfull` object → stubbed.
- `run_efp`: `process` — the **ts/mts of the fluctuation process** (→ `{values,start,frequency}`, chart-ready); `type` (e.g. "OLS-CUSUM"); `par` (bandwidth — **meaningless for CUSUM**, only for MOSUM/ME). The decision comes from `run_sctest(efp_object)`.
- `run_sctest`: returns atomic `statistic`, `p_value`, `method`, `data_name` (`htest` fields). **The primary basis of the decision** — rejecting H0 ⇒ structural change.
- **Trap:** `run_efp.par` is not a decision — do not read it as a break; the decision is the p-value of `sctest`. Also, min-BIC may select 0 breaks (`breakpoints_minBIC = NA`) — that is not an error, it means "no structural change".

**Sources:** `structural_change` — Zeileis, Leisch, Hornik & Kleiber 2002, "strucchange: An the reference Package for Testing for Structural Change in Linear Regression Models", *JSS* 7(2) < Bai & Perron 1998 (*Econometrica* 66:47) & 2003 (*J. Applied Econometrics* 18:1, multiple breaks); Chow 1960 (*Econometrica* 28:591); Brown, Durbin & Evans 1975 (*JRSS-B* 37:149, CUSUM); Andrews 1993 (*Econometrica* 61:821, sup-F).

### #4 Seasonal adjustment X-13ARIMA-SEATS — `seasonal_adjustment_13arima` (`c01_preparation_prechecks/seasonal_adjustment_13arima.py`)
**Functions:** `run_seas` [`seas`+`final`/`original`/`non_parametric_trend`/`irregular`/`series`/`udg`/`qs`], `get_series` [`series`], `check_x13` [`checkX13`]

**When:** when you have a **seasonal** monthly/quarterly series and want to **deseasonalise** it (seasonal adjustment) before modelling/interpretation, or to isolate the trend/seasonal/irregular components. X-13ARIMA-SEATS (US Census Bureau) is the institutional standard: it automatically performs regARIMA (trading days, Easter, outliers) + a SEATS or X-11 decomposition. `run_seas` returns all components ready, plus diagnostics.

**When NOT:** (a) when the question is **whether** seasonal non-stationarity / a unit root exists (not adjustment) → `#89 hegy.test` (a test, not an adjustment). (b) A non-seasonal series (frequency 1). (c) If you want a simple/fast decomposition without installed X-13 binaries → STL (trend/cycle category 10); **`seasonal_adjustment_13arima` requires the X-13 binary** — run `check_x13` first. (d) Structural breaks → `#3`.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** **`check_x13` first** — confirm that the X-13 binaries are installed and functional (otherwise `seas` fails). `x` must be a `ts`/`mts` with frequency > 1. No NA gate (handled by the `na.action = na.omit` argument). `get_series` gate: `inherits(seas_object, "seas")`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`#89 hegy.test / ch.test`** — when you want to **test** for seasonal non-stationarity/stability (inference), not to remove seasonality.
- **STL / X-11 mode** — `run_seas(x, x11="")` for an X-11 instead of a SEATS decomposition (more robust, not model-based).
- **Trend/cycle filters (10)** — if you need only trend extraction (HP/Hamilton) without a seasonal model.

**Reading the output** (L2 `to_mcp`):
- `final` — the **seasonally adjusted series** (the main result, ts → `{values,start,frequency}`); `original`/`non_parametric_trend`/`seasonal_adjustment_13arima`/`irregular` — the components (ts).
- `seas_table` — **which table** was supplied as `seasonal_adjustment_13arima`: `"seats.seasonal"` (s10) under SEATS, `"x11.seasonal"` (d10) under X-11. **Trap:** there is no `seasonal_adjustment_13arima` extractor in the package — the wrapper auto-detects the spec; if no known spec applies (e.g. `seats=NULL`), `seasonal_adjustment_13arima` is `NULL`.
- `qs` — the **QS seasonality test** (post-check): a small p ⇒ seasonality remains (a poor adjustment). `udg` — the full diagnostics (list).
- `err`/`model`/`fivebestmdl` — X-13 warnings, the selected ARIMA, the five best.
- **Trap:** `final` = `original / (seasonal × trading days)` — for ratio diagnostics use `get_series(obj, "seats.adjustfac")`. Do not confuse the adjusted series (`final`) with the trend (`non_parametric_trend`) — the trend has removed the irregular component as well.

**Sources:** `seasonal_adjustment_13arima` — Sax & Eddelbuettel 2018, "Seasonal Adjustment by X-13ARIMA-SEATS ", *JSS* 87(11) < U.S. Census Bureau X-13ARIMA-SEATS Reference Manual; QS test: Maravall (SEATS) / Census Bureau diagnostics.

### #5 Automatic outlier detection (Chen-Liu) — `automatic_outlier_detection` (`c01_preparation_prechecks/automatic_outlier_detection.py`)
**Functions:** `run_tso` [`tso`]

**When:** when you want to detect and classify outliers **automatically** in a univariate ts before modelling: additive outlier (AO), level shift (LS), temporary change (TC), innovational outlier (IO), seasonal level shift (SLS). The Chen-Liu (1993) procedure alternates an ARIMA fit (`auto.arima`) and outlier detection until it stabilises — critical, because a **level shift mimics a unit root** and an outlier distorts ADF/ACF/parameters.

**When NOT:** (a) when the break is in the **regression relationship** (multiple structural breaks in coefficients) → `#3 strucchange`. (b) For one endogenous break in a unit-root setting → `#2 ur.za`. (c) If you merely want to remove seasonality (the X-13 outliers are a special case) → `#4 seasonal` (it has its own outlier spec). (d) Non-ts data.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** gate `is.ts(y)` (`stop` if not a ts, a mild addition). **An explicit documentation requirement for `xreg`**: it must be a `matrix` **with column names** AND `tsp(xreg) == tsp(y)` (otherwise `stop`) — the easiest place to get it wrong. `cval` (the critical value) defaults to NULL ⇒ `tso` computes it from the sample size (n≤50→3.0, n≥450→4.0).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`#3 strucchange`** — if the target is structural change in a relationship, not isolated data-point anomalies.
- **`#4 seasonal` (outlier spec)** — when outlier detection is part of a seasonal adjustment.
- **`tsmethod="arima"`** instead of `"auto.arima"` — when you know the ARIMA order and want speed/stability.

**Reading the output** (L2 `to_mcp`): a `tsoutliers_object` is returned (class `"tsoutliers"`, in full — the documentation does not enumerate named elements). The main components to read:
- `outliers` (DataFrame) — **the outlier table**: `type` (AO/LS/TC/IO/SLS), `ind` (index), `time`, `coefhat` (magnitude), `tstat` → `to_mcp` list of records. This is the main result.
- `yadj` — the series **cleaned** of the outliers (ts); `fit` — the final ARIMA; `effects` — the estimated contribution of the outliers (ts).
- **Interpretation trap:** an **LS (level shift)** is different from an AO — it indicates a permanent shift in the level (a possible structural break / a source of a spurious unit root), whereas an AO is an isolated spike. Before concluding I(1), check whether an LS explains the "non-stationarity". `cval` sets the sensitivity — a larger n ⇒ a stricter threshold.

**Sources:** `automatic_outlier_detection` — López-de-Lacalle (package) < Chen & Liu 1993, "Joint Estimation of Model Parameters and Outlier Effects in Time Series", *JASA* 88(421):284; implemented via `auto.arima` (Hyndman-Khandakar 2008).

### #6 Panel unit-root (LLC/IPS/Fisher/Hadri + Pesaran CIPS) — `panel_unit_root` (`c01_preparation_prechecks/panel_unit_root.py`)
**Functions:** `run_purtest` [`purtest`], `run_cipstest` [`cipstest`], `make_pdata_frame` [`pdata.frame`]

**When:** testing stationarity in a **panel** (many units `i` × time `t`) — e.g. a macro panel of countries/regions. Panel unit-root tests exploit the cross-sectional dimension for **higher power** than univariate ones. The choice is made via `test`: `levinlin` (LLC — a common root, H0: unit root), `ips` (Im-Pesaran-Shin — a heterogeneous root per unit), `madwu`/`Pm`/`invnormal`/`logit` (Fisher-type combined p-values), `hadri` (**H0: stationarity** — the OPPOSITE polarity, KPSS-type). `cipstest` (Pesaran CIPS) = **second generation**, robust to **cross-sectional dependence** (common shocks across units).

**When NOT:** (a) a univariate series → `#1/#2`. (b) When you want to **estimate** a panel equation (FE/RE/GMM), not to test stationarity → category **08 panel-data** (`panel_unit_root`, a separate file/surface — the same package, a different function). (c) Panel cointegration → the corresponding category. (d) A micro panel with **short T** — the panel unit-root asymptotics (T→∞) break down; stationarity matters only in a **macro panel (large T)**.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Input prep:** `make_pdata_frame(df, index=c("id","time"))` → a valid panel structure before `cipstest` (gate: `run_cipstest` requires `inherits(x, "pseries")`).
- **Cross-sectional dependence:** if it is present (common in macro panels — common global shocks), the first-generation `purtest` tests (LLC/IPS/Fisher) are **size-distorted** ⇒ use `cipstest(model="cmg")` (Pesaran 2007). The CD test (Pesaran) lives in another category.
- **Explicit gate:** `ips.stat="tbar"` **does not apply when `lags > 0`** (`stop`). `tbar`/`hadri`/`levinlin` do not apply on **unbalanced** panels (documented, not enforced — left to `purtest`).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`cipstest` (CIPS) vs `purtest` (LLC/IPS)**: CIPS when there is cross-sectional dependence; LLC/IPS when the units are cross-sectionally independent.
- **`ips` vs `levinlin`**: IPS allows a **heterogeneous** root per unit (more realistic); LLC assumes a **common** root (more powerful if it holds).
- **`hadri`** — confirmatory (H0: stationarity) against the others, as KPSS is against ADF.

**Reading the output** (L2 `to_mcp`):
- `run_purtest.statistic` — an **`htest`** object → `to_mcp` atomic `{statistic, p.value, parameter, method, data.name, alternative}`. The primary basis of the decision is `p.value`.
- `args`/`idres` — the arguments and the **per-individual ADF regressions** (DataFrame → records, useful for diagnostics). `adjval`/`sigma2` — simulated means/vars (only levinlin/ips, otherwise NULL). `ips_tbar_crit` — critical values (only with `ips.stat="tbar"` and lags=0).
- `run_cipstest.cipstest` — an `htest` (in full; the Value section does not enumerate fields).
- **Polarity trap (critical):** most of them (LLC/IPS/Fisher/CIPS) have **H0 = unit root** (a rejection ⇒ stationarity), BUT **`hadri` has H0 = stationarity** (a rejection ⇒ a unit root) — the OPPOSITE interpretation, like KPSS. Always check which test you are running before interpreting the p-value.
- **Trap:** a non-rejection in IPS does not mean "all units are I(1)" — IPS rejects if **at least some** units are stationary (a heterogeneous alternative).

**Sources:** `panel_unit_root` — Croissant & Millo, "Panel Data Econometrics in the reference: The plm Package", *JSS* 2008 (`help("purtest")`, `cipstest`, `pdata.frame`) < Levin, Lin & Chu 2002 (*J. Econometrics* 108:1, LLC); Im, Pesaran & Shin 2003 (*J. Econometrics* 115:53, IPS); Maddala & Wu 1999 (*Oxford Bull. Econ. Stat.* 61:631, Fisher); Choi 2001 (*J. Int. Money Finance* 20:249, combined p); Hadri 2000 (*Econometrics J.* 3:148, H0 stationarity); Pesaran 2007 (*J. Applied Econometrics* 22:265, CIPS/CD-robust); Baltagi 2013 *Econometric Analysis of Panel Data* §12.

### #96 Reading delimited / fixed-width flat files (ingest) — `reading_delimited_fixed` (`c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.py`)
**Functions:** `read_csv_data` [`read_csv`], `read_tsv_data` [`read_tsv`], `read_delimited` [`read_delim`], `read_fwf_data` [`read_fwf`/`fwf_empty`], `read_parse_problems` [`problems`]

**When:** as the first step of the DAG when the user uploads a flat file (CSV/TSV/an arbitrary single-char delimiter/fixed-width) — a gated ingest button that produces a long/records `DataFrame` (registered as `data` → Parquet) and, critically, SURFACES the parse problems as data instead of swallowing them. `read_parse_problems` is the diagnostic terminal (re-read + the problems table only).

**When NOT:** for Excel workbooks → `reading_writing_excel` #97; for Parquet/Feather → `canonical_disk_format` #98; for JSON/NDJSON → `json_interchange_parse` #99; for Stata/SPSS/SAS → `import_export_stata` #100. It does not draw charts (the frontend does). `locale` (European decimals) and the `col_positions` fwf spec are NOT exposed in the node schema (non-JSON-portable objects) — the default locale + auto-guessed boundaries; use the L1 wrapper for a custom locale/fwf spec.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition (mechanical reading). Gates (all live-probed): `path` a non-empty string, NOT a directory, an existing file, `size > 0 bytes`; a POST-gate `ncol > 0` (a whitespace-only file passes the byte gate but yields a 0×0 tibble); `col_types` = NULL | a compact string | a `col_spec`; `na` a non-empty character without an actual NA; `read_delimited` requires a delimiter of EXACTLY one character; `read_parse_problems` with format='delim' ⇒ the delimiter is mandatory.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `arw_read_csv` (#98) for the same CSV when the file is large/columnar-friendly or you want the Arrow type inference; `reading_delimited_fixed` is preferred for fine-grained parse diagnostics (the problems table) + compact col-spec strings + fixed width. Within `reading_delimited_fixed`: `read_delim` for non-comma/tab; `read_fwf` for columnar fixed-width without a delimiter.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Readers: `data` (a plain `DataFrame` → records), `n_rows`/`n_cols`/`col_names`/`column_types` (the detected column classes), `problems` (records; the `file`/server-path column is removed), `n_problems`/`has_problems`, `path`.
- **Eager-read trap:** internally `lazy=FALSE`, so that the parse problems materialise IMMEDIATELY; a readr default lazy read would leave the problems empty until the first access.
- **Silent 0×0 trap:** a whitespace-only file does not error in readr — it silently returns an empty tibble; here it is blocked (`no columns`).
- **col_types 'Z' trap:** an unknown compact code → a readr error (wrapped as an `error`), not a silent omission.

**Sources:** readr reference/vignette (`read_delim`, `read_fwf`, `problems`, `cols`, `locale`) — Wickham & Hester, readr 2.2.0 (live `args` introspection) <https://readr.tidyverse.org/> / <

### #97 Reading/writing Excel workbooks (ingest/egress) — `reading_writing_excel` + `openxlsx` (`c00_data_utilities/reading_writing_excel.py`)
**Functions:** `xl_read_excel` [`read_excel`/`excel_sheets`], `xl_excel_sheets` [`excel_sheets`], `xl_read_openxlsx` [`read.xlsx`/`getSheetNames`], `xl_write_xlsx` [`write.xlsx`]

**When:** when the user uploads an Excel workbook (.xls or.xlsx) — a gated button that turns it into a rectangular `DataFrame` (registered as `data` → Parquet) feeding the DAG, with sheet/range/col_types selection. `xl_excel_sheets` = discovery of the sheet names (xls+xlsx). `xl_write_xlsx` = a terminal export of one df (or a named list of dfs) back to.xlsx.

**When NOT:** for CSV/TSV → `reading_delimited_fixed` #96; for Parquet/Feather → `canonical_disk_format` #98; for Stata/SPSS/SAS → `import_export_stata` #100. It does not draw or style (the whole openxlsx styling/plotting API — createStyle/addStyle/conditionalFormatting/insertPlot — is omitted; the frontend does that). The low-level Workbook model (createWorkbook/addWorksheet/writeData) is omitted (the single write.xlsx call suffices).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition. Gates (live-probed): `path` a non-empty string + `file.exists`; `sheet` is validated against the ACTUAL sheet list (`excel_sheets`/`getSheetNames`) — a name ∈ the sheets or a positive position ≤ the number of sheets; `range` pre-validated with `as.cell_limits` (before the cryptic `parsed.ref_v`); `col_types` ∈ {skip,guess,logical,numeric,date,text,list}; `xl_read_openxlsx` gates the.xlsx extension; `xl_write_xlsx` gates the.xlsx extension + overwrite/an existing file.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `xl_read_excel` (readxl) vs `xl_read_openxlsx` (openxlsx): readxl reads BOTH legacy.xls AND.xlsx and supports A1 ranges; openxlsx reads ONLY.xlsx but with startRow/rowNames/detectDates. Prefer readxl for.xls or a range subset; openxlsx when you need row names or strict date detection.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Readers: `data` (a tibble/DataFrame → records; a registered producer → Parquet), `nrow`/`ncol`/`columns`/`sheet`/`source` (+ `range` in readxl). `xl_excel_sheets`: `sheets` (character) + `n_sheets`. `xl_write_xlsx`: `file`/`sheets_written`/`n_sheets`/`bytes`.
- **CRITICAL write.xlsx silent-wrong trap:** `write.xlsx(5,..)` or a list of non-dfs does NOT error — it silently builds an (almost empty) workbook; here it is hard-gated (x = a df or a non-empty list of dfs).
- **openxlsx empty-sheet trap:** it returns NULL for a fully empty sheet — normalised to a 0-row df.
- **.xls in openxlsx trap:** openxlsx does NOT read.xls (a zip-parse error); gated with a clear message.

**Sources:** readxl reference (`read_excel`, `excel_sheets`, the col_types vocabulary) + openxlsx reference (`read.xlsx`, `write.xlsx`, `getSheetNames`) + cellranger (`as.cell_limits`) — live `args`/`the docs documentation` introspection <https://readxl.tidyverse.org/> / <

### #98 The canonical on-disk data-format layer (Parquet/Feather/CSV/Dataset) — `canonical_disk_format` (`c00_data_utilities/canonical_disk_format.py`)
**Functions:** `arw_read_parquet` [`read_parquet`], `arw_read_feather` [`read_feather`], `arw_read_csv` [`read_csv_arrow`], `arw_write_parquet` [`write_parquet`/`codec_is_available`], `arw_open_dataset` [`open_dataset`]

**When:** as the lingua franca of the on-disk data-format layer of the whole canvas — every table the user uploads or a producer node writes lands as Parquet and is read back through ONE gated button. `arw_write_parquet` = the canonical writer (df → Parquet). `arw_open_dataset` = a lazy, (hive-)partitioned dataset opener with a JSON-safe schema/preview and no full materialisation.

**When NOT:** for parse-problem diagnostics or a compact col spec → `reading_delimited_fixed` #96; for Excel → `reading_writing_excel` #97; for JSON → `json_interchange_parse` #99. It NEVER returns an opaque Arrow Table (`as_data_frame=FALSE` — an object wrapper, not JSON-safe; the readers always materialise a plain `DataFrame`). The write side is Parquet-only for the object store (write_feather/write_dataset are omitted). S3/GCS filesystems + schema-authoring helpers are omitted (store paths are resolved by the node layer; schemas are discovered, not authored).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition. Gates (all live-verified to pass through arrow cryptically otherwise): `read_*` file = an existing FILE (not a directory; otherwise `IOError: Failed to open local file`); `write_parquet` x = a `DataFrame` with ≥1 column (a list/matrix → the cryptic `No method for as_arrow_table`) + a sink whose parent directory EXISTS + `compression` via match.arg + `codec_is_available` (portable) + a POST-gate that the file was created; `open_dataset` sources = an existing DIRECTORY.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `arw_read_csv` vs `read_csv_data` (#96) — arrow for large columnar CSV/type inference; readr for parse-problem diagnostics. `arw_open_dataset` (lazy, many partition files) vs `arw_read_parquet` (one file, eager) — a dataset when the data are hive-partitioned in a directory.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Readers: `data` (a plain `DataFrame` — a registered producer → Parquet) + `schema`(column,type)/`n_rows`/`n_cols`/`columns`/`format`/`col_select`.
- Writer: `path`/`bytes`/`schema`/`compression` (NOT a producer). `open_dataset`: the lazy `Dataset` in `.dataset` (to_mcp → a compact stub, an object wrapper/environment) + a JSON-safe `schema` (arrow type strings)/`n_rows`/`n_cols`/`partitioning`/`files`/`preview` (a bounded head).
- **CRITICAL col_select silent-zero trap:** the tidyselect `col_select` of arrow with a VARIABLE = NULL selects ZERO columns silently (and with a character variable → an all_of deprecation warning); here we read ALL columns + a the standard library subset (order-preserving), and unknown columns → a clean gate.
- **Codec trap:** some codecs (zstd/gzip) are compile-time optional; gated with `codec_is_available` before the write.

**Sources:** arrow /Apache reference (`read_parquet`, `read_feather`, `read_csv_arrow`, `write_parquet`, `open_dataset`, `codec_is_available`, Schema.field.type$ToString) — live `args`/probe introspection <https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r/> / <
