### #99 JSON <-> the reference interchange (parse/serialise/validate/stream) — `json_interchange_parse` (`c00_data_utilities/json_interchange_parse.py`)
**Functions:** `json_parse` [`fromJSON`], `json_write` [`toJSON`], `json_validate` [`validate`], `json_stream_parse` [`stream_in`], `json_stream_write` [`stream_out`]

**When:** as the JSON data layer of the canvas — user-uploaded JSON/NDJSON (and API payloads stored by the frontend) enter the graph through ONE gated button, and the structured the reference output leaves as canonical JSON text. `json_parse`/`json_stream_parse` = data producers; `json_write`/`json_stream_write` = serializers; `json_validate` = the diagnostic (is-this-valid-JSON + error/offset).

**When NOT:** for CSV/TSV → `reading_delimited_fixed` #96; for Excel → `reading_writing_excel` #97; for Parquet/Feather → `canonical_disk_format` #98. File IO (read_json/write_json/prettify/minify) is omitted (the reader/writer nodes own the file IO); serializeJSON/unserializeJSON (verbose RDS-in-JSON) + base64/gzip are omitted; the URL/file auto-fetch of fromJSON is BLOCKED (no SSRF/arbitrary read).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition. Gates (live-probed): `json_parse` txt = a single non-NA non-empty string, `validate`-FIRST (invalid JSON → stop with the yajl message, AND this closes the SSRF/file-read path — a URL/path is not valid JSON); `json_write` digits defaults to NA (full precision) + force=FALSE (non-mappable classes = a hard error); `json_stream_parse` a character without NA, EVERY line `validate`d before the stream (a clean "line <i>"); `json_stream_write` x = a df with nrow≥1.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `json_parse` (one JSON document) vs `json_stream_parse` (NDJSON, one line = one record → DataFrame) — stream when the input is newline-delimited records. For tabular data prefer `canonical_disk_format`/`reading_delimited_fixed` (#96/#98); JSON is used for nested/semi-structured payloads.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `json_parse`: `parsed` (vector/list/DataFrame — a registered producer; a df → Parquet, otherwise RDS) + `type`/`n`/`flatten`. `json_write`: `json` (a string) + `nchar`. `json_validate`: `valid`/`error`/`offset`. `json_stream_parse`: `data` (a DataFrame → Parquet) + `n`/`ncol`. `json_stream_write`: `ndjson`/`text`/`n`.
- **CRITICAL toJSON digits=4 trap:** the `toJSON` default `digits=4` SILENTLY rounds numerics (pi → 3.1416) = data corruption for a macro node; here it is overridden to NA (full precision).
- **auto_unbox trap:** length-1 vectors → JSON scalars (default TRUE); disable it if you always need arrays.
- **simplify trap:** an array of objects → a DataFrame only if simplify_dataframe=TRUE (the default); heterogeneous objects stay a list.

**Sources:** jsonlite reference/vignette (`fromJSON`, `toJSON`, `validate`, `stream_in`, `stream_out`) — Ooms, "The jsonlite Package: A Practical and Consistent Mapping Between JSON Data and the reference Objects" (live r-btw introspection) <

### #100 Import/export of foreign statistical files (Stata/SPSS/SAS + labelled→factor) — `import_export_stata` (`c00_data_utilities/import_export_stata.py`)
**Functions:** `hvn_read_stata` [`read_dta`], `hvn_read_spss` [`read_sav`], `hvn_read_sas` [`read_sas`], `hvn_write_stata` [`write_dta`], `hvn_as_factor` [`as_factor`]

**When:** when the user uploads a file from a foreign statistical system (.dta /.sav /.sas7bdat) — a gated button that turns it into a tidy `DataFrame` (registered as `data` → Parquet) TOGETHER with the labelled metadata (variable labels + value labels) the frontend needs. `hvn_write_stata` = a terminal export back to.dta; `hvn_as_factor` = materialising labelled columns as factors for analysis/charts.

**When NOT:** for CSV/TSV → `reading_delimited_fixed` #96; for Excel → `reading_writing_excel` #97; for Parquet/Feather → `canonical_disk_format` #98; for JSON → `json_interchange_parse` #99. Secondary formats (read_por/read_xpt/write_sav/write_sas/write_xpt) are omitted (the macro flow standardises on.dta in/out +.sav/.sas7bdat import); label surgery (zap_*/tagged_na/print_labels) is omitted (the labels are exposed as data, not mutated); non-file inputs (connection/literal/raw/URL auto-download) are omitted (a local path only — determinism + security).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition. Gates (all live-verified, haven 2.5.5): the read path = a string of length 1, NOT a directory, existing; the write path's parent dir exists + a POST-gate that it was written; the write data = a df with ≥1 column; `version` = a length-1 integer in 8-15; `label` NULL or a string ≤ 80 bytes; skip≥0 an integer, n_max>0 an integer or Inf; a non-df input to `hvn_as_factor` MUST be labelled.

**Alternatives + criterion:** among the three readers, choose by file format (.dta→stata,.sav→spss,.sas7bdat→sas). `hvn_as_factor` before categorical analysis/plots when the columns are `haven_labelled` (codes + labels); otherwise the labelled columns serialise as numeric codes with the human labels in `.value_labels`.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Readers: `data` (a tibble — a registered producer → Parquet; labelled columns → numeric codes) + `var_labels`/`value_labels`/`labelled_cols`/`col_types`/`dataset_label` (JSON-safe named atomics). Writer: `path`/`written`/`version`/`n_rows`/`n_cols`/`bytes`. `hvn_as_factor`: `data`/`input_type`/`levels`/`ordered`/`n`.
- **attr partial-match trap:** `attr(col, "label")` does PARTIAL matching and returns the `"labels"` attribute (the value labels/codes) when there is no variable label → WRONG metadata; the wrapper uses `exact=TRUE` everywhere.
- **write_dta version trap:** `version=14.5` is accepted SILENTLY (garbage semantics); `version=c(14,15)` gives the cryptic "condition has length > 1" — gated to a whole-number length-1 value in 8-15.
- **as_factor silent-factor trap:** `as_factor` on a plain numeric (non-labelled) falls back to `as_factor` and SILENTLY factors any vector (silent-wrong); gated (labelled-only for a non-df input).

**Sources:** haven reference (`read_dta`, `read_sav`, `read_sas`, `write_dta`, `as_factor`; labelled metadata) — Wickham/Miller/Smith, haven 2.5.5 (live `args` introspection + the system.file examples iris.dta/.sav/.sas7bdat) <https://haven.tidyverse.org/> / <

### #101 CLOSED-vocabulary tabular manipulation (filter/select/mutate/join/…) — `closed_vocabulary_tabular` (`c00_data_utilities/closed_vocabulary_tabular.py`)
**Functions:** `dpl_filter` [`filter`], `dpl_select` [`select`], `dpl_mutate` [`mutate`], `dpl_arrange` [`arrange`], `dpl_summarise` [`summarise`, `.by`], `dpl_group_by` [`group_by`/`group_keys`/`group_size`/`n_groups`], `dpl_join` [`left`/`inner`/`full`/`anti_join`], `dpl_distinct` [`distinct`], `dpl_rename` [`rename`], `dpl_relocate` [`relocate`], `dpl_slice` [`slice`/`slice_head`/`_tail`/`_min`/`_max`]

**When:** the relational/wrangling layer of the pipeline — filtering, selecting/renaming/reordering columns, closed unary/binary transformations into new columns, sorting, per-group aggregation (`.by`), joins on common keys, distinct, positional slice. One button per verb, output = a new DataFrame ready for the next node.

**When NOT:** for free tidy-eval expressions (structurally EXCLUDED — column names + a closed enum only); for long<->wide reshaping / NA handling → `tidy_reshaping_missing` #102; for fast grouped/panel series transformations (lags/diffs/growth/within/scale) → `fast_transformation` #103; for random row sampling (`slice_sample` was EXCLUDED — every node is deterministic/cacheable).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition (relational operations). Gates: every input `is.DataFrame`; every column (column/columns/by/order_by/before/after) MUST exist (`.dpl_need_cols`, a non-empty character); `dpl_filter` has a **silent-wrong gate** — a numeric column vs a non-numeric value (`1=="a"` → silently 0 rows) is rejected; `dpl_join` keys exist in BOTH; `dpl_rename` |new|==|old| without duplicates; `dpl_relocate` not before AND after together; `dpl_summarise` numeric_stats ⇒ a numeric column; `dpl_slice` positive integers, end>=start.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `fast_transformation` #103 when the issue is a grouped/panel numeric transformation of series (much faster, panel-aware g/t); `tidy_reshaping_missing` #102 when you need reshaping/completion instead of relational operations. `closed_vocabulary_tabular` is preferred for general tabular wrangling by column name.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every verb: `data` (records) + `n_rows`/`n_cols`/`columns` + the arguments that were applied.
- **`dpl_group_by` trap**: a terminal INFO node — it returns `group_keys`/`group_sizes`/`n_groups`, it does NOT chain a grouped_df (the grouped attribute is lost at the stateless Parquet boundary); for a real per-group aggregation use `dpl_summarise(by=)`.
- **`dpl_mutate` op='div'/'log' trap**: it produces `NaN`/`Inf` cells (e.g. sqrt/log of a negative → NaN + a warning that is muffled into a message); checking arithmetic validity is your responsibility.
- **`value` trap**: the numeric-vs-string incompatibility is blocked BEFORE it becomes a silent 0-row filter.

**Sources:** dplyr 1.2.1 reference — "A Grammar of Data Manipulation" (Wickham et al.), <https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/> / < vignettes `closed_vocabulary_tabular`, `grouping`, `two-table` (r-btw docs_help_page: filter/mutate/summarise/across/slice_min).
### #102 Tidy-data reshaping & missing-value handling — `tidy_reshaping_missing` (`c00_data_utilities/tidy_reshaping_missing.py`)
**Functions:** `tidyr_pivot_longer` [`pivot_longer`], `tidyr_pivot_wider` [`pivot_wider`], `tidyr_separate_wider` [`separate_wider_delim`/`_position`/`_regex`], `tidyr_unite` [`unite`], `tidyr_drop_na` [`drop_na`], `tidyr_replace_na` [`replace_na`], `tidyr_fill` [`fill`], `tidyr_complete` [`complete`], `tidyr_nest` [`nest`], `tidyr_unnest` [`unnest`]

**When:** the table-shaping layer — uploaded data.frames change shape (long<->wide), columns are split/joined, implicit combinations are materialised, and NA are cleaned/filled (drop/replace/fill LOCF-NOCB) through ONE deterministic, CLOSED-VOCABULARY button. Every column is given BY NAME (a typed string/vector), validated against `names(data)`.

**When NOT:** for relational operations (filter/mutate/join/summarise) → `closed_vocabulary_tabular` #101; for deep rectangling (hoist/pack/unnest_wider/_longer) and grid builders (expand/crossing) — OMITTED (outside the macro scope); for statistical NA imputation → `imputeTS` #80 (`fill` only does LOCF/NOCB, `replace_na` a constant value); for class/frequency conversion → `time_series_class` #78.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition (mechanical reshaping). Gates: every input `is.DataFrame`; every character column selection ⊆ `names(data)`; `pivot_longer` with names_to>1 ⇒ names_sep/pattern is REQUIRED; `pivot_wider` has a **SILENT-WRONG gate** — a non-unique key (id_cols × names_from) without `values_fn` ⇒ tidyr SILENTLY produces list columns → blocked with a stop demanding an aggregator; `separate_wider` is mode-specific (delim⇒names/names_sep, position⇒NAMED numeric widths, regex⇒NAMED char patterns); in `unnest` every col MUST be a list column.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `closed_vocabulary_tabular` #101 when you need relational operations instead of reshaping; `qsu`/`collap` #103 for a fast summary/aggregation instead of completion. `tidy_reshaping_missing` is preferred purely for long<->wide, split/unite, complete, nest/unnest.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every wrapper: `data` (records; nested list columns are handled recursively) + `class`/`nrow`/`ncol`/`colnames` + metrics (`n_dropped`/`n_added`).
- **`pivot_wider` id_cols trap**: when empty, tidyr **infers** the id_cols from the remaining columns (the wrapper does NOT pass the argument at all — a literal NULL is the sentinel; a non-literal NULL would give an empty selection → 1-row list cols; fixed).
- **`values_fn` trap**: if the key IS unique, do not supply an aggregator; if it is NOT, you MUST (otherwise the gate stops).
- **`separate_wider_regex` trap**: it has NO `too_many` (greedy); `too_few='debug'` emits a warning (muffled into a message) + debug columns.

**Sources:** tidyr 1.3.2 reference — "Tidy Messy Data" (Wickham et al.), <https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/> / < vignettes `pivot`, `nest`, `rectangle` (r-btw docs_help_page: pivot_longer/pivot_wider/separate_wider_delim/complete/fill).
### #103 Fast (grouped/panel) data transformation — `fast_transformation` (`c00_data_utilities/fast_transformation.py`)
**Functions:** `cll_growth` [`fgrowth`], `cll_diff` [`fdiff`], `cll_lag` [`flag`], `cll_cumsum` [`fcumsum`], `cll_scale` [`fscale`], `cll_within` [`fwithin`], `cll_collap` [`collap`], `cll_qsu` [`qsu`], `cll_transform` [`TRA`]

**When:** the high-performance transform layer for macro series and **panels**: lags/leads, differences, growth rates (exact or log-diff), (grouped) cumulative sums, (grouped/weighted) standardization and centering, multi-column aggregation by groups, quick summary statistics, and a generic sweep-out (TRA). It works on plain numeric / ts/mts / DataFrame and supports panel data via `g` (groups) + `t` (time), C/C++-fast and NA-skipping by default.

**When NOT:** for relational operations/joins → `closed_vocabulary_tabular` #101; for long<->wide reshaping → `tidy_reshaping_missing` #102; for class-agnostic conversions + macro-semantic transforms (an index with base_value, deflate, contributions) → `time_series_class` #78 / `macro-arithmetic` #82; for rolling-window reductions → `deterministic_rolling_window` #105.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no formal statistical precondition. Gates (all live-verified): every input a numeric vector/matrix/ts or an all-numeric DataFrame, and non-empty; `g` atomic with length = the observations; `t` atomic of the same length, WITHOUT g ⇒ NO duplicates ("Repeated values in timevar"); `w` numeric of the same length; `n` an integer (0/negative=lead are accepted), `diff` a positive integer; `cll_collap` X a non-empty DataFrame, by mandatory; **`cll_qsu` routes g→by EXPLICITLY for a DataFrame** (otherwise the grouping is ignored SILENTLY); `cll_transform` STATS numeric mandatory, '-+' requires groups.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `time_series_class` #78 / `macro-arithmetic` #82 when you need the macro semantics (the annualize convention, deflate, a base=100 index, contribution additivity) — `fast_transformation` gives the FAST, panel-aware, class-agnostic mechanical transform. `summarise` #101 for small non-panel aggregations; `collap` wins on speed/multi-column.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Transforms: `series` (the same shape as the input — `ts`→{values,start,frequency}, matrix→nested, df→records) + `class`/`n` + the arguments. `stubs=FALSE` ⇒ CLEAN column names (without 'L1G1.' prefixes).
- `cll_collap`: `result` (the aggregated df); `cll_qsu`: `summary` (a plain df via `as.DataFrame(qsu)` — avoiding the qsu-matrix leak).
- **`fscale`/`fwithin` constant-series trap**: the z-score → `NaN` (honest, not silent). **`cll_collap` weights trap**: only the weighted fast-stat functions use them; first/last/min/max/nobs IGNORE them (the warning is muffled into a message). **`cll_qsu` trap**: for a DataFrame supply `g` (routed to `by`); the.default method silently ignores g.

**Sources:** collapse 2.1.7 reference — "Advanced and Fast Data Transformation" (Krantz), <https://fastverse.org/collapse/> / < Krantz (2026) JSS 116(1) <doi:10.18637/jss.v116.i01>; vignettes `collapse_intro`, `collapse_and_plm` (r-btw docs: fgrowth/fdiff/flag/fscale/fwithin/collap/qsu/TRA).
### #104 Deterministic invertible preprocessing transformations (feature engineering) — `deterministic_invertible_preprocessing` (`c00_data_utilities/deterministic_invertible_preprocessing.py`)
**Functions:** `ttk_diff` [`diff_vec`], `ttk_diff_inv` [`diff_inv_vec`], `ttk_standardize` [`standardize_vec`], `ttk_normalize` [`normalize_vec`], `ttk_box_cox` [`box_cox_vec`+`auto_lambda`], `ttk_auto_lambda` [`auto_lambda`], `ttk_augment_lags` [`tk_augment_lags`], `ttk_augment_differences` [`tk_augment_differences`], `ttk_pad_by_time` [`pad_by_time`]

**When:** the "feature" data layer — the EXACT, INVERTIBLE preprocessing a downstream forecasting/ML node expects: differencing/log-differencing (with the `initial_values` for a full inversion), standardization (mean 0, sd 1), min-max normalization (0,1), variance-stabilising Box-Cox (with an auto lambda, guerrero/loglik), lag/difference augmentation of many columns, and regular-timestamp padding.

**When NOT:** for charts (all `plot_*` are omitted); for fast grouped/panel transformations → `fast_transformation` #103; for macro-semantic growth/index → `macro-arithmetic` #82; for rolling-window smoothing → `deterministic_rolling_window` #105 (`slidify_vec`/`smooth_vec` were omitted here); for statistical imputation → `imputeTS` #80.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** Gates (all live-verified against timetk 2.9.1): `ttk_diff` lag*difference < length (otherwise the cryptic "abs(k) must be less than nrow"); `log=TRUE` ⇒ x>0 (otherwise SILENT NaN); `ttk_standardize` n>=2 and sd>0 (a constant series → NaN); `ttk_normalize` min!=max; **Box-Cox/auto_lambda require strictly positive x** (guerrero warns, and lambda<=0 log → SILENT NaN); lambda_lower < lambda_upper (a reversed interval is accepted SILENTLY by optimize → gate); `ttk_pad_by_time` date_col MUST be Date/POSIXct.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `fast_transformation` #103 when you want panel-aware (g/t) fast differencing/scaling without inversion parameters; `macro-arithmetic` #82 when you need the macro convention (annualize/deflate). `deterministic_invertible_preprocessing` is preferred when you need the INVERSION PARAMETERS (lag/mean/sd/min/max/lambda) for reversible ML preprocessing.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Vector wrappers: `result` (the transformed vector) + the inversion PARAMETERS (`initial_values`/`mean`/`sd`/`min`/`max`/`lambda`).
- Augmenters: `result` (a tibble) + `new_columns` (which were added) + the dimensions.
- **`ttk_box_cox` lambda trap**: `lambda='auto'` (default) → it is selected deterministically and reported in `.lambda` (fully reproducible); supply a number for a fixed lambda. **Inversion trap**: `ttk_diff_inv` needs EXACTLY the `initial_values` and the lag/difference of `ttk_diff`.
- **Determinism**: no RNG (auto_lambda guerrero/loglik are deterministic — two calls = an identical lambda); every node is cacheable without a seed.

**Sources:** timetk 2.9.1 reference — "A Tool Kit for Working with Time Series" (Dancho/Vaughan), <https://business-science.github.io/timetk/> / < vignettes `TK04_Plotting_Time_Series` (transforms), `TK07_Time_Series_Data_Wrangling` (r-btw docs: diff_vec/box_cox_vec/auto_lambda/tk_augment_lags/pad_by_time).
### #105 Deterministic rolling aggregations (rolling windows) — `deterministic_rolling_window` (`c00_data_utilities/deterministic_rolling_window.py`)
**Functions:** `sld_slide` [`slide_dbl`], `sld_slide_index` [`slide_index_dbl`], `sld_slide_period` [`slide_period_dbl`], `sld_hop_index` [`hop_index_vec`, `.ptype=double`]

**When:** the "rolling aggregate" layer — given a numeric series, compute a rolling mean/sum/sd/min/max/median under four window regimes: positional (`.before`/`.after`/`.step`), index-relative (the boundaries = i±before, respecting irregular gaps), calendar-period (the index in period blocks via warp), and arbitrary window pairs (`.starts`/`.stops`). vctrs-native, type-stable, with no zoo/xts dependency.

**When NOT:** for charts (the frontend draws them); for differences/growth/lags (not rolling aggregations) → `fast_transformation` #103 / `deterministic_invertible_preprocessing` #104; for a free custom reducer function (structurally EXCLUDED — a closed enum only); for smoothing/rolling with weights → `fast_rolling_expanding`/`TTR` (other data-utility nodes).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** Gates (live-probed against slider 0.3.3): x a numeric NON-matrix vector, non-empty; **`reducer`/`period` a closed enum** (the central safety measure — `.f` is NEVER exposed); `.before`/`.after` a scalar integer or Inf (negatives=look-forward), a non-empty window ⇒ before+after>=0; `.step`/`.every` a positive integer >=1; `.i` of the same length as x, without NA, increasing (ties are OK); `hop` starts/stops of equal length, non-empty, without NA, start<=stop.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `fast_transformation` #103 / `deterministic_invertible_preprocessing` #104 when you want point transforms (diff/growth/scale) rather than a window reduction; `fast_rolling_expanding`/`TTR` when you need specialised weighted/EMA rolling. `deterministic_rolling_window` is preferred for GENERAL, type-stable, index-aware rolling aggregations.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every wrapper: `values` (a double vector = chart-data; the LENGTH = length(x) for slide*, = length(starts) for hop) + `n`/`n_na`/`reducer`/`na_rm` + the arguments that were applied.
- **Empty-window trap**: empty windows (e.g. `complete=TRUE` at the edges, or a hop range outside the index) give `NaN`/`Inf` — **they are reported in `n_na`, not hidden**.
- **`hop_index` trap**: the output does NOT have length length(x) but length(starts); `.before/.after` in `slide_period` count BLOCKS (not observations).
- **Determinism**: zero stochasticity — every node is cacheable without a seed.

**Sources:** slider 0.3.3 reference — "Sliding Window Functions" (Vaughan), < / < vignettes `deterministic_rolling_window`, `rowwise` (r-btw docs: slide_dbl/slide_index_dbl/slide_period_dbl/hop_index_vec).
### #106 Indexed (time-stamped) time-series toolbox — `indexed_time_series` (`c00_data_utilities/indexed_time_series.py`)
**Functions:** `xts_to_period` [`to.period`], `xts_period_apply` [`endpoints`+`period.apply`], `xts_apply_monthly` [`apply.monthly`], `xts_merge` [`merge.xts`], `xts_align_time` [`align.time`]

**When:** when the time/calendar index ITSELF is the object of the manipulation — converting the periodicity into an OHLC summary, aggregating over an arbitrary calendar period (endpoints/period.apply/apply.monthly), an index-based merge/join of two series, and aligning intraday timestamps. The calendar-aware layer for dated/irregular/intraday series; it complements #78 `time_series_class` (class conversion) — here the index is the subject.

**When NOT:** for rolling numeric transforms on a plain series (rate-of-change/moving averages/rolling stats) → `TTR` #107 / `fast_rolling_expanding` #109 / `data.table` #108; for charts (plot.xts/plot.zoo are omitted — the JS frontend draws them); for INCREASING the frequency → `temporal_aggregation_series` #79 (`xts_to_period` goes ONLY to a lower one); for class/frequency plumbing without index semantics → `time_series_class` #78.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** the input coercible to xts with a valid time index (`try.xts`+`is.xts`) and non-empty — a `DataFrame` is rejected (it points to `ts_convert(to='xts')`). Gates: `xts_to_period` has a **hard gate for univariate OR a genuine 4-col OHLC** (otherwise `to.period` silently builds a misleading OHLC from arbitrary columns); k a positive integer; OHLC TRUE/FALSE. `xts_align_time` has a **hard gate that the index is POSIXct** (on a Date/yearmon index `align.time` is a SILENT no-op); n>0 seconds. `xts_period_apply`/`xts_apply_monthly` take FUN from a closed whitelist (no caller code — security). `xts_merge` fill of length 1.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `ts_aggregate` (#78) for class-agnostic aggregation when you need neither OHLC nor calendar-endpoint control; `TTR`/`fast_rolling_expanding` (#107/#109) when the target is a rolling-window statistic rather than a calendar bucket. Prefer `indexed_time_series` when you need OHLC periodicity, calendar endpoints, or intraday alignment/merge on the real time index.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every wrapper: `series` (the xts result → `to_mcp.xts` → `{index, values}`) + `class`/`n`/`ncol`/`periodicity` + the arguments. The output is a classed xts → on the node round trip it serialises to the **RDS bucket** (`is.object==TRUE`), not Parquet.
- `xts_to_period`: `ncol=4` (Open/High/Low/Close) when OHLC=TRUE, `ncol=1` (close) when OHLC=FALSE; the index is end-of-period.
- **Column-prefix trap**: the OHLC columns take the NAME of the caller's series as a prefix (e.g. `gdp.Open`); when the input is not a plain symbol, the fixed prefix `V.` is used (deterministic, not a deparse of the whole object).
- **`periodicity` trap**: on <3 observations (e.g. an inner join with few common timestamps) `NA` is reported instead of noise.
- **`xts_align_time` trap**: `n_seconds` (the window in seconds) is a SEPARATE field from `n` (the number of observations) — it does not overwrite the count.

**Sources:** xts reference (`to.period`, `endpoints`, `period.apply`, `apply.monthly`, `merge.xts`, `align.time`, `periodicity`), xts 0.14.2 — Ryan & Ulrich, "xts: eXtensible Time Series" < the Ryan/Ulrich xts FAQ and vignette.
### #107 Rolling / windowed series transforms — `TTR` (`c00_data_utilities/fast_rolling_expandinging_windowed_series.py`)
**Functions:** `ttr_roc` [`ROC`], `ttr_momentum` [`momentum`], `ttr_ma` [`SMA`/`EMA`/`WMA`/`DEMA`/`ZLEMA`/`HMA`/`ALMA`], `ttr_run` [`runSum`/`runMean`/`runSD`/`runMin`/`runMax`/`runMedian`/`runMAD`/`runVar`], `ttr_run_cor` [`runCor`/`runCov`]

**When:** deterministic rolling and rate-of-change transformations on ONE univariate macro series (a numeric vector/ts): log or discrete % change, n-period momentum, a closed set of moving-average smoothers, single-series rolling-window statistics (sum/mean/sd/min/max/median/mad/var), and a rolling bivariate correlation/covariance. Numeric-in / numeric-out buttons — they produce numeric chart-data, not a graph.

**When NOT:** for OHLC/price technicals (MACD/RSI/ADX/BBands/stoch/williams/chaikin — trading-desk indicators outside the macro scope, NOT exposed); for calendar-aware periodicity/calendar aggregation/intraday alignment → `indexed_time_series` #106; for matrix/panel rolling or rolling regression → `fast_rolling_expanding` #109; for fast C lead/lag and frollapply reducers → `data.table` #108; for charts (the JS frontend draws them).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** the input univariate and numeric (`.ttr_series`: NCOL>1 ⇒ stop; not convertible to numeric ⇒ stop; empty ⇒ stop). Gates: **`n` an integer in [1, length]** — CRITICAL: `ROC`/`momentum` do NOT error when n>length, they SILENTLY return an all-NA result of the wrong length; the gate blocks it. `ttr_run_cor` has a **hard gate length(x)==length(y)** (runCor/runCov do NOT check it → silently partially-NA/garbage). Per-type validation in `ttr_ma`: wilder TRUE/FALSE, ratio∈(0,1] or NULL, wts of length n or of the series, v∈[0,1], offset∈[0,1], sigma>0. match.arg on type/fun/method.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `fast_rolling_expanding` #109 when you need online/weighted rolling, or panel/matrix, or rolling regression; `data.table` #108 (frollmean/frollapply) for large series with C speed and robust reducers (IQR/mad/prod); `apply.monthly`/`period.apply` #106 for calendar buckets instead of a fixed rolling window. Prefer `TTR` for the classic ROC/momentum/MA smoothers and single-series rolling moments with ready-made enums.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every wrapper: `values` (plain numeric chart-data; the 1-col matrix of ALMA is passed through `as.numeric` for uniformity) + `n_obs` + **`n_na`** (an explicit NA count — never a silent drop) + the arguments.
- The leading NA (window length minus 1) are the expected warm-up; `type='continuous'` (ROC) = a log return, `'discrete'` = a simple % return.
- **`runQuantile` trap**: it does NOT exist in TTR 0.24.4 (confirmed live); the "quantile" intent is covered by `ttr_run(fun='median')` (the 0.5 quantile) + `fun='mad'`.
- **`cumulative` trap**: the expanding-window mode is NOT exposed (determinism) — a fixed rolling window only.

**Sources:** TTR reference (`ROC`, `momentum`, `SMA`/`EMA`/`WMA`/`DEMA`/`ZLEMA`/`HMA`/`ALMA`, `runSum`/`runSD`/`runCor`), TTR 0.24.4 — Ulrich, "TTR: Technical Trading Rules" <
### #108 Fast lead/lag + rolling-window aggregates — `data.table` (`c00_data_utilities/fast_lead_lag.py`)
**Functions:** `dt_shift` [`shift`], `dt_roll` [`frollmean`/`frollsum`/`frollsd`/`frollmax`/`frollmin`], `dt_roll_apply` [`frollapply` with a closed reducer set: median/mad/IQR/var/sd/mean/sum/min/max/prod]

**When:** deterministic, C-speed feature engineering on ONE macro series (a numeric vector): lead/lag/shift/cyclic displacement (with several offsets in a single call), rolling moments (mean/sum/sd/max/min) with right/left/center alignment and an optional **adaptive** (per-observation) window, and rolling robust reducers via `frollapply` over a CLOSED named-reducer set. Ideal for large series where speed matters.

**When NOT:** for online/weighted rolling, or matrix/panel, or rolling regression → `fast_rolling_expanding` #109; for the classic ROC/momentum/MA smoothers (EMA/WMA/ALMA) → `TTR` #107; for calendar-aware buckets/OHLC/intraday alignment → `indexed_time_series` #106; for charts (frontend). The fast-but-unsafe paths `algo='exact'`/`has.nf=FALSE` are NOT exposed (has.nf=FALSE can give a SILENTLY wrong max/min in the presence of non-finite values).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** the input a single numeric/logical series (`.dtb_check_x`: a matrix/mts with dim!=NULL ⇒ stop; char/complex/list/df ⇒ stop; empty ⇒ stop). Gates: **`n` an integer (round-based)** — CRITICAL: `shift(x,1.5)` and `frollmean(x,2.5)` SILENTLY truncate the fractional part to an integer (silent-wrong); the gate blocks it; `dt_roll`/`dt_roll_apply` additionally n>=1 (n=0 ⇒ a degenerate all-NaN). `adaptive=TRUE` ⇒ n a vector of length length(x) and align≠center. `fill` of length 1 (a number/NA); logical flags TRUE/FALSE. **SECURITY:** the `dt_roll_apply` FUN is a match.arg over a fixed table of named reducers (mapped to base/stats) — NEVER caller code inside `frollapply`.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `runSum/runMean/runSD` (#107) for the same rolling moments with ready-made macro enums on small series; `fast_rolling_expanding` (#109) when you want weighted/online, a panel matrix, or a rolling `roll_lm`; `rollapply` is not exposed (it is covered by `frollapply`). Prefer `data.table` for speed, multi-offset shift, adaptive windows and robust reducers (IQR/mad/prod).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every wrapper: `result` (a plain numeric vector; for a multi-offset `dt_shift` a **list** of equally long vectors — `to_mcp` handles both) + `n_obs` + `class` + the arguments.
- Leading/trailing NA (window length minus 1) depending on `align`; the padding positions are controlled by `fill`.
- **Multi-offset shift trap**: `n=c(1,2)` returns `result` as a list (one series per offset), not a flat vector.
- **`adaptive` trap**: n must be a vector of length length(x); it does not combine with `align='center'` (a pre-gate before the cryptic data.table error).

**Sources:** data.table reference (`shift`, the `froll` family, `frollapply`), data.table 1.18.4 — Barrett, Dowle, Srinivasan et al., "data.table: Extension of `DataFrame`" < / <https://rdatatable.gitlab.io/data.table/>.
### #109 Fast rolling & expanding window statistics — `fast_rolling_expanding` (`c00_data_utilities/fast_rolling_expanding.py`)
**Functions:** `rll_mean` [`roll_mean`], `rll_sd` [`roll_sd`], `rll_var` [`roll_var`], `rll_cor` [`roll_cor`], `rll_cov` [`roll_cov`], `rll_lm` [`roll_lm`], `rll_scale` [`roll_scale`], `rll_quantile` [`roll_quantile`]

**When:** fast (Rcpp/RcppParallel, online algorithms) rolling and expanding window statistics over a numeric vector (one series) OR a matrix (a panel of series, rows=observations, columns=variables): moving/expanding moments (mean/sd/var), co-moments (cor/cov — pairwise or a k×k×n array of matrices), rolling standardisation (z-score), rolling quantiles, and **rolling linear regression** (`roll_lm` → coefficients/R²/std.error per observation). It supports **weighted** windows (e.g. exponential decay) and a tunable `min_obs` for the expanding warm-up.

**When NOT:** for single-series ROC/momentum/MA smoothers → `TTR` #107; for fast lead/lag and robust `frollapply` reducers (IQR/mad/prod) on ONE series → `data.table` #108; for calendar buckets/OHLC/intraday → `indexed_time_series` #106; for charts (frontend). The niche reducers (roll_sum/prod/min/max/median/idx*/crossprod) are NOT exposed.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** x (and y where present) a numeric vector/matrix, non-empty. Gates — all live-verified against raw `fast_rolling_expanding`: **`width` a positive integer <= nobs** (width>nobs ⇒ SILENTLY all-NA; width=4.5 ⇒ a silent truncation; width="5" ⇒ a silent coercion); **`weights` of length == width**, finite (a mismatched length is accepted silently with unclear semantics); **`min_obs` in [1, width]** (min_obs>width ⇒ SILENTLY all-NA); `p`∈[0,1] (rll_quantile); logical flags (center/scale/intercept/online) TRUE/FALSE; `rll_cor`/`rll_cov`/`rll_lm` require nrow(y)==nrow(x).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `data.table` #108 (frollmean/frollapply) for ONE series with C speed and robust reducers when you do not need weighted/online/panel; `runSD/runCor` #107 for the classic rolling moments/cor on small univariate series. Prefer `fast_rolling_expanding` when you have a **panel/matrix**, want **weighted/online** rolling, a rolling **z-score**, or a rolling **regression** (`roll_lm`).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Most wrappers: `result` (a numeric vector / matrix / k×k×n array) + `class`/shape (`n` or `dim`) + `width`/`min_obs`/`online` (+`center`/`scale`/`p`). `rll_cor(y=NULL)`/`rll_cov(y=NULL)` on a matrix ⇒ a **3D array** of correlation/covariance matrices per window.
- `rll_lm`: a named list `coefficients` / `r.squared` / `std.error` (each a matrix, one row per observation; an extra intercept column when intercept=TRUE) + `n`/`width`/`min_obs`/`online`. **It is NOT a chainable producer** (it does not return a fitted model object — purely rolling coefficient matrices).
- The first `width-1` (or `min_obs-1`) rows are the NA warm-up; `online=TRUE` gives the incremental algorithm (which may show negligible numerical differences vs `online=FALSE` on ill-conditioned data).

**Sources:** roll reference (`roll_mean`, `roll_sd`, `roll_var`, `roll_cor`, `roll_cov`, `roll_lm`, `roll_scale`, `roll_quantile`), roll 1.2.1 — Foster, "roll: Rolling and Expanding Statistics" < / <https://jjf234.github.io/roll/>.

### #111 Date parsing / rounding / components + safe month arithmetic — `date_parsing_rounding` (`c00_data_utilities/date_parsing_rounding.py`)
**Functions:** `lub_parse_date` [`ymd`/`ym`], `lub_parse_datetime` [`parse_date_time`], `lub_round_date` [`floor_date`/`ceiling_date`/`round_date`], `lub_component` [`quarter`/`semester`/`year`/`month`/`wday`], `lub_month_arith` [`%m+%`/`%m-%`]

**When:** the date "cleaning" step BEFORE entering tsbox #78 / the other nodes — when the time column (from the user's upload) is a raw character/numeric string that must become a proper `Date`/`POSIXct` (`lub_parse_date`/`lub_parse_datetime`, which tolerate heterogeneous separators and no separator), be rounded to a calendar boundary (start/end of month, quarter or year, `lub_round_date`), yield calendar features as numeric fields for dummies/seasonality (`lub_component`), or have months added/subtracted with a CORRECT end-of-month rollback (`lub_month_arith`).

**When NOT:** for class/frequency conversion or analytical transformations of an ALREADY time-indexed series → `time_series_class` #78 (tsbox locates the time column FROM THE CLASS, so it needs a `Date`/`POSIXct` already — which is exactly what lubridate produces); for general day arithmetic (`date + n`) the standard library suffices — lubridate is needed ONLY for safe MONTH arithmetic (months have variable length); for charts (the JS frontend draws them).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no formal statistical precondition (purely calendar operations). Gates: `lub_parse_*` → x a non-empty character/numeric; a **hard POST-gate that no non-blank input silently became NA** (ymd/ym/parse_date_time return NA with ONLY a warning — silent-wrong); `orders` a non-empty character vector; `lub_round_date`/`lub_component`/`lub_month_arith` → x a non-empty `Date`/`POSIXct` (floor/ceiling/round_date throws the cryptic "Unsupported date-time class" on a character); `unit` a **closed enum {month,quarter,year,week,day}** (otherwise the cryptic "Invalid unit specification"); `boundary`/`component`/`op` via match.arg; `months` a finite integer of length 1 (`period` rejects non-integers: "periods must have integer values").

**Alternatives + criterion:** `time_series_class` #78 when the series is ALREADY in a time-aware class and you want class/frequency plumbing or transforms — lubridate comes first and builds the `Date` column from raw strings. Base `as.Date`/`format`/`+` when the input is HOMOGENEOUS ISO and you do not need the month rollback — lubridate is preferred for heterogeneous parsing, calendar rounding, and safe `%m+%`/`%m-%`.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `lub_parse_date`/`lub_parse_datetime`: `dates` (Date/POSIXct → ISO-8601 strings), `n`, `n_na` (the number of permitted NA from blank/NA input), `class`, the applied `order`/`orders`/`tz`.
- `lub_round_date`/`lub_month_arith`: `dates` (rounded/shifted), + `unit`/`boundary` or `months`/`op`.
- `lub_component`: `values` (a clean numeric vector — e.g. quarter 1–4, wday 1–7), `component`, `n`.
- **Silent-NA trap**: parsing returns NA silently (a warning only) when it fails; the wrapper does a **hard stop** on any non-blank input that was not parsed (blocked-by-gate ⇒ fix order/orders or the raw column).
- **`%m+%`/`%m-%` rollback trap**: `31 Jan %m+% 1 month = 28/29 Feb` (NOT an overflow into March as with a naive `date + 30/31`); this is the entire reason the button exists.
- **`wday` trap**: the default is `week_start = 7` (Sunday) ⇒ Sunday=1, Monday=2, … (ISO Monday=1 is NOT the default).

**Sources:** lubridate reference (`ymd`/`ym`, `parse_date_time`, `round_date`/`floor_date`/`ceiling_date`, `quarter`/`semester`, `month`/`wday`, `%m+%`/`add_with_rollback`) — live introspection via `Rd_db('lubridate')` (v1.9.5, the the lockfile superset); Grolemund & Wickham, "Dates and Times Made Easy with lubridate", JSS 40(3) 2011 <

### #112 Business-day calendar + working-day arithmetic — `business_day_calendar` (`c00_data_utilities/business_day_calendar.py`)
**Functions:** `bizc_create_calendar` [`create.calendar` — build + VALIDATE + describe], `bizc_bizdays` [`business_day_calendar` — the count of business days from→to], `bizc_offset` [`offset`/`add.bizdays` — a shift by N business days], `bizc_adjust` [`adjust.next`/`adjust.previous` — roll to a business day], `bizc_bizseq` [`bizseq` — enumerate the business days in a span]

**When:** when you need BUSINESS-day arithmetic over a calendar built from a CLOSED specification (a vector of holidays + a weekend/weekdays set): settlement/value dates (T+n), a NETWORKDAYS-style count of business days between two dates, rolling a non-business date (maturity/coupon) to the next/previous business day, and enumerating the business days of an interval. Fixed-income and derivatives day counting. The calendar is ALWAYS built internally from (holidays, weekdays, financial, adjust_from/to, start/end) — never arbitrary code, never a global named-calendar lookup; every node is stateless and deterministic.

**When NOT:** for time-series class/frequency conversions or general transformations → `time_series_class` #78; for fractional business days (year fractions / pricing day-count fractions, `bizdayse`) — not exposed here; for built-in market catalogs (ANBIMA/QuantLib/Rmetrics) — omitted (external, non-deterministic); it is not time-series imputation/aggregation.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition (calendar arithmetic). Gates (all live-probed against the real package): `weekdays` ⊆ the 7 LOWERCASE tokens {sunday.saturday} — {bizdays} SILENTLY accepts "Saturday"/"funday" and treats them as BUSINESS DAYS (silent-wrong); `holidays` valid, without NA/unparseable values; `financial` logical; a NON-EMPTY calendar (≥1 business day in [start,end]); `bizc_offset`: `n` a (vector of) integers — a fractional n returns NA SILENTLY; `from <= to` (bizdays: from>to → a NEGATIVE result; bizseq: a cryptic error); the dates within [start,end] (otherwise "Given date out of range" — a pre-gate with an instructive message to widen start_date/end_date).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `adjust_from=previous`+`adjust_to=next` (the Excel NETWORKDAYS convention) when the business-day count must start/end on a business day; `financial=FALSE` when you need an inclusive count (it counts the final business day too — +1 vs financial); `direction=next`/`following` vs `previous`/`preceding` depending on the market convention (the modified.* rolls are omitted here, we keep to the two canonical ones). For time-series transformations instead of calendar arithmetic → `time_series_class` #78.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `bizc_create_calendar`: `weekdays`/`financial`/`adjust_from`/`adjust_to` (the closed specification), `n_holidays`+`holidays` (ISO strings), `start_date`/`end_date` (Date→ISO), `n_bizdays` (the business days in the range — a validation summary). The raw Calendar object is NEVER returned (it contains closures — not JSON-safe).
- `bizc_bizdays`: `count` (an integer vector; NETWORKDAYS-style), `from`/`to` (Date→ISO), `n`, `financial`.
- `bizc_offset`: `result` (the shifted Dates→ISO), `dates`, `n`, `n_out`.
- `bizc_adjust`: `result` (the rolled Dates→ISO), `dates`, `direction`, `n_out`.
- `bizc_bizseq`: `sequence` (the business Dates→ISO), `n`, `from`/`to`.
- **`weekdays` trap**: lowercase Greek only… no — lowercase English tokens only; "Saturday"/"funday" silently become BUSINESS DAYS if they are not gated.
- **`financial` trap**: `financial=TRUE` (default) does NOT count the final business day — the counts are 1 smaller than the non-financial ones.
- **Range trap**: the default range when holidays are supplied is [min,max] of the holidays — dates outside it error; widen it with start_date/end_date.

**Sources:** bizdays reference/vignette (`create.calendar`, `business_day_calendar`, `offset`/`add.bizdays`, `adjust.next`/`adjust.previous`, `bizseq`) — Wilson Freitas, "bizdays: Business Days Calculations and Utilities" (v1.0.17) < / <https:// business-day / day-count market conventions (following / preceding / modified following, NETWORKDAYS) — the 2006 ISDA Definitions.
### #113 Tidy temporal data frames (the key/index contract + structural gaps + calendar aggregation) — `tidy_temporal_frames` (`c00_data_utilities/tidy_temporal_frames.py`)
**Functions:** `tsib_as_tsibble` [`as_tsibble` key/index/regular; PRODUCER→tbl_ts], `tsib_gaps` [`has_gaps`/`scan_gaps`/`count_gaps`, kind∈has/scan/count], `tsib_fill_gaps` [`fill_gaps`.full/.start/.end; PRODUCER], `tsib_index_agg` [`index_by`+`summarise`, CLOSED bucketers {year/quarter/month/week} × reducers {mean/sum/min/max/median}; PRODUCER]

**When:** the tidyverts DataFrame layer — an uploaded long series becomes a *contract-checked* temporal table with an EXPLICIT index (one time column) + an optional key (grouping): one row per (key,index) — validated, not assumed. You detect implicit gaps (has/scan/count), materialise them as explicit NA rows (fill_gaps), and aggregate to a lower calendar frequency (index_by+summarise) through ONE deterministic, CLOSED-vocabulary button. It produces tbl_ts handles for the other tidyverts nodes (fable/feasts).

**When NOT:** for free tidy-eval expressions in index_by/summarise/fill_gaps (structurally EXCLUDED — column names + a closed enum only); for class-agnostic conversions (ts/xts/df) and simple analyst transformations → `time_series_class` #78; for statistical NA filling (interpolation/Kalman) → `imputeTS` #80 (`fill_gaps` puts ONLY NA into the gaps, it does not estimate them); for INCREASING the frequency → `temporal_aggregation_series` #79; for charts (the JS frontend draws them).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition (structural transformations). Gates: `tsib_as_tsibble` — data `is.DataFrame` and non-empty, index ONE existing col, key existing cols and ≠ index, regular TRUE/FALSE; tsibble rejects duplicate (key,index) rows (a hard error, surfaced). All downstream: the input must be a `tbl_ts` (the chaining handle) and non-empty. `match.arg` on kind/to/reducer; logical flags (.full/by_key). `tsib_index_agg`: value_cols existing, MEASURED (not index/key), NUMERIC.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `time_series_class` #78 when you need class-agnostic conversion/transformation without the key/index contract (lighter); `closed_vocabulary_tabular` #101 / `fast_transformation` #103 for relational/panel wrangling without a time index; `tidy_temporal_frames` is preferred when the TARGET is the EXPLICIT (key,index) contract, gap detection/materialisation, or the tidyverts flow (fable/feasts). For aggregation: `tsib_index_agg` (calendar buckets) vs `ts_aggregate` (#78, class-agnostic).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every producer: `series` (the tbl_ts — `to_mcp` turns it into records, the calendar index → strings e.g. "2015 Q1") + `class`/`n`/`index`/`key`/`measured`/`interval` + the applied arguments. `tsib_gaps`: `result` + `any_gaps` + `n_missing` (has=the number of keys with gaps; scan=the number of missing rows; count=the sum of n).
- **Raw-Date interval trap (silent-wrong, confirmed live):** MONTHLY/quarterly data with a raw `Date` index → tsibble infers an interval of **1 DAY** (the GCD of the days) → thousands of FAKE gaps, and `fill_gaps` explodes into a daily grid. `interval` is returned EXPLICITLY so that "1D" is visible — supply a `yearmonth`/`yearquarter` index.
- **Key-collapse trap:** `index_by+summarise` with a key SILENTLY collapses all keys together; `by_key=TRUE` (the default) applies `group_by_key` → a per-key aggregation.
- **Finer-than-source trap:** asking to coarsen to a HIGHER resolution than the index (e.g. week from yearmonth) → a clean error (caught), not silence.

**Sources:** tsibble 1.2.0 reference/vignettes (`intro-tsibble`, `implicit-na`) — `as_tsibble`/`has_gaps`/`scan_gaps`/`count_gaps`/`fill_gaps`/`index_by` (r-btw docs_help_page + live introspection); Wang, Cook & Hyndman (2020), "A New Tidy Data Structure to Support Exploration and Modeling of Temporal Data", JCGS 29(3):466-478, doi:10.1080/10618600.2019.1695624; <https://tsibble.tidyverts.org/> / <
### #115 Benchmarking a high-freq indicator to a low-freq total (two-step Prais-Winsten + Denton) — `disaggR` (`c00_data_utilities/benchmarking_high_frequency.py`)
**Functions:** `dsg_two_steps_benchmark` [`twoStepsBenchmark`], `dsg_annual_benchmark` [`annualBenchmark`], `dsg_in_sample` [`in_sample`]; the coefficients/std-errors/rho accessors are built into the output of the producers.

**When:** when you have a high-frequency indicator (e.g. monthly/quarterly turnover) and want to "bend" it so that it sums EXACTLY to a low-frequency target total (e.g. annual construction activity) within each benchmark window. The method is two-step: (1) a Prais-Winsten GLS regression `lf ~ indicator` and (2) an additive Denton smoothing of the low-frequency residuals. `dsg_annual_benchmark` is a convenience wrapper with the default windows of the quarterly national accounts. Deterministic (GLS) — no seed.

**When NOT:** for a wider choice of disaggregation method (Chow-Lin maxlog/minrss, Fernandez, Litterman, Denton-Cholette, ols/uniform) → `temporal_aggregation_series` #79; for plain aggregation to a lower frequency (without consistency) → `ts_aggregate` #78; for proportional three-rule smoothing without a regression → `threeRuleSmooth` (OMITTED, outside #115); charts/HTML reports (frontend).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** `hfserie`/`lfserie` must be `ts`; a **frequency gate** (`.dsg_check_freq`): `frequency(hfserie)` STRICTLY HIGHER than `frequency(lfserie)` AND an integer ratio — LIVE TRAP: disaggR SILENTLY accepts an equal frequency (a ratio of 1 = a degenerate non-disaggregation) and errors only on a non-divisor ratio; **`lfserie` WITHOUT NA** (`.dsg_check_lf_na`): a LIVE SILENT-WRONG — an NA in `lfserie` does not error, the regression silently returns ALL-NA coefficients + an all-NA benchmark; `include.differenciation`/`include.rho` a strict logical of length 1 (the package silently accepts `=1` as TRUE); `set.coeff` (optional) a finite number. The span-coverage requirements (the hf series covering the coefficient window of the lf series) are validated cleanly by the package; NA in the extrapolation tail of the hf series (beyond the lf series) is legitimate.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `temporal_aggregation_series` #79 (single-step GLS with the full menu of Chow-Lin/Fernandez/Litterman/Denton methods) — prefer it when you want to choose the disaggregation model explicitly or need high→low (`ta`). `disaggR` is preferred for the specific **INSEE two-step flow** (a Prais-Winsten regression + additive Denton), with built-in `in_sample`/`rho`/`se` diagnostics and the semantics of the French QNA.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `benchmarked` (`ts` high-frequency, →`{values,start,frequency}`) = the MAIN result; it sums EXACTLY to `lfserie` within the benchmark window; it equals `fitted_values + smoothed_part` (the two additive components, also `ts`).
- `coefficients`/`std_errors`/`rho` = the Prais-Winsten regression (constant + the indicator loading); `rho=0` means NO AR term (`include.rho=FALSE`), not a failed fit. `set_coeff` echoes back (NA if it was estimated).
- `n_high`/`freq_high`/`freq_low`/`freq_ratio` metadata; `model` = the fitted `twoStepsBenchmark` handle (RDS) → use it in `dsg_in_sample`.
- `dsg_in_sample`: `comparison` = a 2-column `mts` (Benchmark vs Predicted value), in `changes` (default) or `levels`; the in-sample response-vs-prediction of the regression.
- **Traps**: (1) consistency holds ONLY within the benchmark window — the extrapolation tail (hf beyond lf) is a projection, not a benchmarked value. (2) an equal hf/lf frequency is degenerate (hard-blocked). (3) an NA in lfserie = silently ALL-NA (hard-blocked).

**Sources:** disaggR reference (`twoStepsBenchmark`, `annualBenchmark`, `in_sample`, `se`, `rho` — the Rd help pages, live introspection of the installed 1.0.5.x) < Denton 1971 "Adjustment of Monthly or Quarterly Series to Annual Totals" (*JASA* 66(333):99-102); Prais & Winsten 1954 (Cowles Commission Discussion Paper 383); the INSEE / Bank of France two-step benchmarking methodology.
### #116 Fast row/col panel statistics + diffusion index — `matrixStats` (`c00_data_utilities/fast_row_column.py`)
**Functions:** `panel_row_stats` [`rowMedians`/`rowVars`/`rowSds`, per-period cross-sectional], `panel_col_stats` [`colMedians`/`colVars`/`colSds`, per-series over time], `panel_quantiles` [`rowQuantiles`, the cross-sectional distribution per period], `panel_diffusion_index` [the share of series rising per period = `mean(diff > 0)`]

**When:** when you have a **wide numeric panel** (a plain `matrix`: rows=time, cols=series/countries/sectors — the standard shape once it arrives as a store pointer) and want **fast (C-level) descriptives** along two axes at once: (a) per-period cross-sectional location/spread (e.g. the median of all series in month t), (b) per-series over-time location/spread, (c) the cross-sectional distribution (quantiles) per period for fan charts, and (d) the classic **diffusion index** (breadth: the share of series with a positive change) — a basic leading indicator of the breadth of a macro panel.

**When NOT:** for a single series / ts-class handling → `time_series_class` #78 (matrixStats accepts ONLY a plain numeric matrix, NOT ts/mts/df); for rolling-window reductions over time → `deterministic_rolling_window` #105; for ACF/PACF/correlation descriptives → `descriptive_statistics` #81; for panel-aware grouped aggregation with ids → `fast_transformation` #103; for weighted/robust or econometric moments → the corresponding methods (matrixStats gives the MECHANICAL row/col moments, without inference).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no statistical precondition (mechanical reducers). Gates (ALL live-verified against the package): the input = a **plain numeric matrix** — a `DataFrame` (the cryptic "must be a matrix or a vector"), a `ts`/`mts` (which would PASS silently since `is.matrix`==TRUE), a `character`/`logical` matrix (cryptic type errors) and an empty matrix → all **hard stop**; `na.rm` strictly TRUE/FALSE; `panel_quantiles`: `probs` non-empty/finite and in **[0,1]** (a pre-gate BEFORE the cryptic concatenated "out of range" message), `type` an integer 1.9; `panel_diffusion_index`: **≥2 time periods** (otherwise `diff` yields 0 rows).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `fast_transformation` #103 (`fmedian`/`fsd`/`fquantile` with `g=`) when you need **grouped/panel-aware** aggregation with ids or speed on very large data; `matrixStats` is preferred when the panel is already a **wide numeric matrix** and you want the two-axis row/col moments + quantiles + diffusion in one deterministic button. `time_series_class` #78 when the issue is class/frequency plumbing of one or a few series, not cross-sectional statistics of a panel.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `panel_row_stats`/`panel_col_stats`: `values` = a numeric vector (`row`→of length n_time, `col`→of length n_series) + `margin`/`stat`/`n_time`/`n_series`/`na.rm`.
- `panel_quantiles`: `quantiles` = an `n_time × length(probs)` matrix with named columns ("25%", "50%"…; matrix→nested rows w/ dimnames in to_mcp) + `probs`/`type`. A single prob keeps the matrix (`drop=FALSE`).
- `panel_diffusion_index`: `index` = a vector of length `n_time-1` in **[0,1]** (0.5=balance, >0.5=a broad expansion) + `n_diff`.
- **`na.rm` trap**: with `na.rm=FALSE` an NA **propagates as NA** (VISIBLE — NOT a silent drop); set `TRUE` to ignore NA series. **Axis trap**: `row`=cross-sectional per period, `col`=over time per series — do not mix them up. **var/sd with 1 element trap**: `rowVars` on a one-column matrix gives `NA` (the variance of a single value), not an error.

**Sources:** matrixStats reference (`rowMedians`/`colMedians`, `rowVars`/`colVars`, `rowSds`/`colSds`, `rowQuantiles` — the signatures checked live via `args` against the installed 1.5.0) — Bengtsson H., "matrixStats: Functions that Apply to Rows and Columns of Matrices" < the diffusion index (breadth) as a leading indicator: Stock & Watson, "Diffusion Indexes" / the Conference Board business-cycle diffusion methodology.

### #110 Rolling-window statistics in O(n) — `caTools` (`c00_data_utilities/rolling_statistics_numeric.py`)
**Functions:** `run_mean` [`runmean`], `run_sd` [`runsd`], `run_min` [`runmin`], `run_max` [`runmax`], `run_quantile` [`runquantile`], `run_mad` [`runmad`]

**When:** immediately after data entry (the user's upload), when you need DETERMINISTIC, fast (O(n)) rolling statistics over ONE numeric series or a matrix of series (column by column): a moving average (smoothing), rolling volatility (sd), rolling min/max (envelope/drawdown), rolling quantiles (rolling bands/deciles) and rolling robust dispersion (MAD). Ideal for trailing (`align='right'`) windows in macro monitoring, where look-ahead is not allowed.

**When NOT:** for a rolling mean with **weights** or rolling correlation/covariance/regression/scale → `fast_rolling_expanding` #109 (caTools has no weights/multivariate support); for rolling with an irregular index/period or an arbitrary function → `deterministic_rolling_window` #105 / `data.table` #108; for charts — caTools emits ONLY numbers, the frontend draws them; for NA imputation → `imputeTS` #80 (caTools does not fill gaps).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no formal statistical precondition (mechanical rolling statistics). Gates (all from live probing of the silent-wrong behaviours of the C layer): `x` a non-empty numeric vector/matrix; **`k` a finite integer in [1, nobs]** (k≤0 → returns `x` UNCHANGED; a fractional k → silently truncated to `k %/% 2`; k>n → an over-run); **`align='center'` requires an ODD `k`** (an even one → a silently ASYMMETRIC centred window); `probs`∈[0,1] (`run_quantile`: outside → silently meaningless); `type` an integer in [1,9] (outside → only a WARN-and-reset); `center` (`run_sd`/`run_mad`) of length nobs (a wrong length → silent recycling); `constant`>0.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `fast_rolling_expanding` #109 when you need weights, `min_obs`, an online algorithm or multivariate rolling (cor/cov/lm/scale). `deterministic_rolling_window` #105 for rolling with an index/period or a custom function. `rollapply`/`data.table` #108 for a general rolling apply. `caTools` is preferred for SIMPLE, fast O(n) statistics of one buffer without weights.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- Every wrapper: `series` (the rolling vector; a matrix input → nested rows) + `n` (the output length; `endrule='trim'` → shorter) + `k`/`endrule`/`align` + the applied arguments (`probs`/`type`/`constant`/`center_supplied`).
- **`endrule` trap**: the per-method default (mean/sd/min/max/quantile/mad) fills the edges with the statistic ITSELF; `'NA'` leaves NA; `'trim'` SHORTENS the series (watch the index alignment downstream).
- **`align` trap**: `'center'` requires an odd `k`; `'right'` = trailing (the past only, no look-ahead — prefer it for forecasting features); `'left'` = leading.

**Sources:** caTools reference (`runmean`/`runsd`/`runmin`/`runmax`/`runquantile`/`runmad`; args `k`/`endrule`/`align`/`type`/`center`/`constant`) v1.18.3 — < Tukey (running median/MAD robust smoothing).
### #114 Robust treatment of extreme values + robust location/scale measures — `DescTools` (`c00_data_utilities/robust_outlier_handling.py`)
**Functions:** `dt_winsorize` [`Winsorize`], `dt_trim` [`Trim`], `dt_robscale` [`RobScale`], `dt_huber` [`HuberM`]

**When:** the "tail cleaning" step BEFORE any econometric method — capping extreme values (winsorize) at a quantile or at explicit bounds, symmetric trimming of the tails (trim), robust z-score standardisation via median/MAD (robscale, resistant to outliers unlike the classic `scale`) and robust Huber-M location estimation (± an optional Wald CI). For macro series with rare spikes / crisis observations that would distort OLS/mean/sd.

**When NOT:** for rolling/time-varying cleaning → `caTools` #110 / `fast_rolling_expanding` #109; for NA imputation (not rejection) → `imputeTS` #80; for full robust/quantile regression → `rlm` / quantreg #64. It is not an outlier detector — it does not return flags, it TRANSFORMS. It works on a VECTOR (not a matrix/df).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** `x` a non-empty numeric vector (NOT a matrix/df). Gates (all live-verified silent-wrong traps): `dt_winsorize` `probs`∈[0,1] increasing of length 2 OR `val` increasing of length 2; **an NA with `na_rm=FALSE` → stop** (otherwise the bounds=NA → the WHOLE series NA); `dt_trim` `trim`∈[0,0.5) (≥0.5 → silently NA; <0 → no trimming); `dt_robscale` an NA → stop (it has no na.rm) and **`scale` with MAD=0 → stop** (otherwise everything is NaN); `dt_huber` `k`>0, `conf_level`∈{empty}∪(0,1).

**Alternatives + criterion:** the classic z-score `scale` / `ttk_standardize` #104 when there are NO outliers (mean/sd is more efficient); `dt_robscale` when there are (median/MAD is resistant). `dt_huber` vs the median: Huber-M is a compromise between mean and median (more efficient than the median under near-Gaussian data, robust in the tails). `dt_winsorize` vs `dt_trim`: winsorize KEEPS n (capping at the bounds), trim REDUCES n (dropping the tails).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `dt_winsorize`: `values` (capped) + `lower`/`upper` (the applied bounds) + `probs` + `n_changed` (how many values changed).
- `dt_trim`: `values` (trimmed) + `trimmed_indices`/`n_trimmed` + `trimmed_mean`.
- `dt_robscale`: `values` (the robust z) + `center` (the median) + `scale` (the MAD).
- `dt_huber`: `location` + `lower`/`upper`/`conf_level` (NA without a CI).
- **Trap**: the DescTools `Winsorize` has NO `probs` argument — the wrapper computes `val = quantile(x, probs)` first (a convenience layer; confirmed live). **Trap**: `RobScale` has NO `na.rm` → an NA in the input silently gives an all-NA result (hence the hard gate).

**Sources:** DescTools reference (`Winsorize`(x, val)/`Trim`(x, trim, na.rm)/`RobScale`(x, center, scale)/`HuberM`(x, k, conf.level, ci.type)) v0.99.60 — < Huber (1964), "Robust Estimation of a Location Parameter".
### #117 Composite indicator / dimension reduction with PCA — `stats` (`c00_data_utilities/composite_index_dimensionality.py`)
**Functions:** `pca_composite` [`composite_index_dimensionality`] — PCA (SVD) over a numeric matrix of indicators → the **PC1 composite index** (scores), loadings, the share and cumulative share of variance per component, with a deterministic sign normalization; `pca_biplot_coords` [the scaling convention of `biplot.prcomp`] — the obs/var biplot coordinates (**numbers only**); `pca_predict` [`predict.prcomp`] — the projection of NEW rows with the SAME center/scale; `pca_n_components` — the **rules** for choosing the number of components (Kaiser-Guttman / cumulative variance / broken stick); `pca_stationarity_precheck` [`kpss.test`] — a **STRUCTURED** non-stationarity warning per column.

**When:** when many correlated indicators (e.g. financing conditions, sentiment, activity, sub-indices) must be condensed into **ONE** composite indicator = the first principal component (PC1), with the weights (loadings) determined data-driven from the covariance. Also for dimensionality reduction / checking how many components retain the variance (cum_var). scale=TRUE (default) is the recommended setting: with heterogeneous units, otherwise the indicator with the largest variance dominates. In addition: **biplot chart-data** (obs scores + variable arrows in the SAME scaled space) → `pca_biplot_coords`; **out-of-sample apply** (fit on train, projection of NEW rows with the SAME center/scale) → `pca_predict`; "how many components do I keep, **BY RULE**" → `pca_n_components`; **BEFORE** PCA on **TIME SERIES**: KPSS per column → `pca_stationarity_precheck`.

**When NOT:** for charts as **DRAWING** (frontend; here **ONLY** coordinates are given); for a **latent factor with dynamics / mixed frequency / missing data** → a dynamic factor model (`dynamic_factor_nowcasting`, #03 multivariate-nowcasting); when you want **transparent, a-priori weights** (equal or expert weights) instead of data-driven loadings → a standardised weighted average (#116 `panel_row_stats` / #82 macro-arithmetic); for **NON-STATIONARY series in LEVELS** → #256 pca-nonstationary (`pn_pca_nonstationary`); for the **elbow/scree as a rule** (Cattell 1966: it requires a **VISUAL** judgement → not rule-based, charter §1).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** a numeric **matrix** (NOT a DataFrame — the trap of a silent `as.matrix` character coercion), **>=2 columns**, **>=3 rows** (the N-1 divisor), **without NA/Inf/NaN** (otherwise the cryptic `svd: infinite or missing values`). With **scale=TRUE**: a hard gate that no column is constant/of zero variance (reproducing the prcomp scale factor `sqrt(sum(col_centered^2)/(n-1))==0` → an explicit stop BEFORE `cannot rescale a constant/zero column`). center/scale strictly TRUE/FALSE. **Time series:** run `pca_stationarity_precheck` first (ONLY when the input is time series — in a cross-section stationarity is not even defined).

**Alternatives + criterion:** the `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` DFM (#03) when there is a **common latent factor with dynamics/mixed frequency/gaps** (state space, not a static cross-section). `panel_row_stats` (#116) / macro-arithmetic (#82) when you want **explicit, checked weights** instead of data-driven loadings. `factanal` (factor analysis) when the target is a measurement model with error terms, not maximising explained variance. **#256 pca-nonstationary (`pn_pca_nonstationary`)** when the columns are **NON-STATIONARY** time series (KPSS rejects): there the standardization of classical PCA is **MATHEMATICALLY UNDEFINED** (Hamilton, Ma & Xi, NBER WP 32068).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `composite` = the **PC1 scores** (the composite indicator, a numeric vector of length n; names from the rownames if present). `loadings`/`scores` = matrices (→ nested rows + dimnames). `var_explained`/`cum_var` named per PC1/PC2/…; `pc1_var` = the variance share of the composite; `sdev`, `n_obs`/`n_vars`/`n_comp`, `center`/`scale`.
- **Sign trap:** the signs of the PCs are arbitrary (prcomp help Note: they differ between builds/BLAS). Here they are **normalized explicitly**: every component is flipped so that the loading with the largest |magnitude| is positive → the composite and the loadings are reproducible. Interpret the **direction** of the indicator from the loadings, not from an absolute sign.
- **Scale trap:** PC1 has no "natural" units; it is z-score-like (mean≈0). For a level/base-100 index use a separate rebase.
- **scale trap:** scale=FALSE lets the column with the largest variance dominate PC1 — use it only when the indicators are already on a common scale.
- `pca_biplot_coords`: `obs_coords` (n×2) / `var_coords` (p×2) / `lambda` (the **COMMON** scale factor) / `components` / `var_explained` — **numbers ONLY, no drawing** (charter §5).
- `pca_predict`: `scores_new` / `composite_new` / `rotation` / **`center_used`** / **`scale_used`** (fit/apply externalization — an apply reproducible **OUTSIDE** the node: `scale(new, center_used, scale_used) %*% rotation`) / `scores_train`.
- `pca_n_components`: `k_kaiser` + `kaiser_threshold` + `kaiser_basis` · `k_cum_var` + `cum_var_threshold` · `k_broken_stick` (sequential) + `k_broken_stick_any` + `broken_stick_expected` · `k_min`/`k_max`.
- `pca_stationarity_precheck`: `statistic`/`p_value`/`p_at_bound`/`trunc_lag`/`nonstationary` **PER COLUMN** · `columns_flagged`/`n_nonstationary`/`any_nonstationary`/`small_sample` · **`warning_code`/`warning_message`/`recommended_node`/`recommended_fn`/`source`** (a STRUCTURED field — **NOT** `message`, **NOT** `stop`).
- **`pca_predict` trap (silent-wrong):** `predict.prcomp` matches columns **BY NAME ONLY IF** `rownames(rotation) != NULL` (i.e. if the training matrix had colnames). **WITHOUT** colnames it checks **ONLY the number of columns** and **projects SILENTLY WRONG** when the columns are reordered (live-verified: the same input, entirely different scores) ⇒ `pca_predict` requires colnames on **BOTH** and an `identical` **ORDER**.
- **`biplot_scale` trap:** it is NOT the `scale.` of `composite_index_dimensionality` — it is the **lambda exponent** of `biplot.prcomp`. `stats` **only warns** outside [0,1]; here it is a **hard stop** (charter §5).
- **Biplot on a rank-deficient matrix trap** (a duplicate/collinear column): `sdev ≈ 1.18e-16` (**NOT exactly 0**) → `lam ≈ 0` → silently enormous obs coordinates. Gated with the documented `tol` of `the prcomp documentation`: `sqrt(.Machine.double.eps) * sdev[1]`.
- **Kaiser-Guttman trap:** "eigenvalue > 1" HOLDS **ONLY** on a **CORRELATION** matrix (scale=TRUE, the mean eigenvalue == 1). On a **COVARIANCE** matrix (scale=FALSE) the threshold is `mean(eigenvalues)` (Jolliffe 2002 §6.1.2) — hence `kaiser_threshold` + `kaiser_basis` are returned explicitly.
- **Broken-stick trap:** "ALL pass" is **MATHEMATICALLY IMPOSSIBLE** (`sum(var_explained) == sum(b_j) == 1`); `k_broken_stick` (which stops at the **FIRST** failure) and `k_broken_stick_any` **DIFFER** (e.g. on ~independent columns: k=0 but k_any=2).
- **KPSS p-value trap:** `kpss.test` gives a p-value **ONLY** in [0.01, 0.10] (interpolation in Table 1 of KPSS 1992) and warns at the bounds ⇒ `alpha` is gated to [0.01, 0.10] + `p_at_bound` per column.
- **Non-stationarity is NOT a `stop`:** the node must stay fully useful on **CROSS-SECTION** data (countries/firms), where stationarity is not even defined → a **STRUCTURED** warning, not a blocker.

**Sources:** `composite_index_dimensionality` the reference help (SVD, `sdev`/`rotation`/`x`, the "signs are arbitrary" Note, `tol = sqrt(.Machine.double.eps)`) — Venables & Ripley, *Modern Applied Statistics with S* (2002); Jolliffe, *Principal Component Analysis* (2002) §6.1.1/§6.1.2; OECD/JRC Nardo et al., *Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators* (2008, PCA weighting); `the biplot.princomp documentation` (`lam = (sdev*sqrt(n))^scale`, obs `/lam`, vars `*lam`, `pc.biplot`) & Gabriel KR (1971) *Biometrika* 58(3):453-467; the `predict.prcomp` source (`scale(newdata, center, scale) %*% rotation`, live-verified); Kaiser HF (1960) *Educ. Psychol. Meas.* 20:141-151 & Guttman L (1954); Frontier S (1976) & Jackson DA (1993) *Ecology* 74(8):2204-2214 (the broken stick `b_j = (1/p) sum_{i=j.p} 1/i`); Cattell RB (1966) — the elbow/scree is **rejected** as a rule; **Hamilton, Ma & Xi, NBER WP 32068** (for a non-stationary variable the population mean is undefined and the sample sd diverges ⇒ the PCA standardization is invalid); Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt & Shin (1992) *J. Econometrics* 54:159-178 & `the kpss.test documentation` (`lshort=TRUE` ⇒ the truncation lag `floor(4*(n/100)^0.25)`; Table 1 ⇒ `small_sample = n<30`).
