### #138 meboot (Maximum Entropy Bootstrap) — `maximum_entropy_bootstrap` (`c02_univariate_forecasting/maximum_entropy_bootstrap.py`)
**Functions:** `maximum_entropy_bootstrap` → `meb_ensemble` (an ensemble matrix of replicates; the seed is MANDATORY).

**When:** when you need bootstrap **ensemble** replicates of a time series for downstream inference / confidence bands **WITHOUT** assuming stationarity and **WITHOUT** block-length tuning. The maximum-entropy bootstrap (Vinod) produces replicates that **preserve the dependence and the non-stationarity** of the original series (sorting → an ME density per interval with a mean-preserving constraint → restoring the original order). Uses: the bootstrap distribution of a statistic/parameter, error bands around a trend/forecast, robust inference on small samples.

**When NOT:** for parametric prediction intervals from a correctly specified model → `#7 forecast` (ARIMA/ETS); for charts (the frontend draws them); for panel `pdata.frame` ensembles (colsubj/coldata/coltimes — outside the macro scope); it is not a point-forecast method (it produces DATA, not a forecast).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no formal statistical precondition (mechanical resampling — it does not require stationarity). **Hard gates:** `x` numeric/ts, finite (no NA/NaN/Inf), `length>=2` (otherwise cryptic errors: char → "non-numeric argument", NA → "NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call", n=1 → "need at least two non-NA values"); `seed` **MANDATORY** + a single finite number (stochastic); `reps>=10` and `0<=trim<0.5` — **meboot accepts them SILENTLY** (silent-wrong: reps<10 gives a useless ensemble, trim>=0.5/negative gives degenerate trimming); logical flags single and non-NA.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `#7 forecast` (`run_auto_arima`) when a well-specified parametric model exists → model-based prediction intervals instead of resampling. `force.clt=TRUE` (default) preserves the CLT in the ensemble mean; set `FALSE` for non-gaussian tails or for non-negative ensembles (trim xmin=0). `sym=TRUE` for a symmetric ME density.

**Reading the output** (via L2 `to_mcp`):
- `ensemble` — an `n x reps` matrix of replicates (`mts`/matrix → nested rows + dimnames). **The central DATA / producer field** (→ a parquet pointer for downstream nodes).
- `x` — the original series (as input); `xx` — the ordered order statistics (xx[1]=the minimum); `z` — the class-interval limits.
- `xmin`/`xmax` — the left/right tail limits; `dvtrim` — the trimmed mean of the deviations; `kappa` — the scale adjustment to the variance of the ME density.
- `n`/`reps`/`trim`/`seed` — metadata + the applied arguments (`seed` for reproducibility/caching).
- **Interpretation traps:** (1) **STOCHASTIC** — without a pinned `seed` the node is **uncacheable**; the wrapper calls `set.seed(seed)` BEFORE the draw. (2) `force.clt=TRUE` **changes** the ensemble so that the mean satisfies the CLT — it is NOT a raw resample. (3) `elaps` (elapsed time) is forced to `FALSE` and omitted (non-deterministic, it breaks caching). (4) the choice of `xmin`/`xmax` is not arbitrary — it must be cognizant of `range(x)`.

**Sources:** Vinod, H.D. (2006), "Maximum Entropy Ensembles for Time Series Inference in Economics", *Journal of Asian Economics* 17(6):955-978; Vinod, H.D. (2013), "Maximum Entropy Bootstrap Algorithm Enhancements", SSRN 2285041; Vinod & López-de-Lacalle (2009), *JSS*, "Maximum Entropy Bootstrap for Time Series: The meboot the reference Package"; the `maximum_entropy_bootstrap` reference manual (`maximum_entropy_bootstrap`) — the signature/Value live-verified.

### #134 caretForecast (recursive autoregressive ML forecasting + conformal PI) — `caretForecast` (`c02_univariate_forecasting/caretforecast.py`)
**Functions:** `ARml` → `caf_arml` (autoregressive ML via caret on lagged+fourier features + `diebold_mariano_tscv` point+PI), `conformalRegressor`/`predict` → `caf_conformal` (distribution-free conformal PI), `get_var_imp` → `caf_varimp` (variable importance).

**When:** univariate forecasting with an ML/regularized learner (ridge/lasso/elastic net via glmnet, or lm) over recursive autoregressive + fourier features, with caret resampling, without leaving univariate forecasting; `caf_conformal` for distribution-free prediction intervals (conformal, from the in-sample residuals) instead of the parametric ones; `caf_varimp` for the importance of the lags/regressors.

**When NOT:** a full/ELM NN → #133 nnfor; a classical linear/interpretable model with analytical PI → #7 forecast (auto.arima/ets); state-space ETS+ARIMA → #10 smooth; multivariate → 03; a free choice of caret learner is NOT allowed (a closed whitelist — security/cost); without a seed it is uncacheable (forbidden).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** no formal statistical precondition (ML learns non-parametrically; recursive AR + fourier). Gates: `y` a univariate **ts** with length > max_lag+1; **`seed` MANDATORY** (caret resampling/stochastic learners → without a seed it is non-deterministic/uncacheable); `caret_method` ∈ a **CLOSED whitelist {lm,glmnet,ridge,lasso}** (match.arg → an internal map to the caret method+tune_grid; NEVER a free string); `pre_process` ∈ the allowed set; `cv=FALSE` is rejected (it would require a forbidden tune_grid); `cv_horizon`/`max_lag` positive integers; `h` a positive integer; `level` ∈ (0,100); `xreg` NOT a DataFrame and nrow==n, with a future `newxreg` (nrow==h, the same columns). caf_conformal: `model` of class ARml; `confidence` ∈ (0,1); y_max>y_min. caf_varimp: `model` an ARml or a forecast.

**Alternatives + criterion:** #133 `nnf_mlp`/`nnf_elm` for a full/ELM NN (non-linearities); #7 `run_auto_arima`/`run_ets` for a linear model with analytical PI (lightweight); #10 `run_adam` for state space. Between the point PI: `caf_arml.lower/upper` = the conformal-calibrated PI of caretForecast; `caf_conformal` = explicitly distribution-free from the in-sample residuals — prefer it when you doubt gaussian intervals.

**Reading the output:**
- caf_arml `mean` — the point forecasts (a ts, recursive AR).
- `lower`/`upper` — the h×length(level) PI of forecast.ARml.
- `accuracy` — the in-sample ME/RMSE/MAE/MAPE (computed here from the residuals/fitted values).
- `model` — the whole ARml object → a **producer** (register field=`model`, bucket=rds) for caf_conformal/caf_varimp; a compact stub in `to_mcp`.
- `caret_method`/`max_lag`/`seed`/`n` — the public learner token + what was locked in (the cache key).
- caf_conformal `lower`/`upper` — the conformal bounds for `confidence`; `n_calibration` = the residuals that covered the fit.
- caf_varimp `importance` — a DataFrame of variable/overall (in descending importance).
- **Interpretation traps:** (1) the `seed` is part of the cache key — the same seed ⇒ identical output (live-verified); caret resampling is stochastic. (2) the public `caret_method` token is mapped INTERNALLY (ridge/lasso → glmnet with a fixed alpha) — it is NOT the caret method string. (3) an `xreg` at fit time requires a future `newxreg` (nrow==h) for the forecast. (4) the conformal PI are distribution-free (residual-based), NOT gaussian.

**Sources:** Akay, `caretForecast` reference (`ARml`, `forecast.ARml`, `conformalRegressor`, `predict.conformalRegressor`, `get_var_imp`); Kuhn (2008) *Building Predictive Models in the reference Using the caret Package* (JSS 28(5)); Boström (2022) *crepes: a Python Package for Generating Conformal Regressors and Predictive Systems* (PMLR 179); Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* 3e (fourier/recursive forecasting).

### #139 FCVAR (Fractionally Cointegrated VAR — Johansen-Nielsen) — `FCVAR` (`c05_cointegration/fractionally_cointegrated_var.py`)
**Functions:** `fcv_estimate` (`FCVARestn`), `fcv_rank_test` (`FCVARrankTests`), `fcv_lag_select` (`FCVARlagSelect`), `fcv_boot_rank` (`FCVARbootRank`)

**When:** you have a system of ≥2 series with **fractional integration** (I(d), d not necessarily an integer — long memory) and want **fractional cointegration**: common fractional parameters d/b, cointegrating vectors beta (`beta`) and adjustment coefficients alpha (`alpha`). FCVAR generalises the classical Johansen VECM by allowing the degree of integration d and the degree of cointegration b to be estimated (instead of assumed integer). Flow: `fcv_lag_select` (the order k) → `fcv_rank_test` (the asymptotic LR rank) → `fcv_boot_rank` (a wild-bootstrap rank on small samples) → `fcv_estimate` (the final model, a PRODUCER).

**When NOT:** if the series are purely I(1) of integer order without long memory → classical Johansen `#23 urca`/`#24 tsDyn` (simpler, standard critical values). If it is single-equation with a mixed order → ARDL bounds `#25`/`#26`. For charts (a roots plot) — omitted (frontend). The hypothesis-restriction tests (`FCVARhypoTest`) and forecasting/simulation (`FCVARforecast`/`FCVARsim`) are not implemented — a different concern.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** every series must be **fractionally integrated** — estimate d with `c02_univariate_forecasting/long_memory_fractional.fdf_gph` (GPH) or `c02_univariate_forecasting/long_memory_fractional.fdf_sperio` before choosing FCVAR over integer Johansen; confirm non-stationarity with `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` **and** the confirmatory `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test` (KPSS: H0=stationarity, **a rejection ⇒ non-stationary** — the opposite polarity to ADF). Wrapper gates: the input a matrix/DataFrame/mts with **≥2 columns and without NA**; `k`/`kmax`/`order`/`B` non-negative/positive integers; `r`,`r1`,`r2` integers in **0.p** (r>p → the cryptic "non-conformable arguments"); **`r1 < r2`** in the bootstrap (otherwise an invalid LR); `seed` **REQUIRED** in `fcv_boot_rank` (stochastic).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `#23 urca` / `#24 tsDyn` (the integer Johansen VECM — prefer them when d≈1 is an integer, with standard critical values); `#25 ARDL`/`#26 dynamac` (single-equation, a mixed order of integration); `fcv_boot_rank` over `fcv_rank_test` when the sample is small (the asymptotic p-values of the LR rank are unreliable → a wild bootstrap).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `fcv_estimate`: `d`/`b` (the fractional parameters), `beta` (the p×r normalised cointegrating vectors), `alpha` (the p×r adjustment/loading matrix), `Pi`=alpha·beta', `Gamma` (short run), `Omega` (the covariance), `mu` (the level parameters), `logLik`/`fp` (free parameters)/`SE`, `roots` (the characteristic polynomial as `re`/`im`/`mod`), `object` (an FCVAR_model — a **PRODUCER**, the input to downstream tools).
- `fcv_rank_test`: `LRstat`/`pv` vectors of length **p+1** (the i-th element ⇒ rank=i−1); read the rank bottom-up (the first H0 that is **not** rejected); `pv=999`/NA when the p-value is unavailable.
- `fcv_lag_select`: `aic`/`bic` (+ `i_aic`/`i_bic` = the selected lag), `pvWNQ`/`pvWNLM` (the white-noise tests per lag).
- `fcv_boot_rank`: `LRbs` (the B simulated LR statistics — chart-data), `LRstat` (the observed one), `pv_bs` (the bootstrap p-value = `H.pvBS`).

**Interpretation traps:** (1) the raw `opt` object (~40 fields) is **not** exposed — it is built internally from a curated surface (bounds/restrict_db/constrained/level_param/constants/grid_search). (2) `grid_search` **defaults to FALSE** (a deviation from the package default gridSearch=1); the switching optimizer converges, and the grid search is an expensive accuracy refinement — enable it if you suspect local maxima in d/b. (3) the bootstrap p-value lives in **`br$H.pvBS`** — `br.pv` returns empty (length 0). (4) FCVAR requires `r1 < r2` semantically but does **not** enforce it (a silently wrong negative LR) — the wrapper gates it. (5) a full rank `r=p` produces a singular Hessian in the SE (silenced internally); it means "no rank reduction" (stationary fractional differences).

**Sources:** Johansen & Nielsen 2012 (*Econometrica* 80:2667–2732, "Likelihood inference for a fractionally cointegrated VAR"); Nielsen & Popiel 2018 (the MATLAB→the reference port notes); Doornik 2018 (*Scand. J. Statist.* 45(2), the accelerated switching algorithm); Cavaliere, Rahbek & Taylor 2010 (*J. Econometrics* 158:7–24, the wild-bootstrap rank test); the `FCVAR` 0.1.4 reference manual (`FCVARoptions`, `FCVARestn`, `FCVARrankTests`, `FCVARlagSelect`, `FCVARbootRank`) — the signatures + output slots live-verified via the Rd and probes on `votingJNP2014`.

### #140 Nonlinear (asymmetric) ARDL — NARDL (+ PSS bounds + CUSUM) — `nonlinear_ardl_nardl` (`c05_cointegration/nonlinear_ardl_nardl.py`)
**Functions:** `nar_fit` (`nonlinear_ardl_nardl`), `nar_bounds` (`pssbounds`), `nar_stability` (CUSUM/CUSUMQ chart-data — a reproduction of the `cusum`/`cumsq` formulas)

**When:** single-equation cointegration when the relationship is **ASYMMETRIC** — the regressor acts differently on **increases** vs **decreases** (Shin-Yu-Greenwood-Nimmo 2014; the regressor is decomposed into positive/negative partial sums `x_p`/`x_n`). Regressors of mixed order I(0)/I(1) (bounds testing without pre-classification), **EXACTLY one** decomposed regressor, one dependent variable. It gives the long-run `beta+`/`beta-`, a Wald test of asymmetry (H0: `beta+ = beta-`), the PSS bounds F-test, and CUSUM/CUSUMQ parameter stability.

**When NOT:** if the relationship is **symmetric** → a linear ARDL/UECM suffices (`#25`). If **any series is I(2)** → the bounds test breaks down (it holds for I(0)/I(1) only); run the unit-root tests first. **Multiple** cointegrating relationships / a system → Johansen (`#23`/`#24`). **>1 decomposed regressor** → nardl rejects it (it accepts EXACTLY one).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** confirm that **no series is I(2)** → `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` (+ the confirmatory `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test`) on the levels and first differences. Choose the correct `case` (3 or 5). Gates: `data` a DataFrame; `y`/`x` **column names** that exist, numeric and free of NA (SECURITY: a closed formula via `reformulate` — NOT a free string); `y ≠ x`; `ic ∈ {aic,bic}`; `case ∈ {3,5}`; `maxlag` a positive integer; `object` of class `nonlinear_ardl_nardl`; `nar_stability` requires >1 recursive residuals.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `#25 ARDL` when the relationship is **symmetric** (a linear ARDL/UECM + bounds); `#26 dynamac` for stochastic counterfactual simulation + residual diagnostics; `#23`/`#24` for a system / multiple relationships.

**Reading the output:**
- `nar_fit`: `long_run` (the table of long-run coefficients `x_p`=positive / `x_n`=negative + SE/t/p), `coefficients` (the short-run ECM, including the lagged DV), `ect_coef` (the coefficient on the lagged DV — it must be **negative** for error correction), `asym_lr`/`asym_sr` (the Wald asymmetry test: `statistic`,`p.value`; `asym_lr` H0: `beta+ = beta-`), `fstat`, `orders`, `normality` (a Shapiro htest), `arch` (an Engle ARCH-LM htest), `case`/`k`/`Nobs`, `object` (the producer).
- `nar_bounds`: `statistic` (F), `bounds` (a DataFrame `level`/`I0`/`I1` for 10/5/1%), `decision`, `report` (the raw pssbounds display). **Decision:** F > the upper I(1) at 5% ⇒ cointegration; F < the lower I(0) ⇒ none; **in between ⇒ inconclusive**.
- `nar_stability`: `cusum` and `cusumq`, each with `x`/`process`/`lower`/`upper`/`breach` (numeric **chart-data**, the plot is done in the frontend). `breach=TRUE` ⇒ parameter instability (5%).
- **L2 (`to_mcp`)**: `long_run`/`bounds`/`orders` → records; the htests → atomic fields; `object` (a foreign S3 `nonlinear_ardl_nardl`) → a stub.

**Interpretation traps:** (1) the **inconclusive region** — an F between the I(0)/I(1) bounds ⇒ do **not** conclude "cointegration". (2) `case` is **ONLY 3/5** — 1/2/4 are not supported by nardl (the cryptic "object 'rhnams' not found"; the gate blocks them). (3) a **NON-significant asym_lr** ⇒ the asymmetry is NOT justified → go back to a linear ARDL `#25`. (4) the **CUSUM/CUSUMQ k/n** come from `object.sels`/`object.selresidu` (as in the graph=TRUE path of nardl), **NOT** `object.k`/`object.n` (which stay `1`/`nrow(dx)` when graph=FALSE → silently wrong bounds). (5) the `pssbounds` `k` follows the documented usage `k=fit.k` (the nardl convention).

**Sources:** Shin, Yu & Greenwood-Nimmo 2014 ("Modelling Asymmetric Cointegration and Dynamic Multipliers in a Nonlinear ARDL Framework", in the *Festschrift in Honor of Peter Schmidt*, Springer); Pesaran-Shin-Smith 2001 (*JAE* 16(3):289–326); Narayan 2005 (*Applied Economics* 37(17):1979–1990, small-sample bounds critical values); the `nonlinear_ardl_nardl` reference manual + source (`nonlinear_ardl_nardl`, `pssbounds`, `cusum`, `cumsq`) — the signatures and object slots verified via live `library(nardl)` introspection.

### #141 cointmonitoR (consistent monitoring: stationarity & cointegration) — `cointmonitoR` (`c05_cointegration/consistent_monitoring_stationarity.py`)
**Functions:** `cmo_stationarity` (`monitorStationarity`), `cmo_cointegration` (`monitorCointegration`)

**When:** when you have an **established cointegration relationship** (or a stationary series) and want to **monitor** whether it **breaks down** in a later period — that is, a transition from cointegration to a **spurious** relationship (or from stationarity to non-stationarity). The parameters are estimated **ONLY** over an initial "calibration" period `[1.floor(m·N)]` assumed to be free of breaks (Chu-Stinchcombe-White 1996); a detector statistic is computed cumulatively over the monitoring period, and when it exceeds the critical value it returns the **detection time** (the break point). `cmo_stationarity` = the 1-D special case; `cmo_cointegration` = residual-based FM-/D-/IM-OLS.

**When NOT:** for a **full-sample one-shot** test of the existence of cointegration → `#23` Johansen / `#25` ARDL bounds / `#26`. For **estimating** beta → `#27` (these are monitors, not estimators). If you **cannot** assume a break-free calibration period at the start of the sample → the precondition of the method fails. `m` is the fraction of the **calibration** period (not of the monitoring one).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** (1) I(1) series → `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` (+ the confirmatory `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test`); (2) for `cmo_cointegration`, evidence of cointegration **in the calibration period** → `c05_cointegration/johansen_restricted_vecm.wrap_ca_jo` (without a stable relationship in the calibration period the detector is invalid). Gates: `x`/`y` numeric WITHOUT NA; `y` **one-dimensional**; `nrow(x)==length(y)`; `m ∈ [0.1,0.9]`; `signif_level ∈ [0.01,0.1]`; `model ∈ {FM,D,IM}`; `kernel ∈ {ba,pa,qs,tr}`; `bandwidth ∈ {and,nw}` or a positive number; `non_parametric_trend` logical; `D_options` a list/NULL.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `cmo_stationarity` for a one-dimensional series vs `cmo_cointegration` for a relationship; the model **FM** is the default (a semiparametric LRV, Phillips-Hansen), **D** (=DOLS, leads/lags), **IM** (integrated-modified, without bandwidth tuning). For an **existence test** (not monitoring) → `c05_cointegration/johansen_restricted_vecm.wrap_ca_jo`; for **estimating beta** → `c05_cointegration/modified_ols_cointegrating.creg_fmols`.

**Reading the output:**
- `statistic` = the detector value (H_sm); `critical_value` = the critical value at `signif_level`; `detected` = **the decision** (was a break/deviation detected?); `detection_time` = the detection index (**NA** if none — the raw `time=Inf` is not exposed).
- `statistics_path` = the detector path (**NA over the calibration period**) — chart-data; `residuals` = the residuals of the modified OLS (**cointegration only**); `p_value ∈ [0.01,0.1]` (bounded, not an exact p); `calibration.fraction`/`.index` = `m.frac`/`floor(m·N)`.
- **L2 (`to_mcp`)**: the atomic fields → JSON scalars; `statistics_path`/`residuals` → numeric arrays; `.object` (an S3 `cointmonitoR`) → a stub.

**Interpretation traps:** (1) `m` = the **calibration** fraction ∈ [0.1,0.9]; the last calibration observation = `floor(m·N)`; a bad/break-containing calibration invalidates the whole procedure. (2) `p_value` is **bounded to [0.01,0.1]** (0.1 = far from rejection, 0.01 = a strong rejection) — NOT an exact p-value. (3) `detected=FALSE`/`detection_time=NA` (the raw `time=Inf`) means **no break** — not an error. (4) `model="D"` = Dynamic OLS (=DOLS); `"IM"` = Integrated-Modified — the package has NO `"DOLS"`/`"CCR"` token. (5) Silent-wrong: a multi-column `y` / NA / a length mismatch give **only a WARNING + garbage** in the raw package — hard-gated here. (6) Fully **deterministic** (no RNG) — reproducible without a seed.

**Sources:** Wagner & Wied 2015 (*Monitoring Stationarity and Cointegration*, a Discussion Paper, DOI:10.2139/ssrn.2624657); Chu, Stinchcombe & White 1996 (*Econometrica* 64:1045–1065, monitoring structural change); Phillips-Hansen 1990 (FM-OLS, *RES* 57:99–125); Stock-Watson 1993 (D-OLS, *Econometrica*); Vogelsang-Wagner 2014 (IM-OLS, *J. Econometrics*); Andrews 1991 & Newey-West 1994 (bandwidth); the `cointmonitoR` reference manual (`monitorStationarity`/`monitorCointegration`) — the args, value fields, `floor(m·N)` and `p∈[0.01,0.1]` confirmed via the help page + live introspection.

### #142 High-dimensional penalized VAR (structured penalties + rolling CV) — `BigVAR` (`c03_multivariate_nowcasting/high_dimensional_penalized.py`)
**Functions:** `bvr_fit` (`constructModel` + `cv.BigVAR` → `BigVAR.results`, a producer), `bvr_predict` (`predict` — an `n.ahead x k` path + an optional 95% CI), `bvr_coef` (`coef` — the sparse coefficient matrix `k x kp+1`).

**When:** a multivariate VAR where `k` (or `k·p`) is **large relative to `T`** and an OLS VAR/`reduced_form_var` overfits — BigVAR imposes a **structured penalty (VARX-L / HLAG)** and selects the shrinkage strength `lambda` by **rolling out-of-sample cross-validation** (a structurally controlled selection, not an in-sample fit). The structure is chosen per question: `Basic`/`BasicEN` (element-wise Lasso/EN), `Lag`/`SparseLag` (grouping per lag), `OwnOther`/`SparseOO` (own vs cross lags), `HLAGC/HLAGOO/HLAGELEM` (hierarchical lag-order selection — a data-driven `p`), `Tapered` (lag-weighted), `BGR` (Bayesian ridge).

**When NOT:** a short/medium sample where a Minnesota-prior BVAR is more natural and gives posterior fan charts (→ `BVAR` #12); you want frequentist Granger/IRF/diagnostics (→ `reduced_form_var` #11); a very large `n` with common dynamics → a factor model (→ `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` #15); mixed frequency (→ `mixed_frequency_bayesian`).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Stationarity — methodological.** BigVAR fits a reduced-form VAR-L that **shrinks towards ZERO** (the default `MN=FALSE`, NOT a random-walk prior as in `BVAR`). So apply it to **STATIONARY data** — difference the I(1) series **first** (the opposite guidance to `BVAR` #12, which wants levels). Test the order of integration → `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` (+ the confirmatory `run_kpss_test`). If they are I(1) and cointegrated → consider a VECM (`c05_cointegration/johansen_restricted_vecm.ca.jo`).
- **Hard gates (project):** `Y` a numeric matrix/df/ts, `ncol>=2`, without NA, `nrow > p+1`; `p`/`h` positive integers; `struct`/`cv` via `match.arg`; `gran` = two positive integers `c(grid_depth, number_of_lambdas)`; `T1`/`T2` (if supplied) positive integers with `p < T1 < T2 <= nrow(Y)`. Too few rows for the rolling CV window → a clean `stop` (the estimator error is wrapped, "too few rows for rolling validation").
- **Determinism:** penalized (convex) + rolling/LOO CV = **DETERMINISTIC** — no MCMC/sampling, **no seed**.

**Alternatives + criterion:**

| Alternative | When it is preferred |
|---|---|
| `BVAR` (#12) | a short sample, you want Bayesian shrinkage in LEVELS + posterior fan charts |
| `reduced_form_var` (#11) | `k·p` small, you want frequentist Granger/IRF/diagnostics and p-values |
| `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` (#15) | a very large `n` with a few common factors (a factor structure) |

**Reading the output:**
- `bvr_fit`: `optimal_lambda` (the optimal `lambda` minimising the in-sample MSFE); `in_sample_msfe` / `oos_msfe` (the OOS MSFE on the test set — compare it with the mean/RW/AIC/BIC benchmarks); `sparsity` (the share of coefficients set to zero); `coefficients` = the `k x (kp+1)` sparse matrix (`intercept` + `Y{i}L{l}`); `model` (a BigVAR.results) → the producer handle.
- `bvr_predict`: `diebold_mariano_tscv` = an `n.ahead x k` **path** (built step by step; `predict.BigVAR.results` on its own returns only the final horizon); `confint=TRUE` → `lower`/`upper` 95% CI of the same dimensions.
- `bvr_coef`: `coefficients` + `n_zero`/`n_nonzero`/`sparsity` (the penalized-out structure).
- **Trap (names):** BigVAR **discards** `colnames(Y)`; the variables are named `Y1.Yk` (position = column order) consistently across fit/predict/coef — map the positions in the frontend.
- **Trap (struct):** `EFX` applies ONLY to a VARX (a pure VAR → a clean `stop`); `HLAG*`/`Tapered` are VAR-only. `MCP`/`SCAD` (non-convex) are out of scope (not exposed).
- **Collision trap (implementation):** BigVAR calls `setGeneric` on `predict`/`coef` (S4); the wrapper calls `selectMethod(g, "BigVAR.results")` explicitly — `conflicts(detail=TRUE)` is empty, with no effect on the sibling S3 `predict`/`coef`.

**Sources:** BigVAR 1.1.5 reference/vignette; Nicholson, Wilms, Bien & Matteson (2020) *High-dimensional forecasting via interpretable VAR*, JMLR 21(166); Nicholson, Matteson & Bien (2017) *VARX-L*, Int. J. Forecasting 33(3):627-651; Banbura-Giannone-Reichlin (2010) (BGR).

### #144 Sparse Dynamic Factor Model — `sparseDFM` (`c03_multivariate_nowcasting/sparse_dynamic_factor.py`)
**Functions:** `sdf_fit` [`sparseDFM`], `sdf_predict` [`predict.sparseDFM`], `sdf_factors` [factor-path extraction]

**When:** large-panel nowcasting when you want **interpretable** factors with **sparse loadings** — the sparse EM applies a LASSO penalty to the loading matrix Lambda (a BIC-optimal alpha) so that each factor loads on only a subset of the series. It handles **arbitrary missing-data patterns / a ragged edge** (mixed publication dates) via the Kalman EM (Banbura & Modugno 2014) and also returns the **imputed** panel. `method` selects: `PCA` (static, Stock-Watson), `2Stage` (PCA+Kalman, Doz et al.), `EM` (dense QML), `EM-sparse` (the novel LASSO). `err='AR1'` for autocorrelated idiosyncratic errors.

**When NOT:** for a **dense** (non-sparse) DFM with Bai & Ng IC selection of r and mixed frequency (monthly/quarterly with an explicit quarterly.vars) → `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` #15; for a full **Bayesian** mixed-frequency nowcast with credible bands → `mixed_frequency_bayesian` #17; for non-stationary data (difference/detrend first); for charts (`plot`/`missing_data_plot`/the `summary` console → the JS frontend); **forecasting with `err='AR1'`** is not supported (the upstream predict breaks — a structural blocker in sdf_predict).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** the data must be **stationary** (the DFM is estimated on stationary series) → confirm with ADF/KPSS first. Gates: X a numeric matrix/df/ts, ncol>=2, nrow>=10 (NA are allowed); `r` a positive integer with **1 <= r < ncol(X)**; `q` a non-negative integer < ncol; `method`/`err` via match.arg; `alpha` (if supplied) finite and non-negative; `sdf_predict`: h a positive integer + a **hard block for err='AR1'**; a class check for 'sparseDFM'.

**Alternatives + criterion:** `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` #15 (`df_dfm`) when you want **dense** loadings + automatic Bai & Ng factor selection + explicit mixed frequency (quarterly.vars); `mixed_frequency_bayesian` #17 (`mf_estimate`) for a **Bayesian** nowcast with posterior uncertainty; `sdf_predict` (self) for an h-step nowcast from the same fit. Prefer `sparseDFM` when the target is **sparse/interpretable** loadings on a large panel with missing data.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `sdf_fit`: `factors` (n x r), `loadings` (the p x r Lambda — zeros = a series irrelevant to the factor under EM-sparse), `var_explained`/`var_explained_cum` (the share of variance from the eigen decomposition), `fitted` (the n x p common component, on the original scale), `imputed` (X.bal with interpolated NA — the nowcast panel), `transition`/`Sigma_u`/`Sigma_epsilon`, `converged`/`loglik`/`num_iter`/`alpha_opt`, `na_count`.
- `sdf_predict`: `X_hat` (the h x p nowcast, in the original units with the columns = the varnames), `F_hat` (the h x r factor forecasts).
- `sdf_factors`: `factors` (n x r, the columns F1.Fr) + `factors_cov` (the r x r x n uncertainty).
- **`err='AR1'` trap**: the fit is valid but forecasting is impossible (a package limitation) — sdf_predict blocks it cleanly.
- **`method='PCA'/'2Stage'` trap**: no EM is run → `converged`/`loglik`/`num_iter`/`alpha_opt` = NA (NOT an error).

**Sources:** Mosley, Chan & Gibberd (2023), "sparseDFM: An the reference Package to Estimate Dynamic Factor Models with Sparse Loadings" (arXiv:2303.14125); Banbura & Modugno (2014, J. Appl. Econometrics 29:133-160, EM with arbitrary missing data); Doz, Giannone & Reichlin (2011, J. Econometrics 164:188-205, the two-step method); Bai & Ng (2002, Econometrica 70:191-221, the IC for r); sparseDFM 1.0 reference (`sparseDFM`, `predict.sparseDFM`).

### #145 High-dimensional mixed-frequency regression (MIDAS-ML sparse-group LASSO) — `high_dimensional_mixed` (`c03_multivariate_nowcasting/high_dimensional_mixed.py`)
**Functions:** `mml_fit` [`sglfit` + the `lb`/`gb` MIDAS basis], `mml_cv` [`cv.sglfit` — k-fold tuning of lambda], `mml_predict` [`predict.sglpath` / `predict.cv.sglfit` via `getS3method`]

**When:** when you forecast/nowcast one **low-frequency** variable (e.g. quarterly GDP) from **many high-frequency** indicators with many lags each, and want **automatic variable selection + regularization** instead of a manual specification. Each high-frequency predictor (a group) with `jmax` lags is projected onto a few orthonormal polynomial bases (Legendre `lb` or Gegenbauer `gb`, `degree+1` functions) and the **sparse-group LASSO** (Babii-Ghysels-Striaukas) performs group selection (which predictors) and within-group sparsity simultaneously. `gamma` controls the mix (0 = group LASSO, 1 = LASSO); `lambda` the overall penalty (tune it with `mml_cv`).

**When NOT:** for **few** high-frequency regressors with an interpretable weight shape (a structural weight function, nls) → `midas_regression` #18 (low-dimensional parametric MIDAS); when the predictor block is better summarised by **latent common factors** (a large n, nowcasting through a factor structure) → `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` #15 / `sparseDFM`; for a **Bayesian mixed-frequency VAR** with latent monthly states → `mixed_frequency_bayesian` #17; for a same-frequency high-dimensional VAR → `BigVAR`. It is not a multi-equation/IRF tool (a single low-frequency target).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** aligned mixed-frequency data — `length(y) == nrow(X)` is a **hard gate** (a misalignment = an error), `X`/`y` free of NA/NaN/Inf (`.mml_as_matrix`/`.mml_check_y`), `nrow >= 5`. `group` one label per column (`length == ncol(X)`), without NA. For a weighted basis: every group must have `jmax >= degree+1` (a well-posed orthonormal basis, otherwise rank-deficient). `degree` a non-negative integer; `gamma ∈ [0,1]`; `weight ∈ {legendre,gegenbauer,none}` (`match.arg`); `lambda` (if supplied) positive numbers; `mml_cv`: `nfolds ∈ 3.nrow`, `seed` a positive integer. **Stationarity**: for valid regression inference, run a unit-root test on the target/predictors first (ADF/KPSS, cat. 01).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `midas_regression` (#18) when you have **few** high-frequency regressors and want the **interpretable weight shape theta** (parametric, not sparse selection); `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` (#15) when the number of indicators is large and a **factor structure** summarises them better than sparse selection; `mml_cv` is always preferable to a bare `mml_fit` lambda path for a **principled choice of lambda** (lam.min / lam.1se) instead of the path default (the smallest lambda).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `mml_fit`: `model` (an 'mml_model' producer — an opaque handle, register `field=model` bucket `rds`); `beta` = the (`n_basis` x `nlambda`) coefficients of the **basis** per lambda (NOT per original lag — they live in the space of the Legendre/Gegenbauer functions); `lambda`/`df` (the non-zero counts per lambda); `intercept` (a vector per lambda); `n_groups`/`n_basis`/`gamma`/`degree`/`weight`/`s_default`.
- `mml_cv`: `lambda_min` (which minimises the CV error) and `lambda_1se` (more parsimonious, the 1-SE rule); `cvm`/`cvsd`/`cvupper`/`cvlower` (the CV curve, chart-data); `nzero` (the non-zero counts per lambda); `beta_min`/`beta_1se` + `intercept_min`/`intercept_1se`; `seed` (NA if none was supplied).
- `mml_predict`: `fitted` (length == `nrow(newx)`), `s`, `kind`.
- **Interpretation traps**: (1) the `newx` in `mml_predict` is the **RAW high-frequency block** (the same `group`/`ncol` as at fit time); the wrapper applies the **SAME** MIDAS transform internally — do not pass a pre-transformed design. (2) `beta` is in **basis** coefficients, not per-lag weights; the per-lag weight shape is recovered as `Psi %*% beta_group`. (3) `mml_fit` (a convex block-coordinate descent) is **DETERMINISTIC** (no seed); `mml_cv` uses a **random** fold partition → it **requires a seed** for reproducibility/caching (without one, `lambda_min` fluctuates). (4) `s` for a path model is a numeric lambda (the default = the smallest lambda = the richest model); for a cv model it is `lam.min`/`lam.1se`.

**Sources:** the midasml 0.1.11 reference manual (`sglfit`, `cv.sglfit`, `lb`, `gb`, `predict.sglpath`, `predict.cv.sglfit`) — Babii, Ghysels & Striaukas, "Machine Learning Time Series Regressions With an Application to Nowcasting", *Journal of Business & Economic Statistics* 40(3):1094-1106, 2022 <https://doi.org/10.1080/07350015.2021.1899933>; Babii, Ghysels & Striaukas 2021 (the sparse-group LASSO with dependent/heteroskedastic data); <

### #143 Hierarchical global-local shrinkage BVAR + stochastic volatility — `bayesianVARs` (`c03_multivariate_nowcasting/hierarchical_global_local.py`)
**Functions:** `bvs_estimate` (`specify_prior_phi` + `bayesian_var` → a `bayesianVARs_bvar`, a **producer** + a convergence gate), `bvs_predict` (`predict` — a posterior predictive fan chart + the **LPL** log predictive likelihood), `bvs_irf` (`irf` — reduced-form impulse responses, the posterior median + bands).

**When:** a multivariate BVAR (small to medium `k`) where you want **global-local shrinkage** that **adapts automatically between sparse and dense** to the data (Horseshoe/DL/R2D2/NG/SSVS/normal on Phi) **together with stochastic volatility** (a factor-SV Sigma). It gives the full posterior: the median/quantiles of the coefficients, predictive **fan charts** and the **predictive density** (the LPL for density-forecast model comparison). The right tool when the question is "how much shrinkage?" and you want the prior to decide it data-driven instead of a fixed Minnesota tightness.

**When NOT:** a pure **Minnesota random-walk prior in LEVELS** + a complete IRF/FEVD/companion toolkit → `BVAR` #12; a penalized **frequentist** high-dimensional VAR with rolling CV (no posterior) → `BigVAR` #142; **time-varying coefficients** (TVP) with SV → `tvp_var_stochastic`; a mixed-frequency Bayesian nowcast → `mixed_frequency_bayesian` #17; a very large `n` with a factor structure → `dynamic_factor_nowcasting` #15 / `sparseDFM` #144; **structural identification** (sign/zero restrictions, structural IRF/FEVD) → `04-structural-shocks` (`bvs_irf` here is **reduced-form** only).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Stationarity — methodological.** `specify_prior_phi` has `priormean=0` (the default) → it shrinks the coefficients **towards ZERO** (like `BigVAR` #142, NOT a random-walk prior in levels as in `BVAR` #12). Apply it to **STATIONARY / growth data** (the package's usmacro_growth is growth rates); difference the I(1) series **first**. Test the order of integration → `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` (+ the confirmatory `run_kpss_test`).
- **Hard gates (project):** `data` a numeric matrix/df/ts, `ncol>=2`, without NA/Inf, `nrow > lags+1`; `lags`/`draws`/`thin` positive integers, `burnin`/`min_draws` non-negative, `thin<=draws`; `prior`/`sv_keep` via `match.arg`; `ess_min>0`; `seed` **MANDATORY** (`bayesian_var` is stochastic and has NO seed argument → `set.seed` before the sampling); `predict`: `ahead>0`, `quantiles ∈ (0,1)`, a mandatory `seed`, `LPL=TRUE ⇒ Y_obs [ahead x M]`; `irf`: `ahead>0`, `quantiles ∈ (0,1)`; a class check for `'bayesianVARs_bvar'`.
- **Convergence gate (single chain).** `bayesian_var` runs **one chain** → there is NO between-chain split-Rhat. The gate blocks (unless `allow_nonconvergence=TRUE`, mirroring `general_bayesian_inference`/`MARSS`): retained draws `< min_draws`; the minimum ESS of Phi `< ess_min`; AND **DEGENERACY as non-convergence** — an all-NA ESS (a stuck/constant sampler), a non-finite posterior Phi, `0 stable draws` (`stable_bvar`).

**Alternatives + criterion:**

| Alternative | When it is preferred |
|---|---|
| `BVAR` (#12) `bvar_estimate` | a Minnesota RW prior in LEVELS + a ready IRF/FEVD/companion/sign-restrictions toolkit |
| `BigVAR` (#142) `bvr_fit` | a frequentist penalized VAR-L, rolling-OOS lambda, deterministic (no posterior) |
| `tvp_var_stochastic` `sv_estimate` | **time-varying** coefficients (a TVP-VAR) + SV |
| `bvs_irf` | a reduced-form posterior IRF from the same fit |

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `bvs_estimate`: `phi_median` (the posterior median Phi, `K x M`), `phi_quantiles` (an `nq x K x M` grid; 2.5/25/50/75/97.5%), `convergence` (`n_retained`/`min_ess`/`n_stable`/`phi_finite`/`min_draws`/`ess_min`/`seed`), `converged`/`nonconvergence_reasons`, `model` (a `bayesianVARs_bvar`) → the **producer** handle.
- `bvs_predict`: `quants` (an `nq x horizon x M` predictive fan grid), `mean` (`horizon x M`), `horizons`/`variables`; `LPL=TRUE` → `LPL` (the joint log predictive likelihood per horizon) + `LPL_univariate` (`horizon x M`).
- `bvs_irf`: `irf_median` (`M x shocks x horizon`), `irf_quantiles` (`nq x M x shocks x horizon`), `horizon` (`t=0.t=ahead`).
- **Trap (single chain):** there is NO split-Rhat — non-convergence is detected from sufficient retained/stable draws + **degeneracy** (ESS=NA when the sampler is stuck; live-verified with a constant column). Do not read a low ESS on TINY draws as an error — raise `draws`.
- **Trap (masking):** `library(bayesianVARs)` is NOT called — it exports the generics `bayesian_var`/`irf`, which mask the `BVAR`/`reduced_form_var` siblings in the shared `source` env; all calls are `that package's exports`. The class `'bayesianVARs_bvar'` is **unique** (≠ `'bvar'`) → the S3 dispatch does not clash.
- **Trap (LPL):** `Y_obs` must be the `[ahead x M]` realised values; a wrong dimension → a silent recycling warning upstream (the wrapper blocks it with a hard gate).
- **Trap (structural):** `bvs_irf` is **reduced-form** (dim shocks=1, no orthogonalization) — for structural shocks see `04-structural-shocks`.

**Sources:** bayesianVARs 0.1.8 reference (`specify_prior_phi`, `bayesian_var`, `predict.bayesianVARs_bvar`, `irf`, `stable_bvar`, `summary.bayesianVARs_bvar`); Gruber & Kastner (2023) *Forecasting macroeconomic data with Bayesian VARs: Sparse or dense? It depends!* (arXiv:2206.04902); Kastner & Frühwirth-Schnatter (2014) ASIS/interweaving for SV; Vehtari et al. (2021, Bayesian Analysis 16(2):667-718) rank-normalized ESS diagnostics.
### #146 Time-Varying-Parameter VAR-SV with dynamic global-local shrinkage — `shrinkTVPVAR` (`c03_multivariate_nowcasting/time_varying_parameter.py`)
**Functions:** `stv_estimate` [`shrinkTVPVAR` — the MCMC posterior of the time-varying VAR coefficients, a producer], `stv_forecast` [`forecast_shrinkTVPVAR` — a posterior predictive fan grid], `stv_tvp` [extracting the time-varying coefficient paths of one equation as posterior bands over time]

**When:** a multivariate VAR (k≥2) where the relationships **evolve smoothly over time** (time-varying coefficients, a component-wise random walk) **AND** the volatility changes (stochastic volatility), but many coefficients are in practice 0/constant — the **dynamic shrinkage** (triple/double gamma) selects automatically which are genuinely time-varying (Cadonna-Frühwirth-Schnatter-Knaus 2020). A classic macro case: changing monetary transmission, structural change without explicit breakpoints. `mod_type ∈ {double (default), triple, ridge}`.

**When NOT:** constant (time-invariant) coefficients suffice → BVAR #12 / vars #11; a TVP-VAR-SV with an **explicit Cholesky identification + structural IRFs** (Primiceri) without automatic variable selection → `tvp_var_stochastic` #14; a single-equation TVP regression (not a VAR) → `shrinkTVP`; high dimension with a penalized point estimate → BigVAR #142; nowcasting with an arbitrary missing panel → sparseDFM #144.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** a multivariate numeric series (an mts, k≥2, without NA/Inf, nrow>p+1). The stationarity/scale of the series is checked externally — `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` (+ the confirmatory `run_kpss_test`). Gates: k≥2, p≥1, `mod_type` an enum, `nburn ≤ niter-2`, `nthin ≤ niter-nburn`, a **MANDATORY seed** (an integer), `ess_min>0`. **Convergence gate** (mirroring rstan/MARSS): single chain → no split-Rhat; the minimum ESS (`effectiveSize`) is computed on the `beta_mean` draws **ignoring** coefficients shrunk to a constant (legitimate shrinkage). A degenerate all-NA ESS (every parameter constant → a stuck sampler) or `retained<min_draws` or `min_ess<ess_min` ⇒ **non-convergence** (a hard stop, overridable only with `allow_nonconvergence=TRUE`).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `tvp_var_stochastic` #14 when you need structural identification/IRF (Primiceri) without selection; `BVAR` #12 when the coefficients are plausibly constant (cheaper, IRF/FEVD ready); `mod_type=triple` for more aggressive sparsity, `ridge` for shrinkage without selection.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `stv_estimate`: `model` (the producer handle, register field='model' → the R2 rds), `converged`/`min_ess`/`retained_draws`/`n_varying_params` (the convergence gate), `variables`/`n_vars`/`p`/`mod_type`/`const`/`seed`.
- `stv_forecast`: `quants` = a named list per variable, each `[probs × horizon]` a posterior predictive **fan** + `mean` `[vars × horizon]` + `probs`/`horizon`.
- `stv_tvp`: `paths` = a named list per coefficient `L<lag>.<var>` **and** `intercept`, each `[probs × time]` posterior bands — **the time-varying paths** of the lagged loadings in the target equation; + `coefficients`/`time`/`variable`.
- **SV/knob trap:** the SV is **intrinsic** (it is always a TVP-VAR-SV); **there is no sv toggle** — the only shrinkage knob is `mod_type`. **Only** the VAR-coefficient draws are returned (not those of the variance-covariance).
- **Convergence trap:** the `min_ess` default (10) is a **floor** for tiny-draw development; production (niter≥5000) must raise `ess_min` (≥200).
- **`stv_tvp` trap:** `equation` = the index of the **target** equation (the response), not of the impulse.

**Sources:** Cadonna, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Knaus (2020), "Triple the Gamma—A Unifying Shrinkage Prior for Variance and Variable Selection in Sparse State Space and TVP Models", *Econometrics* 8(2):20 <doi:10.3390/econometrics8020020>; Knaus, Bitto-Nemling, Cadonna & Frühwirth-Schnatter (2021), "Shrinkage in the TVP Model Framework Using the reference Package shrinkTVP", *JSS* 100(13) <doi:10.18637/jss.v100.i13>; the `shrinkTVPVAR` reference (`shrinkTVPVAR`, `forecast_shrinkTVPVAR`) + live introspection.

### #147 Bayesian VAR & VHAR (Minnesota conjugate / SSVS / Horseshoe + a posterior forecast fan) — `bayesian_var_vhar` (`c03_multivariate_nowcasting/bayesian_var_vhar.py`)
**Functions:** `bvh_var` [`bvar_minnesota`(analytic NIW) / `var_bayes`+`set_bvar`/`set_ssvs`/`set_horseshoe`+`set_ldlt`(MCMC)], `bvh_vhar` [`bvhar_minnesota` / `vhar_bayes`+`set_bvhar`], `bvh_predict` [`predict.bvarmn`/`.bvharmn` (analytical) · `predict.bvarldlt`/`.bvharldlt` (MCMC)]

**When:** multivariate Bayesian dynamics with a shrinkage prior when the system has many variables/lags relative to the sample (over-parameterization) and the frequentist VAR (#11 vars) becomes unstable. `bvh_var` = a Bayesian VAR; `bvh_vhar` = a Vector **Heterogeneous** AR (Corsi-type long memory: day/week/month `har=c(5,22)` components) — prefer it for series with multi-scale persistence (e.g. realized volatility, daily macro-financial data). Three priors: **minnesota** (a conjugate Normal-inverse-Wishart, ANALYTICAL closed form — fast, no MCMC, no convergence issue), **ssvs** (stochastic search variable selection) and **horseshoe** (global-local shrinkage) — both MCMC/Gibbs for explicit sparsity/variable selection.

**When NOT:** frequentist Granger/diagnostics with a sufficient sample → #11 vars; a simple hierarchical BVAR without VHAR/SSVS/HS → #12 BVAR (GLP); an explicit Gibbs sampler + gir/sir IRF types → #13 bvartools; TVP/stochastic volatility → #14 bvarsv; mixed frequency/nowcasting → #15 mfbvar/#16 dfms; structural shocks (IRF/FEVD identification) → a separate structural step (bvhar exposes `irf.bvarldlt`/`fevd` BUT they are omitted here — they belong to 04-structural-shocks).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** numeric multivariate data (>=2 columns), finite (no NA/Inf); `nrow > order_max+1` (VAR: p; VHAR: max(har)=22 → nrow>23; too few obs = a cryptic **Eigen assertion** in C++, gated explicitly, and `.bvh_call` converts every residual Eigen error into a clean stop). Stationarity/order of integration: ADF/KPSS confirmatory — the Minnesota prior handles unit roots (a random-walk prior), but check for I(2). **MCMC (ssvs/horseshoe):** `seed` MANDATORY (the reference RNG drives the Gibbs sampler); `num_chains>=2` for a valid split-Rhat.

**Convergence gate (MCMC only; mirroring #68 rstan / MARSS):** the draws are stored as a `draws_df` (`fit.param`); we compute `summarise_draws(rhat, ess_bulk)` and BLOCK before non-convergence escapes — **DEGENERACY** (num_chains<2 · ALL Rhat NA) → NON-convergence; `max(Rhat)>rhat_max` (default 1.1) · `min(Bulk_ESS)<ess_min` (default 100). A non-converged result is returned ONLY with `allow_nonconvergence=TRUE` (converged=FALSE + reasons); otherwise it stops. Analytic Minnesota: converged=TRUE (closed form). **Note:** the tiny defaults (num_iter=200) often do NOT meet the strict thresholds — the gate blocks conservatively; the user raises num_iter or overrides.

**Alternatives + criterion:** #12 BVAR — a hierarchical GLP Minnesota without SSVS/HS/VHAR (if classical shrinkage suffices); #13 bvartools — an explicit Gibbs sampler + gir/sir IRF; #14 bvarsv — time-varying parameters + stochastic volatility; #11 vars — frequentist when the sample suffices.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `bvh_var`/`bvh_vhar`: `model` (a producer; register field=model, bucket=rds), `coefficients` (the posterior mean, K×m; VAR rownames a_lag1. / VHAR a_day,a_week,a_month,const), `pip` (the posterior inclusion probability — ssvs/horseshoe ONLY), `converged`/`max_rhat`/`min_ess`/`nonconvergence_reasons`, `prior`/`kind`/`n_vars`/`is_mcmc`.
- `bvh_predict`: `diebold_mariano_tscv` [n_ahead×m] point forecasts + the pointwise `lower`/`upper`/`se` (credible bands); `draws` (the MCMC predictive draws) + `lower_joint`/`upper_joint` where available; `n_ahead`/`level`.
- **Trap:** `level` = the **significance level** (0.05 → a 95% interval), NOT a confidence level. `sparse=TRUE` uses the SAVS-sparsified coefficients (MCMC only).

**Sources:** bvhar reference/vignettes (`var_bayes`, `vhar_bayes`, `bvar_minnesota`, `bvhar_minnesota`, `set_bvar`/`set_ssvs`/`set_horseshoe`/`set_ldlt`, `predict.*`) — Kim & Baek, "bvhar: Bayesian Vector Heterogeneous Autoregression" (<); Corsi 2009 (HAR-RV, JFE); George-Sun-Ni 2008 (SSVS for VAR, J.Econometrics); Carvalho-Polson-Scott 2010 (the horseshoe); Vehtari et al. 2021 (rank-normalized split-Rhat + Bulk/Tail-ESS, Bayesian Analysis).

### #150 Smooth-Transition / threshold STRUCTURAL VAR (nonlinear, regime-dependent dynamics + GIRF/GFEVD/linear IRF) — `smooth_transition_threshold` (`c04_structural_shocks/smooth_transition_threshold.py`)
**Functions:** `sst_fit` (a 2-phase GA + optim ML estimation → a producer 'stvar'); `sst_girf` (a generalized IRF, simulation-based); `sst_gfevd` (a generalized FEVD); `sst_linear_irf` (a linear IRF per regime)

**When:** you have a multivariate series (d≥2) where the **dynamics change by regime** (e.g. recession vs expansion, high vs low volatility, a monetary regime) — the relationships transition *smoothly* (smooth transition) or *abruptly* (threshold) between M regimes. You want regime-dependent impulse responses (a GIRF) that depend on the history/state, a generalized FEVD, or the linear IRF of a specific regime. The transition weights are chosen with `weight_function`: `relative_dens` (Gaussian weighted densities), `logistic`/`exponential` (M=2, one switching variable+lag), `mlogit` (several switching variables), `threshold` (abrupt), `exogenous` (exogenous weights).
**When NOT:** linear/time-invariant dynamics suffice → a reduced-form `reduced_form_var` (#11) or a Bayesian VAR (#12); **smooth** temporal variation of the coefficients WITHOUT discrete regimes → a TVP-VAR-SV (`shrinkTVPVAR` #146, `tvp_var_stochastic` #14); linear structural identification of shocks in ONE regime → `driven_svar_identification` (#20)/`SVAR` (#19). Fully structural non-Gaussian ID → `fitSSTVAR` (a separate step, outside the surface).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `data`: a multivariate numeric `matrix`/`ts` (**d≥2**), **without NA/Inf** (a gate in the wrapper).
- The stationarity of the inputs → `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` (+ `run_kpss_test`).
- Evidence of **non-linearity/regime switching** (otherwise prefer a linear VAR) → `c01_preparation_prechecks/linearity_battery_linearity.nlt_nonlinearity`.
- `weight_function='relative_dens'` → **only** `cond_dist='Gaussian'`; `logistic`/`exponential` → **M=2**; a non-`relative_dens` choice → `weightfun_pars` is mandatory. Gates in the wrapper.
- Stochastic (GA + simulation) → a **mandatory `seed`** (`sst_fit`/`sst_girf`/`sst_gfevd`).

**Alternatives + criterion:**

| Alternative | When it is preferred |
|---|---|
| `c03_multivariate_nowcasting/reduced_form_var.vr_var` #11 | linear/time-invariant dynamics suffice (there are no regimes) |
| `c03_multivariate_nowcasting/time_varying_parameter.stv_estimate` #146 | smooth *continuous* temporal variation of the coefficients (NOT discrete regimes) + SV |
| `c04_structural_shocks/driven_svar_identification.svar_id_chol` #20 | a linear structural VAR — data-driven shock identification in one regime |
| `sst_girf` vs `sst_linear_irf` | a regime-/state-dependent (nonlinear) IRF versus the linear IRF of one fixed regime |

**Reading the output:**
- `sst_fit`: `model` = the fitted `'stvar'` object (the producer handle → it feeds the analysis functions); `loglik`, `IC` (AIC/HQIC/BIC), `params`, `transition_weights` ((T-p)×M — the estimated probability of each regime over time, chart-data), `identification` (`reduced_form` when no structural ID is imposed), `p`/`M`/`d`.
- `sst_girf`: `girf` = a named list per shock, each with `point_est` [(N+1) × (d+M-1)] + `conf_ints` — the regime-dependent generalized responses (row 1 = the impact at n=0).
- `sst_gfevd`: `gfevd` = a 3D array [horizon × variable × shock] (plus a transition-weight component) — the generalized variance decomposition.
- `sst_linear_irf`: `point_est` = a 3D array [variables × shock × horizon] (slice 1 = the impact); `conf_ints` = the wild-bootstrap bands or `NULL`.

*Interpretation traps:* (1) **the GIRF is non-linear and non-symmetric** — the response depends on the size/sign of the shock AND on the initial state (init_regime); it is not read like a linear IRF. (2) `linear_IRF`/`GIRF` on a **reduced-form** model → an automatic **lower-triangular recursive (Cholesky)** identification (the variable order matters); for a structural ID without an ordering you need the non-Gaussian `fitSSTVAR`. (3) the `linear_IRF` bootstrap `ci` gives bands **only** for models with linear AR dynamics — for a genuinely regime-dependent STVAR it returns `conf_ints=NULL` (use the GIRF). (4) **Stochasticity**: the GA log-likelihood is multimodal — a small `nrounds`/`ngen` (the defaults are TINY) may land on a local maximum; production runs must raise `nrounds`/`ngen`. Without a `seed` it is not reproducible. (5) `sst_fit` **filters out** "inappropriate" solutions (a near-singular Sigma, modulus>0.9985); if no "appropriate" solution is found, the series need rescaling or more rounds.
**S3 collision:** `smooth_transition_threshold` does NOT export the `irf`/`fevd`/`simulate`/`predict` generics (`conflicts(detail=TRUE)` is empty after the `library`) → `library(sstvars)` is safe (no clash with vars/svars/lpirfs/BVAR).

**Sources:** Lanne & Virolainen 2025 (*A Gaussian smooth transition VAR*, JEDC 178:105162); Virolainen (in press, *Identification by non-Gaussianity in structural STVAR*, Econometric Reviews); Hubrich & Teräsvirta 2013 (CREATES 2013-18); Tsay 1998 (JASA 93:443, threshold); Kheifets & Saikkonen 2020 (Econometric Reviews 39:4); Lanne & Nyberg 2016 (Oxford Bull. Econ. Stat. 78:4, GFEVD); Kilian & Lütkepohl 2017 (*Structural VAR Analysis*, CUP); `smooth_transition_threshold` v1.2.4 < (the help pages `fitSTVAR`/`GIRF`/`GFEVD`/`linear_IRF` + live introspection).
### #152 High-dimensional debiased LASSO inference + high-dimensional local projections — `desparsified_debiased_lasso` (`c04_structural_shocks/desparsified_debiased_lasso.py`)
**Functions:** `dsl_desla` [the desparsified/debiased LASSO — `desparsified_debiased_lasso`: a point estimate + SE + honest CIs + a joint/row Wald test for target coefficients in a high-dimensional regression], `dsl_hdlp` [HDLP — `HDLP`: a high-dimensional local-projection IRF path with valid asymptotic CI bands per horizon, optionally state-dependent]

**When:** high-dimensional inference where the number of regressors N is large/≈T and plain OLS/LP breaks down. `dsl_desla`: you want a valid CI + a z/Wald test for specific coefficient(s) (the indices `H`) while controlling for many confounders (van de Geer debiasing + the Adamek HAC/LRV variance for time series). `dsl_hdlp`: an IRF via local projection with MANY controls (`q` fast variables) + honest CIs — the high-dimensional, inference-valid cousin of the lpirfs LP-IV; state-dependent responses (Ramey-Zubairy) via `state_variables`. The shock (`x`) must already be identified/exogenous (a proxy/instrument/orthogonalised series).

**When NOT:** a low-dimensional LP with few controls → `local_projections_lp` #22 (OLS + Newey-West, without a penalty); full-system FEVD/HD and efficiency → `reduced_form_var`/`driven_svar_identification` #19/#20; shock identification from sign priors → `VARsignR` #21 (desla does NOT identify shocks, it takes them already identified); pure forecasting (not inference) → shrinkage/ML forecasters.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** a stationarity precheck (`c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` + the confirmatory `run_kpss_test`) — the LRV/HAC variance presupposes (weak) stationarity. Gates: `X` a numeric T×N matrix without NA/Inf (N≥T is allowed); `y`/`x` numeric vectors of length T (alignment); `H` integer indices ∈ [1,N]; `alphas` ∈ (0,1); `seed` a MANDATORY integer; `hmax`/`lags` positive integers with a **hard gate `hmax + lags < T`** (otherwise the package silently truncates); `r`/`q`/`state_variables` with T rows.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#22 lpirfs** (`c04_structural_shocks/local_projections_lp.lp_linear_iv`) — a low-dimensional LP/LP-IV: few controls, standard OLS + Newey-West bands suffice (no high-dimensional penalty/debiasing).
- **#19 vars/svars** (`c04_structural_shocks/svar_irf_fevd.vr_irf`) — full-system IRF/FEVD/HD with efficiency and lower variance at long horizons (not high-dimensional).
- **#21 VARsignR** — the shock is identified ONLY via sign restrictions (desla/HDLP presupposes an already-identified shock).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `dsl_desla`: `coefficients` (a DataFrame variable/bhat/se, debiased, on the original scale) + `intervals` (a DataFrame variable + lower/upper per alpha — the honest CIs) + `joint_test` (H0 `R*beta=q`, by default the joint nullity of all H → statistic/p.value) + `row_tests` (per-row z_stats + intervals, **ONLY when an the reference or q is supplied**) + `n_selected` (the non-zero coefficients in the initial lasso).
- `dsl_hdlp`: `irf` = a named list per state, each a DataFrame `horizon` + lower/bhat/upper per alpha (the CI bands — chart-data, NOT a plot) + `states`/`n_states`/`hmax`/`lags`/`cumulate_y`/`OLS`/`seed`.
- **Stochasticity trap (live-verified):** although the debiasing is convex+analytic, the lambda selection uses RANDOM CV folds → WITHOUT a seed two calls give different bhat; `seed` is MANDATORY in both tools.
- **`alphas` trap:** it is a significance level (0.05 → a 95% CI); the column `lower 0.05`/`upper 0.05` corresponds to alpha=0.05, NOT the 5% quantile.
- **`q` trap:** in `dsl_hdlp` it is the 'fast' controls (the high-dimensional space); in `dsl_desla` it is the RHS of the H0 `R*beta=q`. The same name, a different meaning.
- **`hmax` trap:** if `hmax+lags` ≥ T the package itself truncates hmax silently; the wrapper blocks it (a gate) or exposes the residual 0.8·eff warning as a message.

**Sources:** Adamek, Smeekes & Wilms 2021 "LASSO inference for high-dimensional time series" (arXiv:2007.10952); van de Geer, Bühlmann, Ritov & Dezeure 2014 (Annals of Statistics 42(3):1166-1202); Plagborg-Møller & Wolf 2021 "Local projections and VARs estimate the same impulse responses" (Econometrica 89(2):955-980); Ramey & Zubairy 2018 (JPE 126(2):850-901); Andrews 1991 (Econometrica 59(3):817-858); the `desparsified_debiased_lasso` reference manual (`desparsified_debiased_lasso`, `HDLP`) <

### #153 VAR residual diagnostics (autocorrelation / ARCH / wild bootstrap) — `VARtests` (`c04_structural_shocks/residual_diagnostics_reduced.py`)
**Functions:** `vtt_fit` [`VARfit`], `vtt_portmanteau` [`ACtest` — a multivariate LM AC test + HC0-HC3 + univariate], `vtt_arch` [`archBootTest` — the combined CA + Eklund-Teräsvirta + MARCH tests, bootstrapped], `vtt_wildboot` [`ACtest`→`wildBoot` — wild-bootstrap AC p-values]

**When:** after a reduced-form VAR has been estimated (from `vr_var` #11 → a `varest`, or natively `vtt_fit` → a `VARfit`), for **checking the adequacy of the model on the residuals** before structural identification/IRF: (a) error autocorrelation with a multivariate LM test (Ahlgren-Catani), HC-robust variants for heteroskedastic errors, and optionally a per-equation breakdown; (b) ARCH/volatility clustering with the combined bootstrap LM (CA) + CCC-ARCH (ET) + multivariate LM (MARCH) tests; (c) wild-bootstrap p-values for the autocorrelation when the sample is small/heteroskedastic.

**When NOT:** for the estimation/lag selection of the VAR itself → #11 (`vr_var`); for the cointegration bootstrap test (`cointBootTest`) → category 05 (it does NOT belong here); for plain residual normality (VARtests has **no** normality test — use the residual diagnostics of vars/#19 or another package); it produces no IRF/FEVD — it is purely diagnostics.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** a **fitted reduced-form VAR** is required — `c03_multivariate_nowcasting/reduced_form_var.vr_var` (a `varest`) **or** `vtt_fit` (a `VARfit`). The gate `.vtt_check_fit`: `inherits(fit, c("VARfit","varest"))` — it does **NOT** accept a bare residual matrix (the LM auxiliary regressions need the data + coefficients; residuals only would be silently wrong). Other gates: `h`/`B`/`p` positive integers; `alpha ∈ (0,1)`; `HCtype` a subset of {LM,HC0,HC1,HC2,HC3}; `univariate`/`const`/`non_parametric_trend` booleans; `dist` match.arg(norm/skT); `WBtype`/`WBdist` match.arg; **`vtt_arch`/`vtt_wildboot`: a MANDATORY integer `seed`** (bootstrap).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `vtt_wildboot` instead of `vtt_portmanteau` when the sample is small or the errors are heteroskedastic — the wild-bootstrap p-values (Ahlgren-Catani Algorithm 1/2) have better finite-sample properties than the asymptotic chi-square; `vtt_arch` when the target is ARCH/volatility clustering (not autocorrelation). If autocorrelation is rejected → raise the lags of the VAR (#11); if ARCH is rejected → GARCH-type errors / robust SE.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `vtt_portmanteau`: a `multivariate` DataFrame (`HCtype`, `statistic` Q, `p.value`, `df`=K²·h, `decision`) + `h`/`K`/`df`/`alpha`/`inputType`; with `univariate=TRUE` additionally a per-equation `univariate` DataFrame (`df`=h).
- `vtt_arch`: a named list per test — `CA` {statistic = 1−min_i p(LM_i), boot.p, uni.stat, uni.boot.p, decision}, `MARCH` {statistic, asymp.p, boot.p, df=K²(K+1)²h/4, decision}, `ET` {statistic, asymp.p, boot.p, df=K·h, decision} + `B`/`dist`/`seed`.
- `vtt_wildboot`: a `wild` DataFrame (`HCtype`, the `statistic` from ACtest, `WB.p`, `df`, `decision`) + `WBtype`/`WBdist`/`numberOfErrors`/`numberOfNA`/`seed`.
- `vtt_fit`: `model` (a `VARfit` handle — a producer) + `K`/`p`/`N`/`variables`/`residuals` (chart-data).
- **Interpretation traps**: (1) **Polarity** — H0 = CLEAN residuals (no AC / no ARCH); `p<alpha` ⇒ **a rejection ⇒ misspecification** (the model FAILS, not the other way round). (2) `vtt_arch`/`vtt_wildboot` are bootstrap-based ⇒ the same `seed` gives the same p-values (the cache key); without a seed they are uncacheable. (3) **CA ALWAYS runs** in `vtt_arch` (a documented package bug `'CA_LMi not found'` when CA=FALSE); the CA statistic is bootstrap-only (no asymptotic p/df). (4) `univariate` takes only FALSE/TRUE — the package's `'only'` errors (blocked). (5) the `MARCH` df=K²(K+1)²h/4 grows rapidly with K ⇒ low power on a small sample; `wildBoot` stores the p-values in `WBr.pv` (recursive) or `WBf.pv` (fixed) — the wrapper handles this transparently.

**Sources:** the VARtests reference manual (`ACtest`, `archBootTest`, `wildBoot`, `VARfit`) — live btw/Rd introspection of the installed (the lockfile) version; Ahlgren & Catani, "Wild bootstrap tests for autocorrelation in vector autoregressive models", *Statistical Papers* 2016 <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00362-016-0744-0>; Catani & Ahlgren 2016 (the combined bootstrap LM ARCH test); Eklund & Teräsvirta 2007 (the CCC-ARCH LM test, *J. Econometrics*); Lütkepohl 2006, *New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis*, sect. 16.5 (the multivariate ARCH-LM test); MacKinnon & White 1985 (HCCME).
