### #181 Network estimation for time series (a sparse VAR Granger network + a partial-correlation network) — `network_estimation_time` (`c09_cross_section_networks/network_estimation_time.py`)
**Functions:** `nets_fit` [`network_estimation_time` — the NETS LASSO; it returns the Granger network `g.adj`, the contemporaneous network `c.adj`, the long-run network `lr.adj`, the concentration matrix `C.hat`, the AR array `A.hat`, + a computed partial-correlation matrix as chart-data]

**When:** you have a multivariate time-series system with a **small N (~4-6)** and want **at the same time** (a) a **directed Granger network** from a *sparse* VAR (which series Granger-predicts which) and (b) an **undirected contemporaneous network** from the partial-correlation structure of the VAR innovations (which series are connected once all the others are controlled for). NETS uses **LASSO shrinkage** instead of dense estimation, so the result is directly a **sparse graph** (a 0/1 adjacency) suitable for network chart-data. The operating map (`GN`/`CN`):

| `GN` | `CN` | what it estimates | algorithm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRUE` | `TRUE` (the default) | the AR matrices + the concentration matrix (the full NETS) | nets |
| `TRUE` | `FALSE` | only the AR matrices of the VAR (the Granger network) | LASSO VAR |
| `FALSE` | `TRUE` | only the concentration/partial-correlation matrix (p auto→0) | space (Peng et al. 2009) |

**When NOT:** (a) a large N without a sparsity assumption, or when you want a **dense** VAR + IRF/FEVD → `vr_var` (category 03). (b) You want **spillover/variance-decomposition connectedness** (Diebold-Yilmaz, FEVD percentages) → #51 `dy_fit`; or by **frequency** → #52 `fq_net`. NETS gives the graph structure (the edges), not quantified spillover shares. (c) A single-equation spatial regression with a **known** weights matrix `W` → #53/#54. (d) You want **point forecasts** — this is a network-estimation node, not a forecaster.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A multivariate `y` of shape `T x N`** (each column one series): the gate `.nts_check_y` — a numeric matrix (or a numeric DataFrame), `N>=2`, `T>=3`, **free of NA/Inf** (`network_estimation_time` fails silently with a cryptic foreign-call error on NA and with "incorrect number of dimensions" on a single column). The colnames default to `v1.vN` if missing, so that the adjacencies carry labels.
- **Stationarity**: the NETS VAR assumes stationary series — non-stationary ones produce a *spurious* network structure. Run `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test` (and/or `run_kpss_test`) first and difference if needed.
- **Choosing `lambda`**: the sparsity (and therefore the **structure** of the graph) depends on `lambda`. Pass either `lambda` (a scalar, or a length-2 `[AR, concentration]` **only** when `GN&CN`), or `lambda_grid` (candidate scalars) and let the node choose by an information criterion (`ic="bic"|"aic"`, `T*log(rss)+npar*penalty`). **Exactly one** of the two (a gate). `lambda` must be `>0` — `network_estimation_time` accepts negatives, zero and length-3 vectors **silently** (silent-wrong) → explicit gates.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#51 `dy_fit` (ConnectednessApproach)** — when you want FEVD-based **spillover** connectedness (from/to/net in percentages) instead of a LASSO Granger/partial-correlation graph.
- **#52 `fq_net` (frequencyConnectedness)** — connectedness decomposed by **frequency** (short/long-run bands).
- **`vr_var` (c03_multivariate_nowcasting/reduced_form_var.py)** — a small N, and you want a **dense** VAR with full IRF/FEVD/causality without sparsity.
- **`CN=FALSE`** — only the directed Granger network; **`GN=FALSE`** — only the undirected partial-correlation network (space).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `granger_network` — `g.adj`, an `N x N` **0/1 directed** adjacency (the Granger network from `A.hat`). NULL if `GN=FALSE`. **A trap**: it is directed (row→col), unlike `concentration_network`.
- `concentration_network` — `c.adj`, an `N x N` **0/1 undirected** adjacency (the partial-correlation network). NULL if `CN=FALSE`.
- `partial_correlation` — an `N x N` matrix of partial correlations `-C_ij/sqrt(C_ii C_jj)`, `diag=1`, values in `[-1,1]` (chart-data; computed from `concentration_matrix`). NULL if `CN=FALSE` or degenerate.
- `concentration_matrix` — `C.hat` (the precision matrix of the innovations); `longrun_network` — `lr.adj`; `ar_matrices` — `A.hat`, an `N x N x P` array (the VAR coefficients); `innovation_precisions` — `c.hat` (the diagonal).
- `lambda_used` — the penalty (of length 1 or 2) actually used; `selected_lambda`+`ic_table` (`{lambda,rss,npar,ic,criterion}`) when a `lambda_grid` was given (the selection = `min ic`).
- `rss`/`npar`/`p_used`/`N`/`T` — fit diagnostics; `degenerate_concentration` — a **flag**: `TRUE` ⇒ `diag(C.hat)<=0` and the `partial_correlation` could not be computed (do not read a network off a degenerate fit).
- **Determinism**: `set.seed(seed=2025)` before the fit (the active-shooting algorithm starts from zero — deterministic).

**Sources:** Barigozzi, M. & Brownlees, C. (2019) "NETS: Network Estimation for Time Series", *Journal of Applied Econometrics* 34(3):347-364; Peng, Wang, Zhou & Zhu (2009) "Partial Correlation Estimation by Joint Sparse Regression Models" (the space algorithm), *JASA* 104(486):735-746; `help("nets","nets")` — `network_estimation_time` 0.9.1 (Christian Brownlees), <

### #182 Factor-adjusted network estimation (high-dimensional TS): a common factor + an idiosyncratic VAR + Granger/partial-correlation networks — `factor_adjusted_network` (`c09_cross_section_networks/factor_adjusted_network.py`)
**Functions:** `fnets_fit`, `fnets_factor`

**When:** many (high-dimensional) time series, T x N, with a strong common (factor) structure; you want to SEPARATE the common from the idiosyncratic part and to estimate the idiosyncratic network (Granger + partial correlation) cleanly of pervasive co-movement

**When NOT:** few series without pervasive factors (a sparse VAR network directly -> #181 nets); a single-equation panel (i,t) (#46 plm); a spatial cross-section with a known W (#53 spatialreg); pure forecasting with no interest in a network

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `fnets_factor (estimate the number of factors q first; degenerate=TRUE or q=0 -> there is no common structure, consider #181 nets directly)`
- `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_csv_data (load the T x N matrix of series)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#181 nets_fit** — no pervasive factors -> a sparse VAR network directly, without factor adjustment
- **#53 spr_fit_lag/error (spatialreg)** — a cross-section with a known spatial weights matrix W instead of an estimated network
- **BVAR/a large VAR (category 04)** — few series, an interest in forecasting/IRF rather than in a sparse network
- **fm.restricted=TRUE** — a static approximate factor model (PCA) suffices; no dynamic (spectral) factors

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- q: the estimated number of factors (or the input, if a number was given)
- granger_network: an N x N directed matrix (the sum of the VAR transition matrices over all the lags, with a zero diagonal) — chart-data
- pc_network: the N x N contemporaneous partial correlation of the VAR innovations (only with do.lrpc=TRUE)
- lrpc_network: the N x N long-run partial correlation (only with do.lrpc=TRUE)
- beta: the (N*var.order) x N VAR parameters (column j = the regression of variable j); Gamma: the innovation covariance; lambda: the regularisation
- fnets_factor: loadings (2D if restricted; a 3D IRF array (p,q,trunc.lags+2) if unrestricted); factors (the factor series/common shocks); a degenerate flag

**Interpretation traps:**
- the edge weights MAY be negative (they are entries of the VAR parameters/partial correlations) — they are not |weights|
- granger_network[i,j] = the effect i -> j (the orientation of network(type=granger)); the diagonal is zeroed (the self-lags are removed)
- pc/lrpc exist ONLY when do.lrpc=TRUE; otherwise out.lrpc is NA and the fields are missing
- q=0 is accepted silently by fnets (only a warning) -> a gate blocks a numeric q<1; fnets_factor sets degenerate=TRUE
- unrestricted loadings are NOT classical factor loadings but impulse response functions (a 3D array); the classical 2D loadings appear only under fm.restricted=TRUE
- input orientation: the columns = the variables (T x N); a single column or NA/Inf fails with a cryptic C error -> explicit gates

**Sources:** Barigozzi, Cho & Owens (2024+) FNETS: Factor-adjusted network estimation and forecasting for high-dimensional time series, JBES · Owens, Cho & Barigozzi (2024+) fnets: An the reference Package for Network Estimation and Forecasting via Factor-Adjusted VAR Modelling, · help('fnets','fnets'), help('fnets.factor.model'), help('network.fnets') ( fnets 0.1.6) · Hallin & Liska (2007) JASA 102:603 (the dynamic factor number); Avarucci et al. (2022); Ahn & Horenstein (2013) Econometrica 81:1203 (the eigenvalue ratio).

### #154 The univariate GARCH family (vanilla/egarch/gjr/aparch/component) — the tidy tsmodels.py`)
**Functions:** `tg_estimate`, `tg_predict`, `tg_backtest`

**When:** modelling conditional volatility in univariate returns (volatility clustering); ML estimation of a GARCH + an h-step forecast of sigma_t + a rolling backtest; a modern tidy API (nloptr, TMB, autodiff SE)

**When NOT:** multivariate volatility/correlation (-> #29 rmgarch/tsmarch); regime-switching volatility (-> #31 MSGARCH); return levels without ARCH effects (run_arch_test not significant); realized/intraday volatility (highfrequency)

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `c15_model_evaluation/arch.run_arch_test (ARCH effects: H0=no ARCH; a rejection -> a GARCH is justified)`
- `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the returns from a file)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#28 rugarch (ga_spec/ga_fit)** — you need the fGARCH/csGARCH submodels, a VaR rolling backtest with coverage tests, or the mature rugarch API
- **#29 rmgarch/tsmarch (dcc_fit)** — a multivariate conditional covariance/correlation (>=2 assets)
- **#31 MSGARCH (msg_fit_ml)** — the volatility switches between regimes (Markov switching)
- **variance_targeting=TRUE** — a large sample + you want a fixed unconditional variance without estimating omega

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- coefficients: named (mu/omega/alpha*/beta*/gamma*/shape/skew..) depending on the model/distribution
- persistence: sum(alpha+beta) ~ the persistence; ~1 => near-integrated (IGARCH-like), see near_nonstationary
- sigma: the conditional sd series (chart-data); tg_predict.sigma_forecast: the h-step sigma_t
- converged/kkt1/kkt2: the KKT optimality conditions (converged=KKT1 first order); a stateless capture
- aic/bic/loglik: for comparing models/distributions; tg_backtest.table: sigma/actual/convergence per forecast

**Interpretation traps:**
- y MUST be returns (log/simple), NOT price levels — the wrapper does no differencing
- persistence>=0.999 (near_nonstationary=TRUE) => the unconditional variance explodes; the long-horizon sigma_t forecast is unreliable
- egarch persistence is measured on the log variance (a different scale from the vanilla alpha+beta)
- converged=FALSE (KKT1) => the solution is not an optimum; do not interpret the coefficients/SE
- std_errors are NULL/NaN when the Hessian is not positive definite (common at boundary persistence)
- tg_estimate/tg_backtest are deterministic (ML); only tg_predict with nsim>0 is stochastic (seeded 2025)

**Sources:** the tsgarch vignette 'Feasible GARCH' + help('garch_modelspec','tsgarch'), estimate.tsgarch.spec, predict.tsgarch.estimate, tsbacktest (tsgarch 1.0.4) · Galanos A. (2024) tsgarch: Univariate GARCH Models, an the reference package (tsmodels) · Bollerslev 1986 (J. Econometrics 31:307, GARCH); Nelson 1991 (Econometrica 59:347, EGARCH) · Glosten Jagannathan Runkle 1993 (J. Finance 48:1779, GJR); Ding Granger Engle 1993 (APARCH).

### #155 Multivariate GARCH — Dynamic Conditional Correlation (DCC/aDCC/CCC) — `multivariate_garch_dynamic` (`c06_volatility_regimes/multivariate_garch_dynamic.py`)
**Functions:** `tm_dcc_estimate` [`garch_modelspec`+`estimate(keep_tmb=TRUE)` → `to_multi_estimate` → `dcc_modelspec` → `estimate.dcc.spec`], `tm_predict` [`predict.dcc.estimate` + `tscov`/`tscor`], `tm_cov` [`tscov.dcc.estimate`/`tscor.dcc.estimate`]

**When:** you have ≥2 series of **returns** and want their **time-varying covariance/correlation** — volatility spillovers, time-varying correlation, dynamic hedge ratios, portfolio VaR inputs. DCC models separately (a) the volatility of each series (a univariate GARCH) and (b) the dynamics of the correlation, in two stages. The `dynamics` map:

| `dynamics` | what it does | when |
|---|---|---|
| `"constant"` (the default) | CCC: a constant correlation, time-varying variances | the correlation does not change substantially; a baseline/fewer parameters |
| `"dcc"` | the Engle DCC: the correlation evolves with `alpha`,`beta` | the correlation rises and falls (e.g. in crises) |
| `"adcc"` | the asymmetric DCC: an extra `gamma` for negative shocks | the correlation rises more in downturns (leverage in the correlation) |

`distribution` selects `mvn` (the normal) or `mvt` (the multivariate t → joint fat tails, it estimates a `shape`). It is the **tidy.

**When NOT:** (a) univariate volatility → #28 `univariate_garch_family`/`univariate_garch_family_2`. (b) Many assets (a very large N) → DCC estimation/parameters become difficult; consider GO-GARCH/factor models. (c) You are working on **levels/non-stationary** series — take returns first (a log difference). (d) Regime-switching volatility → #31 `MSGARCH`.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A T×N matrix of returns** (load it with `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`): numeric, N≥2, **free of NA**, with no constant column. The gates `.tm_check_y`: coercion DataFrame→matrix, N≥2 (otherwise a correlation is undefined), ≥5·N rows, a zero-variance column = a degenerate GARCH → a hard `stop`.
- **ARCH effects per series** (`c15_model_evaluation/arch.run_arch_test`, the ARCH-LM test): if no series has conditional heteroskedasticity, the GARCH is superfluous.
- **Is there dynamic correlation at all?** After estimation, `tm_cov` shows the N×N×T array — if the correlation is roughly flat, `constant`/CCC suffices (the Engle-Sheppard logic).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#29 `rmgarch dcc_fit`** — the legacy `univariate_garch_family`/`dcc_mgarch` pipeline, or the copula/GO-GARCH variants that are not exposed here.
- **`dynamics="constant"` (CCC)** instead of dcc — when `alpha` comes out ~0 or the `tm_cov` correlation is constant; fewer parameters.
- **`distribution="mvt"`** — fat tails / joint tail dependence in the standardised returns.
- **`cgarch`/`gogarch`** (tsmarch, not exposed here) — copula dependence or orthogonalisation for a larger N.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `coefficients` — the **DCC dynamic parameters**: `alpha_1`/`beta_1` (dcc), plus `gamma_1` (adcc), `shape` (mvt). Under `constant` it is **empty** (no dynamic parameter — the correlation is the sample correlation of the standardised residuals). `alpha+beta`→1 ⇒ high persistence; `alpha`~0 ⇒ effectively constant.
- `coef_table` — `term/Estimate/Std. Error/t value/Pr(>|t|)`. **A trap**: a huge/`NaN` Std. Error ⇒ a degenerate/unidentifiable solution — do not interpret the parameters.
- `correlation_last` / `covariance_last` — the N×N **last in-sample** conditional matrix (symmetric, with a unit diagonal in the correlation) → chart-data for a heatmap.
- `loglik`/`AIC`/`BIC`/`nobs`/`n_series`/`n_pars`; `converged` — the convergence of the 2nd stage. **A stateless node**: stderr is lost, so `converged` (and the empty-result check → a `stop`) is the only way to catch degeneracy.
- `tm_cov.covariance`/`.correlation` — the whole **N×N×T** conditional array (the time series of the volatilities/correlations). **A trap**: under `constant` the `.correlation` is **N×N×1** (constant in time) whereas `.covariance` remains N×N×T (the variances vary through the GARCH models).
- `tm_predict.forecast_covariance`/`.forecast_correlation` — the **N×N×h** *mean* forecast (`tscov`/`tscor` with `distribution=FALSE`). The uncertainty lives in the `nsim` simulated paths, not in the central point.
- **An implementation/version trap**: the univariate GARCH models are estimated with `keep_tmb=TRUE` — **mandatory**, otherwise the dynamic `dcc`/`adcc` estimation (the 2nd-stage scores/hessian) fails with "attempt to apply non-function" in `tsgarch ≥ 1.0.4` (which drops the `.tmb`). The matrix is also converted internally to an `indexed_time_series` (`garch_modelspec` requires xts) and the list of univariate estimates is named from the colnames (otherwise `dcc_modelspec` loses the `series_names`).

**Sources:** the tsmarch help/vignette (`help("dcc_modelspec","tsmarch")`, `help("estimate","tsmarch")`, the DCC vignette, tsmarch 1.0.0) < Engle 2002 "Dynamic Conditional Correlation: A Simple Class of Multivariate GARCH Models" (JBES 20:339); Cappiello, Engle & Sheppard 2006 the asymmetric DCC (J. Financial Econometrics 4:537); the Ghalanos `multivariate_garch_dynamic`/`univariate_garch_family_2` documentation (2-stage estimation, `keep_tmb`).
### #156 Realized (co)variance & intraday spot volatility from high-frequency data — `realized_variance_intraday` (`c06_volatility_regimes/realized_variance_intraday.py`)
**Functions:** `hf_realized_var`, `hf_realized_cov`, `hf_spot_vol`

**When:** you have intraday data and want the ex-post realized volatility/covariance of ONE day (rCov=sum r², the jump-robust rBPCov/medRV, the noise-robust rKernelCov/rTSCov), a semivariance decomposition, or the intraday spot-volatility pattern

**When NOT:** daily/low-frequency series -> a parametric GARCH (#28 rugarch/tsgarch); conditional/forecast volatility -> GARCH; a multi-day dynamic covariance -> DCC (#29); you have no intraday observations

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `hf_realized_var (a univariate realized measure; choose the measure according to the microstructure noise / jumps)`
- `hf_realized_cov (a multivariate realized covariance/semicovariance; >=2 assets)`
- `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the intraday CSV: for spotVol you need DT+price columns)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#28 rugarch/tsgarch (ga_fit)** — conditional/forecast volatility from daily returns instead of an ex-post realized measure
- **#29 rmgarch DCC (dcc_fit)** — a dynamic multi-day correlation/covariance instead of a per-day realized covariance
- **measure=rBPCov/medRV** — suspected jumps in the intraday series (a jump-robust integrated variance)
- **measure=rKernelCov/rTSCov** — market microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce) -> noise-robust
- **measure=rSemiCov** — you want the downside/upside (negative/positive/mixed/concordant) semicovariance

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- hf_realized_var: realized_variance (the scalar sum, or a robust variant) + realized_vol=its square root; K (rTSCov only); n_obs/n_returns
- hf_realized_cov: rcov (the N×N covariance, or the correlation if cor=TRUE); correlation (cov2cor when cor=FALSE); asset_names; n_assets
- hf_realized_cov with measure=rSemiCov: semicov=list{mixed,negative,positive,concordant} N×N + rcov (=their sum)
- hf_spot_vol: spot_vol (a numeric intraday series); timestamps; daily (per day); periodic (the intraday shape); n_na

**Interpretation traps:**
- rTSCov multivariate: the package requires a LIST of per-asset xts; a multi-column input collapses SILENTLY to a scalar — the wrapper handles it, but do not call rTSCov directly
- measure='medRV' -> rMedRVar (rMedRV is deprecated in 1.0.3)
- rTSCov/rKernelCov require PRICES (makeReturns=TRUE); rTSCov wants n>=10*K, otherwise a gate stop
- alignBy is NOT exposed in the realized measures: the data must be ALREADY sampled (e.g. at 5 minutes) intraday data for ONE day; the value is timestamp-invariant without alignBy
- spotVol method='detPer' ideally wants >=50 days; fewer -> a warning (an unstable periodicity), not an error; read n_na
- realized variance ≠ conditional/forecast variance: it is an ex-post estimate of one day's integrated variance, not a forecast

**Sources:** Boudt, Cornelissen, Payseur et al., the highfrequency vignette + help (help('rCov'/'rBPCov'/'rKernelCov'/'rTSCov'/'rSemiCov'/'spotVol','highfrequency')) < · Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys 2003 (Econometrica 71:579) — realized volatility · Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2004 (J. Financial Econometrics) — bipower variation (rBPCov) · Andersen, Dobrev & Schaumburg 2012 (J. Econometrics 169:75) — the jump-robust MedRV · Zhang, Mykland & Aït-Sahalia 2005 (JASA 100:1394); Zhang 2011 — two time scales (rTSCov) · Barndorff-Nielsen, Hansen, Lunde & Shephard 2008 (Econometrica 76:1481) — realized kernels (rKernelCov) · Bollerslev, Li, Patton & Quaedvlieg 2020 (J. Econometrics 217:411) — realized semicovariance (rSemiCov) · Boudt, Croux & Laurent 2011 (J. Empirical Finance 18:353) — deterministic-periodicity spot volatility (spotVol detPer).

### #157 HAR realized-volatility models (HAR/HARJ/HARQ/HARQ-J) — `HARModel` (`c06_volatility_regimes/har_realized_volatility.py`)
**Functions:** `har_estimate` [`HAREstimate` + `coef`/`logLik`/`qlike`/`uncmean` + `summary.lm` — a PRODUCER, registers `object`], `har_forecast` [`HARForecast` + `getForc`/`forecastRes`], `har_simulate` [`HARSimulate` — seeded]

**When:** you have a **daily realized measure** (the realized variance `RV`, a consistent estimator of the integrated volatility) and want to model its well-known **long-memory** behaviour with the heterogeneous autoregressive model of Corsi (2009). HAR regresses `RV_t` on daily/weekly/monthly averages (the lags `c(1,5,22)`), reproducing the slowly decaying autocorrelation without genuine fractional integration. The type map (the `type` argument):

| `type` | what it does | when |
|---|---|---|
| `"HAR"` (the default) | vanilla Corsi 2009 (OLS on the RV cascades) | the baseline realized-volatility model |
| `"HARJ"` | it adds a jump component (it needs `BPV`) | significant discontinuities/jumps in the price |
| `"HARQ"` | a measurement-error correction (it needs `RQ`) | the `RV` is noisy; a time-varying attenuation bias (BPQ 2016) |
| `"HARQ-J"` | a combination of jumps + quarticity (it needs `BPV` & `RQ`) | both jumps and measurement error |

`har_estimate` is a **PRODUCER** (it registers `object`) — the estimate is chainable; the `@model` is a plain `lm` (the HAR estimation is OLS on the pre-built cascades). `har_forecast` produces a **rolling out-of-sample** forecast (re-estimating on a rolling/increasing window) and returns QLIKE-compatible residuals + RMSE/MAE. `har_simulate` generates a controlled HAR series (seeded) for validation/benchmarking.

**When NOT:** (a) you have **only daily returns** without a realized measure → a parametric conditional variance with a GARCH (`ga_fit` rugarch / tsgarch, #28), not HAR. (b) You want **multivariate**/conditional-correlation volatility → `dcc_mgarch`/`multivariate_garch_dynamic`. (c) **Regime-switching** volatility → `MSGARCH`. (d) You have only **intraday** data → compute the realized measure FIRST with `hf_realized_var`, then feed it here as `RM`.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **`RM` = the realized VARIANCE** (a positive series, NOT returns, NOT a standard deviation), free of `NA`. The gate `.har_check_rm`: a numeric vector, free of `NA` (the package accepts them **silently** and produces a wrong estimate), and `length(RM) >= max(periods)+2` (otherwise a cryptic armadillo error).
- **`RM` from intraday data**: `c06_volatility_regimes/realized_variance_intraday.hf_realized_var` computes the realized variance from intraday prices — its output becomes the `RM` input.
- **The auxiliary series per type**: `HARJ`/`HARQ-J` require `BPV` (the bipower/continuous component); `HARQ`/`HARQ-J` require `RQ` (the realized quarticity), of the same length as `RM`. Without them the package fails with a cryptic error — the wrapper gives a **clean gate**.
- **A valid `type`**: on an invalid `type` the package returns **`NULL` SILENTLY** (it only prints a message) → it is barred with `match.arg{HAR,HARJ,HARQ,HARQ-J}`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#28 `ga_fit` (rugarch) / `univariate_garch_family_2`** — when you have only daily returns (no realized measure); a parametric conditional variance.
- **`type='HARJ'`** — when there are significant jumps; it separates the continuous part (`BPV`) from the jump part.
- **`type='HARQ'`** — when the `RV` has measurement error; a correction with the realized quarticity (BPQ 2016).
- **`mfGARCH` (#31)** — when you want to link the volatility to a low-frequency macro variable (GARCH-MIDAS).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `coefficients` — a named numeric (`beta0`, the intercept, + a `beta` per period); `coef_table` — a matrix `Estimate/Std. Error/t value/Pr(>|t|)` (from `summary.lm`, base stats; the SE are OLS ones).
- `r_squared`/`adj_r_squared`/`sigma`/`logLik` — fit diagnostics.
- `qlike_mean` — the **QLIKE loss** (the robust volatility-forecast loss of Patton 2011); `qlike` — the per-observation vector. **A trap**: for model comparison prefer QLIKE, NOT the MSE on levels (which is biased by the volatility-proxy noise).
- `uncond_mean` — the unconditional mean volatility **ONLY for `type='HAR'`** (`NA` for HARJ/HARQ/HARQ-J — it is not implemented in the package).
- `fitted`/`residuals` — chart-data; `nobs`/`type`/`periods` — metadata; `object` of class `HARModel` (the chaining handle).
- `har_forecast` — `diebold_mariano_tscv` (the `getForc` vector); `forecast_matrix` (`step × roll`, the dimnames are preserved); `actual` (`forecastComparison`); `forecast_residuals`; `rmse`/`mae` (the out-of-sample loss); `object` of class `HARForecast`.
- `har_simulate` — `simulation` (a numeric vector of length `len`); `coef`/`errorTermSD`/`seed` metadata; `object` of class `HARSim` (`object@simulation`). **Determinism**: seeded (`seed=2025` by default).
- **A gates trap**: `length(coef) == length(periods)+1` in simulate; `h>1 ⇒ nAhead=1` in forecast (multi-period-ahead is not implemented for aggregated volatility); negative `len`/`errorTermSD` are accepted silently by the package → explicit gates.

**Sources:** Corsi 2009 *A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility*, Journal of Financial Econometrics 7(2):174-196; Bollerslev, Patton & Quaedvlieg 2016 *Exploiting the errors*, Journal of Econometrics 192(1):1-18 (HARQ/HARQ-J); Patton 2011 *Volatility forecast comparison using imperfect volatility proxies*, Journal of Econometrics 160(1):246-256 (QLIKE); `help("HAREstimate","HARModel")`, `help("HARForecast","HARModel")`, `help("HARSimulate","HARModel")` + live introspection (HARModel 1.0).

### #158 Generalized Autoregressive Score / Dynamic Conditional Score (GAS/DCS) — `generalized_autoregressive_score` (`c06_volatility_regimes/generalized_autoregressive_score.py`)
**Functions:** `gas_fit` [`gas` — ML estimation, a PRODUCER], `gas_forecast` [`gas_forecast` — mean_path/simulated_paths, a CONSUMER], `gas_simulate` [`gas_simulate` — a seeded simulation, a CONSUMER]

**When:** you have **one** univariate series (e.g. returns) and want **score-driven** (observation-driven) dynamics in a parameter of the distribution — the variance (volatility), the mean/location, or the tails — with an **explicit, full distributional likelihood**. The score of the log-likelihood drives the evolution of the time-varying parameter (Creal et al. 2013; Harvey 2013). `gas_fit` covers 12 univariate continuous distributions (6 with real support: `norm`, `t`, `ged`, `laplace`, `alaplace`, `logistic`; 6 with positive/duration support: `gamma`, `exp`, `weibull`, `lognorm`, `fisk`, `rayleigh`). The usage map (the `par_static` argument):

| goal | `par_static` (norm) | result |
|---|---|---|
| **a volatility model** | `[1,0]` (dynamics in the variance) | `var_tv` = a score-driven variance — what you want for volatility |
| a location/mean model (**the default**) | `NULL` → `[FALSE,TRUE]` | `mean_tv` is dynamic, the variance is static |

`scaling` = the scaling of the score: `unit` (the default, very fast) · `fisher_inv_sqrt` ≈ the inverse square-root Fisher information · `fisher_inv` ≈ the inverse Fisher information (+ full_/diag_ variants). For **orthogonal** distributions the variants coincide; the `fisher_*` ones are **much heavier** (a numerical Fisher information).

**When NOT:** (a) **multivariate** volatility/correlation → `dcc_mgarch`/`multivariate_garch_dynamic` (DCC/BEKK/copula), not here (this is univariate). (b) You want the **classical GARCH interface** (a rolling backtest, variance targeting) → #28 `ga_fit` (rugarch) or `univariate_garch_family_2`. (c) **Regime-switching** volatility (Markov states) → #31 `msg_fit` (MSGARCH). (d) **Realized/intraday** volatility → `realized_variance_intraday`. (e) Static conditional quantiles without dynamics → `quantile_regression` (category 12).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A return series without NA**: `y` must be a numeric vector (or a **single**-column matrix); the gate `.gm_check_y`: `>=10` finite observations, **non-constant** (sd>0), and **strictly positive** (`y>0`) for the duration distributions (gamma/exp/weibull/lognorm/fisk/rayleigh). Loading from a file: `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`.
- **Choosing the distribution is a test, not an assumption**: test the normality of the innovations (`c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_jarque_bera`) — rejecting H0 ⇒ prefer `distr='t'`/`'ged'` (fat tails) over `'norm'`.
- **Convergence before any downstream use**: `gas_fit` returns `converged` + `status_optim`/`status_hessian`; run `gas_forecast`/`gas_simulate` **only** if `converged==TRUE`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#28 `ga_fit` (rugarch)** / **`univariate_garch_family_2`** — when you want a standard GARCH-family variance model or a modern (m)GARCH with a rolling backtest.
- **#31 `msg_fit` (MSGARCH)** — when the volatility switches between **regimes** (Markov switching).
- **`quantile_regression`** (category 12) — static conditional quantiles without score dynamics.
- GAS/DCS is **superior** when you want score-driven dynamics in a **non-Gaussian** parameter (the tails/asymmetry) with an explicit likelihood — something the classical GARCH does not express directly.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `coef_table` — a matrix `Estimate/Std. Error/z value/Pr(>|z|)` (`*_omega`/`*_alpha1`/`*_phi1` per parameter). `coef_est` is the named vector.
- `par_tv` (T×k) / `mean_tv` / `var_tv` — the time-varying parameters / mean / **variance** (chart-data). **A trap**: `var_tv` is the volatility path **only** when `par_static` makes the variance dynamic; under the default the variance is almost constant (it is the mean that is dynamic).
- `resid_tv` / `score_tv` / `loglik_tv` — the standardised residuals, the score path, the per-observation log-likelihood (chart-data).
- `loglik_sum` / `aic` / `bic` — fit criteria for comparing distributions/scalings/orders.
- `converged` (a bool) + `status_optim`/`status_hessian` — **critical**: `converged=FALSE` (e.g. `status_optim='iteration_limit_reached'` because of the bounded `maxeval`, 10000 by default) ⇒ the estimates are **not** reliable. The bound yields `converged=FALSE` instead of a hang in the stateless node.
- `gas_forecast`: `y_ahead_mean` (the point forecast); under `method='simulated_paths'` also `y_ahead_sd` + `y_ahead_quant` (a **fan chart** — the quantiles of the predictive distribution at `quant`) + `par_tv_ahead_quant`. `mean_path` does **not** return quantiles.
- `gas_simulate`: `y_sim` / `par_tv_sim` / `score_tv_sim`. **Determinism**: `gas_forecast(simulated_paths)` and `gas_simulate` are stochastic → internally `set.seed(2025)`.

**Sources:** the gasmodel vignette + `help("gas","gasmodel")` (Vladimír Holý, package 0.6.2); the `distr` table of distributions/parameterisations < Creal, Koopman & Lucas 2013, "Generalized Autoregressive Score Models with Applications", *J. Applied Econometrics* 28(5):777-795; Harvey 2013, *Dynamic Models for Volatility and Heavy Tails* (Dynamic Conditional Score), Cambridge University Press.

---
### #159 GARCH-MIDAS (a short-run GARCH × a long-run MIDAS macro component) — `mfGARCH` (`c06_volatility_regimes/garch_midas.py`)
**Functions:** `mfg_fit` [`fit_mfgarch`, a PRODUCER], `mfg_predict` [`predict.mfGARCH`], `mfg_simulate` [`simulate_mfgarch`, seeded]

**When:** you have high-frequency returns `y` (e.g. daily) and want to explain/forecast their **volatility** by linking it to a **slow macro variable** `x` at a low frequency (e.g. industrial production, the NFCI, a monthly VIX). GARCH-MIDAS decomposes the conditional variance multiplicatively:

> sigma²_t = tau_t · g_t

where **tau_t** = the long-run component (a slow trend, driven by MIDAS-weighted lags of `x` — a beta weighting scheme) and **g_t** = a short-run GARCH(1,1) (± an asymmetric GJR term `gamma`) on the standardised returns. The flow: `mfg_fit` (estimation + an `object` handle) → `mfg_predict` (a forecast of the total volatility). `mfg_simulate` is a **standalone DGP** (you give the parameters, you get a simulated path; seeded).

**When NOT:** (a) there is no macro long-run driver → a plain univariate GARCH (#28 `univariate_garch_family` / #154 `univariate_garch_family_2`). (b) The volatility is driven by a **regime switch**, not by a slow macro trend → #31 `MSGARCH`. (c) Multivariate volatility/correlations → #29 `dcc_mgarch` / #155 `multivariate_garch_dynamic`. (d) You do not have an `x` that is constant within each low-frequency period (MIDAS requires one value per period).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **The data structure (mandatory, the gate `.mfg_check_data`):** a long-format DataFrame with a column **NAMED `date` of class Date**, a numeric `y` (returns, free of NA), a numeric `x` that has **ONE unique value per low-frequency period**, and a `low.freq` column **of class Date** (e.g. `year_month`). A violation of any of these → a clean `stop` (not the cryptic package error).
- **Is there an ARCH effect?** `c15_model_evaluation/arch.run_arch_test` (Engle's ARCH-LM on `y`) — if there is no volatility clustering, GARCH-MIDAS has nothing to model.
- **Loading:** `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited` for the long-format panel of one.
- **Convergence:** `mfg_fit` → **check `converged`/`convergence` before you interpret anything** (see the trap).
- `K` must be a positive integer **< the number of low-frequency periods** (otherwise negative-length vectors in the MIDAS lag).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#28 `univariate_garch_family` / #154 `univariate_garch_family_2`** — when there is no exogenous macro driver; a plain univariate GARCH.
- **#31 `MSGARCH`** — when a regime change (not a slow macro trend) drives the volatility.
- **`weighting = "beta.unrestricted"`** instead of the restricted one — when you want free (non-monotone) MIDAS weighting; it adds a parameter `w1` (restricted ⇒ `w1=1`, monotonically decreasing).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `par` — a named vector of estimates: `mu` (the mean), `alpha`/`beta` (the short-run GARCH), `gamma` (the asymmetry), `m` (the long-run intercept), `theta` (the sensitivity to the MIDAS covariate), `w2` (+ `w1` in the unrestricted case).
- `coefficients` — a `broom.mgarch` DataFrame: `estimate`, `rob.std.err` (sandwich/HAC), `p.value`, `opg.std.err`, `opg.p.value`. **Use the robust (`rob.std.err`) SE** for inference.
- `tau` — the long-run component (chart-data); `g` — the short-run component (chart-data). The total conditional variance = `tau × g`.
- `variance.ratio` — the share (%) of the total log variance explained by the **long-run** (macro) component; a low value ⇒ the macro variable adds little. `tau.forecast` — the one-step-ahead long-run forecast.
- `llh`/`bic` — for comparing models (e.g. different `x`/`K`/`weighting`). `residuals` — the standardised residuals (chart).
- `mfg_predict.forecast` — a vector of the **total** conditional variance per horizon (not tau or g separately); `horizon` = the horizons.
- `mfg_simulate` — `return`/`tau`/`g`/`real_vol` (chart-data) + `object` (the full DataFrame); the same `seed` (2025 by default) ⇒ the same path.

**Interpretation traps:**
- **Silent non-convergence**: `optim` returns a fit **even when `convergence != 0`** — ALWAYS check the field `converged` (logical) before trusting the parameters. A stateless node ⇒ stderr is lost, which is why the convergence goes into the returned list.
- **`x` not constant within a low.freq period** ⇒ the "ONE unique value" gate (the package would emit a cryptic "more than one unique observation per low frequency entry").
- `beta.restricted` ⇒ `w1=1` (a monotonically decreasing weighting of the lags); `beta.unrestricted` estimates `w1` as well.

**Sources:** the mfGARCH help (`fit_mfgarch`, `predict.mfGARCH`, `simulate_mfgarch`); Engle, Ghysels & Sohn 2013 "Stock Market Volatility and Macroeconomic Fundamentals" (Review of Economics and Statistics 95:776); Conrad & Kleen 2020 "Two are better than one: Volatility forecasting using multiplicative component GARCH-MIDAS" (Journal of Applied Econometrics 35:19); Ghysels, Santa-Clara & Valkanov 2004/2006 (MIDAS regressions).

### #160 The BEKK family of multivariate GARCH + a multivariate VaR + a Volatility IRF — `BEKKs` (`c06_volatility_regimes/bekk_family_multivariate.py`)
**Functions:** `bekk_estimate` [`bekk_spec`+`bekk_fit`, a PRODUCER], `bekk_var` [`VaR`], `bekk_virf` [`virf`]

**When:** you have an `N`-dimensional matrix of returns `T×N` (N>=2) and want a **full BEKK dynamic conditional covariance** — that is, to model not only the volatility of each series but also the **volatility spillovers / co-volatility** between them (the A/G matrices capture the cross-effects). Then: (a) `bekk_var` for a **portfolio or per-series VaR** from the estimated conditional covariances, (b) `bekk_virf` for **Volatility Impulse Response Functions** (how a shock to one series propagates into the volatility of all of them). The type map (the `type` argument):

| `type` | parameterisation | when |
|---|---|---|
| `"bekk"` (the default) | full BEKK (A, G full matrices) | you want the full cross-volatility dynamics; a small N |
| `"dbekk"` | diagonal BEKK (A, G diagonal) | fewer parameters; the spillovers only through the covariance |
| `"sbekk"` | scalar BEKK (A, G scalars) | the fewest parameters; the full BEKK is not identified |

`asymmetric=TRUE` adds a **leverage** structure (excess volatility on negative returns, weighted through `signs`).

**When NOT:** (a) a **large N** — the BEKK parameters scale as ~`O(N²)` (the curse of dimensionality); for N>~4 go to **DCC** (#155 `tm_dcc_estimate` / #29 `dcc_fit`). (b) A **univariate** series → a univariate GARCH (#28 `univariate_garch_family`). (c) You need an **asymmetric VIRF** — it is not implemented (only the symmetric BEKK).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Stationary returns:** GARCH presupposes (weakly) stationary returns — check with `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_suite.run_ur_test` before estimating.
- **A valid/stationary BEKK process:** after estimation read `bekk_valid` from `bekk_estimate` — `TRUE` means the estimated BEKK satisfies the stationarity condition; `FALSE` ⇒ it is degenerate and the VaR/VIRF are **unreliable**. The gate `.bk_check_y` enforces a numeric `T×N` (N>=2), no NA, and enough rows (`T >= 3N`).
- **Data source:** if it comes from a file, load the `T×N` matrix through `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#155 `tm_dcc_estimate` (tsmarch)** or **#29 `dcc_fit` (rmgarch)** — mandatory when N is large; a scalable conditional correlation instead of a full BEKK covariance.
- **`type="dbekk"`/`"sbekk"`** — when the full BEKK is not identified (too many parameters for the sample).
- **`c12_distribution_risk/value_risk_expected.pa_var`** — when you want a non-model-based (historical/gaussian/modified) VaR without MGARCH dynamics.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `bekk_valid` — **read it FIRST**: `FALSE` ⇒ a non-stationary/degenerate process, do not use the VaR/VIRF. It is **not blocked** (a valid output with a flag, since the node is stateless and stderr is lost).
- `log_likelihood`/`AIC`/`BIC` — the fit/model selection among bekk/dbekk/sbekk. `theta` — the estimated parameters (in vech form).
- `C0`/`A`/`G` — the parameter matrices: `C0` the lower-triangular intercept, `A` the ARCH (short-run shock) matrix, `G` the GARCH (persistence) matrix. The off-diagonal elements = the cross-volatility spillovers.
- `sigma_t` — the `T × N(N+1)/2` conditional st.dev/covariance path (chart-data).
- `bekk_var`: `var_values` — **`portfolio_weights=NULL` ⇒ per series (N columns)**; a vector of length N ⇒ the portfolio VaR (1 column). `distribution` **defaults to `normal`**; `empirical` **requires >=1000 obs** (an explicit gate); `t` for fat tails. `p` in the open (0,1) (a gate).
- `bekk_virf`: `virf`/`virf_upper`/`virf_lower` — `n_ahead × N(N+1)/2` responses + the `ci` bands. **The symmetric BEKK only** — an asymmetric object is blocked by a clear gate. `time`∈`1.T`, `q`∈(0,1), `index_series`∈`1.N`, `n_ahead>=1`, `ci`∈(0,1) (all gated).

**Sources:** Engle & Kroner 1995 (*Econometric Theory* 11:122, the BEKK parameterisation); Hafner & Herwartz 2006 (*J. Int. Money & Finance* 25:719, Volatility Impulse Responses); the BEKKs help (`bekk_spec`, `bekk_fit`, `VaR`, `virf`) < the Basel Committee (a VaR at 99% confidence, the default `p`).

### #161 (Hierarchical) Hidden Markov Models + Viterbi decoding + forecasting — `fHMM` (`c06_volatility_regimes/hidden_markov_viterbi.py`)
**Functions:** `hmm_fit` [`set_controls`+`prepare_data`+`fit_model`, a PRODUCER], `hmm_decode` [`decode_states` — Viterbi global decoding], `hmm_predict` [`predict.fHMM_model` — states + observations ahead]

**When:** you have a univariate series (returns or observations) that you believe is governed by latent discrete **regimes** (e.g. bull/bear, low/high volatility) and want a full **Hidden Markov Model**: an invisible Markov chain over `k` states, with a state-dependent distribution (`normal`/`t`/`gamma`/`lognormal`/`poisson`) per state, estimated by maximum likelihood. In addition you want to **decode** the most likely sequence of states (Viterbi) and to **forecast** future states/observations. The config-heavy `controls` list of fHMM is built **internally** from the simple arguments `{data, nstates, sdd}` (hierarchy=FALSE).

| argument | what it does | default |
|---|---|---|
| `nstates` | the number of hidden states of the Markov chain (>=2) | 2 |
| `sdd` | the state-dependent distribution: `normal`/`lognormal`/`t`/`gamma`/`poisson` | `normal` |
| `runs` | randomly initialised optimisation runs (the best is selected) | 5 |
| `iterlim` | the iteration limit of nlm per run | 100 |
| `seed` | reproducibility (ncluster=1, single core) | 2025 |

**When NOT:** (a) when the regimes concern **volatility clustering** (the conditional variance) rather than the level/mean → #31 `msg_fit_ml`/`msg_fit_mcmc` (MSGARCH). (b) A Markov-switching **linear** model with exogenous regressors → #30 `msw_fit` (MSwM). (c) Regimes determined by an **observable threshold** variable (self-exciting) instead of a latent Markov chain → #32 `setar_fit`/`lstar_fit` (tsDyn). (d) Hierarchical/multi-scale data on two levels (coarse+fine) — the `hierarchy=TRUE` HHMM is **not exposed** (it requires two levels of data, which does not map onto a single `num_array`).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Data**: a numeric vector of `>= 20` observations, free of NA/Inf, non-constant (the gate `.fhmm_check_data`). fHMM accepts NA silently in `prepare_data` — the gate protects against it.
- **The support of the distribution**: `gamma`/`lognormal` require strictly **positive** data; `poisson` requires **non-negative integers** (explicit gates). For raw returns → `normal` or `t`.
- **Convergence**: after `hmm_fit`, check `converged` (nlm_code ∈ {1,2}) and `n_accepted_runs` **before** interpreting anything — the stateless node loses stderr, so the diagnostics are returned in the list.
- **Decoding**: `hmm_decode` returns `degenerate=TRUE` if fewer than `nstates` states are used (the solution collapsed).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#31 MSGARCH** — the regimes are in the *volatility* (the conditional variance), not in the level.
- **#30 MSwM** — Markov switching with RHS regressors (a linear model per regime).
- **#32 tsDyn SETAR/LSTAR** — the regimes are triggered by an observable threshold, not by a latent chain.
- **`sdd = "t"`** instead of `"normal"` — fat tails in the returns within a regime.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `hmm_fit`: `logLik`/`AIC`/`BIC`/`npar`/`nobs`; `estimates` — a DataFrame `parameter/lb/estimate/ub` (chart-data): `Gamma_i.j` = the transition probabilities, `mu_s`/`sigma_s`/`df_s` = the state-dependent parameters per state with a 95% CI. `nstates`/`sdd`. **Convergence**: `nlm_code`/`converged`/`n_accepted_runs`.
- `hmm_decode`: `states` — an integer sequence of length `T` (the most likely path, Viterbi); `state_counts`/`state_labels`; `n_states_used`; `degenerate`.
- `hmm_predict`: `state_probs` — the `ahead × nstates` probabilities of the future states; `diebold_mariano_tscv` — the `ahead × {lb,estimate,ub}` predicted observations. **Note**: `predict.fHMM_model` requires a decoded model, so `hmm_predict` runs `decode_states` **internally** (deterministically).
- **A label-switching trap**: the numbering of the states (1/2/..) is **not** inherently ordered — identify the regimes through the `mu`/`sigma` in `estimates`, not through the index. **A convergence trap**: `degenerate=TRUE` or `converged=FALSE` ⇒ do not interpret the regimes (increase `runs`/change `sdd`). **An IC trap**: AIC/BIC are comparable only on the same data & within the same `sdd` family.

**Determinism:** `fit_model(ncluster=1, seed=2025)`; `decode`/`predict` are deterministic; the compute cost is SMALL (`runs=5`, `iterlim=100`, `nstates=2`). The generics are package-qualified (`coef/logLik/AIC/BIC/predict`, `npar/decode_states/set_controls/prepare_data/fit_model`) — avoiding search-path collisions in the heavy category 06.

**Sources:** the fHMM vignette/help (`help("set_controls","fHMM")`, `fit_model`, `decode_states`, `predict.fHMM_model`) — Oelschläger, Adam & Michels, *fHMM* < Zucchini, MacDonald & Langrock 2016, *Hidden Markov Models for Time Series* 2nd ed. (Viterbi global decoding §5); Hamilton 1989 (Econometrica 57:357) markov-switching regimes.

### #162 Bayesian univariate Stochastic Volatility (vanilla / Student-t / leverage) — `bayesian_univariate_stochastic` (`c06_volatility_regimes/bayesian_univariate_stochastic.py`)
**Functions:** `sv_sample` [`svsample`/`svtsample`/`svlsample` — dispatched through `model`], `sv_predict` [`predict.svdraws` via `predict`], `sv_simulate` [`svsim`]

**When:** you have a univariate series of **returns** and want to model the **volatility as a latent (unobservable) stochastic process** — the log-variance `h_t` ~ AR(1) — with a **full Bayesian posterior**. Unlike GARCH (where the volatility is a deterministic function of past returns), SV gives you **uncertainty (posterior bands) around the volatility path itself**. The variant map (the `model` argument):

| `model` | fn | what it adds | when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"vanilla"` (the default) | `svsample` | Gaussian innovations | the basic SV; returns without extreme tails |
| `"t"` | `svtsample` | Student-t errors (it estimates `nu`) | fat tails beyond what the stochastic volatility itself delivers |
| `"leverage"` | `svlsample` | a correlation `rho` between the shock and the volatility (it estimates `rho`) | asymmetry / the leverage effect (negative returns ⇒ higher volatility) |

`sv_predict` gives the **posterior predictive** of the future volatility (a point + intervals); `sv_simulate` generates a synthetic SV path (a data-generating / prior-predictive check).

**When NOT:** (a) you want point/ML volatility or closed-form multi-step forecasts → GARCH **#28** (`univariate_garch_family`/`univariate_garch_family_2`). (b) Multivariate volatility + a time-varying correlation → DCC **#29** (`dcc_mgarch`/`multivariate_garch_dynamic`). (c) The volatility changes **regime** (Markov switching) instead of following a continuous AR(1) log-volatility → **#31** `MSGARCH`. (d) Very large samples with a tight latency budget — the MCMC is expensive (which is why the node has small default draws/burnin).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **`y` is returns, not price levels.** SV works on `log(y^2)` (demeaned); price levels ⇒ nonsense. Load/prepare the series (`c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`) as returns. The gate `.sv_check_y`: a numeric vector, of length > 1, free of NA/Inf (the package's own message "should be numeric; not double" is misleading — the gate comes first with a clear message).
- **Convergence first:** `sv_sample` returns `converged`/`min_ess`. Because the node is stateless (stderr is lost), the convergence is **recorded in the returned list**. `converged=FALSE` ⇒ insufficient mixing (typically `phi` has a low ESS) — **do not interpret the posteriors**; increase `draws`/`burnin`.
- **Prior/DGP sanity:** `sv_simulate` for a prior-predictive or data-generating check before fitting to real data.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#28 `ga_fit` (rugarch) / tsgarch** — a deterministic ML GARCH with closed-form forecasts, when you do not need a latent-SV posterior.
- **#31 `msg_fit_mcmc` (MSGARCH)** — when the volatility changes discretely between regimes.
- **#29 `dcc_fit` (rmgarch)** — multivariate volatility/correlation.
- **`model="t"` / `model="leverage"`** — within the same node: fat tails or leverage instead of vanilla.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `para_summary` — a matrix `mean/sd/5%/50%/95%/ESS` per parameter. **`mu`** = the level of the log-variance (⇒ `exp(mu/2)` = the typical volatility in calm times), **`phi`** = the persistence (close to 1 ⇒ an almost non-stationary/very persistent volatility; close to 0 ⇒ volatility ~ white noise), **`sigma`** = the vol-of-vol, **`nu`** (`t` only) = the degrees of freedom, **`rho`** (`leverage` only) = the leverage correlation.
- `ess` / `min_ess` / `converged` — the convergence capture; the **main trap**: SV MCMC can silently have monstrous autocorrelation, so **read `converged` before anything else**. The defaults (500 draws) are smoke-test level.
- `vol_mean` (+ `vol_time`) — the posterior mean of `exp(h_t/2)` per time point, chart-data. **It is a standard deviation, not a variance** — do not compare it directly with a GARCH conditional variance. `NULL` when `keeptime="last"`.
- `sv_predict`: `vol_mean`/`vol_median` + `vol_lower` (5%)/`vol_upper` (95%) per step — the posterior predictive bands of the future volatility (always `vol_lower ≤ vol_upper`).
- `sv_simulate`: `y` (the returns), `vol` (the **true** latent volatility that was generated), `para` — chart-data for the synthetic path.
- **Determinism:** all three paths are stochastic (MCMC / a forward simulation / `svsim`) → `set.seed(seed=2025)` always; the same seed ⇒ the same results (a reproducible node).

**Sources:** the stochvol help/vignette (`help("svsample","stochvol")`, `svtsample`, `svlsample`, `svsim`, `predict.svdraws`) — Kastner (2016) "Dealing with Stochastic Volatility in Time Series Using the reference Package **stochvol**", JSS 69(5) < Kastner & Frühwirth-Schnatter (2014) ASIS interweaving, CSDA 76:408 (the sampler); Jacquier, Polson & Rossi (1994) JBES 12:371 (the Bayesian SV foundations).

---
### #163 Multivariate factor stochastic volatility (Bayesian MCMC) — `multivariate_factor_stochastic` (`c06_volatility_regimes/multivariate_factor_stochastic.py`)
**Functions:** `fsv_sample` [`fsvsample` — a PRODUCER: MCMC posterior draws], `fsv_cov` [`covmat`+`cormat` — the posterior-mean model-implied cov/cor at the last t], `fsv_predict` [`predcov`+`predcor` — the posterior predictive h-step cov/cor]

**When:** you have multivariate returns (a small-to-medium N) and want a **time-varying covariance/correlation** with a parsimonious factor structure (a few latent factors), where every idiosyncratic and factor log-volatility follows **stochastic-volatility** dynamics, AND you want full Bayesian **posterior uncertainty** (not only a point estimate). Typical uses: portfolio co-movement, time-varying correlations between macro series, communalities (how "common" the risk is).

**When NOT:** (a) a univariate series → univariate SV (`sv_sample`). (b) You want a point-estimate parametric **MGARCH** (DCC/GO-GARCH) → `rmgarch dcc_fit` / `tsmarch tm_dcc_estimate`. (c) A very large N without a plausible factor structure. (d) Too few observations (<~50) for a reliable MCMC.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **The input** `y` = a `T×N` matrix of returns with **>=2 columns** and **>=10 rows**, **free of NA** (`fsvsample` throws a cryptic "Couldn't Cholesky-decompose" — the gate `.fsv_check_y` blocks it cleanly) and **without constant/zero-variance columns** (silently wrong, verified live — the returns are undefined). If you load from a file: `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`.
- **factors** an integer in `1.N` (the gate `factors <= N`; more factors than series = a degenerate over-parameterisation). `draws`/`seed` positive integers, `burnin` non-negative.
- **Identification:** the output returns `ledermann_bound` + `exceeds_ledermann`. The package **deliberately allows** more factors than the static Ledermann bound (the loadings are partly identified through the time-varying volatilities), which is why there is NO hard gate — only an interpretation caveat.
- **Output checks:** `fsv_cov` (the posterior-mean cov/cor at the last t — plausible magnitudes/positive diagonal) and `fsv_predict` (the h-step predictive).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`rmgarch dcc_fit` / `tsmarch tm_dcc_estimate`** — when you want a parametric DCC/GO-GARCH point-estimate MGARCH instead of a Bayesian factor structure.
- **`stochvol sv_sample`** — a univariate series (you do not need a multivariate covariance).
- **`restrict="upper"`** instead of the default `"none"` — when you need identifiable/interpretable factor loadings (not only the covariance); it stabilises the MCMC, but it is a strong a-priori assumption.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `fsv_sample.facload_mean` — the posterior-mean matrix of factor loadings `N × factors`; which series load (by size/pattern) on the common factors. **A trap:** the signs of the loadings/factors are NOT identified by the likelihood (sign switching) — interpret magnitudes/patterns, not absolute signs.
- `fsv_sample.communalities` (per series) + `communality_total` — the share of variance explained by the factors (common vs idiosyncratic risk).
- `fsv_sample.para_mean` — the posterior-mean `mu/phi/sigma` per idiosyncratic & factor log-volatility process; `phi`→1 = a highly persistent volatility.
- `fsv_sample.ledermann_bound`/`exceeds_ledermann` — see the Preconditions; TRUE = take care in interpreting the loadings.
- `fsv_cov.cov_mean`/`cor_mean` (+ `cov_sd`/`cor_sd`) — the posterior **mean** & posterior **sd** of the conditional covariance/correlation **at the last t** (keeptime="last" = the current one, not the whole path). The matrices are symmetric, with a unit `cor` diagonal.
- `fsv_predict.pred_cov_mean`/`pred_cor_mean` — a **list** of posterior-mean matrices per horizon (the key = `ahead`, e.g. `"1"`,`"5"`,`"10"`).
- **An MCMC trap:** a small `draws`/`burnin` → noise in the posterior; read the `*_sd` fields as well for the uncertainty, not only the means. Determinism through `seed` (2025 by default).

**Sources:** the factorstochvol vignette/help (`help("fsvsample","factorstochvol")`, `covmat`, `cormat`, `predcov`, `predcor`, `ledermann`) — factorstochvol 1.1.2 < Kastner, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Lopes 2017, "Efficient Bayesian Inference for Multivariate Factor Stochastic Volatility Models", *JCGS* 26(4):905-917; Kastner 2019, "Sparse Bayesian time-varying covariance estimation in many dimensions", *J. Econometrics* 210(1):98-115 (the Normal-Gamma shrinkage prior).

---
### #164 Discrete-time Markov chains: estimating the transition matrix (MLE/Laplace/bootstrap CI) + long-run analytics (the stationary distribution, mean first passage times, irreducibility, period) — `discrete_time_markov` (`c06_volatility_regimes/discrete_time_markov.py`)
**Functions:** `mc_fit`, `mc_analytics`

**When:** a discrete sequence of states (regimes/ratings/states); you want the estimated transition matrix, the long-run (stationary) distribution, the expected first passage times, or a check of irreducibility/period

**When NOT:** continuous return/volatility series (-> GARCH #28/#33/#34); latent-regime switching over continuous observations (-> MSwM #30/MSGARCH #31); a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC); higher-order/order-selection dependence

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `mc_fit (it produces the 'markovchain' object -> the input to mc_analytics)`
- `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the sequence of states from a file)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **MSwM msw_fit (#30)** — the regimes are latent over a continuous observed series, not directly observable states
- **MSGARCH msg_spec/msg_fit_* (#31)** — Markov switching in the variance of continuous returns
- **fHMM (#32)** — a hidden Markov model with emission distributions instead of observable states

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- transitionMatrix: the estimated transition matrix (rows=from, they sum to 1)
- standardError / lowerEndpointMatrix / upperEndpointMatrix: the SE + CI per element (confidenceLevel)
- logLikelihood: the log-likelihood of the fit
- steadyStates: the stationary distribution (a matrix; >1 row if there are several recurrent classes)
- meanFirstPassageTime: the expected number of steps i->j (diagonal=0); NULL + mfpt_note if not ergodic
- is_irreducible / period: an irreducibility bool + the period (NA + period_note if not irreducible)

**Interpretation traps:**
- markovchainFit does NOT fail on NA (it treats them as a separate state) & it accepts a single state — the wrapper's gates block both explicitly
- steadyStates returns a MATRIX: >1 row means several closed recurrent classes (a non-unique stationary distribution)
- period emits a WARNING (not an error) on a non-irreducible chain -> the wrapper returns NA+a note, do not interpret an invalid value
- meanFirstPassageTime requires an ergodic (irreducible) chain -> NULL+a note otherwise, not an error that would blow up the node
- method='bootstrap' is STOCHASTIC (a resampling CI) -> use the same seed for reproducibility; mle/laplace are deterministic

**Sources:** Spedicato, 'Discrete Time Markov Chains with the reference', 2017 (the markovchain vignette) · help('markovchainFit','markovchain'), steadyStates, meanFirstPassageTime, period, is.irreducible · Norris 1997, Markov Chains (CUP) — the stationary distribution, first passage, periodicity.

---

### #183 Bayesian time-varying-parameter (TVP) regression with global-local shrinkage (triple/double/ridge) + SV — `shrinkTVP` (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/bayesian_time_varying.py`)
**Functions:** `stvp_fit`, `stvp_forecast`, `stvp_lpds`

**When:** a single equation y ~ x; you suspect the coefficients CHANGE over time (structural breaks, shifting elasticities); you want a full posterior + automatic shrinkage towards a constant coefficient wherever no variation is needed

**When NOT:** constant coefficients suffice (OLS/#46); multivariate joint dynamics (VAR/#.. 03); a pure trend/cycle decomposition of a single series (#56-61 filters/state-space); very large samples (the MCMC cost)

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the panel/time series as a numeric DataFrame)`
- `stvp_lpds (the out-of-sample log predictive density: compare mod_type / TVP vs constant on a hold-out)`
- `stvp_forecast (a predictive forecast with future values of the regressors)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **dlm/KFAS/bssm (#58-60) state-space** — you want a structural trend/cycle/seasonal decomposition or Kalman filtering, not a TVP regression with shrinkage
- **#46 plm/OLS with constant coefficients** — theta_sr ~0 for ALL the coefficients — there is no time variation, the constant model suffices
- **mod_type='ridge'** — you want a TVP without global-local shrinkage (a baseline; it does not shrink towards a constant)
- **brms/rstan (category 14)** — a non-Gaussian likelihood or a hierarchical structure beyond TVP+SV

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- beta_paths: per covariate, the posterior median + the 95% CI of the time-varying coefficient (chart-data, of length n_obs+1: the states t=0.T)
- theta_sr_median: sqrt(theta), the state standard deviation per covariate; ~0 => the coefficient is CONSTANT (the shrinkage shrank it), a large value => substantial time variation
- beta_mean_median: the constant (mean) level of each coefficient
- sigma2_median: the observation variance — a scalar if sv=FALSE, a path (of length n_obs) if sv=TRUE
- shrinkage: a_xi/a_tau (double/triple only)/kappa2_B/lambda2_B — the global shrinkage hyperparameters
- stvp_forecast: pred_median/pred_lower/pred_upper per horizon; stvp_lpds: lpds (larger=a better forecast)

**Interpretation traps:**
- theta_sr is the sqrt of the variance AND non-centred (it can come out negative in the posterior sample; what matters is the ABSOLUTE value/the distance from 0) — |theta_sr|~0 means a constant coefficient, NOT a zero coefficient (see beta_mean)
- beta_paths have n_obs+1 points (the initial state t=0 is included); beta_time runs 0.T
- stvp_forecast REQUIRES future values of the regressors (newdata); it does not forecast the x by itself — nrow(newdata) >= n.ahead, otherwise it fails
- stvp_lpds accepts EXACTLY 1 hold-out row (the package fails otherwise); compare mod_type through the sum of the LPDS over a rolling hold-out
- ridge has NO a_xi/a_tau (it does no shrinkage selection); do not look for shrinkage fields there
- the MCMC is stochastic: the seed is mandatory; a different seed => different (but compatible) posterior summaries

**Sources:** Knaus, Bitto-Nemling, Cadonna & Frühwirth-Schnatter, 'Shrinkage in the Time-Varying Parameter Model Framework Using the reference Package shrinkTVP', JSS 2021 (the shrinkTVP vignette) · help('shrinkTVP','shrinkTVP'), help('forecast_shrinkTVP'), help('LPDS'), help('simTVP') · Bitto & Frühwirth-Schnatter 2019 (J. Econometrics 210:75, the Normal-Gamma / double shrinkage) · Cadonna, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Knaus 2020 (Econometrics 8:20, the triple gamma prior) · Frühwirth-Schnatter & Wagner 2010 (J. Econometrics 154:85, the non-centred parameterisation / theta_sr).

### #184 Bayesian regression with time-varying (random-walk) coefficients — HMC — `bayesian_regression_time` (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/bayesian_regression_time.py`)
**Functions:** `walker_fit` [`bayesian_regression_time` (gaussian) / `walker_glm` (poisson/binomial), the terms `rw1`/`rw2`], `walker_coef` [`coef.walker_fit` — the time-varying posterior median + a 95% CI]

**When:** you have a regression `y ~ x1 + x2` whose **coefficients change over time** instead of being constant — that is, structural change / time-varying elasticities / shifting sensitivities (e.g. a pass-through, or an Okun/Phillips slope that drifts). The coefficients are modelled as random walks:

| `rw_order` | the coefficient dynamics | when |
|---|---|---|
| `"rw1"` (the default) | a 1st-order random walk (a level) — the coefficient "wanders" | a smooth, non-directional change |
| `"rw2"` | 2nd order (local linear, with a slope `nu`) — smoother, with a local trend | the coefficient has a persistent slope/trend |

`family` selects the likelihood: `gaussian` → `bayesian_regression_time`; `poisson`/`binomial` (counts) → `walker_glm` (a Gaussian approximation + importance weighting). Time = **the row order** of the DataFrame. The estimation is Hamiltonian MC (Stan) with the coefficients marginalised through the state space (efficient sampling). The compute cost is SMALL: `chains=1`, `iter=400`, precompiled Stan models (no runtime compilation), a mandatory `seed` (2025 by default).

**When NOT:** (a) the coefficients are constant → a classical `lm`/GLM (or brms for a Bayesian constant model). (b) You want a pure trend/cycle extraction **without** regressors → the filters/state-space nodes #56–61. (c) You need a formal **out-of-sample forecast** — it is not exposed here (only in-sample time-varying inference). (d) A very large `n` or many covariates → the HMC becomes expensive; keep the model small.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A time-ordered DataFrame**: each row = one time point, in the correct order (the walk is defined over the row order). Loading: `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`. The gate `.wk_check_data`: a DataFrame, ≥5 rows, all the variables present, a numeric `y`, free of NA.
- **Counts for the glm**: `family="poisson"`/`"binomial"` requires the response to be **non-negative integers** — `walker_glm` accepts anything else **silently**; the gate blocks it. `u` (the exposures/trials) positive, of length 1 or n; for binomial `y ≤ u`.
- **Convergence BEFORE interpretation**: `walker_fit` returns `max_rhat`, `n_divergent`, `converged` — check that `converged=TRUE` (Rhat<1.1 & 0 divergences) before reading any coefficient.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`c14_bayesian_toolkit/bayesian_regression.br_fit`** — when you want a hierarchical/multilevel or non-Gaussian GLM **without** a time-varying structure (constant or group-varying coefficients, a full posterior).
- **`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/bayesian_state_space.bs_run_mcmc`** — a general (non-linear/non-Gaussian) state space with particle MCMC, when the HMC-marginalised approach of walker does not suffice.
- **`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/kalman_filter_smoother.kf_local_linear_trend`** — a purely frequentist state-space trend/level **without** time-varying regression coefficients.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `converged` / `max_rhat` / `n_divergent` — the **convergence gate**. `converged=FALSE` ⇒ unreliable; increase `iter`/strengthen the priors. **A trap**: the small `iter=400` produces low-ESS warnings deliberately (this is a node) — increase it for a final analysis.
- `coef_names` / `n_time_varying` — the time-varying coefficients (it includes the time-varying `(Intercept)`/level that the `rw` term adds; the wrapper inserts `-1 +` so that only **one** remains — identifiability).
- `sigma_summary` — the posterior of the standard deviations: `sigma_y` = the observation sd (gaussian); `sigma_rw*` = the **rate of change** of each coefficient. **A trap**: `sigma_rw*`→0 ⇒ the coefficient is practically **constant**; a large value ⇒ strong time variation.
- `fitted` — the posterior mean fitted values (`y_fit`), chart-data.
- `walker_coef.coef_table` — long records `{beta, time, median, lower, upper, mean, sd}`: the **trajectory** of each coefficient over time with a 95% CI (chart-data; `beta` = the coefficient name). **A trap**: for poisson/binomial the coefficients are on the **link scale** — use `exponentiate=TRUE` for a multiplicative interpretation.

**Sources:** the walker vignette & help (`help("walker","walker")`, `help("walker_glm","walker")`, `coef.walker_fit`) — Helske J. (2022), *walker: Bayesian Generalized Linear Models with Time-Varying Coefficients* < Vihola, Helske & Franks (2020), "Importance sampling type estimators based on approximate marginal MCMC", *Scandinavian Journal of Statistics* 47(4):1339–1376 (the exact-approximate weighting of `walker_glm`); Durbin & Koopman (2012), *Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods* 2nd ed. (the state-space representation of random-walk coefficients).

### #185 Particle filtering (bootstrap) log-likelihood + iterated filtering (IF2) MLE for non-linear non-Gaussian state-space models — `particle_filter_log` (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/particle_filter_log.py`)
**Functions:** `pomp_pfilter`, `pomp_mif2`

**When:** a non-linear / non-Gaussian state-space model where the Kalman filter does not apply; you want a particle-filter log-likelihood (pomp_pfilter) or a simulation-based MLE (pomp_mif2) over one of the built-in templates gompertz/ricker/ou2

**When NOT:** a linear-Gaussian model (use KFAS/dlm/MARSS/bssm — an exact Kalman filter); you want custom dynamics outside the three templates (that requires C code, blocked for security reasons); a full Bayesian posterior of the parameters (pmcmc/bssm)

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `pomp_pfilter (run the particle filter first: check for a finite loglik & the min_ess before IF2)`
- `pomp_mif2 (the IF2 MLE; check the converged field & the loglik_trace for convergence)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **KFAS/dlm/MARSS/bssm (category 10)** — the model is linear-Gaussian -> an exact Kalman filter, not a particle approximation
- **the bssm bootstrap/psi particle filter** — you want Bayesian inference (MCMC) with a particle filter instead of a point MLE
- **a larger Np / more Nmif** — a low min_ess (particle depletion) or a non-converging loglik_trace

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- loglik: the particle-filter log-likelihood (pomp_pfilter) or the final IF2 loglik (pomp_mif2); a Monte Carlo estimate, it varies with Np/the seed
- eff_sample_size / min_ess (pomp_pfilter): the ESS per time point; a low min_ess -> particle depletion, increase Np
- cond_logLik (pomp_pfilter): the conditional log-likelihood per time point (chart-data)
- estimates / estimated (pomp_mif2): the final values of ALL the params + which names were estimated
- loglik_trace / traces (pomp_mif2): the loglik & the parameter path per IF2 iteration — a convergence diagnostic (chart-data)
- converged: a finite loglik (& estimates); a stateless-node flag instead of stderr

**Interpretation traps:**
- the loglik is a STOCHASTIC Monte Carlo estimate — two runs with a different seed/Np give a different value; compare only at the same seed/Np
- a low min_ess (e.g. << Np) means particle depletion -> the loglik is unreliable, NOT that the model is bad; increase Np
- IF2 (pomp_mif2) has NO hard convergence test — judge the convergence from the loglik_trace (it must stabilise) & the converged flag, not from a single run
- the initial-value params (…_0, e.g. X_0/N_0/x1_0) are NOT perturbed by default; to estimate them, pass them explicitly in estimate
- SECURITY: ONLY the built-in templates are exposed; there is no way to supply custom C dynamics (the compile/eval surface is blocked)

**Sources:** King, Nguyen & Ionides, 'Statistical Inference for Partially Observed Markov Processes via the reference Package pomp', JSS 2016 < · help('pfilter','pomp'), help('mif2','pomp'), help('gompertz','pomp'), help('ricker','pomp'), help('ou2','pomp') · Ionides, Nguyen, Atchadé, Stoev & King 2015, 'Inference for dynamic and latent variable models via iterated, perturbed Bayes maps', PNAS 112(3):719 (the IF2 algorithm) · Arulampalam et al. 2002, IEEE Trans. Signal Processing 50(2):174 (the bootstrap particle filter).
