### #186 BEAST — a Bayesian trend + seasonality + change-point decomposition — `Rbeast` (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/beast_bayesian_decomposition.py`)
**Functions:** `beast_decompose` [`beast`, method="bayes"; a PRODUCER — it registers `object`], `beast_changepoints` [the extraction of change points from a fitted `beast`; a CONSUMER — the `raw_handle` `object`]

**When:** you have a **regular (evenly spaced)** time series and want AT THE SAME TIME (a) a decomposition into **trend + seasonality** and (b) the detection of **structural breaks / change points with posterior PROBABILITIES** — not a point "yes/no" decision. BEAST performs Bayesian model averaging over all the possible configurations (the number & position of the change points, the trend/harmonic order) and produces, per time point, a **curve of the probability of a change** (`cpOccPr`). Ideal when the number and position of the breaks are **unknown** and you need explicit uncertainty.

**When NOT:** (a) **irregular** / unevenly spaced sampling — that needs `beast.irreg` (outside the node's scope, not exposed). (b) A pure estimate of the **output gap / potential output** → #56 `mFilter` (HP/BK/CF) or #92 `sided_hp_filter`. (c) One **known** break at a known date → strucchange/Chow (#4 structural). (d) An explicit linear-Gaussian **state-space** unobserved-components model (level+slope+seasonal) with Kalman smoothing → #58 `KFAS` / #59 `dynamic_linear`.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A regular numeric series without gaps:** `beast_decompose` requires `y` = a num_array **free of NA/NaN/Inf** (a hard gate). Critical: BEAST **interpolates the NA silently** — the wrapper blocks that for determinism/transparency. Load the series with `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`.
- **An explicit `period` for the seasonality:** `season="harmonic"` or `"dummy"` **requires** `period >= 2` (and `length(y) >= 2*period`). Without it BEAST silently guesses the periodicity (non-deterministic) — the wrapper blocks that. `season="none"` = trend-only (`period` is ignored).
- **The PRODUCER→CONSUMER flow:** run `beast_decompose` (it registers `object`) → pass the handle to `beast_changepoints(object, component, threshold)` for a filtered extraction of the change points.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#56 `mFilter` / #92 `sided_hp_filter`** — if you only want the trend/cycle gap **without** change-point uncertainty.
- **strucchange / Bai-Perron (#4)** — a frequentist multiple-break test with explicit break dates + SC/BIC (not a posterior).
- **#58 `KFAS` / #59 `dynamic_linear`** — an explicit linear-Gaussian state-space UC model with smoothing/forecasting.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `trend$Y` + `trend$SD` — the fitted trend + the posterior SD per time point; use them as a band (chart-data). `season_component$Y` (+ `.amp`) is the seasonal component (**NULL** if `season="none"`).
- `trend.cpOccPr` — **the main chart-data**: the per-time posterior change-probability curve, of length `n`, ∈[0,1]. **A trap:** it differs from `cpPr` — the former is the curve over time, the latter the probability of the top detected change points.
- `trend.cp` / `trend.cpPr` / `trend.cpCI` — the change-point positions (in decreasing probability), the probability of each, the credible interval of the position. The wrapper **has already filtered out the NaN padding** (BEAST returns the maximum number of slots with NaN at the end — do not read the raw slots).
- `trend.ncp` / `ncp_median` / `ncp_mode` — **a trap:** `ncp` is the posterior **MEAN** (not an integer, e.g. 0.14) — NOT a fixed number of breaks; for a decision read `ncp_median`/`ncp_mode` + `cpPr`.
- `R2` / `RMSE` / `marg_lik` / `sig2` — the goodness of fit, the marginal likelihood, the noise.
- `beast_changepoints` → `n_cp`/`cp`/`cpPr`/`cpCI` filtered by `threshold` (it keeps only the change points with `cpPr >= threshold`), + the `order` and `cpOccPr` (the per-time curve) of the chosen component. `component="season"` is blocked on a trend-only fit.
- **Determinism:** stochastic MCMC; the same `seed` (2025 by default) ⇒ an identical result (confirmed live). The compute cost is TINY: `mcmc_samples~2000`, `mcmc_chains=1`.

**Sources:** `help("beast","Rbeast")` — Rbeast 1.0.2 (the arguments `season`/`period`/`tcp.minmax`/`scp.minmax`/`mcmc.*`); Zhao, Wulder et al. 2019, "Detecting change-point, trend, and seasonality in satellite time series data to track abrupt changes and nonlinear dynamics: A Bayesian ensemble algorithm", *Remote Sensing of Environment* 232:111181 (the BEAST algorithm); live introspection of the `.trend`/`.season` fields (`cpOccPr`/`cp`/`cpPr`/`cpCI`/`ncp`) + reproducibility with `mcmc.seed`.
### #187 Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Regression (AutoSTR) — `stR` (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/seasonal_trend_decomposition.py`)
**Functions:** `str_decompose` [`AutoSTR` + `components`], `str_seasadj` [`seasadj`]

**When:** you have a univariate **seasonal** series (a `ts`, or an `msts` for **multiple/complex** seasonality, e.g. weekly+annual) and want to decompose it into **a trend + one or more seasonal components + a remainder**, with **confidence intervals per component**. STR is a regression-based generalisation of STL: it supports (a) **multiple** seasonality, (b) **robust** estimation (`robust=TRUE`, M-estimation — it absorbs outliers/level shifts), (c) confidence intervals. `str_seasadj` returns the **seasonally adjusted** series (the sum of the selected components; by default Trend+Random ⇒ the seasonality is removed).

**When NOT:** (a) a **non-seasonal** series (`frequency<2`) — STR requires seasonality; go to #56 `mFilter` (HP/BK/CF) for a pure trend/cycle decomposition (the output gap). (b) **Forecasting** — STR decomposes, it does not forecast; for a forecast use a state-space model (#58-60) or an ARIMA on the `seasadj` series. (c) **Common latent trends across several series** — that is #61 MARSS DFA, not STR (which is univariate). (d) **Manual custom predictors/covariates** with knots/segments — that needs the low-level `STR` (outside the node's scope; the node exposes only the automatic `AutoSTR`).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A seasonal input**: `y` is a `ts`/`msts`, or a numeric vector + `frequency>=2`. The gate `.str_as_seasonal_ts`: it rejects `frequency<2` with a clear message (instead of the package's cryptic "Non-seasonal time series").
- **A complete series**: a **hard NA gate** — `AutoSTR` accepts NA *silently* and produces an unreliable result; the node requires the data to be filled in first.
- **Sufficient length**: `n >= 2 × max(seasonal period)` (at least 2 full cycles) — otherwise a gate.
- Loading the series from a file: `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited` before constructing the `ts`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#56 `mfl_hp_filter`** — when the series has **no** seasonality (only a trend/cycle).
- **#61 `marss_dfa`** — when you want **common** latent trends across several series (a dynamic factor model), not one.
- **#59 `dl_local_linear_trend(seasonal=TRUE)`** — when you want a state-space trend+seasonal model with filtering/forecasting rather than a pure decomposition.
- **`confidence=NULL`** — when you do not need CIs: it skips the computation (faster).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `components` — a named list of numeric vectors: `Data` (the original), `Trend`, one or more `Seasonality <period>` (e.g. `Seasonality 12`), `Random` (the remainder). Chart-data directly.
- `component_names` / `n_seasonal` — the column order and the number of seasonal components (`>1` for an `msts`).
- `confidence_intervals` — per **predictor** component (the Trend + each Seasonality) `{lower, upper}` vectors; **NULL** when `confidence=NULL`.
- `fitted` — `{fitted, lower, upper}` of the overall fit; NULL when `confidence=NULL`.
- `cvMSE` — the CV MSE of the lambda selection. **A trap**: on the **robust path** the package does not return it ⇒ `NA_real_`; do not read that as a perfect fit.
- `str_seasadj` → `seasadj` = the seasonally adjusted series (the sum of the `include` components; by default `Trend`+`Random`), together with `include`/`start`/`frequency`.
- **Interpretation traps**: (i) `seasadj` **silently ignores** unknown `include` names (a warning + skip → it also returns NULL) — the node **blocks** them with a hard gate (`include ⊆` the component names). (ii) The seasonal component names carry the period (`Seasonality 12`), not a bare "Seasonal".

**Sources:** Dokumentov & Hyndman, "STR: Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Regression", *INFORMS Journal on Data Science* 2022; the stR vignette/help (`help("AutoSTR","stR")`, `help("components","stR")`, `help("seasadj","stR")`, stR 0.7.1) < Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* 3rd ed. §3.7 (STL/STR decomposition).

### #188 STL decomposition (seasonal-trend-loess) tolerant of NA + short series — `stl_decomposition_tolerant` (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/stl_decomposition_tolerant.py`)
**Functions:** `stlplus_decompose`

**When:** a univariate seasonal series; you want a decomposition into seasonal/trend/remainder when there are NA (gaps) or the series is short / spans a non-integer number of periods

**When NOT:** multiple/changing seasonality (-> seasonal X-13 or STL with multiple s.window); a structural state-space model with uncertainty (#58 KFAS/#59 dlm); a pure trend/cycle output gap (#56 mFilter/#92 hpfilter)

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the series when it is not already a ts handle)`
- `stlplus_decompose (the decomposition itself; the robustness weights point to outliers)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **stl (base)** — no NA + complete integer periods; then base stl suffices
- **#56 mFilter (HP/BK/CF)** — you want only the trend/cycle (an output gap), not a seasonal term
- **seasonal X-13-ARIMA-SEATS** — an official seasonal adjustment with calendar/outlier regressors

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- seasonal/trend/remainder: numeric vectors of length n (raw = seasonal+trend+remainder at the non-NA points)
- raw: the original series (with NA at the gaps); weights: the outer-loop robustness weights (0.1, low = outliers)
- time: the numeric time index; n_obs/n_missing: the number of observations / of NA
- n.p/periodic/s.window/t.window/l.window/s.degree/t.degree: the final parameters that were used

**Interpretation traps:**
- an even s.window/t.window is SILENTLY rounded up to the next odd value by stlplus; the wrapper blocks it (an explicit odd-number gate) so that you do not think what you passed was used
- s.window='periodic' -> it forces s.degree=0 & a huge internal span (the seasonality is constant); for an evolving seasonality give a finite odd s.window
- the trend/seasonal components have NO NA even when raw does (block interpolation); the remainder is NA at the original gaps
- low weights (~0) = the points that the robust loop down-weighted as outliers, not an error
- s.degree=1/2 requires enough points per subseries; for very short series prefer s.window='periodic'

**Sources:** Cleveland, Cleveland, McRae & Terpenning 1990 (STL), J. Official Statistics 6:3-73 · stlplus : help('stlplus','stlplus') — Hafen, block interpolation + NA/short-series support · live introspection (btw): args(stlplus), the .data/.pars.win structure, edge-case probes.

### #189 Nonparametric detrending & the output gap (loess / a smoothing spline / the Friedman super smoother) — `stats` (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/nonparametric_detrending_output.py`)
**Functions:** `nonparametric_detrending_output`, `np_output_gap`

**When:** you want a trend/cycle or an output gap without a parametric trend form; a smooth, data-driven detrending of a series (loess/smooth.spline/supsmu); a fast atheoretical benchmark for the gap

**When NOT:** you want economic structure/potential output with shocks (KFAS/dlm/MARSS #58-61); a band-pass cycle at a specific frequency (mFilter BK/CF #56); a real-time/one-sided gap without end-point revision (the one-sided hpfilter #92, Hamilton #57); very short series (n<4)

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `np_detrend (take the trend+cycle; check that the cycle is mean-≈0 and looks stationary)`
- `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the series from a file before detrending)`

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#56 mfl_hp_filter / mfl_bk_filter / mfl_cf_filter** — you want an HP or band-pass cycle at a defined frequency instead of a free nonparametric trend
- **#92 hp_one_sided** — you need a real-time (one-sided) gap without revision of the end points
- **#57 hf_filter (Hamilton)** — you want a regression-based filter without the HP spurious-cycle problem
- **#58-61 KFAS/dlm/bssm/MARSS** — you want a structural unobserved-components/state-space potential output with shocks & credible bands
- **method='smooth.spline' (GCV)** — you want automatic selection of the smoothing instead of a manual span

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- trend: a numeric of the same length as y (the nonparametric trend; chart-data)
- cycle: y - trend (np_detrend; the cyclical component / the gap in levels)
- gap: the output gap according to the mode (np_output_gap; pct=% deviation, log=100*dlog, level=y-trend)
- smoother: the parameters per method — loess {span,degree,equivalent_df}; smooth.spline {spar,lambda,df,crit,cv}; supsmu {span}
- x/y/n: the index, the original series, the number of observations

**Interpretation traps:**
- atheoretical: the gap is statistical, NOT economic potential output — do not read it as structural
- end-point instability: loess/smooth.spline are two-sided -> the ends of the trend/gap are revised as new data arrive (like the HP filter); for real time use #92/#57
- smooth.spline spar↑ => a less flexible trend (a larger gap); span↑ in loess/supsmu => a smoother trend; the smoothing choice determines the amplitude of the gap
- mode='pct' requires trend != 0; mode='log' requires y>0 & trend>0 (explicit gates; for rates/growth around 0 use mode='level')
- supsmu sorts x internally; the trend is realigned back to the original order (approx) so that cycle = y - trend is correct

**Sources:** help('loess','stats'), help('smooth.spline','stats'), help('supsmu','stats') (the reference stats reference) · Cleveland, Grosse & Shyu 1992 (loess, local regression); Friedman 1984 SLAC PUB-3477 (the super smoother) · Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009 ESL §5 (smoothing splines, GCV) · Hamilton 2018 REStat 100:831 (the critique of the HP filter -> the motivation for atheoretical benchmarks).

### #200 A small linear(ised) DSGE — the Klein (2000) solution + Kalman ML estimation, IRFs, forecasts, a historical shock decomposition — `small_linear_dsge` (`c13_dsge_general_equilibrium/small_linear_dsge.py`)
**Functions:** `dsge_solve` [it builds the linear DSGE (the formula interface: `obs/unobs/state`) + `solve_dsge` Klein 2000 → the policy(G)/transition(H)/shock(M) matrices + saddle-path stability; it **registers** → `dsge_irf`], `dsge_estimate` [ML estimation of the params on observed data, the Kalman-filter log-likelihood, BFGS, delta-method SE + `stability`/`check_identification`; it **registers** → the consumers], `dsge_irf` [`irf` structural IRFs + CI bands], `dsge_forecast` [`diebold_mariano_tscv` model-consistent forecasts], `dsge_shock_decomposition` [`shock_decomposition` a historical decomposition + `smooth_shocks` the smoothed structural shocks]

**When:** you have a **small linearised DSGE** — log-linear equilibrium conditions with rational-expectations forward terms (`lead`/`E`), e.g. the **three-equation New Keynesian** model or a linearised RBC — and want the full macro pipeline: (a) a solution at calibrated params → policy/transition matrices + IRFs without data (`dsge_solve`), (b) **ML estimation** of the structural params on real observed macro series through the Kalman filter (`dsge_estimate`), (c) structural IRFs to fundamental shocks (`dsge_irf`), (d) forecasts (`dsge_forecast`), (e) a historical shock decomposition + smoothed shocks (`dsge_shock_decomposition`). The node enforces the **cross-equation RE restrictions** — that is what separates it from a reduced-form VAR/state-space model.

**When NOT:** (a) a large/**non-linear** DSGE with substantive non-linearities or occasionally binding constraints (you need Dynare / a higher-order perturbation — outside this linear formula node). (b) Atheoretical multivariate forecasting → #03 VAR/BVAR/factor models. (c) A general linear **state space** without RE cross-equation restrictions → #56-61 KFAS/dlm/MARSS/bssm. (d) A **Bayesian** DSGE (an RWMH posterior with priors) → a separate node (`bayes_dsge`, deliberately not exposed here). (e) `#shocks != #observed` (the Klein solver requires it — stochastic singularity).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Solve at calibrated params first** (`dsge_solve`): `stable==TRUE` (saddle path / Blanchard-Kahn) ⇒ the model is solvable before you attempt estimation; `stable==FALSE` ⇒ a non-unique/unstable solution, do NOT proceed.
- **Observed = stationary deviations**: `demean=TRUE` removes **only** the mean, NOT a trend/unit root. Check stationarity with `c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf` before `dsge_estimate`; load the data via `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited` (the column names == the observed controls).
- **#exogenous state shocks == #observed controls** (the hard gate `#state_eqs == #obs_eqs`); every equation passes through an **ACE sanitiser** (a character whitelist + the function calls `{lead,E}`) before `as.formula`.
- After estimation: `convergence==0` **and** `identification.identified==TRUE` before you interpret the coefficients/SE/IRFs.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#56-61 KFAS/dlm/MARSS/bssm** — a general linear state space (a local level/trend, unobserved components) **without** RE cross-equation restrictions.
- **#03 VAR/BVAR (Vars/bvartools)** — reduced-form dynamics/forecasting without structural microfoundations.
- **#04 svars/VARsignR** — structural shocks + IRFs with identification restrictions in a VAR (not a full DSGE structure).
- **`bayes_dsge` (dsge, not exposed)** — posterior distributions/credible bands with priors (adaptive RWMH) instead of ML point estimates + delta-method SE.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `dsge_solve`: `policy_matrix` (G, controls×states); `transition_matrix` (H); `shock_matrix` (M); `obs_matrix` (D); `eigenvalue_moduli`+`eigen_classification`; `stable`; `n_stable`/`n_states`; `object`=a dsge_solution.
- `dsge_estimate`: `coefficients`+`se` (the structural params + the log shock SD); `loglik` (Kalman); `nobs`; `convergence` (0=OK); `stable`; `identification{identified,rank,condition_number,strength,summary}`; `policy/transition_matrix`; `object`=a dsge_fit.
- `dsge_irf`: `irf`, a df `{period,impulse,response,value[,se,lower,upper]}`; `has_se` (TRUE only on a fit); `impulses`/`responses`; `source_class`.
- `dsge_forecast`: `forecasts` `{period,variable,value}`; `horizon`; `states` (h×n_states); `obs_matrix` (h×n_obs).
- `dsge_shock_decomposition`: `decomposition_by_obs` (per observed variable: T×{shocks…,initial}); `obs_names`/`shock_names`; `observed` (the deviations); `smoothed_shocks` ((T-1)×n_shocks).
- **Traps**: saddle-path stability is a **prerequisite** (`stable==FALSE` ⇒ a Blanchard-Kahn violation, the IRFs/forecasts are invalid); `lead(x)`/`E(x)` = `E_t[x_{t+1}]` (an RE forward term, NOT a future value); `state` = always an exogenous AR process with a shock; **SE on the IRFs only on a dsge_fit** (the delta method; on a calibrated solution `has_se=FALSE`); `dsge_forecast`/`dsge_shock_decomposition` **require a dsge_fit** (Kalman-filtered/smoothed states; a bare solve does not suffice — a hard gate); ML point estimates (NOT Bayesian — for posterior uncertainty → `bayes_dsge`).

**Sources:** the `small_linear_dsge` vignette *"Introduction to the dsge Package"* + the help pages (`dsge_model/obs/unobs/state`, `solve_dsge`, `estimate`, `irf`, `diebold_mariano_tscv`, `shock_decomposition`, `smooth_shocks`, `stability`, `check_identification` — live introspection) < Klein 2000 "Using the generalized Schur form to solve a multivariate linear rational expectations model", *JEDC* 24:1405; Sims 2002 "Solving linear rational expectations models", *Computational Economics* 20:1; Herbst & Schorfheide 2016 *Bayesian Estimation of DSGE Models* (Princeton; the Kalman likelihood, identification); Galí 2015 *Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle* 2nd ed. (the three-equation New Keynesian model).

### #201 A structural simultaneous-equation macro-econometric model (FRB/US style: estimate → simulate → multipliers) — `structural_simultaneous_equation` (`c13_dsge_general_equilibrium/structural_simultaneous_equation.py`)
**Functions:** `bimets_estimate` [`LOAD_MODEL(MDL)` + `LOAD_MODEL_DATA` + `ESTIMATE` OLS/IV — a PRODUCER: `object` = the estimated `BIMETS_MODEL`], `bimets_simulate` [`SIMULATE` DYNAMIC/FORECAST/STATIC or `STOCHSIMULATE` stochastic], `bimets_multipliers` [`MULTMATRIX` impact/interim/dynamic]

**When:** you have a **structural system of simultaneous equations** for a macro model — behavioural equations with coefficients to be estimated (e.g. consumption, investment, labour demand) **together with** accounting identities (GDP, profits, capital) — defined in an **MDL string** (`MODEL.. END`). You want (a) the **estimation** of the coefficients per equation (OLS by default / IV), (b) the **simulation** of the endogenous variables: deterministic (DYNAMIC baseline, FORECAST out of sample, STATIC one step) or **stochastic** (forecast distributions with automatic NORM(0,SER) disturbances), (c) a **table of policy multipliers** — how much the endogenous targets (consumption, GDP) move when you perturb the exogenous instruments (government spending, taxes). It is the FRB/US-style backward-looking structural macro engine; the reference model is Klein Model I.

**When NOT:** (a) a **single-equation** model (single-equation OLS/IV) → cat. 07 (`iv_fit`/`ols`). (b) A **reduced-form** VAR/VECM without theoretical identities → cat. 03 (`vr_var`) / cat. 05. (c) A **micro-founded rational-expectations DSGE** with structural shocks, Bellman/first-order conditions, IRFs → the sibling `dsge_solve` (bimets solves a backward-looking structural form, NOT a general RE-DSGE with forward-looking expectations beyond simple leads). (d) You do not have data covering **ALL** the vendog ∪ vexog over the estimation/simulation period (+ one period before, when there are TSLAG terms).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **The data as an mts** (one column per variable, a common range): load it via `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited` and convert long→wide mts with `c00_data_utilities/time_series_class.ts_convert`. The gate `.bim_data_to_list`: an mts/named list of ts whose names cover **vendog ∪ vexog** (a missing variable → a clean stop; otherwise the package gives a cryptic error / a silently empty series).
- **A valid MDL string** (`MODEL`…`END`, each behavioural equation with `EQ>`+`COEFF>`): the gate `.bim_check_model_str` + `LOAD_MODEL` itself (a clean stop on bad syntax).
- **An estimated model before simulation/multipliers**: `SIMULATE`/`STOCHSIMULATE`/`MULTMATRIX` require coefficients free of NA + modelData; the gate `.bim_check_estimated` (an unestimated model → blocked). Always use the `bimets_estimate.object` handle (PRODUCER→consumer chaining).
- **TSRANGE**: 4 integers `[startY,startP,endY,endP]`, start ≤ end, periods ≥ 1; the data extend ≥1 period before the start when the equations have lags.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`bimets_simulate`** — a projection/scenario (DYNAMIC/FORECAST) or a stochastic simulation after the estimation.
- **`bimets_multipliers`** — impact (a single-period TSRANGE) / interim / dynamic (multi-period) policy multipliers.
- **#165 `iv_fit` (ivreg, cat. 07)** — a single-equation causal estimate with an endogenous regressor (not a whole system).
- **`vr_var` (Vars-wrapper, cat. 03)** — reduced-form dynamics without theoretical identities/behavioural restrictions.
- **`dsge_solve` (dsge, the same category)** — a micro-founded rational-expectations DSGE (structural shocks/IRFs) instead of a backward-looking structural form.
- **`RENORM`** (bimets, not exposed as a tool) — a targets→instruments inversion (find which instrument value achieves a target); a deliberate omission from the curated surface.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `bimets_estimate`: `coefficients` (a named list per behavioural equation; a named numeric, e.g. `cn.a2`); `statistics` (`RSquared`/`AdjustedRSquared`/`DurbinWatson`/`Fstatistics`/`StandardErrorRegression`/`AIC`/`BIC`/`LogLikelihood`/`SumSquaresResiduals`/`DegreesOfFreedom` per behavioural equation); `residuals` (a ts per behavioural equation, chart-data); `endogenous`/`exogenous`/`behaviorals`/`identities`; `estTech`; `object` (the registry handle — stubbed in the serialised summary).
- `bimets_simulate` (deterministic): `mode='deterministic'`; `simulation` (a named list of ts per endogenous variable, chart-data); `simType`/`simAlgo`/`tsrange`.
- `bimets_simulate` (stochastic): `mode='stochastic'`; `sim_mean` & `sim_sd` (a named list of ts per endogenous variable); `stoch_replica`; `seed`.
- `bimets_multipliers`: `multiplier_matrix` (a matrix `TARGET × INSTRUMENT` with the dimnames `var_period`, e.g. `y_1`,`g_1`); `target_labels`/`instrument_labels`; `tsrange`.
- **Traps**: (i) in the multipliers, a cell = **0** when the INSTRUMENT period > the TARGET period (causality does not run backwards); a single period ⇒ impact, multiple periods ⇒ interim/dynamic. (ii) `stochastic=TRUE` perturbs **only** the behavioural equations (not the identities) with NORM(0,SER); the seed is mandatory (2025 by default) for reproducibility. (iii) `FORECAST` vs `DYNAMIC` vs `STATIC`: DYNAMIC/FORECAST use **simulated** lagged endogenous variables (FORECAST also beyond the historical sample), STATIC uses the **actual** lagged ones — do not confuse them. (iv) `estTech='IV'` requires IV expressions in the MDL or in the `iv` argument; `CHOWTEST/PDL/RESTRICT/ERROR(AUTO)` are defined **inside** the MDL (ESTIMATE honours them).

**Sources:** the bimets vignettes *"Getting started with bimets"* & *"US Federal Reserve quarterly model (FRB/US) in the reference with bimets"* + `help(LOAD_MODEL/ESTIMATE/SIMULATE/STOCHSIMULATE/MULTMATRIX)` — Luciani & Stok < (live introspection, bimets 4.1.2); Klein, L. (1950) *Economic Fluctuations in the United States 1921–1941*, Cowles Commission Monograph 11 (Klein Model I — the reference model); Pindyck & Rubinfeld (1998) *Econometric Models and Economic Forecasts*, 4th ed. (structural simultaneous-equation estimation, simulation, multipliers); Fair, the reference.C. (1984) *Specification, Estimation, and Analysis of Macroeconometric Models*, Harvard Univ. Press (FRB/US-style structural macro modelling).

### #202 Computable/Applied General Equilibrium — a structural dynamic model (`sdm`) — `CGE` (`c13_dsge_general_equilibrium/computable_applied_general.py`)
**Functions:** `cge_solve` [`sdm`, a fixed-point GE solver; the demand structure via `CD_A` (Cobb-Douglas) / `CES_A` (CES) / a constant demand-coefficient matrix (Leontief/Sraffa)]

**When:** you have a **calibrated technology/demand structure** in IO/SAM form — either (a) a constant demand-coefficient matrix `A` (Leontief/Sraffa input-output), or (b) Cobb-Douglas/CES **shares** `Beta` (+ `alpha`, + `sigma` for CES) — together with a supply matrix `B` and exogenous supplies `S0Exg` (labour/land/capital). You want to **compute the general equilibrium**: the relative prices `p` (a numeraire), the activity/output levels `z`, the demand matrix `A·diag(z)`, the endogenous growth rate (a purely productive economy). `sdm` solves the fixed point (Li's structural dynamic model / a Sraffa system); optionally it also returns the **adjustment time series** of the prices towards equilibrium (`ts=TRUE`).

**When NOT:** (a) you want a **linearised DSGE** with rational expectations, policy functions, IRFs, Bayesian estimation on data → `dsge_solve`/`dsge_estimate`. (b) **Stock-flow-consistent** macro accounting with behavioural equations & balance-sheet consistency → `sfcr_simulate`. (c) An **econometric structural macro model** (estimated equations + multipliers) → `bimets_simulate`. (d) You have time series and want a regression/forecast (not a calibrated GE). (e) You need the multi-money / policy-experiment / intertemporal-path features of `sdm` — outside the curated surface (deliberately not exposed).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **The demand structure** (a CLOSED `dstype`): `constant` requires a non-negative `A` (n-by-m); `CD`/`CES` require a non-negative `Beta` (n-by-m). **CD**: every column of `Beta` must sum to **1** (Cobb-Douglas shares) — a hard gate. **CES**: it requires `sigma` (of length 1 or m); `Theta` is an optional positive n-by-m matrix.
- **The supply matrix** `B` (n-by-m; the default `diag(n)` requires `m==n`) and **`S0Exg`** (n-by-m): `NA`=an endogenous commodity, a non-zero value=an exogenous supply; **0 is forbidden** (the `sdm` documentation) — a hard gate.
- Load the coefficient matrices via `c00_data_utilities/canonical_disk_format.arw_read_parquet` (a Parquet IO/SAM) or `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited` (CSV) and pass the handles.
- Run `dstype='constant'` first as a **baseline** (Leontief/Sraffa); then `CD`/`CES` for a price-responsive demand.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`dsge_solve`** — a linearised rational-expectations DSGE (policy functions, IRFs, forecasts, a shock decomposition) instead of a calibrated Walrasian GE on an IO/SAM.
- **`sfcr_simulate`** — stock-flow-consistent macro accounting (behavioural equations + balance-sheet consistency).
- **`bimets_simulate`** — an econometric structural macro model (estimated equations + multipliers).
- **`cge_solve(dstype='CES')`** — a price-responsive demand with an adjustable elasticity of substitution (CD is the limit sigma→0).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `p` / `p_normalized` — the equilibrium prices (an n-vector) & the same normalised to the commodity-1 numeraire (`p/p[1]`). **A trap**: GE determines prices **up to scale** — ALWAYS use `p_normalized`, the absolute `p` are arbitrary.
- `z` — the equilibrium levels of activity/output/utility (an m-vector).
- `demand_matrix` — `A_eq %*% diag(z)` (chart-data); `S` — the supply matrix of the initial period; `A_eq` — the equilibrium demand-coefficient matrix (for CD/CES it **differs** from the inputs — it is computed at the equilibrium prices).
- `growth_rate` — the endogenous equilibrium growth rate (a purely productive economy without `S0Exg`; `NA` otherwise).
- `tolerance` / `tolCond` / `converged` — the convergence error vs the threshold; **`converged=FALSE` ⇒ the solution is NOT an equilibrium** (increase `maxIteration` / check the structure; a stateless node — no silent retry).
- `ts_p`/`ts_z`/`ts_S`/`ts_q` (only with `ts=TRUE`) — the adjustment time series of the last iteration. **`maxIteration=1` ⇒ a pure simulation of the dynamics** (not an equilibrium computation).
- **Traps**: `dstype='constant'` = price-**independent** demand (Leontief/Sraffa); `CD`/`CES` = **price-responsive** (the `A` is recomputed at every iteration) — a different economic interpretation. The CES `sigma` is the parameter (sigma<0 is the usual case; sigma→0 ⇒ Cobb-Douglas, sigma→−∞ ⇒ Leontief), **not** the elasticity of substitution `1/(1−sigma)`.

**Sources:** the `CGE` help — `sdm` (a structural dynamic model: general equilibrium + dynamics), `CD_A` (the Cobb-Douglas demand coefficient matrix), `CES_A` (the CES demand coefficient matrix), `F_Z` the exchange function (live introspection) < **LI Wu** (2019, ISBN 9787521804225) *General Equilibrium and Structural Dynamics: Perspectives of New Structural Economics*; LI Wu (2010) *A Structural Growth Model and its Applications to Sraffa's System* (the 18th IIOA conference); **Torres** (2016, ISBN 9781622730452) *Introduction to Dynamic Macroeconomic General Equilibrium Models* (2nd ed.), Vernon Press; **Varian** (1992, ISBN 0393957357) *Microeconomic Analysis*, W. W. Norton (general equilibrium, p.352).

### #203 Stock-Flow-Consistent (Godley-Lavoie) macro simulation — a baseline solve, policy scenarios, accounting validation — `stock_flow_consistent` (`c13_dsge_general_equilibrium/stock_flow_consistent.py`)
**Functions:** `sfcr_simulate` [`sfcr_set` equations+external → `sfcr_baseline` a steady-state solve], `sfcr_scenario_run` [`sfcr_shock` + `sfcr_scenario` — a policy shock on top of the baseline], `sfcr_balance_check` [`sfcr_matrix` + `sfcr_validate` — balance-sheet / transactions-flow accounting consistency + the accounting residuals]

**When:** you have a **theoretically specified SFC model** (a system of accounting identities + behavioural equations à la Godley-Lavoie, e.g. SIM/PC) and want to **solve** it at a steady state (`sfcr_simulate`), to run **policy scenarios** with shocks to exogenous variables/parameters — e.g. ↑government spending, ↑the tax rate — (`sfcr_scenario_run`), and to **certify** that the balance-sheet or transactions-flow matrix is *water-tight* (`sfcr_balance_check`). A purely **deterministic** simulation: block-ordered Gauss-Seidel / Broyden / Newton-Raphson root solving (the independent blocks are solved in sequence, the cyclical ones iteratively). The equations are written in the reference formula syntax (`Y ~ Cs + Gs`), with `x[-1]` for a lag and `d(x)` for a first difference.

**When NOT:** (a) you want to **estimate** parameters from data — SFC is *calibrated/theory-driven*, not estimated (go to an econometric structural model). (b) You want a **micro-founded DSGE** with rational expectations / optimisation & log-linearisation — a different paradigm. (c) You have a single behavioural equation to estimate → a regression (cat. 07/08). (d) You want a **stochastic/Monte Carlo ensemble** or a sensitivity sweep → `sfcr_multis`/`sfcr_random` (deliberately outside this deterministic node).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Solve the baseline FIRST** (`sfcr_simulate`): `sfcr_scenario_run` & `sfcr_balance_check` require a solved `sfcr_tbl` handle (`.object`) — the hard gate `inherits(baseline,"sfcr_tbl")`, with the explicit message "a scenario is not defined without a baseline".
- **Well-formed equations**: every element of `equations`/`external`/`shock_variables` must be a valid formula (`lhs ~ rhs`, parseable with `as.formula`) — a malformed one (without `~`) is blocked. They are built with `as.formula` + `do.call(sfcr_set,.)` — **NEVER** `eval(parse(user_string))`.
- **A valid shock window**: `1 <= shock_start <= shock_end <= periods` (a gate); `periods >= 2` (a steady state wants ~50+).
- **A well-formed matrix** (`sfcr_balance_check`): `columns`/`codes` of the same length & with unique codes; every row has a `name` + valid codes (an unknown code → a stop).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`sfcr_scenario_run`** — a counterfactual/policy shock on top of an already solved baseline.
- **`sfcr_balance_check`** — certification that the accounting identities close (every TFM/BS column/row sums correctly; leak detection).
- **#204 `structural_simultaneous_equation` (an econometric structural macro model)** — if you want an **estimated** structural macro-econometric model (Klein type) with multiplier analysis instead of a calibrated SFC one.
- **04-structural-shocks (SVAR/BVAR)** — empirically identified shocks & IRFs from data instead of a theory-driven counterfactual.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `sfcr_simulate`: `paths` (a DataFrame period × all the variables; chart-data); `steady_state` (the last-period values; e.g. for SIM `Y* = G/theta`); `variables`/`n_variables`; `method`; `converged`; `object` (the baseline `sfcr_tbl` handle → the scenario/balance functions).
- `sfcr_scenario_run`: `paths` (the scenario; chart-data); `final_values`; `shocked_vars`; `shock_start`/`shock_end`; `object` (the scenario handle).
- `sfcr_balance_check`: `consistent` (a bool; TRUE = water-tight); `leaking_rows`/`leaking_cols` (the names that leak); `max_row_residual`/`max_col_residual` (the largest absolute accounting residual); `row_residual_by_period`/`col_residual_by_period` (chart-data); `message`.
- **Traps**:
 - `sfcr_validate` (the package function) **returns no value** — it does `cat("Water tight!")` or `abort`. The wrapper traps it (tryCatch → `consistent` + the leaking rows/cols) **and** computes explicit numeric residuals per period (otherwise they would not surface).
 - SFC is **calibrated**, not estimated; the parameters are given exogenously — the steady state depends on them.
 - **Growth models** (perpetually increasing stocks): a hidden equation & validation with `rhtol=TRUE` (relative), not absolute — otherwise a spurious failure from computational buildup.
 - `hidden` (a redundant/hidden identity, e.g. `list(Hh="Hs")` in SIM): if given, it is checked; a failure = a misspecified model.
 - The scenario **inherits** the block structure & the final state from the baseline; a shock before convergence gives a transient that is not a policy effect.
 - `sfcr_matrix` rows: the 1st element = the row name, the rest name-value pairs per code; do **NOT** add a `sum` column to a TFM by hand (it is automatic); in a BS the non-zero rows need an explicit `Sum`.

**Sources:** the `stock_flow_consistent` package + vignettes (`stock_flow_consistent`, `sfcr_multis`) — João Macalós, `sfcr_set/sfcr_baseline/sfcr_shock/sfcr_scenario/sfcr_matrix/sfcr_validate` (live introspection + the Rd help) < Godley W. & Lavoie M. (2007) *Monetary Economics: An Integrated Approach to Credit, Money, Income, Production and Wealth*, Palgrave Macmillan (the SIM/PC models, transactions-flow & balance-sheet matrices, water-tight accounting); Kinsella S. & OShea T. (2010) *Solution and Simulation of Large Stock Flow Consistent Monetary Production Models via the Gauss Seidel Algorithm*, SSRN doi:10.2139/ssrn.1729205 (cited in the `sfcr_baseline` help); Peressini, Sullivan & Uhl (1988) *The Mathematics of Nonlinear Programming*, Springer (Broyden & Newton-Raphson, cited in the `sfcr_baseline` help).

### #204 Bayesian Structural Time Series — `bayesian_structural_time` (`c14_bayesian_toolkit/bayesian_structural_time.py`)
**Functions:** `bsts_fit` [flag-driven `AddLocalLinearTrend`/`AddSemilocalLinearTrend`/`AddSeasonal`/`AddAr` + `bayesian_structural_time` MCMC; a PRODUCER], `bsts_predict` [`predict.bsts` the posterior forecast + bands], `bsts_components` [the posterior mean contributions `state.contributions` per component]

**When:** you want **Bayesian structural** modelling of a univariate series where (a) you decompose it explicitly into **interpretable state components** — a trend (a local or semilocal linear trend), **seasonality** (`nseasons`), an **AR** term — with **full posterior uncertainty** (predictive quantile bands, not a point estimate), or (b) you do a **Bayesian regression on a time series** with **variable selection** through a spike-and-slab prior (`expected_model_size`) when you have many candidate regressors (nowcasting à la Scott-Varian). `bsts_components` gives the posterior mean contributions of each component over time (stacked-decomposition chart-data); `bsts_predict` gives the mean/median + bands over H steps.

**When NOT:** (a) you want a **point/frequentist** state-space model without MCMC → `KFAS`/`dynamic_linear` (cat. 10, a fast Kalman filter). (b) Multivariate/cointegration dynamics → VAR/VECM/BVAR. (c) A fully **custom likelihood/hierarchical** model → `general_bayesian_inference`/`bayesian_regression`/`general_bugs_style`. (d) A pure ARIMA/ETS forecast without a component decomposition. (e) A very long series where the MCMC cost is not justified.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **`bsts_fit` = a PRODUCER**: it builds the `state.specification` incrementally from **flags** (at least ONE component — a gate) and runs the MCMC; it returns an `object` handle consumed by `bsts_predict`/`bsts_components`. **`seed` is MANDATORY** (MCMC).
- **Regression mode**: load a `DataFrame` (the response + the regressors) with `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited` and give a `formula` + `data`; the gate: all the formula variables present, a valid response.
- **A comparison baseline**: `c10_trend_cycle_statespace/kalman_filter_smoother.kf_local_linear_trend` — the same structural decomposition with an MLE Kalman filter; compare before you invest in MCMC.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`bs_run_mcmc`** (cat. 10) — a Bayesian state space with an explicit prior specification / non-Gaussian observation models (SV) instead of the flag-driven builder.
- **`kf_local_linear_trend`** (cat. 10) — a point/frequentist MLE (a fast Kalman filter, without posterior draws).
- **`nim_bayes_mcmc`** — a fully customised hierarchical/state model outside the bsts components.
- **`bsts_fit(family="student")`** — outliers/heavy tails → a robust observation model.
- **`bsts_fit(semilocal_linear_trend=TRUE)`** — long horizons → a mean-reverting slope (it avoids an explosive trend).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `bsts_fit`: `state_components` (the names `non_parametric_trend`/`seasonal.N.k`/`Ar_k`/`regression`); `residual_sd` (the posterior mean `sigma.obs`); `sigma_obs_quantiles`; `coefficients` `{variable, inclusion_prob, posterior_mean, posterior_mean_incl}` (regression only); `burn`; `fitted_series`+`time`; `object` (the handle → the registry).
- `bsts_predict`: `mean`/`median` (chart-data); `lower`/`upper` predictive bands at the quantiles; `step`; `has_regression`.
- `bsts_components`: `contributions` (time × component posterior means; a stacked decomposition); `contributions_lower`/`upper` bands; `components`; `time`; `burn`.
- **Traps**: **DETERMINISM** — bsts is MCMC (the Boom C++ RNG); ONLY `set.seed(seed)`+`bsts(seed=)` together give reproducible results (the wrapper does both, in the fit AND the predict). `local` vs `semilocal` trend are mutually exclusive (a gate); the local linear trend can "explode" at long horizons. `inclusion_prob` = the posterior probability of inclusion; `posterior_mean` (OVER ALL the draws, shrunk) ≠ `posterior_mean_incl` (conditional on inclusion). `expected_model_size` applies ONLY in regression mode (a gate). A regression forecast: `newdata` (the future regressors) is MANDATORY, with `nrow==horizon` (a gate). Keep `niter` large enough (>=500 in production; 100-250 only for smoke tests).

**Sources:** the `bayesian_structural_time` help (`bayesian_structural_time`, `AddLocalLinearTrend`, `AddSemilocalLinearTrend`, `AddSeasonal`, `AddAr`, `predict.bsts`, `SuggestBurn` — live introspection) < Scott & Varian 2014 "Predicting the present with Bayesian structural time series", *IJMMNO* 5:4; Scott & Varian 2015 "Bayesian Variable Selection for Nowcasting Economic Time Series" (NBER/Univ. Chicago); Brodersen et al. 2015 "Inferring causal impact using BSTS", *Annals of Applied Statistics* 9:247; Durbin & Koopman 2012 *Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods* (Oxford); George & McCulloch 1997 (*Statistica Sinica* 7:339, spike-and-slab).

### #205 Sequential Monte Carlo / particle filters (bootstrap · auxiliary · Liu-West · ensemble Kalman) — `nimbleSMC` (`c14_bayesian_toolkit/general_bugs_stylesmc.py`)
**Functions:** `smc_filter` — a method-selected particle filter (`match.arg`, `bootstrap` by default) over a BUGS-style state-space model: `buildBootstrapFilter`/`buildAuxiliaryFilter`/`buildLiuWestFilter`/`buildEnsembleKF` → `compileNimble` → `run(m)`. It returns an estimate of the marginal log-likelihood, per-time filtered summaries of the latent states (mean/quantiles = chart-data) + the per-time ESS.

**When:** you have a **BUGS-style state-space / hidden-Markov model** with latent states `x[t]` and observations `y[t]`, and you want either (a) an **estimate of the marginal log-likelihood** (for model comparison, likelihood-based inference, or as a building block of particle MCMC) or (b) the **filtered distribution** `f(x[t]|y[1:t])` per time point (mean/quantiles). It handles **NON-linear / NON-Gaussian** transition & observation equations — exactly where the Kalman filter does not apply. Macro use: nowcasting/filtering non-linear DSGE-like or stochastic-volatility latent states.

**When NOT:** (a) a **linear-Gaussian** SSM → use an exact Kalman filter (`c10_trend_cycle_statespace/kalman_filter_smoother.kf_fit`, `MARSS`, `dynamic_linear`) — analytic, without Monte Carlo noise & with a closed-form likelihood. (b) You want a **full Bayesian posterior of the parameters** with MCMC diagnostics → `c14_bayesian_toolkit/general_bugs_style.nim_bayes_mcmc` (an Rhat/ESS convergence gate). (c) Simple trend/cycle smoothing without a latent-state model (HP/`mFilter`).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A BUGS-style state-space `code` as a string** (parse-only, **injection-safe** — no `eval`, as in `nim_bayes_mcmc`); `constants`/`data`/`inits` as named lists; the `data` **WITHOUT NA** (nimble treats an NA as a MISSING node to be imputed → a hidden parameter, a hard gate).
- **`latentNodes`** a non-empty character vector in **time order** (`'x'` or `'x[1:10]'`); a post-build gate: they exist & are **stochastic**; `inits` covers **ALL** the top-level stochastic parameters (otherwise NaN samples).
- **`seed` is MANDATORY**, a single integer (`set.seed` before the `run` → deterministic); `nParticles>=1`; `thresh∈(0,1]`; `d∈(0,1)` (liuWest); `probs∈(0,1)`.
- **Post-run correctness gates:** the filtered samples must be finite (particle depletion → a hard stop); where a logLik exists (bootstrap/auxiliary) it must be finite (`-Inf` = a collapse → a stop).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`kf_fit` (10-…)** — a linear-Gaussian SSM → an exact Kalman filter (no MC variance).
- **`nim_bayes_mcmc`** — the full posterior of the parameters + Rhat/ESS, not only filtering/the logLik.
- **`method='auxiliary'`** — a peaked/informative observation likelihood → lookahead resampling reduces the degeneracy relative to bootstrap.
- **`method='liuWest'`** — joint state+parameter inference in ONE pass (⚠ didactic/often poor; no logLik).
- **`method='ensembleKF'`** — a high-dimensional latent state with additive normal observation error → EnKF (no logLik).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `method` / `latent_vars`; `log_likelihood` + `log_likelihood_available` (numeric for bootstrap/auxiliary; **NA_real_ + FALSE** for liuWest/ensembleKF — **STRUCTURALLY so, NEVER fabricated**).
- `state_summary`: a `DataFrame {node, mean, sd, q..}` **per latent node/time** — the per-time filtered summaries (chart-data); `state_mean`: the per-time posterior mean.
- `ess` + `ess_available`: the per-time ESS (numeric for bootstrap/auxiliary; **NULL + FALSE** otherwise); `filtered_samples`: equally weighted samples (particles × nodes).
- `param_summary` + `param_vars`: (**liuWest ONLY**) the posterior of the top-level parameters; `NULL` for the rest. `n_particles`/`n_time`/`metadata`.
- **Traps:** (1) **METHOD HETEROGENEITY** (live-verified) — only bootstrap/auxiliary give a logLik & an ESS; for liuWest/ensembleKF `run→NULL` and there is no `returnESS` → do not read an `NA logLik` as "a bad model". (2) **Monte Carlo variance** in the logLik estimate → for model comparison use the same `seed` & `nParticles`. (3) Liu-West "often performs poorly, didactic" (the package warning) → the parameter posteriors are over-concentrated (impoverishment). (4) **Filtered, NOT smoothed** (`f(x[t]|y[1:t])`). (5) `thresh<1` → mvEWSamples are equally weighted only at the resampled time points; `thresh=1` (the default) → equally weighted everywhere.

**Sources:** the `nimbleSMC` help (`buildBootstrapFilter`/`buildAuxiliaryFilter`/`buildLiuWestFilter`/`buildEnsembleKF`, live introspection v0.11.1) < Michaud, de Valpine, Turek, Paciorek & Nguyen (2021) "Sequential Monte Carlo Methods in the nimble and nimbleSMC the reference Packages", *J. Statistical Software* 100(3); Gordon, Salmond & Smith (1993) *IEE Proc. F* 140(2):107 (bootstrap); Pitt & Shephard (1999) *JASA* 94(446):590 (auxiliary); Liu & West (2001) in *SMC Methods in Practice*, Springer 197-223; Houtekamer & Mitchell (1998) *Monthly Weather Review* 126(3):796 (EnKF); Doucet, de Freitas & Gordon (2001) *Sequential Monte Carlo Methods in Practice*, Springer.

### #206 High-dimensional k-way fixed-effects GLM (logit/probit/Poisson) with an incidental-parameter bias correction + average partial effects — `high_dimensional_way` (`c16_limited_dependent/high_dimensional_way.py`)
**Functions:** `alpaca_feglm` [`feglm` family=binomial(logit/probit)/poisson, the formula `y ~ x | fe1 + fe2`, + an optional `biasCorr`] · `alpaca_apes` [`getAPEs` the average partial effects + delta-method SE]

**When:** you have **panel / pseudo-panel micro-data with several high-dimensional fixed effects** (e.g. `unit + time`; or a network `exporter + importer + time`) and a **binary** (recession/default/transition) or **count** response, and you want a consistent nonlinear FE estimate **together with the correction of the incidental-parameter bias** (critical in short-T panels — Neyman-Scott; Fernández-Val/Weidner) and **interpretable average partial effects with SE**. `alpaca_feglm` is the PRODUCER (the fit + an optional bias correction → an `object` handle); `alpaca_apes` consumes the handle and gives the marginal effects — the node's reason for existing in macro interpretation.

**When NOT:** (a) without fixed effects → a plain `glm`/probit. (b) A single FE with few levels → a classical conditional logit or **#83 `run_feglm_binom` (fixest)**. (c) You want only fitted probabilities/an AUC **without** a bias correction → **#83** (faster). (d) A continuous response → linear FE (**#33 fixest feols** / **#46 plm**). (e) APEs for **poisson** — `getAPEs` supports ONLY binary choice (it is blocked). (f) Functional forms (interactions/polynomials) in the APEs — not supported by `getAPEs`.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **A panel `DataFrame`** with the response + the regressors + the FE columns; load it with `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`. The gate `.al_check_data`: non-empty, all the formula variables present, **no NA** (`feglm` drops rows with NA silently — a silent alteration).
- **A formula with `| fe` (mandatory)**: the gate `.al_check_formula` — the top-level RHS operator must be `|` (`y ~ x1 + x2 | unit + time`); a simple response variable (not an expression). Without `| fe` → a clean stop (go to a plain GLM).
- **A response compatible with the family**: binary (`0/1`, logical, a 2-level factor) for binomial; non-negative integers for poisson (the gate `.al_check_response`).
- **The bias correction**: `bias_correct=TRUE` only for binomial (`biasCorr` is not defined for poisson); `L` a non-negative integer; `panel_structure ∈ {classic, network}`.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **#83 `run_feglm_binom` (fixest)** — a binomial FE GLM with fitted probabilities/clustered SE/a pseudo-R2 when you do NOT need the bias correction (a long T or large groups).
- **`alpaca_apes`** — from log-odds coefficients to interpretable average partial effects (marginal effects) + delta-method SE.
- **#33 `fx_feols` / #46 `pd_fit`** — a continuous response (linear fixed effects).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `alpaca_feglm.coefficients` — the uncorrected structural beta (log-odds/log-rate); `.coefficients_bias_corrected` — the bias-corrected beta (`NULL` if `bias_correct=FALSE`). **Compare them**: the difference (often ~20-30%) is the incidental-parameter bias.
- `.coef_table` — a matrix `Estimate/Std. error/z value/Pr(>|z|)` of the primary estimate (bias-corrected if requested); `.deviance`/`.null_deviance`/`.converged`/`.iterations`.
- `.nobs` (full/na/pc/effective); `.fe_names`/`.fe_levels` (the number of levels per FE)/`.n_fe`; `.bias_term`/`.bandwidth`/`.panel_structure` (when bias-corrected).
- `alpaca_apes.ape` — the average partial effects per covariate (in **probability** units); `.ape_se` the delta-method SE; `.ape_table` (Estimate/SE/z/p); `.vcov` the covariance matrix.
- **Traps**: (i) the `feglm` betas are **log-odds/z-scores**, NOT changes in probability — use `alpaca_apes`. (ii) `biasCorr`/`getAPEs` are **binomial only**. (iii) `L=0` only if all the regressors are strictly exogenous; with a lagged outcome (dynamics/state dependence) use `L=1.4` (the order of the FE matters when `L>0`). (iv) `network` vs `classic` for bilateral flows (trade); the wrapper reads the structure from the `biasCorr` object in `alpaca_apes` for consistency. (v) Perfect classification → a silent row/FE-group drop (`nobs.pc`). (vi) `converged=FALSE` (hard-gated) → a linear dependence between a regressor and the FE.
- **Masking**: `feglm` is exported by `fixed_effects_ols` too (the sibling `fixest-feglm` calls `library(fixest)`) → the wrapper does not call `library(alpaca)` but uses `requireNamespace` + everywhere (the mutual masking of `feglm` is avoided).

**Sources:** the `high_dimensional_way` help (`feglm.Rd`, `biasCorr.Rd`, `getAPEs.Rd`, `simGLM.Rd` — live introspection 0.3.5) < Stammann 2018 (ArXiv, high-dimensional k-way FE GLM); Fernández-Val & Weidner 2016 (*J. Econometrics* 192(1):291-312) & 2018 (*Annual Review of Economics* 10:109-138); Neyman & Scott 1948 (*Econometrica* 16(1):1-32, the incidental parameter problem); Cruz-Gonzalez, Fernández-Val & Weidner 2017 (*Stata Journal* 17(3):517-545, average partial effects); Czarnowske & Stammann 2020 (ArXiv, long panels).

### #207 Online probabilistic forecast combination (CRPS-Learning) — `online_probabilistic_forecast` (`c17_forecast_combination/online_probabilistic_forecast.py`)
**Functions:** `profoc_online` [`online` — an online-learning combination of probabilistic experts through CRPS-Learning; `method ∈ {bewa (the default), boa, ml_poly, ewa}`, `loss_function ∈ {quantile (pinball/CRPS), expectile, percentage}`]

**When:** you have **>=2 experts** producing **probabilistic (quantile) forecasts** at the SAME `tau` levels, organised into a **3D array `experts` `[T x quantiles(P) x experts(K)]`** together with `y` (the `Tx1` realised values), and you want to combine them **adaptively online** — the per-quantile weights are learned sequentially from the past loss, **optimally in CRPS terms**. Ideal when the relative performance of the experts **changes over time** (regime shifts): the online aggregation shifts weight to the good experts without look-ahead. It returns the combined probabilistic forecast (`T x P`), the final & mean adaptive weights (`P x K`), the cumulative loss of the combination vs each single expert, and `beats_best_expert`.

**When NOT:** (a) **point-only** forecasts (not quantiles) → `#85 run_hybrid` (forecastHybrid). (b) You want **hierarchical/temporal reconciliation** (coherence in a hierarchy) instead of learning weights from a loss → `foreco_reconcile` / `fable_reconcile`. (c) Only **one** expert (`K<2` — there is nothing to combine; a hard gate). (d) You want **batch/offline** fixed optimal weights (not online adaptivity — outside the curated surface). (e) You want only the **evaluation** of a density forecast (CRPS/LogS/PIT), not a combination → `#74 sr_crps_sample` (scoringRules).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **An `experts` array `[T x P x K]`** with `dim1 == length(y)`, `dim2 == length(tau)`, `K >= 2`, **free of NA** (a hard gate; NA are fatal). Build it by stacking the quantile forecasts of several experts: `c02_univariate_forecasting/fable.run_fable_arima` + `::run_fable_ets` (each one = one slice `[,,k]`).
- **`tau` ∈ (0,1), strictly increasing/unique**, of length `P == dim(experts)[2]`, in the same order as the quantile levels at which the experts were computed (a hard gate on the range/sortedness).
- **`y`** a `Tx1` numeric matrix of realised values, free of NA (`c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`#85 run_hybrid` (forecastHybrid)** — a point-forecast combination (not probabilistic) over a single `ts`.
- **`foreco_reconcile`** — hierarchical/temporal **reconciliation** (coherence), not learning weights from a loss.
- **`fable_reconcile`** — reconciliation inside the fable ecosystem (MinT/WLS/OLS).
- **`#74 sr_crps_sample` (scoringRules)** — only the **evaluation** of a density/quantile forecast (CRPS/LogS/PIT), not a combination.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `predictions`: a `T x P` matrix — the combined probabilistic forecast per time × quantile (chart-data; monotone within each `t` when `allow_quantile_crossing=FALSE`).
- `final_weights` (`P x K`): the adaptive weights at time `T+1` — the experts will be combined with these in the **next** forecast (they sum to ~1 per quantile for `boa/bewa/ewa`); `mean_weights` = the average weight per expert over time.
- `forecaster_loss_total`/`_mean`/`_per_quantile`: the cumulative & mean CRPS-learning loss of the **combination**; `expert_loss_total` (`length K`) = the cumulative loss of each single expert; `best_expert`.
- `beats_best_expert`: **TRUE** ⇒ the combination beats the best single expert out of sample (the reason online learning exists).
- **Traps**: (i) **the axis order** — `[T x P x K]`; a wrong order (e.g. `[T x K x P]`) passes through silently WRONG; the gate checks `dim2==length(tau)` but not the semantic correspondence quantile↔level (the caller's responsibility). (ii) `beats_best_expert=FALSE` is **not** a failure — with a small `T` the online learning needs time to converge; look at `mean_weights`. (iii) `method`: `bewa`=BOA regret+an EWA update, `boa`=the full BOA (2nd order), `ewa`=simple exponential weighting, `ml_poly`. (iv) `allow_quantile_crossing=FALSE` (the default) → monotone quantiles (a valid CDF); leave it FALSE. (v) Smoothing (B-splines/P-splines) & `predict`/`update` (incremental) are **not** exposed (a stateless node ⇒ a full re-fit per call; the defaults = no smoothing).

**Sources:** the `online_probabilistic_forecast` `help('online')` + vignette (live introspection: `online(y, experts, tau, method, loss_function,..)`) < Berrisch & Ziel 2023 "CRPS Learning", *J. Econometrics* 237(2):105221 <doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.11.008>; Gaillard & Goude 2015 (BOA/ML-Poly expert aggregation); Wintenberger 2017 "Optimal learning with Bernstein Online Aggregation", *Machine Learning* 106:119.

### #208 Coherent forecast reconciliation (cross-sectional / temporal / cross-temporal, MinT) — `FoReco` (`c17_forecast_combination/coherent_forecast_reconciliation.py`)
**Functions:** `foreco_reconcile` — one tool with a `type` dispatch: `'cs'` → `csrec` (cross-sectional; `agg_mat`), `'te'` → `terec` (temporal; `agg_order`), `'ct'` → `ctrec` (cross-temporal; `agg_mat`+`agg_order`). The MinT/covariance method through `comb` (a closed set PER type); the projection `approach` proj/strc(+osqp); optional non-negativity `nn`.

**When:** you have **incoherent base forecasts** of a **linearly constrained** set of series — hierarchical (GDP = the sum of the sectors, national = the sum of the regions) and/or **temporal** (annual = the sum of the quarters) — and want to make them **coherent** (the aggregates equal the sum of the components *exactly*) while improving accuracy at the same time through **MinT** (trace minimisation, Wickramasuriya 2019). `type='cs'` is a purely cross-sectional hierarchy; `type='te'` is one series in a temporal hierarchy (several frequencies); `type='ct'` is both at once (Di Fonzo & Girolimetto 2023).

**When NOT:** (a) a single series without a constraint structure — there is nothing to reconcile. (b) You want to **combine alternative models of the SAME series** (an ensemble/model averaging) → **#85 `run_hybrid`** or a `tidy_hierarchical_grouped` combination — reconciliation ≠ an ensemble. (c) You do not have base forecasts for **all** the levels of the hierarchy. (d) You want probabilistic/bootstrap reconciled paths (`csboot/teboot/ctboot` — outside the curated surface).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **Base forecasts for ALL the levels**, stacked in the right order: cs columns `[upper.., bottom..]`, te a vector from the **low→high** frequency, ct rows = the series. They are produced by `c02_univariate_forecasting/fable.run_fable_arima` or `forecast-run_ets` (per series/level).
- **`agg_mat`** (n_a × n_b, the map bottom→upper) for cs/ct; **`agg_order`** (the maximum m, or a vector of factors) for te/ct — a hard gate on the dimensions (`ncol(base)`/`nrow(base) = n_a+n_b`, `length/ncol` a multiple of `k*+m`).
- **`res`** (the in-sample residuals) are NECESSARY for the WLS/GLS/MinT `comb` options (shr/wls/sam/wlsv/acov…); without res → a gate stop. Take the residuals from the same forecasting tool.

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`comb='shr'` (MinT shrinkage)** — the normal default for accuracy when residuals are available; `ols`/`seasonal_trend_decomposition` ignore the error covariance (a structural/OLS baseline).
- **`type='ct'`** — simultaneous cross-sectional **and** temporal coherence (quarterly regional → annual national).
- **#85 `run_hybrid` (forecastHybrid)** — a combination of several models for **one** series (an ensemble), not the reconciliation of a hierarchy.
- **`nn='sntz'`/`'osqp'`** — reconciled forecasts that must be non-negative.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `reconciled`: the coherent forecasts — cs an `(h × n)` matrix; te an `(h·(k*+m))` vector with `labels`; ct an `(n × h·(k*+m))` matrix (**chart-data**).
- `type`/`comb`/`approach`/`nn`: the reconciliation that was performed; cs: `n`/`n_upper`/`n_bottom`/`h` + `coherence_err` (max|upper − agg_mat·bottom| ≈ 0 ⇒ coherent, a post-check); te/ct: `agg_order`/`m`/`kt`/`h`/`tew`.
- **Traps**: (1) **the column/row order** of base — cs = `[upper.., bottom..]`; a wrong order ⇒ a *silently* wrong reconciliation (the wrapper checks only the dimensions, not the semantics). (2) `comb` **differs per type** (`wlsv` only for te/ct, `oasd` only for cs) — an invalid comb for the type is blocked. (3) MinT requires `res`. (4) The temporal base ordering runs from the **low→high** frequency. (5) A scalar `agg_order` `m` ⇒ all the divisors of `m` (`k*+m` = the sum of the divisors; 4→7, 12→28). (6) Reconciliation is **not** an ensemble.

**Sources:** the `FoReco` help for `csrec`/`terec`/`ctrec` + `cscov`/`tecov`/`ctcov` (the comb sets) — live introspection FoReco 1.3.1 < Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos & Hyndman 2019 "Optimal forecast reconciliation through trace minimization (MinT)", *JASA* 114(526):804-819; Hyndman, Ahmed, Athanasopoulos & Shang 2011 "Optimal combination forecasts for hierarchical time series", *CSDA* 55(9):2579-2589; Athanasopoulos, Hyndman, Kourentzes & Petropoulos 2017 "Forecasting with temporal hierarchies", *EJOR* 262(1):60-74; Di Fonzo & Girolimetto 2023 "Cross-temporal forecast reconciliation", *IJF* 39(1):39-57; Panagiotelis, Athanasopoulos, Gamakumara & Hyndman 2021 "Forecast reconciliation: A geometric view", *IJF* 37(1):343-359.

### #209 Tidy hierarchical / grouped forecast reconciliation (aggregate_key + MinT / bottom_up) — `tidy_hierarchical_grouped` (`c17_forecast_combination/tidy_hierarchical_grouped.py`)
**Functions:** `fable_reconcile` → `as_tsibble` → `aggregate_key` (nested `grp1/grp2` or grouped `grp1*grp2`) → `model` (a base `ARIMA`/`ETS`/`SNAIVE` per node) → `reconcile` with `min_trace(method=…)` (MinT) or `bottom_up` → `forecast(h)` + `hilo` for the PI.

**When:** you have a **long panel** (one time `index` column + **>=1 key/grouping** columns + one **numeric `value`** that **aggregates naturally**) and the structure forms a **hierarchy/grouped** set where the leaves must sum to the aggregates — e.g. GDP/employment per **region within a country**, sales per **sector × region**, or **CPI subindices → the headline index**. You want **COHERENT** forecasts (the sum of the leaves = the aggregate, guaranteed) instead of inconsistent independent forecasts per node. `fable_reconcile` fits **one** base model per node and reconciles: `method="wls_struct"` (the default, a robust structural MinT) or `mint_shrink` (the theoretically optimal MinT) or `bottom_up` (a simple aggregation of the leaves).

**When NOT:** (a) **a single univariate series without a hierarchy** → `#85 forecastHybrid` (an ensemble) or a standalone `fable`/ARIMA (cat. 02). (b) An **online/adaptive** combination of expert forecasts with time-varying weights → `online_probabilistic_forecast`. (c) Reconciliation over **ready numeric base forecasts** (matrices), or purely **temporal/cross-temporal** aggregation without a tidy tsibble → `FoReco` (`csrec`/`terec`/`ctrec`). (d) A `value` with **NA** or a **non-regular/gappy index**, or a `value` that **does not aggregate** (ratios/percentages/index levels). (e) A structural/causal analysis (VAR/VECM).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **no stationarity pre-test is needed** — the base models (`ARIMA`/`ETS`) handle the differencing/seasonality per node themselves.
- **structural hard gates (the wrapper):** `data` a non-empty DataFrame; `index`/`value` = ONE existing column name each; `keys` = a character vector of **>=1** existing names, **distinct** from `index`/`value`; `structure="grouped"` requires **keys >= 2**.
- **`value` numeric, free of NA/NaN/Inf** (reconciliation requires complete base forecasts at every node) — otherwise a hard stop.
- **`index` a valid tsibble index**: of class ∈ {`Date`, `POSIXct/lt`, `yearweek`/`yearmonth`/`yearquarter`, `numeric`, `integer`}. A `character`/`factor` time column → a clean stop with instructions to convert (e.g. `yearquarter`). Load it via `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`.
- **`h`** a positive integer; **`level`** numeric in (0,100) (the default is `c(80,95)`).

**Alternatives + criterion:**

| Alternative | When it is preferable |
|---|---|
| `csrec`/`terec`/`ctrec` | reconciliation over **ready** base forecasts (numeric matrices), cross-temporal or temporal aggregation — without a tsibble→mable round trip |
| `#85 run_hybrid` | **ONE** series without a hierarchy — an ensemble of several models instead of coherence |
| `fable-run_fable_arima` (cat. 02) | a single node / no need for coherence |
| Bayesian model averaging (cat. 14) | a posterior-weighted combination with full uncertainty quantification instead of a MinT projection |

**Reading the output** (a named list, JSON-safe through `to_mcp`):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reconciled` | **the main output**: DataFrame records (the key cols + `index` + `point` + `lower_L`/`upper_L` per level) — the COHERENT forecasts; the aggregated nodes carry the label `"<aggregated>"` |
| `base` | the corresponding records of the **unreconciled** base forecasts (it shows the effect of the reconciliation) |
| `hierarchy` | a DataFrame of the nodes (each row = a key combination; `"<aggregated>"` = an aggregated level) |
| `n_series` / `n_leaf` | the total number of nodes (leaves + aggregates) / the leaves — a structural check |
| `method` / `reconciliation` | `min_trace(<method>)` or `bottom_up` |
| `structure` / `base_model` | `nested`/`grouped` · `arima`/`ets`/`snaive` |
| `h` / `level` | the horizon / the PI levels |
| `object` | the reconciled mable (stubbed by `to_mcp`; no downstream consumer) |

**Interpretation traps:**
- **coherence ≠ accuracy:** reconciliation GUARANTEES only that the leaves sum to the aggregates. **MinT** (`min_trace`) typically improves accuracy; **`bottom_up`** can make the top level **worse** when the leaves are noisy.
- **choosing the MinT method:** `wls_struct` (the default) = structural scaling, **always robust** (no covariance estimation); `mint_shrink` (Wickramasuriya 2019) = shrinkage MinT, **theoretically optimal** but it needs enough residuals — on **short/few** series it can be unstable; `ols` ignores the scale of the nodes.
- **`"<aggregated>"`** in the key fields = an aggregated level (`is_aggregated`), **NOT** a category with that name — do not read it as a leaf.
- **`nested` (`grp1/grp2`) vs `grouped` (`grp1*grp2`):** nested = genuine nesting (a region **within** a state); grouped = crossed without natural nesting (e.g. purpose × state). The wrong choice changes **which nodes exist**.
- **The PI:** they come from the reconciled predictive distribution (`hilo`) — valid per node, but the coherence concerns the **points** (the means), not the joint coverage of the intervals.
- **`value` must aggregate meaningfully** (a flow/stock): the constraint is `sum of the leaves = the aggregate`; **ratios/percentages/index levels do NOT aggregate** — do not pass them as `value`.

**Sources:** the fabletools reference manual — the `aggregate_key`/`reconcile`/`min_trace`/`bottom_up`/`hilo` help pages (O'Hara-Wild, Hyndman); Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos & Hyndman (2019) "Optimal forecast reconciliation … through trace minimization", JASA 114(526):804 (MinT); Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* (3rd ed.), ch. 11 Hierarchical/grouped series (https://otexts.com/fpp3/hierarchical.html); Hyndman, Ahmed, Athanasopoulos & Shang (2011) "Optimal combination forecasts for hierarchical time series", CSDA 55:2579.

### #210 Parametric yield-curve factor models (Nelson-Siegel / Svensson / a cubic spline + Diebold-Li) + curve transforms — `parametric_yield_curve` (`c18_yield_curve/nelson_siegel_svenssons.py`)
**Functions:** `yc_fit` [`nelson_siegel/svensson/cubic_spline` via an enum; a single curve `rates` OR a panel `time × maturity`; panel+NS = Diebold-Li factor dynamics], `yc_transform` [`spot` (`yc_predict`) / `forward` (`yc_forward`, instantaneous or forward-forward) / `discount` (`yc_discount`) / `pca` (`yc_pca`, Litterman-Scheinkman)]

**When:** you have **observed yields per maturity** — either **one cross-sectional curve** (a `rates` vector of the same length as the maturities) or a **time series of curves** (a `panel` matrix time × maturity) — and you want (a) a compression into **level/slope/curvature** factors (+ an extra term in the Svensson model) with an explicit decay `lambda`, (b) **Diebold-Li** factor dynamics (a Nelson-Siegel fit per date over a panel → the factors + the fitted yields per date), or (c) the production of **forward rates / discount factors / spot rates** on a free maturity grid, or a **PCA** of a panel of yields. `yc_fit` registers the fitted `object` (a yc_curve or a panel matrix), which feeds `yc_transform` as a handle.

**When NOT:** (a) you have **coupon-bond cash-flow micro-data** (prices+coupons, not ready spot yields) → **#212 `ycevo_estimate`** (nonparametric). (b) You want a **no-arbitrage / affine term-premium** decomposition (expectations vs the term premium) — `parametric_yield_curve` is a **descriptive fit only**. (c) You want only a simple **10y-2y slope spread** (a transform, cat. 00). (d) The time-series stationarity/cointegration of a single tenor (cat. 01/05). (e) **Fewer pillars than parameters** (NS<4, Svensson<6, cubic<3) → an underdetermined fit (a hard gate).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **The maturities**: a numeric vector of length ≥2, **positive & STRICTLY INCREASING** — a hard gate (duplicated/unsorted maturities are accepted **silently** by the package). A consistent unit (years), otherwise the lambda is distorted.
- **EXACTLY ONE** of `rates` (a single curve) or `panel` (time × maturity) — a hard gate; `ncol(panel) == length(maturities)`, `nrow(panel) ≥ 2`.
- **Enough pillars per method**: NS ≥4, Svensson ≥6, cubic ≥3 (below that it is underdetermined → a gate). `rates`/`panel` numeric, finite, free of NA. `weights` (if given) positive & **NOT** allowed with `cubic_spline`.
- Load the yields via `c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited`. Fit a single curve with `yc_fit` (the `object` is registered → a handle for `yc_transform`).

**Alternatives + criterion:**
- **`c18_yield_curve/nelson_siegel_svensson.fit_nelson_siegel`** — you want an xts/Date-indexed factor series ready as an input to the recession probit #83, or Diebold-Li through the established `YieldCurve` interface.
- **`c18_yield_curve/nelson_siegel_svensson.fit_svensson`** — a 4-factor Svensson model on an xts panel with a which_rate Spot/Forward choice.
- **`c18_yield_curve/nonparametric_time_varying.ycevo_estimate`** — you have a coupon-bond cash-flow panel (not ready spot yields); a nonparametric time-varying discount/yield surface.
- **`yc_transform` (`transform='pca'`)** — you want **empirical** (data-driven) level/slope/curvature factors as loadings instead of a parametric fit.
- **an affine no-arbitrage model (ACM/ABG)** — you want an expectations vs term-premium decomposition (outside `parametric_yield_curve`).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `yc_fit` (a single curve): `factors` `{level,slope,curvature}`; `params` (`beta0.`, `tau`/`tau1`/`tau2`); `lambda` (=1/tau — NS: `lambda`; Svensson: `lambda1,lambda2`; cubic: `NA`); `fitted` (chart-data yields); `residuals`; `rmse`; `object` (a yc_curve, the register handle).
- `yc_fit` (a panel, Diebold-Li): `factors` a matrix `[dates × {level,slope,curvature}]`; `params` `[dates × params]`; `lambda` `[dates × lambda(s)]`; `fitted` `[dates × maturities]`; `rmse` per date; `object` = the panel matrix (the register handle → pca).
- `yc_transform`: `spot` → `maturity/rate`; `forward` → `maturity/forward_rate`; `discount` → `maturity/discount_factor`; `pca` → `loadings [tenors × components]`, `scores`, `variance_explained`, `cumulative_variance`, `sdev`, `center`, `tenors`.

**Interpretation traps:**
- `lambda = 1/tau` is a **decay rate** (the position of the hump/loading), **NOT a yield** — do not use it as a spread. The `tau` is **estimated** (by optim), so the final `lambda` differs from `tau_init`.
- `cubic_spline` has **no** parametric beta/tau → `lambda=NA`; its factors are computed **empirically** (yc_level_slope_curvature), not from betas — do not compare them one-to-one with the NS betas.
- panel + NS = Diebold-Li: an **independent** fit per row (not a common lambda/state space); for joint dynamics run a VAR on the extracted factors (cat. 03).
- The PCA defaults to `scale=FALSE` (the covariance matrix) = the standard in yield-curve PCA; `scale=TRUE` (the correlation matrix) changes the loadings; the **sign** of the loadings/scores is arbitrary (identifiability up to sign).
- `forward` without `horizon` = instantaneous; with `horizon>0` = forward-forward (between maturity and maturity+horizon) — a different quantity.
- `n_components` (pca) is limited to `min(n_obs-1, n_maturities)`; exceeding it → a silent reduction by the package (the gate blocks it).

**Sources:** the `parametric_yield_curve` reference manual/help (`yc_fit`→`yc_nelson_siegel/yc_svensson/yc_cubic_spline`, `yc_level_slope_curvature`, `yc_predict`, `yc_forward`, `yc_discount`, `yc_pca` — live introspection, 0.1.0) < Nelson & Siegel 1987 (*J. Business* 60:473); Svensson 1994 (IMF WP 94/114); Diebold & Li 2006 (*J. Econometrics* 130:337); Litterman & Scheinkman 1991 (*J. Fixed Income* 1:54, PCA level/slope/curvature).
