### #257 Categorical association / contingency tables (chi-square, Fisher's exact test, measures of association) — `DescTools` + `stats` (`c25_expectations_surveys/categorical_association_contingency.py`)
**Functions:** `ca_contingency` [`table`, `outer` — the table + the expected counts + Cochran diagnostics], `ca_chisq` [`chisq.test`], `ca_fisher` [`fisher.test`], `ca_assocs` [`CramerV`/`ContCoef`/`TschuprowT`/`Phi`/`UncertCoef`/`GoodmanKruskalTau`/`GoodmanKruskalGamma`/`Assocs`]

**When:** the node for **CATEGORICAL QUESTIONNAIRES**: two categorical answers **per respondent** (e.g. "do you expect prices to rise/stay flat/fall?" × "are you planning a major purchase?"; sector × the assessment of orders in a business survey). The flow: `ca_contingency` (what the data look like — the table, the expected counts, the sparsity) → **routing**: `cochran_ok = TRUE` ⇒ `ca_chisq` (the asymptotic Pearson chi-square); `cochran_ok = FALSE` ⇒ `ca_fisher` (EXACT) or `simulate_p_value = TRUE` (Monte Carlo, seeded) → `ca_assocs` for the **SIZE** of the relationship (V/C/T/U/tau, + the ordinal measures only on request) with confidence intervals. The **input is numerically coded OBSERVATION VECTORS** (one integer code per respondent), **NOT** a ready contingency table — the table is built by the node **after** the cross-section gate.

**When NOT:** on **time series / temporally dependent data** — a hard gate (see the Preconditions); the HAC path: `hac_robust_standard` (cat 07). On **continuous** variables (discretise first: `c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column.bn_quantile_bins`, and `bn_apply` for the next wave with the SAME breaks). For the **quantification** of survey shares into quantitative expectations (balance/Carlson–Parkin) → `quantifying_qualitative_survey`. For **weighted/complex samples** (weights/strata/clusters) → `design_complex_survey` (`svychisq`, Rao–Scott) — #257 presupposes a SIMPLE random sample. For **stratified / ≥3-dimensional** tables (`mantelhaen.test`/`loglin`/Breslow–Day) — another family. For a **continuous vs categorical** comparison → #250 `tests-parametric` / #251 `tests-nonparametric`. Charts: **only** in the frontend (§5).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **NORMATIVE GATE 4 — CROSS-SECTION ONLY** (the normative gate spec §3b): every exported function calls the **SHARED** `gate_cross_section_only` (`the reference/wrapper_gates` — written ONCE, shared with #250/#251; it is not duplicated here) on the **original** vectors: an explicit rejection of `ts/mts/xts/zoo/tsibble/…` **and** a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck (lag = `min(10, n/5)`, FPP §5.4; **`gate_alpha`** 0.05 by default, only when `ordered = TRUE`). Autocorrelation **inflates the Type I error** ⇒ a spuriously significant chi-square. The diagnostics are returned as `cross_section_gate` (with `gate_alpha`, `ordered`, `branch`). **This is why the input is observation vectors** — the Ljung-Box test is not defined on an aggregated table.
- **`gate_alpha` (0.05 by default) — DECOUPLED from the `alpha` of the test.** `alpha` exists **only** in `ca_chisq`/`ca_fisher` (the only functions with a `decision`) and governs **only** that; `ca_contingency`/`ca_assocs` **do not expose it at all** (it would be a silent no-op). **The precheck is a test of size `gate_alpha`** ⇒ by construction it blocks a small share of **valid i.i.d.** input; measured live (version 4.6.1, `rnorm`, 5000 replications): `n = 200` → **1.6% / 5.7% / 10.1%**, `n = 60` → **2.3% / 6.7% / 10.8%** for `0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10`.
- **`ordered` (`TRUE` by default) — an EXPLICIT declaration about the row order.** Survey answers are the archetypal **exchangeable** population, but a sorted CSV makes the Ljung–Box test reject (live-verified: the same numbers, `sort` ⇒ blocked), whereas `chisq.test`/`fisher.test`/`CramerV` are **permutation-invariant** (the contingency table does not change). `ordered = FALSE` ⇒ an explicit skip of the Ljung–Box test (`branch = "skipped-by-declaration"`, `decision = "pass-unordered"`), with the structural checks and the **rejection of a time-series class** (`branch: class-rejected`) **always** active. `lb_lag` together with `ordered = FALSE` ⇒ a hard `stop`.
- **The input:** `x`/`y` plain **numeric** vectors of INTEGER codes, **of the same length** (paired answers), free of NaN/Inf; non-integer values ⇒ a stop (for a continuous variable `table` would create one level per unique value). `na_action` is **explicit**: `'fail'` (the default) | `'omit'` pairwise (`n_input`/`n_na` are always in the output). ≥ 4 complete pairs. **≥ 2 levels** per variable and **≤ `max_levels`** (20 by default, permitted range [2,50]). A **ZERO MARGIN** (an empty row/column) ⇒ a stop. Declared `x_levels`/`y_levels` must be a **superset** of the observed ones (otherwise `factor` silently produces NA); `x_labels`/`y_labels` unique, non-empty, one-to-one with the **sorted** codes.
- **The expected frequencies (`ca_chisq`)**: `rule = 'cochran'` (the default) — no expected count < 1 **AND** ≤ 20% of the cells < 5; `rule = 'strict'` — none < 5 (exactly the condition of the warning). It does not apply when `simulate_p_value = TRUE` (the Monte Carlo test does not rest on the asymptotics). The checking tool: **`ca_contingency`** (`min_expected`, `n_cells_below_1/5`, `share_below_5`, `cochran_ok`, `strict_ok`).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `ca_chisq` (asymptotic, fast, it gives per-cell residuals/contributions) **vs** `ca_fisher` (exact, for small/sparse samples, + an odds ratio & CI in the 2×2 case) **vs** `simulate_p_value = TRUE` (when Fisher does not fit in memory: a "FEXACT error"). The criterion is given **numerically** by `ca_contingency` (Cochran), not by judgement. In the measures: `scale = 'nominal'` (a safe default) ⇒ V / C / T / U / the Goodman–Kruskal **tau** (a PRE measure); `scale = 'ordinal'` **only if the codes encode an ordering** ⇒ + Gamma / Kendall's tau-b / Stuart's tau-c / Somers' D / Pearson–Spearman. `Phi` **only** for 2×2.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `ca_contingency`: `counts`/`expected` (bare r×c double matrices with dimnames) + `prop_total`/`prop_row`/`prop_col` + `row_sums`/`col_sums` + `min_expected`/`n_cells_below_1`/`n_cells_below_5`/`share_below_5`/`n_cells` + **`cochran_ok`/`strict_ok`** (the routing criterion) + `df`.
- `ca_chisq`: `statistic` (**the statistic OF THE TEST** — Yates-corrected when `correct = TRUE` **and** the table is 2×2) / **`statistic_pearson`** (**always** the UNCORRECTED Pearson X²) / `df`/`p_value`/`significant`/`decision` (`reject-independence` | `fail-to-reject`) + `cramers_v` (**always computed from `statistic_pearson`** ⇒ **identical** to `ca_assocs.nominal.cramers_v[["estimate"]]`) + the **per-cell** `residuals` (the Pearson (O−E)/sqrt(E)), `stdres` (~N(0,1)), `contribution` (= the residual squared), `contribution_share` (the share of `statistic_pearson` — it **always sums to 1**) — **these are the chart-data**: which cell "drives" the relationship. `yates_requested` vs **`yates_applied`** (what was ACTUALLY done).
- `ca_fisher`: `p_value`/`decision` + `odds_ratio` & `odds_ratio_lwr`/`upr`/`conf_level` (**2×2 only**, the conditional MLE — `NA` elsewhere) + `is_2x2` + `workspace` or (`simulate_p_value`, `B`, `seed`).
- `ca_assocs`: `nominal$*` (each one `c(estimate, lwr.ci, upr.ci)`), `phi` (2×2, otherwise `NULL`), `gamma` (ordinal, otherwise `NULL`), `assocs` = the **(16 or 9)×3** `Assocs` matrix (estimate + CI) + `assocs_measures` / `ordinal_excluded`.
- **Common to all of them:** `x_codes`/`y_codes` + `x_labels`/`y_labels` (**§3b gate 6 — externalising the coding**: the node performs no fit/transform, but the *coding* is the "fitted" object; it is always returned and passed back as `x_levels`/`y_levels` in the next wave ⇒ tables that are comparable cell by cell), `n`/`n_input`/`n_na`/`na_action`, and `cross_section_gate` (`lb_statistic`, `lb_p_value`, `lb_lag`, `n`, `n_na`, `alpha`, `tested`, `decision`).
- **Yates vs the effect size (CRITICAL, live-verified):** Cramér's V is defined (Cramér 1946 §21.9) on the **UNCORRECTED** Pearson X², **not** on the Yates-corrected `statistic` — which is the **default** for 2×2 tables (`correct = TRUE`). The node always computes the **size** measures from `statistic_pearson`, regardless of `correct`, so that `ca_chisq.cramers_v` **coincides** (< 1e-12, pinned in a regression test) with `ca_assocs.nominal.cramers_v[["estimate"]]` (`CramerV`). Live (2×2, n = 120): from Yates **0.5009034** vs from Pearson **0.5175817** — a 4.4% **understatement** of the relationship and **two different numbers for one named statistic**. Likewise `contribution_share` is divided by `statistic_pearson` (otherwise it summed to 1.0678 — "shares" > 100%). On the Monte Carlo path the reference sets `YATES = 0` ⇒ `statistic == statistic_pearson`.
- **A `factor` input ⇒ a hard stop with an instructive message:** a factor is the **most likely** wrong type in a categorical node **and** exactly the type about which `mode` **lies** (live: `mode(factor(x))` == `"numeric"` while `is.numeric(factor(x))` == `FALSE`). The gate names the argument, gives the **class** + `nlevels` (never the `mode`) and the explicit conversion `as.integer(x)` (the codes 1.k in the order of the levels) + `levels(x)` → `x_labels`.
- **Traps (all live-verified, version 4.6.1):** `chisq.test` with expected counts < 5 ⇒ **only a warning** "Chi-squared approximation may be incorrect" (which is why we have our own hard gate); a table with **one** row ⇒ a **silent** fallback to a goodness-of-fit test (the post-check `df == (r−1)(c−1)`); `table` drops NA **silently**; a zero margin ⇒ `X-squared = NaN`, `p = NA` with only a warning; `Phi` on a 3×3 table of perfect association = **1.414214 > 1** (it returns sqrt(X²/n), not phi); `fisher.test` on an r×c table **silently ignores** the `alternative` (a 3×3 "less" = the two-sided p); Yates is silently ignored outside the 2×2 case; FEXACT: a 4×4 table with n=300 fails at the default `workspace = 2e5` ("FEXACT error 6. LDKEY=620 is too small"), some such tables pass with 2e6 while denser ones fail there too ("FEXACT error 7"), and a 12×12 table fails even with 2e8 ⇒ then **only** `simulate_p_value` remains.
- **Determinism (§5):** all the default paths are algebraic (and `CramerV(method='fisher')` = the Fisher z transformation, not a simulation); the two Monte Carlo paths run with `set.seed(seed)` **and** restore the caller's `.Random.seed` (L1 purity); `Assocs` is PINNED to `verbose = 3` (with 1/2 it returns 3 of the 16 measures ⇒ the shape would change).
- **The boundary with #114** (`c00_data_utilities/robust_outlier_handling.py`, `dt_winsorize`/`dt_trim`/`dt_robscale`/`dt_huber`): that one is a **numeric data utility** (cleaning the tails of **continuous** series); this one is **categorical inference** on survey data. Zero shared DescTools functions, zero shared names (`dt_` vs `ca_`), different category folders ⇒ CLAUDE.md §3.b is respected. **Masking**: both files use `requireNamespace` + — in the shared `source` env DescTools masks `Phi` (the target function of this node **and** critical for the VAR wrappers), `BoxCox`, `Lc/Gini/…`, `MAPE`, %c%`, `BrierScore`, `Quarter`, `AUC`.

**Sources:** Cochran (1954) "Some Methods for Strengthening the Common chi-square Tests", *Biometrics* 10(4):417-451 (the rule <1 / ≤20% <5); Cramér (1946) *Mathematical Methods of Statistics* §21.9; Goodman & Kruskal (1954) "Measures of Association for Cross Classifications", *JASA* 49:732-764; Agresti (2013) *Categorical Data Analysis* 3rd ed., ch. 2-3 (nominal vs ordinal); Fisher (1935) *The Design of Experiments* ch. II; version 4.6.1 `the chisq.test documentation` / `the fisher.test documentation` ("For 2 by 2 tables, the null of conditional independence is equivalent to the hypothesis that the odds ratio equals one"); the DescTools 0.99.60 reference — < the normative gate spec §3b normative gate 4 + Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, *FPP* 3rd ed. §5.4 (lag = min(10, n/5)).

## §28. Text-as-data / textual sentiment — `c26_text_as_data/`

**Text as data**: from a corpus of texts (e.g. central-bank communications/news) to lexicon-based sentiment, temporal aggregation into indices, and sparse-regression forecasting of macro quantities (#234). NOT for structured numeric data.

### #234 — Textual sentiment → time aggregation → sparse-regression forecasting · `textual_sentiment_pipeline`

**Category:** `26-text-as-data` · **Wrapper:** `c26_text_as_data/textual_sentiment_pipeline.py` · **Tool fns:** `snt_corpus`, `snt_sentiment`, `snt_measures`, `snt_model`

**What/Why.** The full text-as-data chain (Ardia-Bluteau-Boudt): it turns time-stamped **text** (news/reports) into numeric **sentiment indices** per lexicon×feature×time-scheme, aggregates them into **time series**, and uses them as **sparse (elastic-net) predictors** of a macro variable `y`. 4 stages chained through registry handles: `snt_corpus` (a df {id,date,texts,+numeric features} → a `sento_corpus`) → `snt_sentiment` (lexicon-based document sentiment) → `snt_measures` (the temporal aggregation) → `snt_model` (a glmnet elastic net).

**When.** You have a text corpus with dates and want: (a) the tokenizable corpus, (b) document-level sentiment with the built-in lexicons (LM_en/HENRY_en/GI_en/FEEL/…) and a `how` scheme (counts/proportional/TFIDF/UShaped/…), (c) time-aggregated measures (lexicon×feature×time-scheme), or (d) a sparse elastic-net forecast of a `y` on top of them.
**When NOT.** You have no text (only numeric series → #219/#220 shrinkage/ML); you want a general sparse regression without textual sentiment; word embeddings/transformer NLP (outside the surface); the ingestion of the data (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node).

**Master-tree routing.** Build the corpus → `snt_corpus` (it registers `corpus`) · document sentiment → `snt_sentiment` (`lexicons`, `how`; it registers `sentiment`) · the time aggregation → `snt_measures` (`by`, `lag`, `how_time`, `how_docs`, `fill`; it registers `measures`) · the sparse-regression forecast → `snt_model` (`model` gaussian/binomial/multinomial, `type` BIC/AIC/Cp/cv, `alphas`, `train_window`/`test_window`, `seed`). Each stage feeds the next through a raw handle.

**Key output fields.** `snt_corpus`: `corpus` (registered) + `n_documents`/`date_min`/`date_max`/`features`. `snt_sentiment`: `sentiment` (registered; the per-document records = chart-data) + `sentiment_columns`/`lexicons`/`how`. `snt_measures`: `measures` (registered) + `measures_table` (the date + the measure columns = chart-data) + `measure_names`/`n_measures`/`n_dates`/`dimensions`. `snt_model`: `coefficients`, a df {term,coefficient (+class in the multinomial case)} + `alpha`/`lambda` (the selected one)/`n_predictors`/`n_selected` (the non-zero ones excluding the intercept)/`discarded`/`ic_criterion` (NA under cv)/`fit_dates` + the raw `fit` (to_mcp → a stub).

**Interpretation traps (CRITICAL, pinned in the tests).**
- **A 4-stage chain:** each stage **registers** the raw sentometrics object (`corpus`/`sentiment`/`measures`) as a handle that is passed to the next one as a **raw_handle**; `snt_model` is **TERMINAL**.
- **The information criteria** (`type`=BIC/AIC/Cp) are supported **ONLY for `model='gaussian'`**; `binomial`/`multinomial` **REQUIRE** `type='cv'` (with a `train_window`/`test_window`) — a hard gate.
- `y` must be **aligned** with the measure dates (`length == n_dates`); gaussian numeric; binomial exactly 2 values; multinomial ≥3 values.
- `how_time` & `alphas` are **vectors that are tried** (ALL of them are attempted, NOT a match.arg); `how_time='own'` is not supported (a custom weight matrix is outside the surface). `alpha`=0=ridge, =1=lasso; `n_selected` = the sparse (non-zero) coefficients.
- **MASKING:** `library(sentometrics)` does **not** attach data.table/quanteda (the search path stays clean). `type='cv'` performs a **runtime `require(caret)`** (→ ggplot2/lattice are attached); the wrapper calls no bare generic (everything is /). The package's stdout ("alphas run…/Training model…") is swallowed by `.snt_call` (capture.output). The `seed` locks the cv fold RNG (the IC path is deterministic anyway, identical when seeded).

**Sources.** sentometrics v1.0.1 reference manual · Ardia-Bluteau-Boudt-Borms-Vrontos 2021 JSS 99(2) · Ardia-Bluteau-Boudt 2019 IJF 35(4) (sparse news-sentiment forecasting) · Loughran-McDonald 2011 JF / Henry 2008 / the General Inquirer (the lexicons) · Zou-Hastie 2005 (the elastic net) / Friedman-Hastie-Tibshirani 2010 JSS (glmnet) · the wrapper footer.

## §29. Frequency domain: wavelet & spectral — `c27_frequency_domain/`

**Frequency / time-frequency analysis**: wavelets (the Morlet CWT, cross-wavelet, coherence, phase — the non-stationary detection of cycles that change over time; #235) and a classical spectral overview (a smoothed periodogram / spectrum / cumulative periodogram + KS bands for business-cycle peaks & seasonality; #236). They return NUMERIC grids — no graphics (charts belong to the frontend only).

### #235 — Wavelet time-frequency analysis (the Morlet CWT) · `WaveletComp`

**Category:** `27-frequency-domain` · **Wrapper:** `c27_frequency_domain/wavelet_time_frequency.py` · **Tool fns:** `wv_wavelet`, `wv_coherency`

**What/Why.** A time-frequency analysis with the continuous wavelet transform (the CWT, Morlet): how the spectral power of a macro series changes OVER TIME (evolving/non-stationary cycles) and how TWO series are related per period/time. It returns ONLY the numeric grids (power/coherence/phase/period/the axes/the COI) — never plots (charts = the frontend only, §5). The input data = a `DataFrame` of evenly spaced, complete series (a df_handle); the column is chosen with `series`/`x`/`y`.

**When.** You suspect that the spectrum is NOT constant (a time-varying business-cycle period, structural breaks in the periodicity) and want the power spectrum (period × time) with a ridge & significance; or you want the DYNAMIC (localised) relationship of two series: the cross-wavelet power, the wavelet coherence ∈[0,1], and the phase difference (a lead/lag per frequency).
**When NOT.** A stationary series with a constant spectrum → a classical spectral analysis (`stats` spectrum / an AR spectrum, #234); a time-invariant band isolation → band-pass/HP/Baxter-King filters (#56–61); a simple lead-lag correlation without a frequency dimension → ccf.

**Master-tree routing.** One series → `wv_wavelet` (`analyze.wavelet`): power/phase/amplitude/ridge/the global power + surrogate p-values · two aligned series → `wv_coherency` (`analyze.coherency`): the cross power / the coherence ∈[0,1] / the phase difference (angle) + p-values. The `method` (white.noise by default · shuffle · Fourier.rand · AR · ARIMA) selects the null-model surrogate; `n_sim` sets the number of simulations.

**Key output fields.** `wv_wavelet`: `power` (a period×time matrix), `phase`, `amplitude`, `ridge` (0/1), `power_avg` (the global spectrum), `power_pval`/`power_avg_pval` (NULL if `make_pval=FALSE`), `period`/`scale`, `axis_time`/`axis_period`, `coi_time`/`coi_period` (the cone of influence), `n_time`(=nc)/`n_period`(=nr). `wv_coherency`: `cross_power`, `coherence` (∈[0,1]), `angle` (the phase difference), `power_x`/`power_y`, `ridge_xy`/`ridge_co`, `*_avg`, `*_pval`, `period`/`scale`/the axes/the coi. All of it is numeric chart-data; the raw `fit` (to_mcp → a stub, a complex Wave).

**Interpretation traps (CRITICAL, pinned in the tests).**
- **The cone of influence:** power/coherence INSIDE the COI (`coi_time`/`coi_period`) is edge-affected → interpret only outside the COI. An `upper_period > n*dt` gives a spectrum that lies ENTIRELY inside the COI (not one full cycle) = plausible-but-nonsense; WaveletComp **does not error** → a **hard gate** (a silent-wrong blocker).
- **Determinism:** the CWT power/phase/period is **seed-invariant** (a pure transform); ONLY the surrogate p-values (`make_pval=TRUE`) are stochastic → `set.seed(seed)` before the call (identical p-values confirmed). Keep `n_sim` small.
- **The coherence ∈[0,1]** is a localised squared-correlation analogue; a high coherence does NOT mean causality; the `angle` (the phase difference → a lead/lag) is interpreted ONLY where the coherence is significant.
- `loess_span` removes a trend BEFORE the CWT (0 = none); the series MUST be complete (NA/Inf → silent-wrong → a gate).
- The `method` null model: `white.noise` (the default) vs `AR`/`ARIMA` (which suit autocorrelated series) vs `Fourier.rand`/`shuffle` → a different strictness of significance.
- **Masking:** the wrapper does NOT call `library(WaveletComp)` — the package exports `ARIMA` (masking `ARIMA`/`ARIMA`), `AR`, `canonical_disk_format` (masking the Parquet `canonical_disk_format` of the node layer), `reconstruct`, `ridge` → `requireNamespace` + everywhere (the §3.a exception).

**Sources.** WaveletComp v1.2 reference manual + vignette (Roesch & Schmidbauer 2018) · Torrence & Compo 1998 BAMS (the CWT, the COI, Monte Carlo significance) · Aguiar-Conraria & Soares 2014 J. Econ. Surveys (macro time-frequency analysis, coherence & phase) · the wrapper footer.

### #236 — A spectral / periodogram quick look · `stats`

**Category:** `27-frequency-domain` · **Wrapper:** `c27_frequency_domain/spectral_periodogram_quick.py` · **Tool fns:** `sp_periodogram`, `sp_spectrum`, `sp_cumulative_periodogram`

**What/Why.** A frequency-domain quick look at ONE univariate macro series: which periodicities (seasonality, business-cycle cycles) dominate. Base `stats`, NO new dependency. The input data = a stored `ts` or a single-series `DataFrame` (a series_handle; the ts adapter converts a df through `ts_ts`).

**When.** (a) A smoothed periodogram with full control (spans/taper/detrend/pad) → `sp_periodogram`; (b) a smooth AR (Yule-Walker) spectral estimate for a clean dominant cycle when the raw periodogram is noisy → `sp_spectrum(method="ar")`; (c) a numeric cumulative periodogram + KS bands to test for white noise → `sp_cumulative_periodogram`.
**When NOT.** Multivariate coherency/phase between series (the node handles ONE series); wavelets / a time-varying spectrum (`WaveletComp`, #237); spectral causality/connectedness; plain ARIMA/seasonal modelling; series with < 4 observations or with NA (a gate).

**Master-tree routing.** A smoothed/raw periodogram (the dominant frequency+period) → `sp_periodogram` (`spans` = odd modified-Daniell smoothers; `NULL` = raw) · a high-level dispatcher → `sp_spectrum` (`method` = `pgram` | `ar`; the AR `order` chosen automatically by AIC or given; `n_freq` points) · a white-noise test → `sp_cumulative_periodogram` (Bartlett's Tp: a curve outside the ±`crit` bands around the diagonal ⇒ white noise is rejected).

**Key output fields.** `sp_periodogram`: `freq`/`spec` (chart-ready numeric vectors), `peak_frequency`+`peak_period` (=1/freq), `df`/`bandwidth`/`taper`/`pad`/`detrend`/`demean`/`n_used`/`orig_n`, `smoothed`+`spans`, the raw `spec_object` (to_mcp → a stub). `sp_spectrum`: `freq`/`spec`, `method`+`method_label`, `ar_order` (NA under pgram), `peak_frequency`/`peak_period`. `sp_cumulative_periodogram`: `frequency`, `cumulative` (0→1, monotone), `band_upper`/`band_lower` (the KS bands clamped to [0,1]), `crit`, `nyquist`, `mp`, `n_exceedances`+`white_noise_rejected`.

**Interpretation traps (CRITICAL, pinned in the tests).**
- **`spans` = ODD positive integers:** `spec.pgram` accepts even spans **SILENTLY** and returns the **WRONG** modified-Daniell smoother → a hard gate (it blocks them).
- **`cpgram` is PLOT-ONLY** (it draws + returns `invisible`, with NO numeric return) → it is **NOT** called; `sp_cumulative_periodogram` reproduces THE SAME algorithm numerically: center → `spec.taper` → `Mod(fft)^2/n` → `y[1]=0` → `cumsum/sum`; `crit = 1.358/(sqrt(mp)+0.12+0.11/sqrt(mp))`; the bands = `fr/xm ± crit` (a slope of 1/Nyquist), verified against the source of `cpgram`.
- **The AR spectrum on a trending/persistent series** peaks at frequency **0** → `peak_period = 1/0` → **NA** is returned (not Inf).
- `spec.pgram` omits frequency 0 (`freq` is always > 0); the peak is always a genuine cycle. `detrend=TRUE` (the default) removes the trend + the mean; `taper` defaults to 0.1 (a split-cosine bell).
- The node handles ONE series (an mts → a gate; no coherency/phase); NA → an explicit gate (`na.action=na.fail`).
- The FFT + Yule-Walker are **deterministic** (no RNG; `identical` across two runs) → no seed is needed.

**Sources.** The the reference `stats` spec.pgram / spectrum / cpgram help pages (cpgram verified to be PLOT-ONLY through the `cpgram` source) · Venables & Ripley 2002 (MASS) pp. 392–397 (the cumulative periodogram / Bartlett's Tp) · Bloomfield 1976 · Brockwell & Davis 1991 · Priestley 1981 · the wrapper footer.

## §30. Trade, gravity & economic complexity — `c28_trade_gravity/`

**Bilateral trade & the external sector**: gravity models (OLS/PPML/FE/BVU/tetrads with a treatment of multilateral resistance; #237), penalised PPML for high-dimensional fixed effects (#238), and economic complexity / the product space (RCA-Balassa, ECI/PCI, proximity; #239). NOT for the univariate forecasting of trade flows.

### #237 — Gravity models of bilateral trade (OLS / PPML / FE / BVU / tetrads) · `gravity_bilateral_trade`

**Category:** `28-trade-gravity` · **Wrapper:** `c28_trade_gravity/gravity_bilateral_trade.py` · **Tool fns:** `gr_ppml`, `gr_ols`, `gr_fixed_effects`, `gr_bvu`, `gr_tetrads`

**What/Why.** The estimation of **gravity models of bilateral trade** on a dyadic panel/cross-section `DataFrame {origin, destination, flow, distance, (GDPs), (dummies)}` (a df_handle). Five complementary estimators that differ in how they handle the **Multilateral-Resistance (MR) terms** (Anderson-van Wincoop) and the **zero flows**: PPML (a multiplicative form that accepts zeros), log-log OLS (without MR), importer+exporter fixed effects (which absorb the MR with dummies), Bonus vetus OLS (MR through demeaning, which keeps the comparative statics), and the Head-Mayer-Ries tetrads (a ratio of ratios that eliminates the monadic effects). It returns tidy coefficients, the **distance elasticity**, numeric fit statistics, and the raw fit (to_mcp → a stub).

**When.** You have a bilateral structure {exporter × importer} and want trade elasticities with respect to distance/income/trade-cost proxies (rta, contig, comlang). Choosing the estimator: **zeros or heteroskedasticity → `gr_ppml`** (the safe default, the log-of-gravity critique); **a log-log baseline → `gr_ols`** (flow>0 only); **a theoretically consistent MR treatment without counterfactuals → `gr_fixed_effects`**; **MR + comparative statics → `gr_bvu`**; **the elimination of monadic effects without dummies → `gr_tetrads`** (a reference exporter+importer, it requires ≥1 dyadic regressor).
**When NOT.** No dyadic structure (a time series/univariate problem); input-output/networks (#48–55); a plain panel FE model without a gravity structure (#46–47 `panel_unit_root`); censored/tobit trade (`gpml`/`tobit` — separate cards); the ingestion of the data (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node).

**Master-tree routing.** Zeros in the flow → `gr_ppml` (`>=0`) · a traditional log-log model with explicit incomes → `gr_ols` · the absorption of all the MR/monadic terms with country dummies → `gr_fixed_effects` · MR-consistency with the comparative statics preserved → `gr_bvu` · a reference-based ratio of ratios (multi-way clustered SEs with `multiway=TRUE`) → `gr_tetrads`.

**Key output fields.** `coefficients` (a tidy df {term, estimate, std_error, statistic, p_value}); `distance_term`/`distance_coef` (the central gravity elasticity); `fitstats` (numeric: n_obs, r_squared/adj, sigma, logLik, aic/bic, deviance/null_deviance, `pseudo_r2`=1−dev/null.dev **for glm/ppml only**, df_residual); `method`/`fit_class`/`robust` + the method flags (family, accepts_zeros, uie, mr_terms, fixed_effects, method_family, multiway, filters); `fit` (a glm/lm/rlm/coeftest object → a stub).

**Interpretation traps (CRITICAL, pinned in the tests).**
- **A silent row drop:** the distance & (for OLS/FE/BVU/tetrads) the dependent variable & the incomes are logged AUTOMATICALLY → they must be **STRICTLY POSITIVE**; non-positive values give log=NaN/−Inf and the rows are dropped **SILENTLY** (verified: `gravity_zeros` 500→355 obs with no warning) → hard gates. For zeros in the flow → `gr_ppml` (`>=0`).
- **`gr_ols` with `uie=TRUE` is broken (a package bug, gravity 1.1):** the formula refers to `inc_o_log`/`inc_d_log`, which the `uie=TRUE` path does not create → `object 'inc_o_log' not found` (regardless of additional_regressors, verified live) → **HARD-GATED**; the only working value is `uie=FALSE`.
- **`robust=TRUE` → `rlm`:** the summary has 3 columns (Value/Std.Error/t) **without a p-value** → `p_value=NA` (as expected).
- **`gr_tetrads`:** it requires ≥1 `additional_regressor` (dyadic); NULL → a cryptic dplyr join error (verified) → a gate; `filter_origin`/`filter_destination` must EXIST in the code columns. `multiway=TRUE` → an `coeftest` matrix (the fit statistics come from the attributes nobs/df/logLik).
- **`gr_ppml`:** quasipoisson → AIC/logLik = NA; use `pseudo_r2`, not `r_squared`. **`gr_fixed_effects`:** the unilateral GDPs are absorbed by the FE — they are not estimated.
- All the estimators are **deterministic** (OLS/IRLS/rlm/cluster.vcov) → no seed; `identical` across two runs confirmed. **Masking:** `nls` masks `nls` → the wrapper does not call `library(gravity)` (requireNamespace + everywhere).

**Sources.** gravity v1.1 (Wölwer-Burgard-Kunst) reference manual · Silva & Tenreyro 2006 ReStat 88(4) (PPML) · Feenstra 2002 SJPE 49(5) (FE) · Baier & Bergstrand 2009 JIE 77(1) / 2010 CUP (BVU) · Head-Mayer-Ries 2010 JIE 81(1) (the tetrads) · Head & Mayer 2014 Handbook of Int'l Econ vol 4 + Anderson-van Wincoop 2003 (MR) · the wrapper footer.

### #238 — Penalised PPML gravity with high-dimensional fixed effects · `penalized_poisson_pml`

**Category:** `28-trade-gravity` · **Wrapper:** `c28_trade_gravity/penalized_poisson_pml.py` · **Tool fns:** `pp_hdfeppml`, `pp_penhdfeppml`, `pp_mlfitppml`

**What/Why.** Structural gravity on ONE long bilateral-trade panel with **Poisson Pseudo-Maximum-Likelihood** (Santos Silva & Tenreyro 2006: it models `E[y]=exp(x·beta)` in levels, and handles zero flows & heteroskedasticity) and **several high-dimensional fixed effects** (exporter-time, importer-time, pair) through the fast Correia-Guimaraes-Zylkin (2020) partialling out. When the regressors are MANY (e.g. hundreds of dummies for the provisions of trade agreements), **penalisation** (lasso/ridge/plugin; Breinlich et al. 2021) selects the relevant subset. The data = ONE gravity `DataFrame` (a df_handle); `dep`/`indep`/`fixed`/`cluster` are passed BY COLUMN NAME.

**When.** You have a dyadic (exporter x importer x [time]) trade panel and want: (a) the HDFE PPML baseline (`pp_hdfeppml`), (b) a penalised fit at one lambda (`pp_penhdfeppml`, lasso/ridge or plugin), or (c) the whole penalisation path with an automatic BIC choice of lambda / a plugin lasso (`pp_mlfitppml`).
**When NOT.** A log-OLS gravity model on positive-only flows (biased); few regressors with no need for selection (→ `fepois`, #33); economic complexity ECI/PCI (#237); a negative/non-count dependent variable; the ingestion of the data (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node).

**Master-tree routing.** Unpenalised baseline coefficients + SE → `pp_hdfeppml` · a single-lambda penalised fit (a known lambda) → `pp_penhdfeppml` (`penalty` lasso/ridge; `plugin=TRUE`+`cluster` for data-driven loadings) · the path + a BIC-selected lambda or plugin → `pp_mlfitppml` (`lambdas` a vector, or `plugin=TRUE`+`cluster`; `post=TRUE` for a de-biased post-lasso).

**Key output fields.** `pp_hdfeppml`: `coefficients` (named) + `se` + `deviance`/`bic` + `n_obs`/`n_coef` + `fixed_effects`. `pp_penhdfeppml`: `coefficients` + `deviance`/`bic` + `lambda` + `penalty` + `n_selected` (the non-zero ones) + `phi` (the plugin loadings, or NULL). `pp_mlfitppml`: `beta_path` (a regressors×lambdas matrix) + `lambdas` + `bic_path` (a matrix [lambda,bic]) + `selected_lambda`/`selected_bic` + `selected_coefficients` (the argmin-BIC column) + `n_selected` + `phi` (plugin) + `seed`.

**Interpretation traps (CRITICAL, pinned in the tests).**
- **PPML in levels, a non-negative dependent variable:** negative/NA `dep` → `log(y/mu)=NaN` → a cryptic crash; a hard gate (non-negative flows, free of NA, ≥1 positive value).
- **`fixed` MUST be a list:** penppml requires `fixed` in **list** form (a list of character vectors = interaction FE); a plain character vector fails cryptically ("not all arguments have the same length"); the wrapper **normalises** it into a list (each plain name → a single FE).
- **lasso vs ridge:** the lasso (L1) zeroes/selects (`n_selected` = the non-zero ones); ridge (L2) **NEVER** zeroes.
- **IC selection:** `selected_lambda` = the argmin of the **finite** BIC in `bic_path` (DETERMINISTIC); an all-NA/degenerate BIC (too large a lambda → an all-zero fit) → the 1st lambda with `bic=NA`.
- **plugin requires cluster:** `plugin=TRUE` (in both penalised functions) → a gate on `cluster` (cluster-robust penalty loadings); it returns `phi`.
- A non-numeric `indep` regressor is coerced **SILENTLY** into a meaningless coefficient → a hard gate (all numeric, free of NA).
- IRLS/glmnet are deterministic (`identical` when seeded); the `seed` is exposed as defence in depth; the raw fit is **NOT** returned (heavy per-observation internals → a to_mcp stub); `_int`/`xvalidate`/`selectobs`/`bootstrap`/`iceberg` were omitted (outside the node's estimator surface).

**Sources.** Santos Silva-Tenreyro 2006 (PPML); Correia-Guimaraes-Zylkin 2020 (fast HDFE PPML); Breinlich et al. 2021 (penalised/plugin PPML provisions); Belloni et al. 2016 (the plugin loadings); the penppml v0.2.4 reference manual+vignette (live-verified).

### #239 — Economic complexity: RCA / ECI-PCI / product-space proximity · `economic_complexity_rca`

**Category:** `28-trade-gravity` · **Wrapper:** `c28_trade_gravity/economic_complexity_rca.py` · **Tool fns:** `ec_balassa`, `ec_complexity`, `ec_proximity`

**What/Why.** Economic-complexity metrics on a bipartite `country×product` network of export values: (a) the Revealed Comparative Advantage / Balassa index (specialisation), (b) the Economic Complexity Index (the ECI per country) + the Product Complexity Index (the PCI per product), (c) product-space proximity (country×country & product×product similarity, Hausmann–Hidalgo). The input data = a long trade `DataFrame {country, product, value(>=0)}` (a df_handle).

**When.** You have a country×product export matrix and want: (a) which countries have a comparative advantage in which products (RCA), (b) how "complex" the productive base of each country/product is (ECI/PCI), or (c) which products/countries are "close" in the product space (proximity, capability diffusion).
**When NOT.** Gravity/PPML trade-flow models (#237/#238 in the same category); a univariate time series (no bipartite structure); input-output / network centrality (#48–55); downstream product-space diffusion (complexity_outlook/density/distance/projections — a separate card if requested); the ingestion of the data (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node).

**Master-tree routing.** A specialisation matrix / diversification / ubiquity → `ec_balassa` (`discrete=TRUE` ⇒ 0/1 for RCA≥`cutoff`; `FALSE` ⇒ continuous) · ECI+PCI → `ec_complexity` (`method` = fitness [Tacchella, non-linear iterative] / reflections [Hidalgo–Hausmann iterated averaging] / eigenvalues [the 2nd eigenvector]) · product-space proximity → `ec_proximity` (`compute` = both/country/product).

**Key output fields.** `ec_balassa`: `balassa_index` (a country×product matrix with dimnames; discrete ⇒ 0/1) + `diversification` (the rowSums, per country) + `ubiquity` (the colSums, per product) + `n_countries`/`n_products`/`discrete`/`cutoff`. `ec_complexity`: `eci` (a named numeric per country) + `pci` (per product) + `method`/`iterations`/`extremality`. `ec_proximity`: `proximity_country` (country×country, or NULL) + `proximity_product` (product×product, or NULL) + `compute` + `n_countries`/`n_products` (NA if that side was not requested).

**Interpretation traps (CRITICAL, pinned in the tests).**
- **Masking:** `density` **masks `density`** in the shared `source` global env → the wrapper uses `requireNamespace` + `fn` everywhere (NEVER `library`; `conflicts(detail=TRUE)` live-confirmed).
- `balassa_index` **silently accepts negative values** and returns a plausible-but-wrong RCA → a **hard non-negativity gate** (Balassa is defined only on non-negative exports).
- **One country OR one product → a degenerate all-1 RCA** (silent-wrong) → a hard gate of **≥2 countries AND ≥2 products** (the convergence of the iterated reflections/eigenvalue methods).
- `discrete=TRUE` (0/1 for RCA≥`cutoff`) is the classical input for ECI/proximity; `continuous` changes the meaning of the downstream metrics.
- `extremality` affects **ONLY** `method='fitness'` (it is inert but still passed for reflections/eigenvalues); `eigenvalues` prints a cosmetic sign-correction **message** (suppressMessages, not a warning).
- **Deterministic** (linear algebra / iterated reflections); no RNG → no seed; `identical` across 2 runs is pinned. A **TERMINAL** node (no register/chaining): it returns chart-ready numbers, not a fitted model. `rca` (a deprecated alias) & the downstream outlook/density/distance/projections were omitted.

**Sources.** economiccomplexity v2.1.0 reference manual · Balassa 1965 (RCA) · Hidalgo–Hausmann 2009 PNAS (ECI/PCI, the reflections method) · Hausmann–Hidalgo 2014 Atlas (the product space) · Hidalgo et al. 2007 Science (proximity) · Tacchella et al. 2012 Sci. Rep. (fitness) · the wrapper footer.

## §31. Unsupervised clustering & similarity — `c29_unsupervised_clustering/`

**Clustering countries / series / regimes without a dependent variable**: distance & similarity matrices (#240), partitional clustering with k-means/PAM and a **rule-based** choice of k (#241), hierarchical clustering + dendrogram data (#242), DTW shape similarity (#243), model-based clustering with an automatic k (#244) and classical/non-metric MDS (#245). The flow is **always** the same: `#240` produces the `dist` object → `#242`/`#245` (and `#241` for the silhouette) consume it as a handle.

⚠️ **Two normative gates that are non-negotiable in EVERY node of the category** (`the normative gate spec` §3b):
1. **THE KEOGH GATE** — the clustering of **subsequences taken with a sliding window** is *provably meaningless*: the output **does not depend on the input** (the k-means centres degenerate into sine waves regardless of the data/k/algorithm). The node **explicitly rejects** such input for **any fixed step `k ≥ 1`** — not only `k = 1`: the "slide" is a free parameter of the construction of the subsequences, so a step-2 window is covered equally by the result. The **detection is written once** in `the reference/gate_sliding_window_step` (shared across #240/#241/#243/#244; `k ≤ ⌊m/2⌋` so that the overlap stays ≥ 50%); **whole-series** clustering is not affected (Keogh, Lin & Truppel).
2. **DO NOT impose detrending** — the macro clustering literature **deliberately** uses raw, non-seasonally-adjusted, non-detrended data (arXiv:1807.04004); detrending introduces **artificial distortions** (Hamilton on the HP filter). `transform`/`distance`/`method` are **explicit gated choices** (`match.arg`), **NEVER** a silent default differencing/scaling.

⚠️ **Determinism (charter §5):** only `k-means`/`clusGap` (#241) has a random initialisation ⇒ **a seed + `nstart>=2` + the canonicalisation of the cluster ids**. Everything else (`dist`, `hierarchical_clustering_distance`, `cutree`, `agnes`, `diana`, the `pam` build phase, `cmdscale`) is **fully deterministic without a seed**.

### #240 A distance / dissimilarity matrix (dist · correlation-based · proxy) — `stats` + `proxy` (`c29_unsupervised_clustering/distance_dissimilarity_matrix.py`)

**Functions:** `dm_dist` [`dist` — the 6 documented metrics, `p` for minkowski], `dm_cor_dist` [`cor` + `as.dist` — 3 coefficients × 3 r→distance transforms], `dm_proxy_dist` [`dist` — 14 allowlisted metrics that `dist` does **not** have].

**When:** it is the **first** node of every unsupervised flow. It produces the dissimilarity between "objects" — countries, macro series, regimes — which is the **mandatory** input for hierarchical clustering (#242), PAM/silhouette (#241) and MDS (#245). Typical uses: clustering countries on macro indicators, "which series move together" (correlation-based), regime identification. **The orientation is `required=TRUE`**: `rows_are_objects` (the objects in the rows) or `columns_are_objects` (the series in the **columns**, time in the rows = the typical macro panel).

**When NOT:** on **sliding-window subsequences** (the KEOGH gate — a hard stop); for shape-based similarity that is **robust to a time shift** → DTW (#243); for the cross distance between **two different sets** (`proxy` `y=`/`pairwise` → node #243); for **mixed-type** data (numeric + categorical; `daisy`/Gower is not exposed); for a **significance test** of a correlation (p-values/CI) → #81 `desc_cor_test` (`c00_data_utilities/descriptive_statistics.py`); for **filtering collinear columns** → #252 `cf_find_correlation` (`c00_data_utilities/correlation_filter_greedy.py`); for heatmaps/distance maps (**the frontend**, charter §5); with **one** object (n≥2, a hard gate).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- The input: a **numeric matrix, or a DataFrame whose columns are all numeric** (the non-numeric ones are **named** in the message). **Free of NA/NaN/Inf** — this is not politeness: `dist` **does not error** on NA, it excludes them and "*the sum is scaled up proportionally to the number of columns used*" (the dist documentation) ⇒ it returns a rescaled value **silently**. **n ≥ 2** objects (with n=1 it silently returns an empty `dist`), **≥ 1** feature, labels **non-empty & unique** (duplicates ⇒ an ambiguous matrix downstream).
- **The KEOGH gate** (normative): the detection of an overlap between successive rows with **any fixed step `k ≥ 1`** (**in either direction**) ⇒ a hard stop; the shared detector `the reference/gate_sliding_window_step`.
- `dm_dist` has **per-metric preconditions** (hard gates, not recommendations): `binary` ⇒ **every element ∈ {0,1}** (the dist documentation: "*The vectors are regarded as binary bits, so non-zero elements are 'on'*"); on continuous data everything is `on` and the result is **silently a matrix full of zeros**. The rule is `{0,1}` and **not** "exactly two distinct values" (a `{3,7}` input passes the loose check and gives **the same** zero matrix); the message points at the binning node (**#251 `bn_quantile_bins`**). `canberra` ⇒ **no negative** value (the dist documentation: "*This is intended for non-negative values (e.g., counts)*"). The checking tool: `c00_data_utilities/descriptive_statistics.desc_summary` / `dp_column_profile`.
- `dm_cor_dist`: **≥ 3 observations per object** (with 2 points `r = ±1` always — degenerate) and **no zero variance** (`cor` gives **only a warning** "the standard deviation is zero" and returns `NA`). The checking tool: `c00_data_utilities/fast_row_column.panel_col_stats(stat='sd')`.
- `dm_proxy_dist`: gates **per family** — norm-based (`cosine`/`angular`/`Chord`/`Geodesic`) ⇒ **no zero-norm** row; compositional (`Bray`/`Soergel`/`Whittaker`/`Hellinger`/`Kullback`/`divergence`/`Wave`/`Podani`/`eJaccard`) ⇒ **no negatives, no zero row sum**; `Mahalanobis` ⇒ **n > p** and `qr(cov).rank == p`.
- `dm_dist`: `p` **positive and finite** (live: `p<=0` → "distance: invalid p").

**Alternatives + criterion:** a **distance between levels** (the same scale of magnitude) → `dm_dist` (`euclidean` by default; `manhattan` is more robust; `canberra` **only** for non-negative counts; `binary` for on/off data; `minkowski` with an explicit `p`). **Shape synchronisation (co-movement)** → `dm_cor_dist`: `mantegna` `d=√(2(1−r))` is a **genuine metric** (Mantegna 1999) ⇒ **prefer it** when `ward.D2` (#242) or classical MDS (#245) follows; `one_minus` (`d=1−r`) when the **direction** matters (countercyclical series = far apart); `one_minus_abs` (`d=1−|r|`) when the **opposite phase** counts as similarity. `spearman`/`kendall` for a monotone/robust relationship. **An angle/profile without magnitude** → `dm_proxy_dist(cosine/angular/Chord/Geodesic)`. **Shares/compositions** → the compositional family. **Correlated variables** → `Mahalanobis`. **A time shift/a different phase speed** → DTW (#243).

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `distance_dissimilarity_matrix` = the full **symmetric** n×n double matrix with `dimnames` — the main **chart-data** (a distance map/heatmap in the frontend); `lower_tri` = the lower triangle **by column** (of length n(n−1)/2, the natural storage of the `dist` class); `labels`/`n_objects`/`n_features`.
- `min_distance`/`max_distance`/`mean_distance` = the **scale** (a range of ~0 ⇒ there is no structure to cluster). **`n_zero_pairs`** = the pairs at distance **exactly 0** (duplicate objects): `>0` warns about the downstream traps — `isoMDS` "zero or negative distance between objects i and j" (#245), **all the heights zero** in `hierarchical_clustering_distance`/`ac`,`dc` = `NaN` (#242), and the bound `k ≤ the number of DISTINCT rows` (#241).
- **`dist_object`** = the `dist`-class object itself, which L2 serialises with an **explicit** `to_mcp.dist` → `{lower_tri (the lower triangle by column), length, Size, Labels, method}`. The explicit method is **necessary**: merely loading the `proxy` namespace registers engine-wide `dim.dist`/`names.dist` methods, so the default path produced `dim = c(n,n)` for a vector of length `n(n−1)/2`, **lost** the `length` and filled in **bogus** `names`. The full symmetric matrix is **not** repeated there (it already exists as `distance_dissimilarity_matrix`). → **`register(field="dist_object")` in all 3 functions**: this is the **producer** node of the category (a handle → #241/#242/#245; an object-store pointer, `docs/architecture/wrapper-to-node.md`). The input data are passed as a **`matrix_handle`** — never inline in the JSON schema.
- `method`/`orientation`/`family` = what was computed **exactly** (`family` = `dist` | `cor + as.dist` | `dist`); `p` **only** for `minkowski` (otherwise `NA_real_`). `dm_cor_dist` additionally: **`correlation_matrix`** (the n×n `r` with dimnames — chart-data **and** the interpretation of the sign) + `cor_method` + `transform`.

**Critical traps:**
- **KEOGH (normative gate 1).** Sliding-window subsequence input ⇒ a hard stop, for **every fixed step `k ≥ 1`**: the output **does not depend on the input**. Whole-series clustering is not affected.
- **DO NOT impose detrending (normative gate 2).** The node **never** transforms silently: no differencing, no seasonal adjustment, no standardisation. The metric & the transform are **explicit** `match.arg` choices.
- **The `orientation` is NEVER guessed.** A wrong orientation **does not error** — it produces a completely different, apparently valid matrix (silent-wrong). Hence `required=TRUE`, with no default.
- **The NA silent-wrong case (documented).** `the dist documentation`: the NA are excluded and the sum is **scaled up proportionally** ⇒ a result with no warning. A hard gate here (the same for `dist`).
- **Zero variance is silent-wrong.** `cor` gives **only a warning** + `NA`. A hard gate, naming the offending objects.
- **The metrics are NOT scale-invariant.** A variable in millions dominates one in percentages. Standardisation is an **explicit decision** upstream (or `transform` in #241) — never implicit here.
- **proxy silent-wrong cases (live-verified).** A zero norm: `cosine` → **silently 1**, `angular`/`Chord`/`Geodesic` → **silently NaN**; negatives in the compositional family: `Hellinger`/`Kullback` → **only a warning** "NaNs produced", the rest return meaningless numbers; `Mahalanobis` with `n<=p`/collinear columns → "Lapack routine dgesv: system is exactly singular". All three = hard gates **per family**, plus a **global post-check**: no non-finite, no **negative** distance.
- **MASKING (critical).** **Never** `library(proxy)` — nor `library(dtw)`, which **attaches** `proxy`: attaching **masks** `dist`, `as.dist` **and** `as.matrix` in the shared `source` env. `requireNamespace` + fully qualified // are used. **Careful:** even a **bare** `loadNamespace("proxy")` registers S3 methods for the `dist` class (`[`, `[[`, `dim`, `dimnames`, `names`, `subset`) ⇒ `dim(d)` becomes `c(n,n)` and `names(d)` becomes non-`NULL`. **The rule for every sibling node:** use `attr(d,"Labels")`/`attr(d,"Size")`, **never** `names(d)`/`dim(d)`.
- **1−r vs 1−|r| vs Mantegna.** Only `√(2(1−r))` satisfies the **triangle inequality**; `ward.D2` (#242) and classical MDS (#245) assume a metric/Euclidean structure (with the other two the computation runs, but the geometric interpretation changes — e.g. negative eigenvalues in `cmdscale`).
- **`canberra`/`binary` carry semantics — and they are HARD GATES.** `binary` = the asymmetric Jaccard measure on on/off data: on **continuous** macro data every element is `on`, so the metric returns **silently** a matrix **full of zeros** ("every country is identical") which then feeds `hierarchical_clustering_distance`/PAM/MDS (**live-verified silent-wrong**) ⇒ a gate on `∈ {0,1}` + a pointer to #251 `bn_quantile_bins`. `canberra` = `sum|x_i−y_i|/(|x_i|+|y_i|)` with the 0/0 terms **omitted**, "*intended for non-negative values (e.g., counts)*" ⇒ a gate on **negative** values (the same reasoning as the non-negativity gate of `dm_proxy_dist`).
- **Determinism.** Pure arithmetic, no RNG, no seed; the `attr(d,"call")` is **removed** explicitly so that two calls written differently are `identical` (pinned in the tests).

**Sources:** version 4.6.1 `the dist documentation` (the 6 methods + their formulas; "canberra: Terms with zero numerator and denominator are omitted"; binary = the asymmetric Jaccard measure; **"Missing values are allowed, and are excluded from all computations involving the rows within which they occur … the sum is scaled up proportionally to the number of columns used"** = the documentation behind the NA gate; the attributes `Size`/`Labels`/`method`/`call`); version 4.6.1 `the as.dist documentation` / `the cor documentation` (computation **by column**; a warning only on a zero standard deviation); **proxy 0.4.29** reference manual — the `pr_DB` registry of the metrics (<); **Mantegna, the reference.N. (1999)** "Hierarchical structure in financial markets", *Eur. Phys. J. B* 11(1):193–197 (`d=√(2(1−r))` as a genuine metric); **Keogh, Lin & Truppel**, "Clustering of Time Series Subsequences is Meaningless", Proc. IEEE **ICDM 2003** (extended in Keogh & Lin, *KAIS* 8(2):154–177, 2005) — `the normative gate spec` §3b normative gate 1; **arXiv:1807.04004** "Clustering Macroeconomic Time Series" + **Hamilton (2018)** "Why You Should Never Use the Hodrick-Prescott Filter", *REStat* 100(5) — normative gate 2; the wrapper footer `IMPLEMENTATION NOTE` (masking live-verified through `conflicts(detail=TRUE)` before/after + the S3 registration for the `dist` class).

### #241 K-Means / PAM partitional clustering + a rule-based choice of k (silhouette, gap) — `stats` + `cluster` (`c29_unsupervised_clustering/partitional_clustering_rule.py`)

**Functions:** `km_kmeans` [`kmeans` — Hartigan–Wong/Lloyd/Forgy/MacQueen; the centroids + the within/between SS], `km_pam` [`pam` — Partitioning Around Medoids, a robust k-medoids method; the medoids are **actual** observations], `km_silhouette` [`silhouette` — the silhouette width per observation/cluster for a **given** clustering], `km_gap` [`clusGap` + `maxSE` — the gap statistic and **all 5** selection rules].

**When:** flat (partitional) clustering of objects in a **numeric observations×features matrix** — typically countries × macro indicators or series × features. The normal flow: **`km_gap`** (a rule-based k) → **`km_kmeans`** (fast, centroids) or **`km_pam`** (robust, a "typical country" per cluster) → **`km_silhouette`** (a diagnostic of the quality of the chosen k).

**When NOT:** when you want **the whole hierarchy** and a dendrogram → #242; when you want a **probabilistic** model with k from the BIC/ICL → #244 (`mclust`); when the natural input is a **ready distance matrix** `dist` (this node takes **data**; a dist-based flow → #242/#245); on **sliding-window subsequences** (the KEOGH gate); for the **lead/lag alignment** of series → DTW (#243); for a two-dimensional display of similarity → MDS (#245); for charts (**the frontend**, §5); with **NA** in the input (no imputation here).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- A **matrix or DataFrame whose columns are all numeric**, the rows = the observations; **free of NA/NaN/Inf** (`kmeans` throws a cryptic "NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call"; the `dist` inside the silhouette **does not error at all**); **n ≥ 2**, **p ≥ 1**; the **KEOGH gate**.
- **`k ≤ the number of DISTINCT rows`** (**not** `k ≤ n`): duplicate countries break `k<n`. `km_pam`/`km_gap` additionally require **`k ≤ n−1`**; `km_gap` requires **`k_max ≥ 2`**.
- **Determinism:** `nstart ≥ 2` (a hard gate) and a **mandatory integer `seed`** in `km_kmeans`/`km_gap`.
- `km_silhouette`: `cluster` = an integer vector of length n **free of NA**, with **consecutive** ids `1.k` and **2 ≤ k ≤ n−1**.
- `km_pam`: `stand=TRUE` **together** with `transform="scale"` is **forbidden** (a double standardisation); with `stand=TRUE` no column may have a zero mean absolute deviation.
- `transform` (**explicit**, `"none"` by default): `"log"` requires **strictly positive** values; `"scale"` forbids a column of **zero variance**. The checking tool: `c00_data_utilities/fast_row_column.panel_col_stats(stat='sd')`.

**Alternatives + criterion:** **`km_kmeans`** for spherical clusters of similar size and a large n (it minimises the sum of **squares**; `Hartigan-Wong` = the default and "generally does a better job" than Lloyd/Forgy/MacQueen, the kmeans documentation). **`km_pam`** when there are **outliers** or you want **a representative that is a real observation** (it minimises the sum of **dissimilarities**; `metric="manhattan"` is even more robust; **deterministic without a seed** thanks to the build phase). **`km_gap`** for choosing k: `method="firstSEmax"` (the default, Maechler 2012) vs `"Tibs2001SEmax"` (the **original** rule — it may legitimately give **k=1** = "no clusters at all") vs `"globalSEmax"` (Dudoit & Fridlyand) vs `firstmax`/`globalmax`; `fun_cluster="pam"` + `B=500` for final (non-exploratory) results; `d_power=2` for **exactly** the Tibshirani proposal (the default `1` is the historical the engine). **`transform`**: `"scale"` when the units are incommensurable, `"log"` for multiplicative magnitudes, `"none"` when the scale **is meaningful**.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `km_kmeans`: `cluster` (a named integer, **canonicalised**) + `centers` (k×p — chart-data) + `size` + `withinss` + `tot_withinss`/`betweenss`/`totss` + `between_ratio` + `iter`/`ifault` + `canonical_order`.
- `km_pam`: `cluster` + `medoids` (k×p, **actual** observations) + **`medoid_ids`/`medoid_labels`** (which country is the representative) + `clusinfo` (`size`/`max_diss`/`av_diss`/`diameter`/`separation`) + `objective_build`/`objective_swap` + `isolation` + `silhouette` (n×3) + `avg_silhouette`/`clus_avg_silhouette`.
- `km_silhouette`: `silhouette` (n×3: `cluster`/`neighbor`/`sil_width`) + `sil_width` per observation + `avg_silhouette` + `clus_avg_silhouette` + `size` + **`n_negative`** (the observations with `s(i)<0` = probably in the **wrong** cluster).
- `km_gap`: **`gap_table`** (k×5: `k`/`logW`/`E.logW`/`gap`/`SE.sim` — the chart-data of the gap curve with error bars) + `gap`/`se_sim`/`logw`/`e_logw` + `optimal_k` + **`optimal_k_by_rule`** (all 5 rules, so that any disagreement between them is **visible**).
- **Common:** `k`/`n`/`p`/`n_distinct`, `transform` and **`transform_center`/`transform_scale`** (**§3b gate 6 — fit/apply externalisation**: the fitted parameters are returned as **numbers**, so that an out-of-sample apply can be reproduced outside the node — the KNIME "Normalize Model" pattern), `observations`/`variables`, `seed`.

**Critical traps:**
- **KEOGH (normative gate 1).** A sliding-window subsequence matrix (each row = the previous one shifted by a **fixed step `k ≥ 1`** — not only `k = 1`; the shared detector `gate_sliding_window_step`) ⇒ a hard stop: the centres degenerate into **sine waves regardless of the data** — the output **does not depend on the input**. Whole-series/cross-section clustering is not affected.
- **No silent standardisation/detrending (normative gate 2).** `transform` is an explicit `match.arg` choice with the default `"none"`.
- **DETERMINISM — three parts together.** (a) A **mandatory seed** in `km_kmeans`/`km_gap`; (b) **`nstart ≥ 2`** as a hard gate (a single random start = a local minimum that depends on the initialisation); (c) the **canonicalisation of the cluster ids**: "*The clusters are numbered in the returned object, but they are a set and no ordering is implied. (Their apparent ordering may differ by platform.)*" (the kmeans documentation Note) ⇒ a renumbering by **decreasing size**, with ties broken **lexicographically ascending** on the centroid/medoid coordinates. The caller's `.Random.seed` is **restored** (L1 purity). `identical` across 2 runs is pinned in the tests.
- **`k ≤ the DISTINCT rows`, not `k ≤ n`.** `kmeans` → "more cluster centers than distinct data points."; **`pam` does not error at all** — it returns **duplicate medoids** (silent-wrong) ⇒ a hard gate **and** a post-check on distinctness.
- **Empty clusters (silent-wrong).** "*Except for the Lloyd–Forgy method, k clusters will always be returned*" (the kmeans documentation) ⇒ with `Lloyd`/`Forgy` **fewer** than k may be returned (NaN centres) **without an error** → a post-check. `ifault=4` = non-convergence in the Quick-Transfer stage (it exists **only** in Hartigan–Wong; `NA` elsewhere). A post-check of the identity `totss == tot.withinss + betweenss`.
- **The silhouette is defined only for `2 ≤ k ≤ n−1`.** With `k=1` it returns `NA` **without an error** (and `km_pam(k=1)` gives `silinfo=NULL`, live-verified) ⇒ a hard gate.
- **The row order of the silhouette (silent-wrong).** `silhouette.partition` returns the rows **sorted** by cluster/decreasing width (`attr "Ordered"`), **not** in the order of the observations ⇒ the wrapper **restores** them through the rownames; without that, joining them back to the countries would be silently wrong.
- **`stand=TRUE` + `transform="scale"` = a double standardisation** ⇒ a hard stop. The `stand` argument of `pam` divides by the **mean absolute deviation**, not by the sd.
- **`between_ratio` always increases with k** — it is **not** a criterion for choosing k, and the "elbow" is **visual** (outside the rule-based contract). Use `km_gap` (a rule) or `km_silhouette` (a quality measure).
- **The gap statistic is a bootstrap** ⇒ it depends on the seed; `the clusGap documentation` notes that "*using B = 500 gives quite precise results*" — the default `B=100` is exploratory. `Tibs2001SEmax` **legitimately selects k=1** when all the SE exceed the differences.
- **Interpreting `s(i)`:** ~1 very well classified; ~0 between two clusters; **negative = probably in the wrong cluster** (the silhouette documentation). A singleton cluster ⇒ `s(i) := 0` by definition.
- **PAM `variant="original"` is PINNED.** `variant="faster"`/`pamonce` change the initialisation to **random** (`medoids="random"`, `nstart=1`) ⇒ they would break the determinism; they are not exposed.
- **Masking.** `library(cluster)` is **safe** — `conflicts(detail=TRUE)` after the attach is **identical to the baseline** (live-verified); no S3 method on a **foreign** generic. ⚠️ `library(proxy)`/`library(dtw)` are **forbidden** in a clustering wrapper (they mask `dist`/`as.dist`/`as.matrix`) ⇒ every call here is / qualified.
- **TERMINAL nodes** (no `register`/chaining): they return chart-ready numbers. The data come in as a **`matrix_handle`**, the `cluster` argument of `km_silhouette` as an **`int_array`** (the output of a previous node).

**Sources:** version 4.6.1 `the kmeans documentation` (the algorithm enum; "Except for the Lloyd–Forgy method, k clusters will always be returned"; `ifault=4`; the Note that the cluster ids are **a set with no ordering**); **Hartigan & Wong (1979)** *Applied Statistics* 28(1):100–108; Lloyd (1982) *IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory* 28(2):129–137; Forgy (1965); MacQueen (1967); **Kaufman & Rousseeuw (1990)** *Finding Groups in Data*, Wiley (PAM) + cluster 2.1.8.2 `the pam documentation`; **Rousseeuw (1987)** *J. Comput. Appl. Math.* 20:53–65 + `the silhouette documentation` ("silhouette statistics are only defined if 2 ≤ k ≤ n−1"; a negative `s(i)` ⇒ "probably placed in the wrong cluster"; `attr "Ordered"`); **Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie (2001)** *JRSS-B* 63(2):411–423 + `the clusGap documentation`/`the maxSE documentation` (`spaceH0`, `d.power` 1 vs 2, the 5 rules; Dudoit & Fridlyand 2002 *Genome Biology* 3(7) for `globalSEmax`); **Keogh, Lin & Truppel** ICDM 2003 / Keogh & Lin *KAIS* 8(2) 2005 (gate 1); **arXiv:1807.04004** + **Hamilton (2018)** *REStat* 100(5) (gate 2); `the normative gate spec` §3b gate 6 (fit/apply externalisation); the wrapper footer `IMPLEMENTATION NOTE` (live-verified gate messages & the masking verdict).

### #242 Hierarchical clustering + dendrogram data (hclust / cutree / agnes / diana) — `stats` + `cluster` (`c29_unsupervised_clustering/hierarchical_clustering_distance.py`)

**Functions:** `hc_hclust` [`hierarchical_clustering_distance` — agglomerative, **all 8** documented methods; an optional cut], `hc_cutree` [`cutree` (+ `as.hclust` for `agnes`/`diana`) — it cuts an **existing** tree at k **or** h], `hc_agnes` [`agnes` — agglomerative **+ the agglomerative coefficient `ac`**], `hc_diana` [`diana` — **divisive** (top-down) **+ the divisive coefficient `dc`**].

**When:** when you want **the whole hierarchy** of similarity rather than a single k — clustering countries/macro series with a **dendrogram**, so that the number of groups can be chosen **afterwards** (a cut at k or at a height h). The input is **always** a `dist` object (typically a handle from node **#240**). The flow: `hc_hclust`/`hc_agnes`/`hc_diana` → `register(tree)` → **`hc_cutree`** for further cuts of **the same** tree without recomputation.

**When NOT:** when k is **already** decided and you want centroids/medoids → #241; for a **probabilistic** k from the BIC → #244; when you have a **bare data matrix** (pass it through #240 first — `hierarchical_clustering_distance` on a matrix gives the cryptic "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"); for a **two-dimensional map** of similarity → #245 (MDS); on **sliding-window subsequences** (the KEOGH gate); for **drawing** a dendrogram (**the frontend**, §5 — we supply `merge`/`height`/`order`); for **several k at once** (one cut per call; fan out from the frontend).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- The input **must** be of class **`dist`** (a valid `attr "Size"`, of length **exactly** `n(n−1)/2`). The producer: `c29_unsupervised_clustering/distance_dissimilarity_matrix.dm_dist|dm_cor_dist|dm_proxy_dist` (#240).
- **n ≥ 2** objects ("must have n >= 2 objects to cluster" / "'n' must be >= 2"); **free of NA/NaN/Inf**; **no negative** dissimilarity (they are accepted **silently** by `hierarchical_clustering_distance`/`agnes`!).
- **The KEOGH gate** (normative): an explicit rejection if the `dist` carries the marker `attr "sliding_window_subsequences"`. **The contract of the marker:** from a `dist` the original `observations×features` matrix **cannot be recovered**, so the detector `gate_sliding_window_step` cannot run again here; and **our own** producers (#240, #243) stop it **at the source**, so they **never set** the attribute. It is an **accepted-input contract** for *external* producers of a `dist` (a `as.dist` on a user matrix, a raw handle from another flow).
- `k`/`h`: **exactly one** of the two (in `hc_cutree` one is **mandatory**; elsewhere neither is allowed ⇒ dendrogram data only); `k` a positive integer **≤ n**; `h` finite, **≥ 0** and **only on a monotone** tree. The checking tool: `hc_hclust` without `k`/`h` → look at `height`/`monotone`.
- `hc_agnes`: `par.method` **only** for `flexible` (**mandatory**, with no default) / `gaverage` (−0.1 by default); a numeric of length **1, 3 or 4**.

**Alternatives + criterion:** **`ward.D2`** for compact spherical clusters — **the only** one that implements the Ward (1963) criterion; it presupposes a **metric** distance (euclidean, or the `cor`-mantegna one from #240). **`complete`** (the default of `hierarchical_clustering_distance`): "furthest neighbour", clusters of small **diameter**, robust to chaining. **`average`/`mcquitty`** (UPGMA/WPGMA): a middle solution for clusters of dissimilar size. **`single`**: chain-like/elongated structures & outlier detection (beware of chaining). **`median`/`centroid`**: only on an explicit request — they produce **inversions**. **`hc_agnes`** when you also want the **`ac`** or the Lance–Williams generalisations (`flexible`/`gaverage`); **`agnes(method="ward")` == `hclust(method="ward.D2")`** (documented & live-verified). **`hc_diana`** for a **divisive** hierarchy: it finds the **large** structures better (splitting by diameter), whereas the agglomerative methods optimise the small ones. **`hc_cutree`** for a new cut of **the same** tree (it also accepts `agnes`/`diana` "twins").

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- **The dendrogram payload for the frontend**: `merge` (an (n−1)×2 **integer** matrix: a negative `j` = the merging of the **single** observation `|j|`, a positive `j` = the merging with the cluster formed at step `j`), `height` (the n−1 heights), `order` (a **permutation** of 1.n that gives a leaf ordering **without crossing** branches), `order_labels`, `labels`. **No drawing here** (§5).
- **`monotone`**: `FALSE` ⇒ **inversions** (median/centroid) ⇒ cutting at a height is **blocked**.
- `cluster` (a named integer per object) + `cluster_sizes` + `n_clusters` = the result of the cut (the leaf colouring); `NULL`/`NA` when neither `k` nor `h` was given.
- `hc_hclust`: `method` + `dist_method` (the metric that produced the `dist`, or `NA` if the attribute is missing). `hc_agnes`: **`ac`** (0.1) + `par_method`. `hc_diana`: **`dc`** (0.1).
- **`tree`** = the **normalised** `hierarchical_clustering_distance` object → **`register(field="tree")`** in `hc_hclust`/`hc_agnes`/`hc_diana` (a chaining producer; an object-store pointer, `docs/architecture/wrapper-to-node.md`); `hc_cutree` is **TERMINAL**. The `call` of `hierarchical_clustering_distance` is turned into a compact stub by `to_mcp.default` ⇒ no leakage.

**Critical traps:**
- **`ward.D` ≠ `ward.D2` (documented).** "*The one used by option `ward.D` … does not implement the clustering criterion of Ward (1963), whereas option `ward.D2` implements that criterion (Murtagh and Legendre 2014). With the latter, the dissimilarities are squared before cluster updating*" (the hclust documentation). The heights **differ** (pinned in the tests). Also documented: `agnes(*, method="ward")` ⇔ `hclust(*, "ward.D2")`.
- **A silent k/h precedence.** "*At least one of k or h must be specified, k overrides h if both are given*" (the cutree documentation) ⇒ if both are given, the `h` is **silently ignored**. Our gate: **exactly one**.
- **Cutting at a height only on an ultrametric tree.** "*Cutting trees at a given height is only possible for ultrametric trees (with monotone clustering heights)*" (the cutree documentation); `median`/`centroid` produce "*inversions or reversals which are hard to interpret*" (the hclust documentation) ⇒ the node exposes `monotone` and **blocks** a cut at `h` with a clear message (the reference would say "the 'height' component of 'tree' is not sorted (increasingly)").
- **The input must be a `dist`.** A bare matrix ⇒ a **cryptic** "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" (live-verified) ⇒ a hard gate with an instructive message pointing to #240 / `as.dist`.
- **Negative dissimilarities are silent-wrong.** They are **accepted** by `hierarchical_clustering_distance`/`agnes` and produce a "result" (live: `agnes` gave `ac=0.63` on a `dist` containing −3) ⇒ a hard gate. NA/NaN/Inf ⇒ "NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 10)" / "NA values in the dissimilarity matrix not allowed." — we pre-empt them (and remember: `dist` **does not error** when it produces such values, #240).
- **Degenerate input (silent-wrong).** Identical objects (all the distances 0) ⇒ `hierarchical_clustering_distance` **does not error**: it returns an **arbitrary** tree with all the heights 0; `agnes`/`diana` return **`ac`/`dc` = NaN silently** ⇒ explicit post-checks (a finite `ac`/`dc` **before** anything else; a stop when `all(height==0)`). The upstream warning signal: **`n_zero_pairs > 0`** in #240.
- **`ac`/`dc` are not comparable across samples of different size.** "*Because `ac` grows with the number of observations, this measure should not be used to compare datasets of very different sizes*" (the agnes.object documentation; the identical wording applies to `dc`). It measures **how much structure** was found **within** the same dataset.
- **`par.method` silently ignored.** It is required for `flexible` (live: "argument \"par.method\" is missing, with no default"), it has a default **only** for `gaverage` (−0.1, Belbin et al. 1992), and in every other method it is **silently ignored** (live: the same `ac` with and without) ⇒ a hard gate.
- **The normalisation of `agnes`/`diana` through `as.hclust`.** The **`diana.height` is not sorted** (it holds the **diameters** of the clusters before the split) — without the normalisation the frontend's dendrogram would be **invalid**. `hc_cutree` uses the same path ("twins" → `as.hclust`).
- **`diana` is divisive.** It starts from **one** cluster, each time picks the one with the **largest diameter** and splits it through a "splinter group" (the most distant observation); row `i` of `merge` describes the **split at step n−i** (the diana documentation) — **different** semantics from the agglomerative methods.
- **KEOGH (normative gate 1) — a second net, with an explicit contract.** #240 (and #243) already block sliding-window input structurally **at the source** — so **no producer in the engine ever sets** `sliding_window_subsequences`. The attribute exists as an **accepted-input contract** for a `dist` that came from elsewhere (a hand-made `as.dist`, a raw handle), since the original matrix cannot be recovered from a `dist` and the structural detection cannot be repeated here.
- **DO NOT impose detrending (normative gate 2).** The node **never** transforms the input — it takes the `dist` **as it is**; every transform is an explicit gated choice in #240.
- **Determinism.** `hierarchical_clustering_distance`/`cutree`/`agnes`/`diana` are **fully** deterministic (Lance–Williams updates / a splinter-group split; **no** random initialisation, unlike `kmeans`) ⇒ **no seed**; `identical` across 2 runs is pinned. **`keep.diss`/`keep.data` are PINNED to `FALSE`**: the documented default `keep.diss = n < 100` **changes the shape/size of the output exactly at n = 100**.
- **Masking.** `library(cluster)` is safe (live: `setdiff(the conflicts after, before) == character(0)`; `cluster` does not even export `plot`); **nevertheless** all the calls stay / qualified, because a **sibling wrapper of the same category** (`dtw` → it attaches `proxy`) **masks** `dist`/`as.dist`/`as.matrix` in the shared `source` env — the wrapper stays correct **regardless of the `source` order**.

**Sources:** version 4.6.1 `the hclust documentation` (the 8 methods; ward.D vs **ward.D2** + "*agnes(\*, method="ward") corresponds to hclust(\*, "ward.D2")*"; median/centroid ⇒ **inversions**; the values `merge`/`height`/`order`/`labels`/`method`/`dist.method`); version 4.6.1 `the cutree documentation` ("k overrides h"; the ultrametric requirement) / `the as.hclust documentation`; **Ward (1963)** *JASA* 58(301):236–244; **Murtagh & Legendre (2014)** *Journal of Classification* 31(3):274–295; **cluster 2.1.8.2** `the agnes documentation`/`the agnes.object documentation` (the method enum; the Lance–Williams `par.method`; the definition & the **size warning** about `ac`; `keep.diss = n < 100`) and `the diana documentation` (the divisive algorithm, the splinter group, `dc`, "stop.at.k: Non-default NOT YET IMPLEMENTED", `height` = the diameters); **Kaufman & Rousseeuw (1990)** *Finding Groups in Data*, ch. 5 (AGNES) & 6 (DIANA); **Lance & Williams (1966)** *Computer J.* 9:373–380; **Belbin, Faith & Milligan (1992)** *Multivariate Behavioral Research* 27:417–433 (flexible-beta/`gaverage`); **Keogh, Lin & Truppel** ICDM 2003 / Keogh & Lin *KAIS* 8(2) 2005 (gate 1); **arXiv:1807.04004** + **Hamilton (2018)** *REStat* 100(5) (gate 2); the wrapper footer `IMPLEMENTATION NOTE` (live-verified silent-wrong paths & the masking verdict).
