### #243 Dynamic Time Warping — a shape-based distance with a non-linear alignment in time — `dtw` + `proxy` (`c29_unsupervised_clustering/dynamic_time_warping.py`)

**Functions:** `dw_dtw` [`dtw` + the allowlist `symmetric2/symmetric1/asymmetric/…P0/P05/P1/P2` through `getExportedValue` — **never** `eval(parse)`] — the alignment of **one** query/reference pair → `distance`, `normalizedDistance`, the warping path. `dw_dist_matrix` [`dist(method = <a DTW closure>)`] — a **cross-distance matrix** over a set of series → a `dist` object (a **producer** node, `register(field='dist_object')`).

**When:** the node for **SHAPE similarity** when the **timing** differs: the GDP/industrial production of countries around the same recession but with a **lead/lag** or a different cycle **duration**; series of **unequal length**. DTW finds them "close" where the Euclidean distance (#240) considers them far apart. The flow: `dw_dtw` for the **diagnosis of one pair** (and for the warping path as chart-data) → `dw_dist_matrix` for the WHOLE set → a **handle** consumed by `hierarchical_clustering_distance`/`cutree` (#242), `pam`/`silhouette` (#241) and MDS (#245) — **the same chaining contract as #240**.

**When NOT:** series that are **already aligned** and of equal length, where Euclidean/Manhattan/Minkowski suffices → #240 `dm_dist` (far cheaper; DTW is O(N·M) **per pair**); contemporaneous linear co-movement → #240 `dm_cor_dist` (`1−cor`); **subsequence matching with a sliding window** → **forbidden** (the Keogh gate); the clustering itself (#241/#242) or the embedding (#245) — **only distances** are produced here; a cross-section `observations×features` without a time dimension (there is no warping freedom); a lead-lag **test** (CCF, cat 00/02); charts → **only** the frontend (§5).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- `dw_dtw`: `query`/`reference` **numeric vectors or `ts`** (a series_handle; the data are **never** inline in the JSON schema), **≥ 2 observations**, **free of NA/NaN/Inf**. They **may have different lengths** — that is the point of DTW.
- `dw_dist_matrix`: a **rectangular** numeric matrix/DataFrame (a matrix_handle), **≥ 2 series**, **≥ 2 observations**, free of NA/Inf, with **unique non-empty** series names (duplicates ⇒ an ambiguous matrix downstream), the **Keogh gate**. ⚠️ Because the input is rectangular, **all the series have the same length** (N = M = m in the window gate ⇒ `|N−M| = 0` and `M/N = 1` always pass); for **unequal-length** sets → pairwise `dw_dtw` calls.
- **`window.type` is MANDATORY** in both (`missing` → a `stop`) — the unconstrained `'none'` permits **pathological** alignments (one point matching dozens) and **we do not choose it silently**. **`orientation` is MANDATORY** in `dw_dist_matrix` (`rows_are_objects` vs `columns_are_objects`, the typical macro panel) — the orientation is **never guessed**.
- The checking tool: **`dw_dtw`** with the **same** settings before the O(n²) matrix (if there is no valid path, you will learn it on one pair); **`#240 dm_dist`** as a baseline (if the ranking does not change, the cheap one suffices).

**Alternatives + criterion:** the **window** — `'slantedband'` (a band around the **slanted** diagonal `[1,1]→[N,M]`) is the **right** choice for series of unequal length; `'sakoechiba'` (a band around the **main** diagonal) **requires** `window.size ≥ |N−M|`; `'itakura'` takes **no** `window.size` and **requires** `0.5 ≤ M/N < 2`; `'none'` = an explicit acceptance of unconstrained DTW. The **step.pattern** — `symmetric2` (the default, `norm = N+M`) vs `symmetric1` (**not** normalised, `norm = NA`) vs `asymmetric*` (`norm = N`, every query point matches **exactly once**, but `d(a,b) ≠ d(b,a)` ⇒ **hard-gated** in the matrix) vs `*P0/P05/P1/P2` (increasing Sakoe–Chiba slope constraints). The **transform** — `'zscore'` when the **shape** matters independently of the level/scale; the default `'none'` = **raw**. **normalize** — `TRUE` when comparing pairs of **different total length**.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `dw_dtw`: `distance` (**not** normalised — `the dtw documentation`: "the minimum global distance computed, *not* normalized") · `normalizedDistance` + `normalized_defined` + `normalization` (`"N+M"` | `"N"` | `NA`) · **`index1`/`index2` = the warping path as numeric chart-data** (`NULL` when `distance.only=TRUE`) + `path_length` + `jmin` + `N`/`M` · an echo of the settings (`window_type`/`window_size`/`step_pattern`/`transform`/`distance_only`).
- `dw_dist_matrix`: `distance_dissimilarity_matrix` (the full **symmetric** n×n double matrix with dimnames = the labels — the "distance map" chart-data) + `lower_tri` (the lower triangle by column) + `labels`/`n_objects`/`series_length` + `min_/max_/mean_distance` (the heatmap scale) + **`n_zero_pairs`** + `dist_object`.
- **`n_zero_pairs > 0` is a warning about the next step:** #245 `mds_isomds`/`mds_sammon` will **block** ("zero or negative distance between objects i and j"). Use `multidimensional_scaling_classical` or remove the identical objects.
- **Chaining:** `register(field='dist_object')` → a handle to a `dist` object for #242/#241/#245 (**the same contract as #240**). `dw_dtw` is **TERMINAL** (chart-data only).

**Critical traps (all live-verified, version 4.6.1):**
- **NORMATIVE GATE 1 — Keogh.** `.dw_prep_set` **explicitly** rejects sliding-window subsequence input (an overlap between successive rows with **any fixed step `k ≥ 1`**, **in either direction**; the shared detector `gate_sliding_window_step`). The clustering of subsequences is **provably meaningless**: the output **does not depend on the input**. Whole-series objects are **not** affected.
- **NORMATIVE GATE 2 — do not impose detrending.** The `transform` is an **explicit** `match.arg` choice with the default `'none'` (raw data); **no** silent differencing/detrending.
- **`dtwclust` was REJECTED after a live check** (the original recommendation of the research was wrong): it masks `as.matrix`/`predict`/`update`/`plot`/`show` (S4) ⇒ it **would break the forecasting wrappers** (forecast/fable/smooth/tsgarch) in the shared `source` env, **and** it drags in `flexclust`+`modeltools`+`ggrepel`+**`shinyjs`**. The functionality is **not lost**: `dtw` + `dist` give the same numbers (live-verified against `dtwDist`).
- **MASKING — never `library(dtw)`.** `library(dtw)` **attaches** `proxy`, which masks **`dist`, `as.dist` AND `as.matrix`** (`conflicts(detail=TRUE)` → ``$`package:proxy` : "as.dist" "dist" "as.matrix"``) ⇒ it would break the sibling nodes #240/#241/#242 and **every** wrapper that calls `as.matrix`. The solution: `requireNamespace` + /// everywhere. **A consequence:** the proxy entry `"DTW"` is registered only in `.onAttach` ⇒ it does not exist; that is why the `method` is passed to `dist` **as a function** (a documented API) — the same numbers, **without** mutating the global `pr_DB`.
- **SILENT-WRONG — an asymmetric step pattern in the matrix.** `dist` fills **only the lower triangle**; with `asymmetric*` we have `d(a,b) ≠ d(b,a)` (live: 18.67 vs 22.98) ⇒ the "symmetric" matrix would be **silently wrong** → a hard gate (only the 6 symmetric patterns).
- **SILENT-WRONG — `normalize=TRUE` with `symmetric1`** (`attr 'norm' = NA`) ⇒ `normalizedDistance = NA` **silently** → a hard gate.
- **SILENT-WRONG — the input.** `NA/NaN/Inf` do not give a clear message but the cryptic **"No warping path exists that is allowed by costraints"** (sic); a series of **length 1** is accepted **silently** and returns a degenerate number; `transform='zscore'` on a **constant** series ⇒ `0/0 = NaN` **silently**. All three = hard gates.
- **The windows are mathematical bounds, not a matter of taste.** A `window.size` under `'none'`/`'itakura'` would be **silently ignored** → a hard gate. The remaining "No warping path exists" (a sufficient condition for the slope-constrained `*P1/P2`) is **translated** into a structured `blocked-by-gate` message with `N`/`M`/the window/the step **and a remediation instruction** — never a cryptic error shown to the user.
- **Determinism (§5):** pure dynamic programming, **no RNG → no seed**; the `attr 'call'` is removed from the `dist` so that `identical` holds regardless of the call expression (pinned across 2 runs).
- **Omissions:** `dist.method` (LIVE: `dtw` itself warns that it "does not usually make a difference with single-variate timeseries" — Euclidean/Manhattan gave an **identical** 13.12938); `open.begin`/`open.end` (subsequence matching — the Keogh gate); `keep.internals`/`costMatrix`/`directionMatrix` (heavy N×M internals; the frontend draws from `index1`/`index2`); all the `dtwPlot*` functions (§5); `rabinerJuang`/`typeI–IV` (the same mathematics, different names); `mori2006` & `rigid`.

**Sources:** Giorgino, T. (2009) *Computing and Visualizing Dynamic Time Warping Alignments in the reference: The dtw Package*, **JSS 31(7)**, 1–24 (`citation("dtw")`, live); version 4.6.1 `the dtw documentation` (dtw 1.23.3) / `the stepPattern documentation` (the `norm` attribute) / `the dtwWindowingFunctions documentation` ("If the window size is too small … warping becomes impossible"); Sakoe & Chiba (1978) *IEEE Trans. ASSP* **26**(1) 43–49 (the sakoechiba band, the slope constraints); Itakura (1975) *IEEE Trans. ASSP* **23**(1) 67–72 (the parallelogram, the slope [1/2, 2]); `the normative gate spec` §3b normative gate 1 — Keogh, Lin & Truppel (2005) *Clustering of Time Series Subsequences is Meaningless*, **KAIS 8(2)**; `the normative gate spec` §3b normative gate 2 — *Clustering Macroeconomic Time Series* (arXiv:1807.04004) + Hamilton (2018) *REStat* 100(5); Rakthanmanon et al. (2012) KDD '12 (z-normalisation as the standard); **proxy 0.4.29** `the dist documentation` (the `method` as a function); `the normative gate spec` §3b REJECTED (the dtwclust masking, live); the wrapper footer *IMPLEMENTATION NOTE*.

### #244 Model-based clustering with an AUTOMATIC k (BIC/ICL) — `mclust` (`c29_unsupervised_clustering/clustering_rule_choice.py`)

**Functions:** `mb_mclust` [`Mclust`] — the fit + a **rule-based** choice of `(modelName, G)` by the maximum BIC → the classification / uncertainty / the posterior `z` / `pro`-`mean`-`sigma`. `mb_bic` [`mclustBIC`] — the **whole** BIC table per `model × G` (the "BIC plot" chart-data) + the top k. `mb_icl` [`mclustICL`] — the same grid under the **ICL** criterion. `mb_predict` [`predict.Mclust`] — an out-of-sample assignment with the **same** transform and the **same** canonicalisation.

**When:** a cross-sectional **`observations × features`** matrix (countries × macro indicators, households × characteristics) where **you do not know how many groups there are**. Unlike the geometric heuristics (#241 kmeans/PAM), here **both** the number `G` **and** the geometric shape of the covariance are chosen by an **information criterion** over a `model × G` grid — **no visual knee/elbow choice** (the charter: correctness is structural, not probabilistic). Also when you want a **probabilistic** assignment (the posterior `z` + the `uncertainty` **per observation**) rather than a hard one, or **non-spherical / unequal-volume** clusters (14 volume–shape–orientation configurations).

**When NOT:** when **`n ≤ p`** — the component covariances are not defined (a **hard gate**; reduce the dimensions with #117 `pca_composite` or by selecting variables); geometric/robust partitioning with a **given** k → #241; a **hierarchy/dendrogram** → #242; when the input is a **distance matrix** — `mclust` wants **raw data**, not a `dist` (→ #241 PAM or #242); the similarity of **time-series shapes** → #243 DTW; latent **dynamic** factors of time series → `dynamic_factor_nowcasting`/`sparseDFM` (cat 03); **supervised** classification (`MclustDA`), dimension reduction (`MclustDR`), **density** estimation (`densityMclust`) — they are not exposed; sliding-window subsequences (the Keogh gate); charts → **only** the frontend (§5).

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):** a numeric **matrix/DataFrame** (a matrix_handle; the data are **never** inline in the JSON schema) with **rows = observations**, **columns = variables**; **free of NA/NaN/Inf**; **n ≥ 2**, **p ≥ 1**, **`n > p`**; `G` positive integers with **`max(G) ≤ n`**; `model_names` **only** from the live `mclust.options("emModelNames")` (p>1) or `c("E","V")` (p=1); `seed` an integer; the **Keogh gate**. In `mb_predict`: a `newdata` with **exactly** the same columns (the same number **and** names/order). The checking tools: **`mb_bic`** (is the peak clear, or do several models tie?), **`mb_icl`** (if the BIC and the ICL disagree, the components **overlap**), **`dp_column_profile`** (the scale/constant columns before you decide on a `transform`).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `mb_bic` = the **diagnostic** step (the whole table as chart-data, without committing to a fit); `mb_icl` when you suspect **overlapping** components (it penalises the entropy of the classification ⇒ it prefers **distinct** clusters, typically a smaller `G`); `mb_predict` for an out-of-sample assignment; `model_names = c("EII","VII")` when n is small or **all** the models fail (the spherical ones are the most parsimonious in parameters); `transform = "scale"` when the variables have **incommensurable units** — the shapes `EEI/VVI/…` **depend on the scale**; the default `"none"` = **no silent standardisation**.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- `mb_mclust`: `model_name` + `G` (the **selected** ones) · `cluster` (a named integer, **canonicalised**) + `size` · `uncertainty` (a named numeric) and `z` (the n×G posterior) = **the main chart-data** (which observations sit "on the boundary") · `pro` / `mean` (p×G) / `sigma` (p×p×G) · `loglik`/`df`/`bic`/`icl` · **`bic_table`** (G×models — the "BIC plot") + `top_bic` (a DataFrame `{model,G,value,label}`) · `avg_uncertainty` · **`g_at_upper_bound`** · `G_tried`/`models_tried`/`n`/`p`/`n_distinct`.
- `mb_bic` / `mb_icl`: `criterion` + `bic_table` | `icl_table` + `top` + `best_model`/`best_G`/`best_value` + **`n_failed`** (how many `(model,G)` combinations failed).
- `mb_predict`: `classification` (the **same** canonicalisation) + `z` (n_new×G) + `uncertainty` + `n_new`/`new_observations` + `train_cluster`/`train_size` for reference.
- **Common:** `transform` + **`transform_center`/`transform_scale`** (§3b gate 6 — **fit/apply externalisation**: they are returned as **numbers** and applied **as they are** to the `newdata`) + `observations`/`variables` + `seed` + **`subset_init`** + `canonical_order`.

**Critical traps (all live-verified, version 4.6.1):**
- **Determinism — the critical point.** For `n ≤ mclust.options("subset")` (**2000 by default**) the initialisation is **model-based hierarchical clustering** (hc/SVD) ⇒ **deterministic WITHOUT a seed** (2 runs `identical`, asserted). **But** for `n > subset` `mclustBIC` performs `initialization.subset <- sample(..)` ⇒ it is **non-deterministic** (two unseeded runs gave a different `loglik`/classification). That is why **every** function takes a `seed` (1234 by default) and runs inside `.mb_with_seed`, which **restores** the caller's RNG state (L1 purity); the field **`subset_init`** states explicitly which path was taken.
- **SILENT-WRONG — `p > n`.** `Mclust` with **3 observations × 4 variables** **does not error**: it returns a fit (G=2, EEI) with singular covariances ⇒ **our own hard gate `p < n`**.
- **SILENT-WRONG — NA.** `Mclust` **does not error** on NA: it **silently drops** the rows (n 40 → 39) ⇒ the classification **no longer corresponds** to the input rows. (`Inf` throws the cryptic "NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call".)
- **SILENT-WRONG — `max(G) > n`.** `G = 1:20` with `n = 10` **does not error**: it truncates **silently** and returns `G = 9`. (`G = 0` → the cryptic "No classification with the specified number of clusters".)
- **SILENT-WRONG — total failure.** When **all** the candidate `(modelName, G)` combinations fail, `Mclust` **returns `NULL`** instead of erroring ⇒ a hard gate; likewise an all-NA BIC/ICL table is blocked with an instructive message.
- **SILENT-WRONG — `mb_predict`.** `predict.Mclust` checks **only** the `ncol` ⇒ a **shuffled column order** gives **wrong assignments without an error** → a hard gate on the number **and** the names/order.
- **Label switching → CANONICALISATION.** The component ids of a mixture are **a set with no ordering**; they are renumbered by **decreasing size** with ties broken **lexicographically ascending** on the `mean` coordinates, and the **same** permutation is applied to `cluster`/`z`/`pro`/`mean`/`sigma`/`size` **and** in `mb_predict` (`canonical_map`). Without it the labels are **not** reproducible.
- **The BIC convention of `mclust` — the OPPOSITE sign.** `BIC = 2·loglik − df·log(n)` ⇒ **the larger the better** (verified numerically: `loglik = −182.0873`, `df = 8`, `n = 40` → `−393.686 == fit.bic`). `BIC` uses the **reverse** convention ⇒ do **not** compare it with the BIC of other packages; `top` sorts in **decreasing** order.
- **NORMATIVE GATE 1 (Keogh).** A sliding-window subsequence matrix (each row = the previous one shifted by a **fixed step `k ≥ 1`** — not only `k = 1`; the shared detector `gate_sliding_window_step`) is **explicitly rejected** — the output **does not depend on the input**. Whole-series / cross-section matrices are not affected.
- **NORMATIVE GATES 2 & 6.** `transform` = an **explicit** `match.arg` choice (`none`/`center`/`scale`/`log`, `none` by default) — **no** silent standardisation; `scale` on a column of **zero variance** → a hard stop (a division by 0 → NaN); `log` requires **strictly positive** values; the fitted `center`/`scale` are **externalised** and applied as they are to the `newdata`.
- **The 14 configurations** (read live from `mclust.options("emModelNames")`, **never** from memory): `EII VII EEI VEI EVI VVI EEE VEE EVE VVE EEV VEV EVV VVV` (volume–shape–orientation; E=equal, V=variable, I=identity); for `p = 1` **only** `c("E","V")`. An unknown name → the cryptic "invalid model name" ⇒ an allowlist gate.
- **`g_at_upper_bound` is a diagnostic, not a gate:** if the selected `G` equals `max(G)`, the search was **truncated** — widen the range. It is not an invalid result, so it is not blocked.
- **MASKING — `library(mclust)` is used here** (the §3.a #1 exception is not needed): `conflicts(detail=TRUE)` before/after is **identical** (`identical == TRUE`, `setdiff == character(0)`) ⇒ **zero masking**; and the `.__S3MethodsTable__.` registers methods **only** on generics of the same package (cf. the `quanteda $.dfm` incident). The attach is **necessary**: `Mclust` calls `mclustBIC` **unqualified**. ⚠️ **Never** `library(proxy)`/`library(dtw)` in this category (they mask `dist`/`as.dist`/`as.matrix`) — hence `sd`/`setNames`/`predict` are fully qualified.
- **L2 safety:** `mclustBIC`/`mclustICL` carry an `attr initialization.hcPairs` (an `hc` object **with a `call`** = language) ⇒ they are **stripped** down to a bare numeric matrix before leaving the wrapper. `top` is a **DataFrame** because `json_interchange_parse` serialises a named numeric as an **anonymous array** (the "MODEL,G" labels would be lost).
- **TERMINAL nodes:** no `register`/handle chaining; `mb_predict` **re-fits** on `x` (the same deterministic path) so that the node stays **stateless** (§4).
- **Post-checks (independent recomputations, not trust in the package):** `sum(pro) = 1`; `rowSums(z) = 1`; `uncertainty = 1 − max(z)`; the shapes of `mean` (p×G) / `sigma` (p×p×G); `length(classification) = n`; the selected `G` within the range.

**Sources:** Scrucca, Fraley, Murphy & Raftery (2023) *Model-Based Clustering, Classification, and Density Estimation Using mclust in the reference*, Chapman & Hall/CRC (ISBN 978-1032234953 — `citation("mclust")`, live); the **mclust 6.1.3** reference manual (`?Mclust`, `the mclustBIC documentation`, `the mclustICL documentation`, `the predict.Mclust documentation`, `the mclust.options documentation`); Fraley & Raftery (2002) *JASA* **97**(458) 611–631 (choosing `(modelName, G)` by BIC); Banfield & Raftery (1993) *Biometrics* **49**(3) 803–821 (the volume–shape–orientation parameterisation); Biernacki, Celeux & Govaert (2000) *IEEE TPAMI* **22**(7) 719–725 (ICL); Schwarz (1978) *Ann. Statist.* **6**(2) 461–464 (the BIC — ⚠️ the opposite sign in mclust); `the normative gate spec` §3b normative gates 1/2/6 + the live-verified notes ("the mclust default init = model-based hierarchical ⇒ deterministic without a seed"; "`Mclust` with p>n **does not** error"); the wrapper footer *IMPLEMENTATION NOTE*.

### #245 Multidimensional Scaling — a similarity map from a distance matrix — `stats` + `MASS` (`c29_unsupervised_clustering/multidimensional_scaling_classical.py`)

**Functions:** `multidimensional_scaling_classical` [`cmdscale(eig = TRUE, add)`] — **classical/metric** MDS = principal coordinates analysis (Gower 1966; Mardia 1978) → the points + **all** the eigenvalues + **both** GOF measures + the **Cailliez** constant `ac`. `mds_isomds` [`isoMDS`] — **non-metric** MDS after Kruskal (a monotone transform of the dissimilarities) → the points + the `stress` **as a percentage**. `mds_sammon` [`sammon`] — the **non-linear** Sammon (1969) mapping, with the stress **weighted by 1/d** ⇒ an emphasis on the **small** distances.

**When:** the node for the **"similarity map"**: you have a `dist` matrix (typically from #240 `dm_dist`/`dm_cor_dist`/`dm_proxy_dist` or from #243 `dw_dist_matrix` with DTW) and want a **2D scatter** of "which countries/indicators are close to which", together with a **scree** plot (the eigenvalues) and **quality measures** of the mapping. The node is **visualisation/embedding**, **not** clustering: it produces no labels.

**When NOT:** for **assignment to groups** → #241 `kmeans`/`pam`, #242 `hierarchical_clustering_distance`/`cutree`, #244 `mclust`; from a **raw data matrix** without a preceding distance node (the input **must** be a `dist`); for the dimensional reduction of the **variables** with loadings/a biplot → #117 `pca_composite`/`pca_biplot_coords` (MDS maps **objects** from **dissimilarities**; on a Euclidean distance `cmdscale` **coincides** with PCA on the scores); for **mixed I(0)/I(1) time series** → #256; subsequence embedding (the Keogh gate); charts → **only** the frontend (§5): here **only the coordinates** are returned.

**Preconditions (+ checking tool):**
- **The central gate:** the input **must** be a **`dist`** object (a raw handle → `resolve_handle(as="raw")` returns it **as it is** so that the wrapper can decide); a **valid `Size`**, a consistent `length == n(n−1)/2`, **n ≥ 2**; **free of NA/NaN/Inf**; **no negative** dissimilarity; **not all zero**; the **Keogh gate** (the `sliding_window_subsequences` attribute).
- **`k` in `{1, 2, …, n−1}`** (documented, `the cmdscale documentation`) **and** the **positive** eigenvalues must be **≥ k** (otherwise the solution has fewer columns → the node blocks with "ask for a smaller k").
- **`mds_isomds`/`mds_sammon` additionally: no ZERO distance** (duplicate objects). The parameters: `maxit`/`niter` **positive integers**, `tol > 0`, `magic > 0`, `p ≥ 1`.
- The checking tools: **`dm_dist`** (the typical producer of the handle); **`dw_dist_matrix`** → read the **`n_zero_pairs`**: `> 0` ⇒ `isoMDS`/`sammon` **will block**, use `multidimensional_scaling_classical`; **`multidimensional_scaling_classical` always first** (it gives `n_eig_negative` and `gof_abs`/`gof_pos`, and it is **the initialisation** of the other two).

**Alternatives + criterion:** `add = TRUE` **only** when `n_eig_negative > 0` or `gof_abs < gof_pos` (non-Euclidean dissimilarities ⇒ the additive **Cailliez** constant, the field `ac`); `mds_isomds` when the dissimilarities are **ordinal** / their absolute scale is not reliable (it keeps only the **ordering**); `mds_sammon` when you want the **small/local** distances preserved (the stress is weighted by `1/d`); **a smaller `k`** when the positive eigenvalues do not suffice; #117 PCA when you start from raw data and want **loadings**.

**Reading the output** (aligned with L2 `to_mcp`):
- **`points`** = an n × k numeric matrix with `rownames = the labels` and `colnames = Dim1.Dimk` — **the main chart-data** (a 2D scatter). The same dimensions/labels in **all three** methods. It is accompanied by `labels`/`n`/`k`/`method`.
- `multidimensional_scaling_classical`: `eig` (**all** n eigenvalues = the scree) + `eig_retained` + `n_eig_positive` + **`n_eig_negative`** (`>0` ⇒ non-Euclidean dissimilarities) + `var_explained_abs`/`var_explained_pos` (**both** denominators from `the cmdscale documentation`) + `gof`/`gof_abs`/`gof_pos` + **`ac`** (Cailliez; `0` when `add=FALSE`).
- `mds_isomds`: `stress` **as a percentage** (`the isoMDS documentation`: "The final stress achieved (in percent)") + `stress_fraction` + `maxit`/`tol`/`p` + `init_method = "cmdscale"`.
- `mds_sammon`: `stress` (the Sammon one — **not** a percentage) + `niter`/`magic`/`tol` + `init_method = "cmdscale"`.
- **Common diagnostics (ours, computed identically ⇒ COMPARABLE):** `stress_raw = sqrt(sum((d−d_hat)^2)/sum(d^2))` (the Kruskal stress-1 **without** a monotone transform; 0 = perfect) · `fit_correlation = cor(d, d_hat)` (**`NA_real_`** when either side is constant, e.g. an equilateral configuration — that is **not** an error) · `dist_fitted` (the Shepard chart-data).

**Critical traps (all live-verified, version 4.6.1):**
- **The input must be a `dist`.** `cmdscale` **also** accepts a matrix/DataFrame ("a full symmetric matrix") **but** it **silently** accepts a **non-symmetric** matrix too (with `m[1,2] = 99` it returned a GOF of `0.577/0.99` **without a warning**) ⇒ silent-wrong. A `dist` is symmetric with a zero diagonal by definition.
- **ZERO / DUPLICATE DISTANCES — the main trap of this node.** `isoMDS` **and** `sammon` require **strictly positive** distances ("must be positive except for self-distance", `the isoMDS documentation`/`the sammon documentation`) and fail with **"zero or negative distance between objects i and j"** on **duplicate rows**. The node blocks **before** the call and **names** the objects (MASS gives only indices). `multidimensional_scaling_classical` does **not** have this restriction. The upstream indicator: `dw_dist_matrix.n_zero_pairs > 0` (#243).
- **SILENT-WRONG in `cmdscale`:** **negative** dissimilarities are accepted **silently** (a live GOF of `0.668/0.818`); **all** the distances zero → `GOF = NaN/NaN` **silently**. Also `dist` **does not error** when it produces NA ⇒ an explicit `NA/NaN/Inf` check here.
- **SILENT-WRONG in the MASS arguments:** `maxit = 0` / `niter = 0` are **accepted silently** → they return the **unoptimised** initial configuration; `tol ≤ 0` is accepted silently → it stops prematurely (live: a stress of **0.44** instead of **0.0069**); `magic ≤ 0` is accepted silently → **no** optimisation at all; `p = 0` **hangs** (it does not terminate; the Minkowski distance is a metric only for `p ≥ 1`). All hard gates.
- **A dimension post-check.** `cmdscale` returns **fewer** columns than `k` when the positive eigenvalues are `< k` (live: `k = 9` → **7** columns, with the warning "only 7 of the first 9 eigenvalues are > 0") and **then** `isoMDS`/`sammon` fail with the cryptic **"invalid initial configuration"** ⇒ the node requires **exactly** n × k and gives a clear message.
- **The stress values are NOT comparable across methods:** the `isoMDS` stress is **a percentage** and allows a monotone transform; the Sammon stress is **weighted by 1/d** and is not a percentage. That is why the common **`stress_raw`** is also given — that is the comparable quantity.
- **The two GOF measures:** `g_i = (sum_{j≤k} lambda_j)/(sum_j T_i(lambda_j))` with `T₁ = |·|` and `T₂ = max(·,0)` ⇒ `gof_abs ≠ gof_pos` **only** when there are negative eigenvalues; `var_explained_abs`/`var_explained_pos` use the **same** denominators (a post-check: `sum(var_explained_*) == gof_*`).
- **NEVER interpret the sign of an axis.** The configuration is determined **only** up to translation/rotation/reflection (`the cmdscale documentation`: "the reflection chosen may differ between **the reference** platforms"; `the isoMDS documentation`/`the sammon documentation`: "the result can vary considerably from machine to machine"). In the container the versions are **pinned** (the lockfile) ⇒ a stable result, but the **interpretation** rests on **distances between points**, never on signs.
- **Determinism (§5):** all three are **fully** deterministic ⇒ **no seed**; the initialisation of `isoMDS`/`sammon` is passed **explicitly** (`y = cmdscale(d, k)` = the **documented** default; an identical result live-verified) so that the determinism does not depend on a future change of the default; `identical` across 2 runs is pinned.
- **NORMATIVE GATE 1 (Keogh):** if the `dist` carries the attribute `sliding_window_subsequences`, the node **explicitly rejects** it — **mapping** subsequences is just as meaningless as clustering them. **The contract of the marker:** the producers #240/#243 reject such input **at the source**, so **no producer in the engine ever sets** the attribute; it exists as an **accepted-input contract** for a `dist` that came from elsewhere (a raw handle / an `as.dist` on a user matrix), because the original `observations×features` matrix cannot be recovered from a `dist` and the structural detection is not repeated here.
- **NORMATIVE GATE 2 (do not impose detrending):** the node **never** transforms the input — it takes the `dist` **as it is**. The `transform`/`distance` are **explicit gated** choices of the **upstream** distance node.
- **MASKING:** `library(MASS)` is **not** called — the live `conflicts(detail=TRUE)` before/after shows **only** the dataset `npk` (**no** function), but because masking **does** exist the §3.a #1 exception applies: `requireNamespace("MASS")` + `isoMDS`/`sammon`. **In addition** all the calls are fully qualified because the **sibling** wrapper `dtw-distance` brings in `proxy` (which masks `dist`/`as.dist`/`as.matrix`) into the **shared** `source` env — the wrapper stays correct **regardless of the `source` order**.
- **Omissions:** `x.ret` (the heavy n×n doubly centred matrix); `eig`/`list.` are **PINNED TRUE** (we always need the eigenvalues + the GOF); `trace` is **PINNED FALSE** (it prints progress, §5); `y` (the initial configuration: **data** of size n×k, never inline in the JSON schema); `Shepard` (the same numbers are given as `dist_fitted`/`stress_raw`/`fit_correlation`); `smacof` (**REJECTED** in `the normative gate spec` §3b: `cmdscale` + MASS suffice, live-verified with the GOF). **TERMINAL** nodes: no `register`/chaining.

**Sources:** version 4.6.1 `the cmdscale documentation` ("Also known as *principal coordinates analysis* (Gower 1966)"; `k` "must be in {1, 2, …, n−1}"; the definition of the `GOF`; "only determined up to location, rotations and reflections … the reflection chosen may differ between **the reference** platforms"); Gower (1966) *Biometrika* **53**(3/4) 325; Mardia (1978) *Communications in Statistics – Theory and Methods* **7**(13) 1233–1241; Cailliez (1983) *Psychometrika* **48**(2) 305–308 (the analytic solution behind `add=TRUE`); version 4.6.1 `the isoMDS documentation` (MASS 7.3-65; "must be positive except for self-distance"; "stress … in percent"; the default `y = cmdscale(d, k)`); `the sammon documentation` (the stress "weighted by the distances … scale-free"; `magic` = the diagonal-Newton step); Sammon (1969) *IEEE Trans. Comput.* **C-18** 401–409; Kruskal (1964) *Psychometrika* **29**(1) 1–27; Cox & Cox (2001) *Multidimensional Scaling* 2nd ed. + Venables & Ripley (2002) *MASS* 4th ed. (Rs of the help pages); `the normative gate spec` §3b live-verified gates ("'k' must be in {1, 2,. n − 1}"; "isoMDS: zero or negative distance between objects i and j ⇒ a gate on duplicate rows"; "`dist` with NA **does not** error") + normative gates 1 & 2 + the REJECTED `smacof`; the wrapper footer *IMPLEMENTATION NOTE*.
